item.title: Friday, May 3, 2024
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: The previous newsletter said that things were, considering the forecast for no rain, the Knicks and Rangers were trending up. Rain may be in the forecast this weekend, but the Knicks and Rangers have since both won their first playoff…
item.content:encoded:
The previous newsletter said that things were, considering the forecast for no rain, the Knicks and Rangers were trending up. Rain may be in the forecast this weekend, but the Knicks and Rangers have since both won their first playoff series, so things are still trending up. Also, just like last week, I doubt anyone signed up for this for sports, so I'll shift to civics.

First, we started the week with a CB6 Permits & Licenses meeting on Monday, where we saw three liquor license applications that were recommended for approval. One was for 347 Van Brunt Street in Red Hook, another in Gowanus at 267 Douglass Street, and the third was for 295 5th Avenue in Park Slope. Those three items, along with two approved by our Landmark Committee last week, now advance to a vote from our Full Board at our May meeting. The May Full Board meeting, in-person at Van Alen & virtually over Zoom, is this Wednesday, May 8th, starting at 6:30 PM.

Secondly, a bill (sponsored by CM Alexa Aviles) that required NYC DOT to redesign the city truck route became law last year. Today, thanks to that law, a portal for feedback on how the truck routes should be withdrawn was launched. We've wanted and been on the record for years, calling newer and safer truck routes, especially in Red Hook. So go to bit.ly/dottruckfeedback and let DOT know your thoughts on how this should be done.

Speaking of thoughts and how things should be done, I'll stop here and suggest you read the rest of this email, which includes information on Open Streets, a bike tour, Open Studios, Atlantic Ave Art, ASP, and more.

No matter what you do, I wish you the best, and let's go Rangers and Knicks.

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: It’s rare to send this email and not expect rain, so things ar
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: It’s rare to send this email and not expect rain, so things are trending up. Hopefully, that trend will continue and be applied to the postseason play of the Knicks and Rangers.
item.content:encoded:
It’s rare to send this email and not expect rain, so things are trending up. Hopefully, that trend will continue and be applied to the postseason play of the Knicks and Rangers. But since I doubt anyone subscribed to this newsletter to read about sports, I’ll shift to civics. 

First, on Thursday, April 25th, our Landmarks/Land Use committee met and recommended approval, with conditions, for two Certificates of Appropriateness (C of A). The first was for doors at 218 Lincoln Place, and the second was for the front and rear facade, materials, and massing at 431 7th Avenue. Those landmark items and liquor licenses slated to be reviewed Monday will be on the Agenda at our May 8th Full Board meeting.  

Second, check out the interactive housing production maps the Department of City Planning released. From macro and micro perspectives, the maps help highlight the city’s lacking and uneven housing production amid an absolute crisis. Looking at it by community district, you’ll see that of the 59 community districts, housing production in 10 equals the other 49, and those ten relatively high-producing districts do not include CB6. We only added 207 housing units in CB6 last year. 

Third, I recommend that you read the rest of this email. If you do, you’ll find meetings, petitions, coffee, cleanups, surveys, lobsters, ASP, Arts, and more. Whether you read it or not, I wish you the best, and Let’s Go Rangers & Knicks!

It’s rare to send this email and not expect rain, so things are trending up. Hopefully, that trend will continue and be applied to the postseason play of the Knicks and Rangers. But since I doubt anyone subscribed to this newsletter to read about sports, I’ll shift to civics. 

First, on Thursday, April 25th, our Landmarks/Land Use committee met and recommended approval, with conditions, for two Certificates of Appropriateness (C of A). The first was for doors at 218 Lincoln Place, and the second was for the front and rear facade, materials, and massing at 431 7th Avenue. Those landmark items and liquor licenses slated to be reviewed Monday will be on the Agenda at our May 8th Full Board meeting.  

Second, check out the interactive housing production maps the Department of City Planning released. From macro and micro perspectives, the maps help highlight the city’s lacking and uneven housing production amid an absolute crisis. Looking at it by community district, you’ll see that of the 59 community districts, housing production in 10 equals the other 49, and those ten relatively high-producing districts do not include CB6. We only added 207 housing units in CB6 last year. 

Third, I recommend that you read the rest of this email. If you do, you’ll find meetings, petitions, coffee, cleanups, surveys, lobsters, ASP, Arts, and more. Whether you read it or not, I wish you the best, and Let’s Go Rangers & Knicks! 

Related tools

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Saturday, April 20, 2024
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: As usual, it’s either raining, about to rain or recently rained, as I am sending this. However, correlation isn’t causation, so regardless of the rain, I’ll keep sending these emails as the weekend begins.
item.content:encoded:
As usual, it’s either raining, about to rain or recently rained, as I am sending this. However, correlation isn’t causation, so regardless of the rain, I’ll keep sending these emails as the weekend begins. This weekend has a lot going on, especially with Earth Day approaching, but before that, I’d like to look back on two things that happened in the week that was.  

First, on Monday, with DOT, CB8, and CB9, we hosted a Grand Army Plaza redesign meeting. The main “news” of the meeting was that DOT laid out a schedule, which ended with a construction timeline being announced this winter; you can see the presentation at bit.ly/dotgap4152024

Second, the 341 10TH Street rezoning was approved by the City Council yesterday. It’s essentially identical to what we supported in December, so this is great news. It adds hundreds of units of affordable housing in a transit-rich location, and, as was part of our conditions, it includes a community benefit agreement that gives current tenants a greater role in ensuring this plan is implemented correctly. Big credit, thanks, and congrats to Council Members Aviles and Hanif for getting this across the finish line. 

I’ll stop here and let the rest of the email speak, or in this case, type, for me. If you read the rest, you’ll find information about Earth Day, upcoming meetings, alternate side parking, and more. Whether you read the rest or not, I wish you the best. 

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Remind, Recap, Close
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Hopefully, you’re doing well as we close out a week that started with an eclipse and ended with rain. In between all that, our Full Board met on Wednesday.
item.content:encoded:
Hopefully, you’re doing well as we close out a week that started with an eclipse and ended with rain. In between all that, our Full Board met on Wednesday. At that Full Board meeting, we recommended approving three liquor licenses, one land use item, and increasing the budget for NYC Parks. 

One liquor license was for a cafe, catering, and event space at 177 Dwight Street in Red Hook, another for a Chinese restaurant at 392 5th Avenue in Park Slope, and a bar in Gowanus at 274 3rd Avenue. The bar will be owned and operated by the same people who own and operate the neighboring establishment, Cafe Mars. The rezoning was for a ULURP application for 150 Mill Street to change the zoning from the current M1﻿-1 to an M1-5 to facilitate the development of a mixed-use building for retail, health care, and office space with the condition that the applicant agrees to a binding Community Benefits Agreement with NYCHA Red Hook Tenant Associations and other community-based organizations. The vote supporting our parks reiterated support for the Play Fair Campaign. 

I’ll stop here and let the rest of the email speak, or in this case, type, for me. Read the rest, and you’ll find information about this weekend’s BQE closure, Monday’s Grand Army Plaza meeting, and more. No matter what you read or do, I wish you the best.

item.title: Earthquakes, Eclipses, Meetings & More
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I'm glad you've survived the earthquake, and that rain is unlikely to fall this weekend. I suspect all the attention given to the upcoming eclipse led to earthquakes, feeling neglected, and thus acting out.
item.content:encoded:
I'm glad you've survived the earthquake, and that rain is unlikely to fall this weekend. I suspect all the attention given to the upcoming eclipse led to earthquakes, feeling neglected, and thus acting out. With that, I'll cease attempting analysis and shift to civics.   

First, the asylee shelter in Gowanus has opened. I've been clear that we support the shelter and continue to do so. While not perfect by any means, the reality is that not supporting shelters would result in more people sleeping on the street. With that in mind, we've joined Council Member Hanif, Assemblymember Simon, Senator Gounardes, and Congressman Goldman in a joint statement of support for the shelter and making clear that we'll work with DHS and the shelter provider to ensure a safe and welcoming environment for everyone.

Secondly, I'd like to highlight two upcoming CB6 meetings. The first of those meetings is our Full Board meeting this Wednesday, April 10th. It'll start at 6:30 p.m. in person at Van Alen and virtually over Zoo. The second meeting involves us joining CB8 and CB9 to hear from DOT regarding plans(increased safety and pedestrianization) for Grand Army Plaza. It will be held on Monday, April 15th, from 6 until 8 p.m. in person at the Brooklyn Public Library Central Branch.

I'll let the rest of the email speak, or in this case, type, for me. I hope you read it. If you do, you'll learn about prior earthquakes, puzzles, participatory budgeting, alternate side parking, and, of course, the eclipse.

No matter what you do, I wish you the best. 

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: For those who observing Easter or Ram
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: For those who observing Easter or Ramadan I hope you’re able to find peace and joy.Of course, the same hope extends to those not observing or celebrating anything, and regardless of religion, there's some hope that it may not rain this…
item.content:encoded:
For those who observing Easter or Ramadan I hope you’re able to find peace and joy.Of course, the same hope extends to those not observing or celebrating anything, and regardless of religion, there's some hope that it may not rain this weekend. Regardless of religion or rain I’ll recap some recommendations and make some suggestions.

On Monday, our Permits & Licenses Committee met at 250 Baltic Street and voted to recommend approval of three liquor license applicants: one for a cafe, catering, and event space at 177 Dwight Street in Red Hook, another for a Chinese restaurant at 392 5th Avenue in Park Slope, and a bar in Gowanus at 274 3rd Avenue. The bar will be owned and operated by the same people who own and operate the neighboring establishment, Cafe Mars. On Thursday, at Van Alen & Zoom, our Land Use committee met and reviewed a ULURP application for 150 Mill Street to change the zoning from the current M1﻿-1 to an M1-5 to facilitate the development of a mixed-use building for retail, health and care, and office space. The committee voted to recommend approval with conditions that community benefits, such as a supermarket, be part of a binding community benefit agreement. 

The recommended approvals in the preceding paragraph now progress to a vote at our next Full Board meeting on Wednesday, April 10th, beginning at 630 PM, in person at the Van Alen Institute and virtually via Zoom.

I'll stop here and suggest reading the rest of this email, which contains information on the impacts of downzoning during the Bloomberg era (raised rents, reduced housing options, and increased displacement)t. You'll also find egg hunts, voting, puzzles, open streets, gardening, drawing, and more. 

No matter what you read or don't read, I wish you the best.

But before the weekend, I'll recap some recommendations and make some suggestions.

On Monday, our Permits & Licenses Committee met at 250 Baltic Street and voted to recommend approval of three liquor license applicants: one for a cafe, catering, and event space at 177 Dwight Street in Red Hook, another for a Chinese restaurant at 392 5th Avenue in Park Slope, and a bar in Gowanus at 274 3rd Avenue. The bar will be owned and operated by the same people who own and operate the neighboring establishment, Cafe Mars. On Thursday, at Van Alen & Zoom, our Land Use committee met and reviewed a ULURP application for 150 Mill Street to change the zoning from the current M1﻿-1 to an M1-5 to facilitate the development of a mixed-use building for retail, health and care, and office space. The committee voted to recommend approval with conditions that community benefits, such as a supermarket, be part of a binding community benefit agreement. 

The recommended approvals in the preceding paragraph now progress to a vote at our next Full Board meeting on Wednesday, April 10th, beginning at 630 PM, in person at the Van Alen Institute and virtually via Zoom.

I'll stop here and suggest reading the rest of this email, which contains information on the impacts of downzoning during the Bloomberg era, which raised rents, reduced housing options, and increased displacement. You'll also find egg hunts, voting, puzzles, open streets, gardening, drawing, and more.

item.title: Saturday, March 23, 2024
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Correlation is not causation, but with rain expected on yet another Saturday, I contemplated not clicking send on this email and seeing what shook out. However, since we're advisory, aside from advising that environmentally conscious…
item.content:encoded:
Correlation is not causation, but with rain expected on yet another Saturday, I contemplated not clicking send on this email and seeing what shook out. However, since we're advisory, aside from advising that environmentally conscious policies be implemented, we have no role in the weather, and you can, of course, see that I clicked send. I've got two things to go over.

First, according to extensive research conducted by the Citizens Budget Commission, CB6 is the happiest place in the city, and apparently, by comparison with the present, quality of life was higher when a tall CB6 resident was Mayor. That's an oversimplification of the study, so I recommend reading about it on your own. When reading, you'll see a city experienced differently based on how resources are distributed. Resources such as access to schools, parks, and, most importantly, housing can all be made more accessible with better policy choices. With this in mind, we've made and will continue to support policy, like approving the Gowanus Rezoning and shelters and pushing for park funding.

Secondly, keeping with the theme of taking positions, we'll review liquor licenses this Monday, March 25th, and on Thursday, March 28th, we'll review a rezoning for 150 Mill Street. Both meetings start at 6:30 PM. Monday's meeting will be held at 250 Baltic Street, and Thursday's will be held at Van Alen & Zoom.

On that note, I'll stop and suggest you scroll down to read the rest. If you do, you'll find an exhibit at the Old Stone House, a presidential primary, a 4th Avenue survey, meetings, alternate-side parking suspension, and more. If you don't, I still wish you the best.

Related tools

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Weekly Update
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: To those who'll soon celebrate snakes being driven into the sea, I say "Happy Saint Patrick's Day or, in Gaelic, "Lá Fhéile Pádraig sona duit!". Whether or not you're celebrating, I hope this email finds you well as we start a weekend…
item.content:encoded:
To those who'll soon celebrate snakes being driven into the sea, I say "Happy Saint Patrick's Day or, in Gaelic, "Lá Fhéile Pádraig sona duit!". Whether or not you're celebrating, I hope this email finds you well as we start a weekend that'll include the more famous Saint Patrick's Parade on Saturday and the better Saint Patrick's Parade right here in CB6 along Prospect Park West on the actual Saint Patrick's Day, Sunday Match 17th. There's also a half marathon on Sunday, so be mindful of traffic changes. 

The parades and half marathon follow a week that saw our Full Board Meet on Wednesday, March 13th. At the full board meeting, we approved a street co-naming for the D'amicos, two landmark applications, exciting plans for the Old Stone House, and five liquor licenses. A liquor license of particular interest was for 521 Hicks Street, where the owners of Cafe Spaghetti and Swoony's will open a Chinese restaurant. 

This week also saw Park Slope's Fifth Avenue named the coolest street in the city. Unfortunately, one of the things that makes it so cool, Open Streets, is threatened by budget cuts, which has spurred efforts to avoid such a shortsighted fate. I could go on, but I'll stop and suggest you scroll down to read the rest of this email, where you'll find even more useful information. 

Whether you heed this suggestion or stop here, I hope you have a good weekend.

item.title: Friday, March 8, 2024
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: We head into a rainy weekend after a busy week. I'll offer a week recap, a reminder for the next week, and some recommendations.
item.content:encoded:
We head into a rainy weekend after a busy week. I'll offer a week recap, a reminder for the next week, and some recommendations. 

On Monday night, Council Member Hanif hosted a meeting regarding the emergency shelter planned for 3rd Street, which still needs an opening date and is hardly perfect. Eric McClure and I were on the dais with the shelter operator BHRAG, the Department of Social Services, and CM Hanif, who did a great job running the meeting. Echoing what we said in December, we made clear that we support the "fair share" of locating shelters and, therefore, this shelter and that our community must contribute to ensuring that those who claim refuge are sheltered during the process. Unfortunately, also like in December, racist rhetoric was common among those opposing the shelter. That racist sentiment was reported on in many articles about the meeting, but, to me, New York Magazine's Curbed captured it most effectively by reporting when a request to "keep in mind the humanity of our new neighbors" was "met with robust laughter'.

Thankfully, other, much happier things happened throughout the week. For example, Council Member Aviles's Intro 4 passed the City Council on Thursday. The legislation will reduce emissions by requiring shore power for cruise ships docking in Red Hook and traffic mitigation plans for such ships. As I've mentioned, we're proud to have supported this legislation and thrilled to see the organizing efforts of the Red Hook community come to fruition. Congratulations to CM Aviles and her team on this big win for the community.

Another slightly less exciting thing on Thursday was our Landmarks meeting, during which we approved two C of A's. Those C of As will now join some liquor licenses and plans for the Old Stone House on the agenda at next week's Full Board meeting, which starts at 6:30 PM on Wednesday, March 13th, at the Van Alen and over Zoom starting at 6:30 PM. 

I'll stop and suggest scrolling to read the rest. Whether you scroll or not, remember that this weekend is daylight savings, and have a good weekend. 

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Saturday, March 2, 2024
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope March has been good thus far. We enter a weekend with rain after a busy week and before another busy week.
item.content:encoded:
I hope March has been good thus far. We enter a weekend with rain after a busy week and before another busy week. Two CB6 committees met this week, and another will meet next week.

On Monday, our Permits & Licenses Committee met and recommended approval for five liquor licenses. item.title: Friday, February 9, 2024
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I'll focus on three things today. The first of those three is Council Member Aviles's legislation, formerly Intro 1050, which would reduce cruise ship pollution and traffic in Red Hook by requiring shore power for ships and traffic…
item.content:encoded:
I'll focus on three things today. The first of those three is Council Member Aviles's legislation, formerly Intro 1050, which would reduce cruise ship pollution and traffic in Red Hook by requiring shore power for ships and traffic mitigation plans. We support this and want it to become law. If you want to help make that happen, you should visit City Hall this Tuesday, February 13th, at 9 AM for a press conference in support and stick around for a hearing on the legislation at 10 AM. If you can't make it, you can submit testimony electronically. 

Second, the New York City vacancy rate has hit a record low of 1.4%. This isn't a record to be proud of. It's a record that's made it difficult and, in many cases, impossible for people to live here despiting wanting to. This results from decades of bad policy choices, including choices that restricted the housing supply at rates that didn't keep up with the demand. Hopefully, that can change going forward, and today gave me some hope for the supply portion of policy as I attended Governor Hochul's housing agenda event in Gowanus. The Governor's goals align with our support for the Gowanus Rezoning, and today's event, including a groundbreaking, makes one of the rezoning's main goals, adding to the supply of affordable and market-rate housing, closer to reality. It was good to be there with Deputy Mayor Maria Torres-Springer, Comptroller Lander, Assemblymember Simon, Arts Gowanus, and others. 

Third, I'd like to remind you that our next Full Board Meeting is on Wednesday, February 21st, at 6:30 PM at Van Alen & Zoom. That's a change from our usual second Wednesday of the month, but rest assured, we'll return to our regularly scheduled meeting day next month. 

On that note, I suggest scrolling and reading the rest of this email. No matter what you decide to do, have a good weekend.

item.title: Friday, February 2, 2024
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope February's first 40 hours have been fun and you've enjoyed Groundhog Day. In a literal and figurative sense, this year's Groundhog Day has some dark clouds as it's the 10th anniversary of a tall CB6 resident dropping Staten Island…
item.content:encoded:
I hope February's first 40 hours have been fun and you've enjoyed Groundhog Day. In a literal and figurative sense, this year's Groundhog Day has some dark clouds as it's the 10th anniversary of a tall CB6 resident dropping Staten Island Chuck to his eventual death. 

As a city, we've carried on, and today's festivities occurred and concluded with Chuck safe and sound, not seeing his shadow and predicting an early spring. Despite this lack of a shadow, Chuck is only advisory, and spring starts on March 19th. While we wait for spring, there's a lot of activity across our community.

In CB6's immediate orbit, our Permits & Licenses committee met on Monday and recommended the approval of liquor license applications at 305 Douglass Street, 215 Smith Street, and 293 Van Brunt Street. Those applications now join last week's Landmark and Land Use items for a vote from our Full Board on Wednesday, February 21st. 

There's much more happening; if you read the rest of this email, you'll see it. Before doing that, I'd like once again to highlight Council Member Aviles's legislation, Intro 1050. We're supportive of this legislation because its functions are things we've long called for, such as requiring shore power for ships at Red Hooks cruise terminal and requiring traffic mitigation plans to reduce the traffic, noise, and pollution caused by increased activity of ships arriving at such cruise terminals. If this interests you, please note that on February 13th, at City Hall, there will be a hearing on this bill, and you can testify. You can also sign a petition or attend a Zoom meeting that folks organizing in support of this bill are hosting on Sunday.

item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Hopefully, 2024’s 4th week has gone well. I’ve got a few things to share, recap, and remind you about.
item.content:encoded:
Hopefully, 2024’s 4th week has gone well. I’ve got a few things to share, recap, and remind you about. 

Firstly, last night at Van Alen and on Zoom, our Landmarks & Land Use(LMLU) committee met to review four items over about 3 hours. The first two items were Landmark applications at 28 Prospect Park West and 487 Henry Street, which the committee conditionally approved. The 3rd item was an application to the Board of Standards and Appeals (BSA) to waive side yard requirements at 92 King Street was tabled. 

The 4th item was a ULURP application for the Red Hook Coastal Resiliency(RHCR) project. RHCR isn’t a typical ULURP application where we’d evaluate a use group for an entire project. RHCR’s ULURP application is related to map changes to regrade and elevate several streets, map new parkland to enlarge Todd Triangle Park, and allow for negotiations with property owners for easement in some potentially impacted locations. The committee conditionally approved it. Additionally, RHCR has entered FEMA’s environmental assessment(EA) public review period. For more information, go to nyc.gov/site/rhcr/index.page. 

Except for the tabled application for 92 King Street, those items move to a vote at our February full board meeting on Wednesday, February 21st. Before that, this Monday, January 29th, at 250 Baltic Street, at 6:30, our Permits & Licenses committee will meet and review Liquor license applications for 305 Douglass Street and 293 Van Brunt Street. 

More has happened and will happen. Read the rest of this email, and you’ll see what I'm referring to. 

I hope you read the rest, but no matter what, have a good weekend.

item.title: Friday, December 15, 2023
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Hopefully, you’re doing well as we head into the weekend following our final full board meeting in 2023.
item.content:encoded:
Hopefully, you’re doing well as we head into the weekend following our final full board meeting in 2023. 

While the meeting was the last of the year, it was certainly not the least. Seven items were on the agenda, and there was a big turnout for stuff not even on it, such as an asylee shelter planned for 130 3rd Street. We made clear, disappointing those who opposed this shelter location, including, unfortunately, some who resorted to repulsive and racist rhetoric, that our community must contribute its fair share to ensure that those who claim refuge are sheltered during the process. Those with questions about the site may contact the operator by calling 718-930-8910 or emailing yfuksman@bhragalliance.org. 

Regarding the scheduled agenda, we approved plans for two liquor licenses, two landmark applications, plans for Boerum Park, and a ULURP application for 41 Richards Street, increasing modern industrial capacity. We also conditionally disapproved a ULURP application for 341 10th Street. What that translates to is that we approve of the plans presented, which would build hundreds of deeply affordable family and senior housing units, but due to community concerns that we as a board shared about the history of the developer, we insist that this rezoning be tethered to an ironclad Community Benefits Agreement (CBA). A CBA that protects the interest of current tenants and ensures the number of, and the permanent affordability of, new units covered by HPD programs and existing units. I look forward to continuing to work with the tenants (who’ve been incredibly helpful and welcoming) and the City Council to ensure that such a CBA becomes a reality. 

That’s enough ULURP for Friday, so I’ll shift to my usual reminder to read the rest of this email. If you do, you’ll find time left for the Red Hook Holiday Market, a Humbug Bash in Cobble Hill, BQE lane closures, and more. Even if you don’t read the rest, I hope you have a good weekend.

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager

item.content:encoded:
Hopefully, you're doing well with lots to be thankful for this Thanksgiving. While not universally festive, I've got some items to share as the holiday season starts.

First, after years of advocacy, the 7 Av F/G subway station has elevators, making it fully accessible. It was great to be at the ribbon cutting with multiple CB6 members, including Bob Levine, as we've long supported and advocated for this. That advocacy took place alongside Assemblymember Carroll, Councilmember Hanif, their predecessors, former Assemblymember Jim Brennan and Comptroller Brad Lander, the Park Slope Civic Council, Good Neighbors of Park Slope, and many others. While we're certainly thankful to the MTA for making this a reality, we still need many more stations to become fully accessible. 

Secondly, Alternate Side Parking, meters, sanitation, and postal services will be suspended for Thanksgiving tomorrow, Thursday, November 23rd. On Friday, November 24th, they'll return to normal. 

Third, we've got two CB6 meetings next week. On Monday, we'll review liquor licenses; on Thursday, we'll review Landmarks and Land Use Items; however, before and after those meetings, there's plenty planned across the community. Read the rest of this email, and you'll see what I'm talking about. 

No matter what you do, I'm thankful you've read this sentence, and have a happy Thanksgiving!

item.content:encoded:

Looking to more welcome things, we’ve got Red Hook Open Studios & Community Cinema, coverage of the GCC’s work with rain gardens, universal composting, Alternate Side Parking is suspended through Monday, and Wednesday’s our Full Board meeting. I could write and rant a bit more, but it would boil down to a recommendation that you read the rest of this email and find information more welcome and useful than the preceding paragraph.

Whether you find it neither welcome nor useful, I hope you stay safe and have a great weekend.

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Friday, September 29, 2023
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Despite the rain, there was a good turnout at last night’s Gowanus Task Force meeting. In the hours since, “good” is a word you hear less and less with record rain and flooding across the community and city.
item.content:encoded:
Despite the rain, there was a good turnout at last night’s Gowanus Task Force meeting. In the hours since, “good” is a word you hear less and less with record rain and flooding across the community and city. The Governor and Mayor have issued emergency orders that’ll remain in place for at least the next few days. 

As I write this, it’s not raining, but it’ll likely start again. All forms of transportation are severely delayed and disrupted; it’s best to stay home, avoid dealing with those delays, and allow more space for emergency operations to get around. Also, Alternate Side Parking, to the extent that it exists on weekends, will be suspended through Sunday. 

We won’t know the full impact of this weather for some time, but we can get there quicker and assist those who need it sooner if those with damaged property report it at reportdamage.nyc.gov. Also, the 5th Avenue Bid compiled resources found at bit.ly/5Avebid929 for businesses seeking assistance. 

Things are still scheduled for the weekend, including the Van Alen Block Party and the Atlantic Antic. 

Past the weekend, universal composting starts on Monday, DEC hosts a Brownfield meeting on Tuesday, and we’re having a Landmarks meeting on Thursday. The agenda consists of 1 item: an application to allow for one of over one window at 229 Baltic Street. Unless withdrawn or tabled, that application will move to our full board on Wednesday, October 11th, at 6:30 p.m. at Van Alen. 

I’ll stop here and continue to share information as received on our social media platforms.

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.content:encoded:
First, in an unpleasant homage to a few weeks back, our air quality may worsen tomorrow, Wednesday, June 28th, and Thursday, June 29th. The Air Quality Index (AQI) could reach unhealthy levels due to smoke from ongoing Canadian wildfires. Monitor air quality by going to airnow.gov.

Second, polls for primary elections are open until 9 PM. In CB6, the most high-profile primary is for Civil Court Judge. In a low-turnout year like this, your vote has a greater impact on the outcome. So, if you haven’t voted, go to findmypollsite.vote.nyc. 

Third, Alternate Side Parking will be suspended for EID tomorrow, Wednesday, June 28th, through Friday, June 30th. Parking meters will remain in effect.

Fourth, shifting into CB6’s sphere of influence, our Permits & Licenses Committee met last night and approved two liquor license applications. One was for a Caribbean restaurant at 236 6th Street named Cozy On The Slope, and the other was for an American restaurant at 215 Columbia Street. Both approvals were unanimous.

item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Our CB6 Transportation/Public Safety Committee met at Principles Cafe on Wednesday to review DOT's plans to extend the protected bike lane on 9th Street down to Smith Street. The committee approved the plans with conditions that DOT add…
item.content:encoded:
Our CB6 Transportation/Public Safety Committee met at Principles Cafe on Wednesday to review DOT's plans to extend the protected bike lane on 9th Street down to Smith Street. The committee approved the plans with conditions that DOT add Leading Pedestrian Intervals (LPIs) on 2nd Ave crossing 9th Street, extend those LPIs beyond the current 7 seconds, LPI signage, markers for driveways where the protected bike lane would stop, and additional traffic calming measures. Public Safety Chair Jerry Armer emphasized the need for quick implementation, demanding the plan be implemented this summer. The full board will vote on this motion at our June 14th meeting.

Of course, plenty is happening before our June meeting. In the coming week, we have two CB6 committee meetings: Liquor Licenses on Monday and Landmarks on Thursday. Additionally, our district and borough have a half marathon running through it tomorrow and the 5th Avenue fair on Sunday.

item.title: Tom Miskel
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Sadly, it’s necessary to start by announcing the passing of long-time CB6 member Tom Miskel. In addition to being a member of CB6, Tom was a member of The Friendly Sons of Saint Patrick and the Park Slope Civic Council and remained…
item.content:encoded:
Sadly, it’s necessary to start by announcing the passing of long-time CB6 member Tom Miskel. In addition to being a member of CB6, Tom was a member of The Friendly Sons of Saint Patrick and the Park Slope Civic Council and remained involved with many other community organizations, such as the Brooklyn Public Library, the YMCA, and Methodist Hospital. He was also a military veteran who ran the Park Slope Veterans museum for years. 

These organizations and our shared community benefited from Tom Misklel. I learned a great deal from him when I became a member of CB6 almost a decade ago and was on the same committees (Permits & Licenses. Landmarks/Land Use). He also co-chaired our Transportation Committee for years with our current Chair, Eric McClure. He’ll be missed by many across our community, including his sister Helena. For those that don’t know, Helena was an extraordinary volunteer in the CB6 office for many years.

Tom’s funeral mass is at 9:30 AM tomorrow, Saturday, April 1st, at Saint Saviour’s, followed by interment at Green-Wood Cemetery.

You’ll find more of the usual civic content in the rest of this email, so I recommend scrolling down and reading the rest. However, before that, I must announce that April’s Full Board meeting is on Wednesday, April 19th, beginning at 6:30 PM and will be held at Van Alen and over Zoom. This is of note due to it being 3rd Wednesday of the month instead of the usual second Wednesday. 

Enjoy your weekend.

item.title: Loss, Anecdote, Empathy
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I’ll get into more mundane things below my signature, but I couldn’t start today without commenting on the death of the great New York writer Pete Hamill. Pete Hamill was born and raised in our community long before community boards or…
item.content:encoded:
I’ll get into more mundane things below my signature, but I couldn’t start today without commenting on the death of the great New York writer Pete Hamill. Pete Hamill was born and raised in our community long before community boards or community districts were a thing. His father worked in a Gowanus factory, and he, a Regis high school dropout, became a powerful voice in our city. No one is perfect, but he’s up there in the annals of tabloid journalism with Jimmy Breslin. We’d be well served to remember his love for the city; it’s constant change and diversity expressed in most of his writing. 

I only got to meet Pete Hamill once, but I’ll never forget. It was, fittingly, in CB6 at Red Hook's Rocky Sullivan's just after I had graduated college in 2007. He read from his then-new book North River, told stories about Brooklyn, and at one point, he discussed what a great day it was when his Italian neighbor had taught his Irish mother how to make red sauce,or ,as some would say, gravy. After this anecdote, he explained to the crowd, “some may not know this, but the Irish and Italians hated each other until they started marrying each other.” 

Being the offspring of precisely this type of marital mix (Italian father, Irish Mother), it resonated with me, and when I was introduced to him, I was able to tell him so. I’m sure countless people had told him how his words had resonated with them, but for the few minutes I got to speak with him, he gave the impression that it was a unique experience that he wouldn’t forget. Regardless, I never forgot it and will always appreciate it.

His ability to speak to someone he didn't know with care and empathy certainly contributed to his success. No matter the field, we'd all do better with a bit more empathy, especially as there is so much human suffering around us.

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.content:encoded:
Tomorrow, March 16th, we have a BQE-focused CB6 Transportation/ Public Safety Committee meeting. It’s a Zoom meeting, and it’ll start at 6:30 PM. Nearly a hundred neighbors have registered for the meeting, so it’s clearly the place to be. To join them, go to bit.ly/cb6bqe316. 

Yesterday at the Miccio center, DOT kicked off the Red Hook Traffic & Truck Study. More meetings will be held in the coming months, but if you couldn’t make it last night, you'll find DOT’s presentation and additional info at bit.ly/redhookportal. 

Today saw the groundbreaking for the first of 2 CSO tanks in Gowanus. We stood with Mayor Adams, DEP, EPA, Council Members Hanif & Restler, NYCHA leaders, and the Gowanus Canal Conservancy. As designed, this tank will hold 12 million gallons of sewer overflow during rainstorms leading to less canal pollution and creating 3.6 acres of new public space. Additionally, DEP will host a meeting about the CSO tanks tomorrow, Thursday, March 16th; register at bit.ly/depcso316.

I hope you're doing well as we head into the weekend. But, first, I’ll offer a quick look at the week that was. 

On Monday, we hosted a town hall with Representative Goldman focused on the U.S. Army Corp of Engineers (USACE) storm resiliency plans and what it would mean for Red Hook and Gowanus. Thanks to an extension announced during the town hall, comments on the plan are being accepted until March 31st. I've compiled information, including how to submit comments and a town hall recording at bit.ly/cb6usaceinfo.

Our March meeting was on Wednesday through Zoom and at the Van Alen Institute. We approved two NYC Landmarks Preservation Commission applications and reaffirmed support for the New Yorkers for Parks “Play Fair” Campaign, seeking 1% of the City budget devoted to parks. In addition to those approvals, there were ample announcements; a CB6 BQE meeting this coming Thursday, and on Tuesday,  there’ll be a Red Hook Library meeting and, later on, that same day, a kickoff meeting for DOT’s Red Hook traffic study.

item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Before starting your weekend, it can be a good idea to reflect on the week that was, especially if earlier in the week held our full board meeting. That being the case, I’ll summarize and suggest some stuff.
item.content:encoded:
Before starting your weekend, it can be a good idea to reflect on the week that was, especially if earlier in the week held our full board meeting. That being the case, I’ll summarize and suggest some stuff. 

Our February Full board meeting was held on Wednesday, February 8th, in-person at the Van Alen Institute and virtually over Zoom. CB6 chairperson Eric McClure ran the meeting; we heard from government officials at the federal, state & city levels, held a community session, and ratified four motions from CB6 committees. 

Two of those motions were for new liquor licenses; a Thai restaurant at 204 Smith Street and a Caribbean fusion restaurant at 321 9th Street. The CB6 Permits & Licenses Committee approved both on January 30th. On Wednesday, after Permits & Licenses chair Rebecca Kobert summarized both applications, the CB6 Full Board voted to approve. 

Two applications for Certificates of Appropriateness were up next. The first would allow for a rear yard and roof extension at 30 Tompkins Place. On January 26th, the CB6 Landmarks Committee approved this application on the condition that the rooftop’s fenestration is reduced. Landmarks Chair David Briggs presented this; just like in committee, the full board approved it. The last of these four motions was an application to allow mechanical equipment on the roof and a rear door in the garden facade of 17 Prospect Park West. Our Landmarks Committee disapproved of this application, David Briggs presented it, and the Full Board concurred with the committee and disapproved. 

If that summary has made you impatient for your next CB6 meeting, remember that our Parks & Environmental Protection Committee meets this coming Wednesday, February 15th. It’ll be held over Zoom with an agenda that includes updates on Prospect Park and recreation in Red Hook. To register, go to: bit.ly/feb15cb6. 

I’ll stop here and suggest you read the rest. Either way, have a great weekend. 

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Maybe it’s an homage to Groucho Marx, but despite seeing snow yesterday, our snowless streak continues. Regardless, macro and micro civic life continue.
item.content:encoded:
Maybe it’s an homage to Groucho Marx, but despite seeing snow yesterday, our snowless streak continues. Regardless, macro and micro civic life continue. 

On the macro side, Mayor Adams gave his second State of the City Address this afternoon. I haven’t watched it yet, but I understand it included plans for citywide composting, office conversions, and other items. On the micro side, we’ve got a Landmarks meeting tonight, and the MTA hosts a Brooklyn Bus town hall. Both meetings are virtual and start at 6:30 PM. 

The MTA’s Town Hall will focus on the Brooklyn Bus Redesign in CB6. To register, go to: bit.ly/mtabkbustownhall. At the same time, the CB6 Landmarks committee will review three items- 2 in Park Slope and 1 in Cobble Hill. To register, go to: bit.ly/cb6jan26.

Whether you read the rest of this email or not, stay safe, enjoy the rest of your Thursday, and fill out the fourth street survey today.

Best,

item.title: Friday, January 20, 2023
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: First, this morning I, along with CB6 Chair Eric McClure, and Transportation chair Doug Gordon participated in a walk-through on 9th Street in the wake of the crash that killed Carroll Gardens resident Sarah Schick on January 10th. We…
item.content:encoded:
First, this morning I, along with CB6 Chair Eric McClure, and Transportation chair Doug Gordon participated in a walk-through on 9th Street in the wake of the crash that killed Carroll Gardens resident Sarah Schick on January 10th. We joined DOT Commissioner Rodriguez and his team members, CM Hanif and Sen. Gounardes and AM Simon, and a rep from Congressman Goldman’s office to begin the process of making significant safety improvements along the corridor. We expect that DOT will come to our Transportation Committee soon with proposed design changes and will share meeting details as soon as they’re available.

Secondly, on a sandwich-related note, the City Council approved the Defonte’s Street co-naming. For those unfamiliar, Defonte’s is a sandwich shop of renown in Red Hook, at the corner of Columbia and Luquer, that has been in business for over a century. I’ve been in touch with Council Member Avelis’s office on this, and when I know more, you’ll know more. In the meantime, I’d recommend trying their potatoes and egg sandwich. 

I’ll make no further dining recommendations but strongly suggest you read the rest of this email. No matter what you decide to do, have a great weekend, and for all who will celebrate it, Happy Lunar New Year!

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201

item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Of the immediate, 16 CB6 restaurants are participating in NYC restaurant week. Go to bit.ly/cb6restaurantweek to see the participants from all corners of the community.
item.content:encoded:
Of the immediate, 16 CB6 restaurants are participating in NYC restaurant week. Go to bit.ly/cb6restaurantweek to see the participants from all corners of the community. The “week” is closer to a month as it runs through February 12th. We’ve got great local business here, and this can help more people see that.

Shifting to the existential and things “seen,” it’s been over 300 days since it last snowed in the city. This snowless streak may set records, but none that we should celebrate. No, the flurries on Saturday don’t count. The warmer temperatures that lead to less snow result from climate change. Hopefully, this can remind us that our best tool to fight this is better policy choices.  

I’ll stop here and recommend that you read the rest of the email. Stay safe, and enjoy the rest of your Tuesday.

item.title: Friday, January 13, 2023
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: If the first day of a month falls on a Sunday, that month's 13th day will be a Friday, and with it comes the risk associated with superstitions and a lame film franchise. Alas, today is Friday the 13th.
item.content:encoded:
If the first day of a month falls on a Sunday, that month's 13th day will be a Friday, and with it comes the risk associated with superstitions and a lame film franchise. Alas, today is Friday the 13th. Referencing the lameness of a film franchise is in itself a lame attempt at humor and not CB6's official position. 

Our official positions are reserved mainly for but are not limited to, local landmarks, land use, and liquor licenses. Speaking of liquor licenses, three were approved at Wednesday's board meeting, which marks the first meeting of the McClure era. The only votes on the agenda were for the previously mentioned liquor licenses, but there was discussion of the tragic crash on 9th Street that left a 37-year-old mother dead. We've been on the record asking DOT to extend safety measures west of 3rd Avenue as the "status quo" is clearly not working. We reiterate that request.

Also mentioned at the meeting, Monday, January 16, is Martin Luther King, Jr. Day. Schools, libraries, government offices, the DMV, and courts will be closed in observance. Also, there's no alternate side, sanitation pickup, or mail.

I recommend reading the rest of this email, but no matter what you do, enjoy your weekend.

item.description: Hoping your 2023 is off to a great start on this too-warm Wednesday. Our state and federal legislatures, in Albany and D.C., have kicked things off.
item.content:encoded:
Hoping your 2023 is off to a great start on this too-warm Wednesday. Our state and federal legislatures, in Albany and D.C., have kicked things off. For once, with quick leadership elections, Albany looks like a legislative role model. D.C., on the other hand, has made clear that, despite the chaos, with Senator Schumer being elected Majority Leader and Hakeem Jeffries having received the most votes for speaker on six different ballots, Brooklyn is the place to be. Senator Schumer is even a CB6 resident residing in Park Slope. 

Speaking of leadership from Park Slope, Eric McClure is officially the chairperson of CB6. His tenure's first full board meeting is a week from tonight, over Zoom, on Wednesday, January 11th, at 6:30 PM. Register at bit.ly/cb6jan11. 

But before that, on Monday, January 9th, at 6:30 PM, our Permits & Licenses Committee will meet and vote on liquor licenses for some local bars and restaurants. Register at bit.ly/cb6jan9. For all we know, in light of the Times declaring a restaurant renaissance for Park Slope, this meeting could capture the zeitgeist of 2023. 

On that note, I'll stop speculating. I recommend reading the rest of this email but no matter, have a good evening and year!

item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo

item.content:encoded:
Today may be Festivus, but I’m not airing any grievances in this email; I’ll stick with civics as a cold Christmas weekend begins. 

Christmas is Sunday, December 25th; as such, it’ll be observed on Monday, December 26th. What’s “observed” mean in this context? It means that on Monday, government offices are closed, there will be no sanitation service, no mail, alternate side parking, and parking meter will be suspended, and schools will be closed. Public schools are on winter recess and are closed through January 2nd, while the other entities mentioned return on Tuesday, December 27th. 

I’ll stop here and wish everyone celebrating a very Merry Christmas. No matter what, or whether you celebrate, stay safe, stay warm, and have a great weekend.

item.title: Week Was, Weekend Will
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: We're heading into a final fall weekend that'll see rain stop and Hanukkah start. A happy Hanukkah to those who celebrate.
item.content:encoded:
We're heading into a final fall weekend that'll see rain stop and Hanukkah start. A happy Hanukkah to those who celebrate. This weekend follows a work week that included BQE workshops and, on Wednesday, our final meeting of 2022.  

Our final meeting of 2022 was also the last meeting of Peter Fleming's tenure as CB6 chair.

Unfortunately for us, but a respite for Peter, who was term-limited after four years. I say respite because we're fortunate that he's agreed to continue serving as a CB6 member and rejoin our Landmarks/ Land Use Committee. His time as chair included covid, the Gowanus Rezoning, and more. As expressed by many during the meeting, including former CB6 member and current Comptroller Lander, Peter's leadership and hard work have been greatly appreciated.

Speaking of our Landmarks/Land Use (LM/LU) Committee, there was 1 LM item up for a vote during Wednesday's full board meeting. That item, presented by David Briggs, was an application for the enlargement of a backyard extension at 101 Saint John's place, which was overwhelmingly approved. There were also votes on three liquor license applications from our Permits & Licenses committee. Rebecca Kobert presented, and all were approved. 

With a glance towards 2023, starting on January 1st, Eric McClure will be chairperson, Angelica Ramdhari will be 1st Vice-chair, Karen Broughton 2nd Vice-chair, Jerry Armer will become Secretary, and Rebecca Kobert will be Treasurer. I've worked with them and am excited to continue to do so in their new roles as CB6 officers. 

I'll stop the synopsis here and suggest you read the rest of this email. Stay safe, stay warm, and have a great weekend.

item.title: Friday, November 18, 2022
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: The sun’s already set as we begin a weekend with a potential for frost. If one enjoys the cold, our community has plenty to offer outside.
item.content:encoded:
The sun’s already set as we begin a weekend with a potential for frost. If one enjoys the cold, our community has plenty to offer outside. That includes a potluck harvest in Cobble Hill, bulb planting in Red Hook, sludge stories in Gowanus, Mozart in Park Slope, and more. 

If one prefers to be a spectator of the cold, you can stay inside and avail yourself of 2 applications. One application, which will be open until November 30th, is for the Gowanus Oversight Task Force. To apply, go to bit.ly/gowanustaskforceapplication. The other application is for all 18 Brooklyn Community Boards (CB). To apply, go to bit.ly/bkcbapplications2023. The applications will be open until Valentine’s Day 2023 for those who love their communities.

Even if you receive emails from a CB, you may wonder what CBs do and what our role is or can be in city government. A recent op-ed from Brooklyn Borough President (BP) Reynoso articulated an excellent explanation of our role. He discussed how CB advisory power could determine the outcome of things we review, such as land use applications. The BP used one prime example to demonstrate this point: us at CB6 and our work on the Gowanus rezoning. The BP wrote that “Because of Community Board 6’s advocacy,” the “Gowanus Houses and Wyckoff Gardens Houses will see about $200 million in renovations, and the rezoning was the first to have an independent racial impact study, showing that it would increase income and racial diversity in the community.”.

On that note, I’ll stop, but you should keep reading and scrolling down this email. No matter what you do, have a great weekend.

item.title: Civically Contrasting
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: We start this weekend on Veterans Day with wind, rain, and appreciation for all who served. This follows a week that saw a midterm election for federal & state offices as well as our November board meeting.
item.content:encoded:
We start this weekend on Veterans Day with wind, rain, and appreciation for all who served. This follows a week that saw a midterm election for federal & state offices as well as our November board meeting. It was a civic contrast between the macro & micro varieties.

The macro side of that equation isn’t complete as federal tabulations (which party controls Congress) are still to be determined. However, here in New York, we generally know where the election leaves us. In CB6-specific terms, Assemblymembers Carroll, Mitaynes, and Simon won, as did State Senators Gounardes and Myrie; Dan Goldman was elected to the House of Representatives. On the statewide scale Comptroller Dinapoli, Attorney General Tish James, and Governor Hochul (who became the first woman to be elected Governor of New York State) retained their offices. Also last but not least, CB6 resident Chuck Schumer was re-elected to the United State Senate.

Moving to the micro, there's nothing left to be tabulated from Wednesday’s full board meeting. It was held at the Van Alen Institute and over Zoom. All items up for a vote, five liquor licenses, and a budget overview were approved. Assemblymember Simon joined us via Zoom, as did Senator Gounardes and Representative-elect Dan Goldman. Ben Margolis, formerly of SWBDIC, announced that applications to be part of the Gowanus Oversight Task Force are now open and will close on November 30th. Last but not least, the nominations for CB6 officers were closed. All offices had nominations but no challenges. That means, beginning January 1st, 2023, Jerry Armer will be board secretary, Rebecca Kobert will serve as Treasurer, Karen Broughton as 2nd the Vice Chair, Angelica Ramdhari as 1st Vice Chair, and our new chair will be Eric McClure. 

Each incoming officer will do a great job, and I look forward to working with them. On that note, I’ll stop, but you may keep reading and scrolling down this email. No matter what you do, have a great weekend. 

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Vote Tomorrow, Meet Wednesday
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: It may feel late, but you can't vote early anymore. After nine days of early voting, Brooklyn led the city & state with over 135k ballots cast.
item.content:encoded:
It may feel late, but you can't vote early anymore. After nine days of early voting, Brooklyn led the city & state with over 135k ballots cast. While it's undoubtedly good, the election isn't just about proving we're more dedicated to democracy than Manhattan. The election is also about who will be our Governor, Attorney General, State Comptroller, federal & state legislators, judges, and what will be of various ballot proposals.  

So, If you haven't voted yet but want to ensure that we (Brooklyn) stay in the lead, make sure to cast your ballot tomorrow, Election Day, Tuesday, November 8th. Voting sites will be open from 6 am until 9 pm. To find out where to vote, go to findmypollsite.vote.nyc/.

There are also some service changes to note for election day. Public schools will be closed, there will be no sanitation pickup, and Alternate Side Parking regulations will be suspended.

The next night, Wednesday, November 9th at 6:30 pm, is our full board meeting, during which I'd expect we hear from many Tuesday night winners. It's a hybrid meeting with the in-person portion at Van Alen and the virtual part on Zoom. 

You can read past this point for more interesting information, but enjoy the rest of your Monday, even if this is where you stop.

The election will determine who'll be the Governor, Attorney General, State Comptroller, federal & state legislators, judges, and the fate of various ballot proposals. Hundred of thousands of our fellow New Yorkers have already voted. If you're not one of them, you can change that by voting this weekend. Poll sites are open tomorrow Saturday, November 5th, and Sunday, November 6th, from 9 until 5 pm. You may also drop your absentee ballot at any poll site. To find your designated poll site, as they sometimes change, go to findmypollsite.vote.nyc/.

The Marathon is on Sunday, November 6th. It's a great annual event that literally, on 4th Avenue, runs through our community. For a comprehensive list of places to watch and street closures, go to bit.ly/262info11522. 

The extra hour is due to the end of Daylight Savings Time on Sunday at 2 am. Clocks go back one hour, and people say you can get extra sleep, but no matter what you do with the hour, it amounts to a 25-hour Sunday. 

There's more going on this weekend and week than what's mentioned in the preceding paragraphs. For example, tomorrow, Saturday, November 5th, there's a boat house art show, community clean-ups, a lanternfly workshop, and smashing pumpkins that have nothing to do with Billy Corgan.  

Also, just so you know, Tuesday, November 8th, is election day and our full board meeting is Wednesday, November 9th. On election day, polls will be open from 6 am until 9 pm, schools will be closed, there will be no sanitation pickups, and Alternate Side Parking Regulations will be suspended. Our full board meeting will be a hybrid meeting, so starting at 6:30 pm on Wednesday, we'll meet at the Van Alen Institute and over Zoom. 

You should scroll down for even more evidence of our ever-active community. No matter what you do, have a great weekend.

item.description: We start November with disturbingly warm weather and seven days left to vote. Years ago, democracy and weather may have seemed unrelated.
item.content:encoded:
We start November with disturbingly warm weather and seven days left to vote. Years ago, democracy and weather may have seemed unrelated. However, in the present day, they're directly connected to what kinds of policies are implemented at all levels of government. To be clear, I'm not referring to rain in Ohio 18 years ago; I'm talking about the existential threat of climate change. 

This year's election will determine who will be Governor, LT Governor, and represent us in the US. Senate & House, our state legislature, and include various ballot proposals.

Early voting sites are open until 8 pm tonight and every day through Sunday, November 6th, followed by election day on Tuesday, November 8th. For more information on the candidates, go to nycvotes.org. To find out where to vote, go to findmypollsite.vote.nyc/.

I'll stop here and suggest you keep reading, as democracy isn't just election day; it's a year-round activity. For example, just like in 2016, we have our November full board meeting the day after the election, which will be on Wednesday, November 9th, at 6:30 pm over Zoom and at the Van Alen Institute.

Enjoy the rest of your Tuesday regardless of what you decide to read past this point.

item.title: Thursday, October 13, 2022
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Today, "Thursday the 13th" is not associated with any horror film franchises. However, at least in this newsletter, it's associated with being the day after Brooklyn Community Board 6's first hybrid meeting, which occurred last night.
item.content:encoded:
Today, "Thursday the 13th" is not associated with any horror film franchises. However, at least in this newsletter, it's associated with being the day after Brooklyn Community Board 6's first hybrid meeting, which occurred last night. It may not be a widely shared position, but community board meetings, among some civic-minded folks, are considered more interesting than any horror film. The synopsis of last night's meeting in the prose below may explain why. 

The in-person portion of the meeting was held at the Van Alen Institute and when attendees arrived they were offered cake. People were overheard saying they liked the cake. The virtual portion was on Zoom. 

Eric Mcclure filled in for Peter Fleming and chaired the meeting. At 6:42 the meeting was called to order and Assemblymember Carroll joined us on Zoom and Council Member (CM) Hanif spoke in person with updates on items such as Participatory Budgeting. I was then given the floor and reported on a few items. The "few" were the Gowanus Task Force, Van Alen Block Party, Park Slope Halloween Parade, Open Meetings, and DEP's October 26th meeting regarding the Gowanus Canal "Owls Head" CSO Facility. 

The CSO facility was also a subject during the next part of the agenda which was reviewing three items from our Landmarks/Land Use Committee. Jerry Armer filled in for David Briggs and presented the committee's recommendations. The first 2 items were applications to LPC at 611 11th Street and 281 Carroll Street. The final item was a resolution regarding the design of the CSO facility seeking to include a launch site for recreation boating on the Gowanus, as well as a comfort station and community room similar to the one in Carroll Park. All three items were overwhelmingly approved. 

We also heard from representatives of additional electeds, and CM Restler joined the zoom. The meeting was adjourned at 7:54. 

We'll smooth out some hybrid issues, and hopefully, hybrid meetings will be our meeting format going forward. I'll stop here and hope you now understand my preference for CB meetings over horror films. Last but not least, I'd like to thank Van Alen Institute for being such a welcoming host. Enjoy the rest of your rainy Thursday, the 13th.

item.content:encoded:
There are two items I'd like to highlight before you get started on your weekend if you haven't already done so.

First, Brooklyn Community Board 6’s Landmarks/Land Use (LMLU) Committee met last night to review three Certificates of Appropriateness (C of A) applications. Two of the three applications, 611 11th Street & 281 Carroll Street, were recommended for approval. The other application, 529 1st Street, was tabled. As a result, 529 1st Street will have to return and present at a future LMLU meeting. 281 Carroll Street & 611 11th Street will proceed to a vote by our full board this coming Wednesday, October 12th, at the Van Alen Institute. 

Secondly, I’d like to draw your attention to some potentially good news regarding the Brooklyn Queens Expressway (BQE) plans. The news I’m referring to is in DOT’s most recent presentation, which states: “NYC DOT is initiating studies of Gowanus and Red Hook that will be integrated with this process.” We don’t know the details, but this is encouraging, especially as we’ve asked for such studies multiple times over multiple years.  

That’s all from me. But, as always, I’ll suggest you keep reading past this point, but even if don't, have a great weekend!

item.description: Last night, as advertised, we had our first in-person meeting since the Zoom ignorant days of February 2020.
item.content:encoded:
Last night, as advertised, we had our first in-person meeting since the Zoom ignorant days of February 2020.

With quorum reached, our Chair, Peter Fleming, called the meeting to order at 6:40, and we made our way through a light agenda. The items up for a vote came from our Landmarks Committee and consisted of 2 applications for Certificates of Appropriateness. The first application was for a new rear facade at 91 8th Avenue, and the other was to allow for door and window replacement, as well as window enlargement on the secondary facade at 60 Montgomery Place. Both share the distinction of being in the Park Slope Historic District and overwhelmingly approved by us. 

Council Member Lincon Restler and representatives of other city and state officials joined the meeting. Also, former CB6 member, and current comptroller, Brad Lander stopped by a few minutes after we’d adjourned.  

I’ll stop the synopsis soon, but I’d like to reiterate that seeing and meeting so many folks for the first time was great. Also, as I announced, our next full board meeting is on October 12th, 6:30 PM, at the Van Alen Institute, located at 303 Bond Street. 

Whether we’ve met or if you read this email any longer, enjoy the rest of your night. 

Best,

As a reminder, this shift and postponement are due to Governor Hochul not renewing Executive Order (E.O.) 11., which suspended the Open Meetings law allowing us to meet remotely. Letting the E.O. expire was done despite Covid statistics, such as hospitalizations, remaining above the threshold used to justify extensions just a few weeks back. Go figure. item.title: Friday, September 9, 2022
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: First, Governor Hochul declared a state of emergency regarding the spread of polio. The declaration aims to get as many people vaccinated as quickly as possible.
item.content:encoded:
First, Governor Hochul declared a state of emergency regarding the spread of polio. The declaration aims to get as many people vaccinated as quickly as possible. This will expand those who can administer the polio vaccine, which will now include pharmacists, midwives, and emergency medical personnel. With polio being especially dangerous for young children, vaccine hesitancy becoming more prevalent, and school starting, the declaration of emergency is well founded. If you’re uncertain about whether you’ve been vaccinated against polio, if you went to school in New York State, you almost certainly are. The reason for such certainty is that New York state has required it to attend school since the 1960s. For more information, go to health.ny.gov/polio.

Secondly, we’ve got a lot happening in the coming weeks. I’ve listed much of it below my contact information, and I suggest checking it out. However, before you do that, remember that our September meeting is this Wednesday, and read about possible permitting for last-mile warehouses.

I’ll stop here and hope you have a great weekend, whether you keep reading or not.

Best,

item.content:encoded:
While it's not officially fall, indicators, such as pumpkin spice and autumnal imagery, are already here. However, more than any fall "vibes", especially for families with children, it’s definitely not summer. That's because, while questions about the budget remain, the New York City 2022-2023 school year starts tomorrow, Thursday, September 9th.

Good luck to everyone going back to school tomorrow. All the best to students, teachers, support staff, principals, and parents! Also, families may want to review the school calendar by going to on.nyc.gov/3TMxOAO.

Another sign of summer's end is the return of CB6 full board meetings on the second Wednesday of the month. That means next Wednesday, September 14, at 6:30 PM, we’ll meet over Zoom. The voting agenda consists of 2 landmark items, but I’m sure they’ll be more to hear. Register for the meeting at bit.ly/BKCB691422.

I’ll stop here and suggest you read further down this email. Whether you do so or not, enjoy the rest of your day.

item.title: Friday, September 2, 2022
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: There’s a good chance you’re focused on the unofficial end of summer known as labor day weekend. While summer doesn’t officially end until September 22nd, Monday, September 5th, Labor Day, is an officially recognized federal holiday.
item.content:encoded:
There’s a good chance you’re focused on the unofficial end of summer known as labor day weekend. While summer doesn’t officially end until September 22nd, Monday, September 5th, Labor Day, is an officially recognized federal holiday. Labor day celebrates workers and the labor movement. 

What the labor movement has done, and continues to do, is work to improve the rights and conditions of workers. For example, without the labor movement, Saturday & Sunday would just be two consecutive days, not the “weekend.” In New York, our history, present, and future are inextricably linked to the labor movement. For example, New York City celebrated Labor Day in 1882, 12 years before it became a federal holiday. New York State and New York City have always been among the most unionized cities and states. We may eventually take the top spot back as New Yorkers are now ten times more likely to join a union than the rest of the country. 

On a hyper-local level, our CB6 staff is unionized. With that, I’ll stop and suggest you scroll down and check out the items below my contact information. However, no matter what, whether or not you’re a union member, an unrepresented worker, a freelancer, or even a boss, have a great Labor Day weekend!

item.content:encoded:
I planned to just focus on reminding you that early voting for the State Senate and U.S House of Representatives begins tomorrow, Saturday, August 13th. However, when the Health Department detected Polio in our city’s wastewater, it fell in paragraph placement. 

So, if you aren’t vaccinated against Polio, contact your healthcare provider about changing that asap. Go to nyccare.nyc or call 844-692-4692 if you don’t have a healthcare provider but need to receive the polio vaccine. Also, New York State schools have required the polio vaccine since the mid-1960s, so if you went to school here anytime after, you’re ahead of the game. 

Early voting runs through Sunday, August 21st, with Election Day on Tuesday, August 23rd. To confirm your polling place, when it is open and if you also want to know who is on the ballot, go to vote.nyc.

item.description: First, New York State & New York City have declared monkeypox a public health emergency. NYC has about a quarter of the country's monkeypox cases.
item.content:encoded:
First, New York State & New York City have declared monkeypox a public health emergency. NYC has about a quarter of the country's monkeypox cases. On the Covid-19 front, statistics indicate that being vaccinated is the best way to avoid ending up among the over 300 deaths across our state in the last two weeks. So remember, visit vax4nyc.nyc.gov or vax4nyc.nyc.gov/monkeypox and make an appointment to get vaccinated.

Second, speed cameras will now operate 24/7. Before today, they had only been in effect on weekdays from 6 AM until 10 PM. The expansion of speed cameras is something we've long supported, and you may notice in the press coverage, our CB6 Transportation Chair, Eric McClure, is quoted.

Third, if you want an absentee ballot for the upcoming primary elections, you have until Monday, August 8th, to request it. Go to vote.nyc to find out more. Speaking of the forthcoming primaries, there will be a virtual candidate forum for the 10th congressional district this Sunday, August 7th. Register for the forum at bit.ly/ny10aug7.

The committee approved all three Certificate of Appropriateness applications and saw presentations of waterfront plans for 420 Carroll Street and 300 Nevins Street. If the preceding prose makes you want to learn more about it, watch the meeting on our YouTube page or check out the presentations at bit.ly/728lmlumaterials.

Secondly, even as we approach August, a lot is going on. That includes surveys, jams, tastes, music, art, open streets, and more. The safest way to enjoy these things is to be vaccinated and boosted against covid and possibly monkeypox. So don't forget you can visit vax4nyc.nyc.gov or vax4nyc.nyc.gov/monkeypox and make an appointment.

Third, Borough President Reynoso conditionally approved the 9th Street Rezoning yesterday. In June, we also issued conditional approval. You’ll notice many parallels in both our and the BP’s conditions. Most notably, the need for the affordable housing component to be deeply affordable with MIH option 3 and for DCP to follow through and rezone the IBZ to expand its capacity. The next stage in the ULURP process is the City Planning Commission.

item.description: Despite the sunny day, Covid-19 rates and hospitalizations due to the BA5 variant are a dark cloud rising. However, those rates are lower than the Omicron peak, thanks to vaccination.
item.content:encoded:
Despite the sunny day, Covid-19 rates and hospitalizations due to the BA5 variant are a dark cloud rising. However, those rates are lower than the Omicron peak, thanks to vaccination. So, keep testing and, now that everyone six months old is eligible for a vaccine, make an appointment to get your child vaccinated and yourself boosted by going to vax4nyc.nyc.gov.

Many things are happening throughout the week, and they’re certainly more enjoyable the safer everyone is. Happenings include music in Cobble Hill Park, movies in Brooklyn Bridge & Washington Park movies, a housing fair, and a Congressional Town Hall.

More information on those events and additional items are listed below my email signature. You should check them out, or at least click them. But, no matter what, stay cool, safe, and enjoy the rest of your day.

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Thursday, June 30, 2022
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: In these final hours, I’ll remind you that tonight, from 6 until 8 pm, the Gowanus CAG will be holding an in-person town hall at PS 32 on the clean-up of the canal with EPA.
item.content:encoded:
In these final hours, I’ll remind you that tonight, from 6 until 8 pm, the Gowanus CAG will be holding an in-person town hall at PS 32 on the clean-up of the canal with EPA.

Looking back briefly to the life of someone who cared about the canal and all things neighborhood, it was great to see so many people come out for the co-naming of First Place & Court Street in honor of Salvatore “Buddy” Scotto. Included in the crowd were multiple CB6 members like his daughter Deb and his successor at the funeral home John Heyer II, whom Councilmember Hanif graciously permitted to emcee the reveal. In addition, Councilmember Hanif, Comptroller Lander, Assemblymember Simon, Justice Pesce, and a former Mayor from CB6 spoke, and our current Mayor issued a heartfelt proclamation.

More information is below my email signature, so I suggest scrolling past here. However, enjoy the rest of your day whether you scroll or not.

item.title: Friday, June 17, 2022
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well as we head into the weekend. It’ll be a very busy weekend and workweek.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well as we head into the weekend. It’ll be a very busy weekend and workweek. So I’ll quickly highlight some of what I’m referring to. 

Starting tomorrow, Saturday, June 18th, early voting in primary elections for Governor, Lieutenant Governor, State Assembly, Judges, & other partisan positions will begin. Saturday is also the day to go on an art walk, get a free bike helmet, participate in a “Teach-In,” and stop by a farm stand. Sunday, June 19th, there are events for Juneteenth, a street fair, and more.

On Monday, June 20th, the city observes Juneteenth. For that reason, Alternate Side Parking and sanitation services will be suspended, NYC Public Schools will be closed, and all city-run Covid-19 Vaccination and Testing sites will be closed. Looking to the workweek, we have a BQE meeting, a Last Mile Warehouse Forum, and a Gowanus Update. 

Lastly, the Health Department’s Covid-19 alert system remains at high risk (Orange). So, if you haven’t already, get vaccinated and boosted by going to vax4nyc.nyc.gov.

More information can be found by scrolling down this email. However, whether you scroll or not, stay safe and have a great weekend.
