item.title: Pride, Town hall, More
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well as we head into the weekend after a week highlighted by Wednesday’s Full Board meeting.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well as we head into the weekend after a week highlighted by Wednesday’s Full Board meeting.

If you missed the full board meeting, you could watch it here on Youtube. However, if you'd prefer, I'll provide a meeting synopsis. We began by welcoming new members and voting to allow us to continue to meet virtually until the city’s emergency order is no longer in place. After that, we moved on to the committee reports, which consisted of three items from our Landmarks/Land Use Committee.

The first item was a Land Use item and discussion of a motion to disapprove a rezoning and special permit on 9th Street between 2nd & 3rd Avenue. The committee’s motion to disapprove was rejected, and the application was approved with conditions. The other two items were motions to approve applications for Certificates of Appropriateness. The full board approved both. We were also joined by elected officials from City and State governments throughout the meeting.

The June full board meeting was our final full board meeting until September. However, there will be other meetings between now and September. For example, on Wednesday, June 15th, our Parks & Environmental Protection committee will meet at 6:30 PM over Zoom. The focus will be discussing the possibility of making Upper Van Voorhees park into a dog run. Register for the meeting by going to bit.ly/June15ParksCB6.

However, before Wednesday, plenty is going on. Such as PRIDE festivities on 5th Avenue and Sunday's Town Hall with Councilmember Shahana Hanif at the Old Stone House. No matter what you choose to do, have a great weekend!

Tomorrow, Wednesday, June 8th, at 6:30 pm, we’ll hold our June Full Board Meeting over Zoom. Register for the meeting by going to bit.ly/June8BKCB6.The agenda will focus on three motions from our CB6 Landmarks/Land Use (LMLU) Committee.

From the LU side of the committee, there’s a motion to disapprove a rezoning and special permit on 9th Street between 2nd & 3rd Avenue. The other two items are motions to approve applications for Certificates of Appropriateness ("C of A"). One of those two allows for installing visible railings at the roof and replacing existing leaded glass windows on the front facade at 121-123 6th Avenue in the Park Slope Historic District. The other would allow for installing a new, black steel rear deck with a glass canopy at 483 Henry Street in the Cobble Hill Historic District.

item.title: Friday, May 27, 2022
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well as summer unofficially begins with Memorial Day weekend. I have a couple of items to highlight.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well as summer unofficially begins with Memorial Day weekend. I have a couple of items to highlight.

First, last night, our CB6 Landmarks/Land Use (LMLU) Committee met and reviewed three items. From the LU side of the committee, the first was for a rezoning and special permit on 9th Street between 2nd & 3rd Avenue. The committee, citing support for the IBZ, voted to disapprove of this application by a vote of 11 to 4. The other items for review were both applications for Certificates of Appropriateness ("C of A"), and the committee overwhelmingly approved them. The next stop for these three items will be our June 8th General Board meeting, when the full board will vote on the committee's motions. 

Second, on a functionary note, on Memorial Day, Monday, May 30th, Alternate Side Parking, and even meters will be suspended, as will trash, recycling, and compost collection. Lastly, the Health Department’s Covid-19 alert system remains at high risk (Orange). So, if you haven’t already, get vaccinated and boosted by going to vax4nyc.nyc.gov.

If you read past my contact information, you’ll find a lot is happening across our community in the near future. However, regardless of your thoughts on that future, have a great Memorial Day Weekend.

item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well on this 24th Day of May, also the 139th anniversary of the Brooklyn Bridge. I have three items and a suggestion to highlight.

First, as I’m sure you’ve heard, there’s a baby formula shortage. The Mayor signed an executive order to prevent price gouging. To report being overcharged,  file a complaint at nyc.gov/dcwp or by calling 311 and saying “overcharge.”

Secondly, if you believe, as CB6 has, that  .6 percent of the city’s budget is not enough for parks, you should, if you have the time, head down to City Hall Park on Thursday, May 26th at 10:00 am and join the Play Fair Coalition to rally and demand 1% of the city budget be allocated for NYC Parks.  Thanks to CB6 Parks Chair Glenn Kelly for highlighting this event.

Third, the Health Department’s Covid-19 alert system remains at high risk (Orange). So, if you haven’t already, get vaccinated and boosted by going to vax4nyc.nyc.gov.

If you read past my contact information, you’ll find a lot is happening across our community. That includes tonight’s Gowanus CAG meeting, tomorrow’s Cobble Hill Association Annual meeting, the Southwest Brooklyn Tenant Union’s May meeting, and other items of interest.  However, whether you check out any of these happenings or not, stay safe and enjoy the rest of your day.

item.title: Friday, May 20, 2022
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well as we head into what’s expected to be a warm weekend. I have four items to highlight.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well as we head into what’s expected to be a warm weekend. I have four items to highlight.

First, the court-appointed special master hasn’t released his final and binding maps for New York’s State Senate and Congressional districts. Those maps are still expected to be released today, but closer to 7 or 8 pm. You may have heard about a CB6 resident already running despite this lack of finality.

Second, speaking of legislators, a deal, in line with the community board stance, was reached to keep the city’s speed camera program in place for another three years. Along with the extension of years, the cameras will now run 24 hours a day instead of the current schedule, where they are shut off from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m.

Third, if you have some time to read, I suggest checking out HPD’s housing and vacancy study that shows the number of apartments available for low- and- middle-income households has reached a 30-year low. At the same time, Airbnb has more listings than apartments available for rent.

Fourth, I’ll remind you that the Health Department’s Covid-19 alert system is now at high risk (Orange). So, if you haven’t already, get vaccinated and boosted by going to vax4nyc.nyc.gov.

If you read past my contact information, you’ll find a lot is happening across our community this weekend and the weekend ahead. That includes tonight’s District 15 Superintendent Town Hall,  Saturday’s Brooklyn Conservatory of Music’s Open Stages, and Thursday’s Landmarks/Land Use Committee meeting. However, whether you check out any of these happenings or not, stay safe and have a great weekend.

item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Due to calendar conflicts, our 2nd Vice-Chair, Jerry Armer, chaired the meeting. Running a full board meeting was a familiar role for Jerry as he’s previously been board chair for multiple terms and may hold a record for most meetings…
item.content:encoded:
Due to calendar conflicts, our 2nd Vice-Chair, Jerry Armer, chaired the meeting. Running a full board meeting was a familiar role for Jerry as he’s previously been board chair for multiple terms and may hold a record for most meetings chaired. Thank you to Jerry for getting us through last night's agenda.

That agenda focused on four applications for Certificates of Appropriateness (C of A). All four were approved and located within the Cobble Hill Historic District. The application to install a new rooftop bulkhead and solar canopy at 171 Baltic Street required more debate and something resembling a roll call vote. The remaining three items required less debate for their approval. In between those votes, Councilmember Restler discussed his climate action plan and legislation.

We also heard from other legislative and government offices and community members. One of the topics was the proliferation of last-mile warehouses in Red Hook and work being done to curtail their impact. If that summary doesn’t cut it for you, a meeting recording is on our Youtube page. Our next full board meeting is on June 8th over Zoom.

I recommend you read past my contact information as you’ll find some items of interest. However, no matter what you do, stay safe and enjoy the day's remaining hours.

I hope this email finds you well on this sort of sunny 25th Day of April. I have three items to highlight, followed by a standard suggestion.

First, in response to recent efforts to ban books across the country, the Brooklyn Public Library launched its Books UnBanned campaign. What this means is that any 13 to 21-year-old nationwide can apply for a free one-year BPL e-card, which provides access to 350,000 e-books, 200,000 audiobooks, and over 100 databases. If you, or anyone you know, like to spread the word and/or know anyone who would benefit from such access, click here or go to bklynlibrary.org/books-unbanned.

Secondly, the city's Summer Rising program application is now available. The program is open to all elementary and middle school students. Parents can apply for their children by clicking here or going to schools.nyc.gov/enrollment/summer.

Third, Covid infections have climbed closer to a “medium” risk rate category from our current “low” risk rate. Even with the innumerable and undocumented at-home testing for the first time since February, we’re seeing over three thousand positive cases a day. However, within this data, a clear narrative is that it’s much safer if you’re vaccinated, boosted, and if eligible, double boosted. item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well on this twentieth day of April. A date that (420) has many, including the Mayor and Governor, celebrating marijuana becoming legal in New York. However, I fall far short of 420 and have three items I’d like to highlight today.

First, earlier today, after years of work and millions of dollars spent to remediate, the Red Hook Ball Fields, specifically fields 5 through 8, officially reopened. Celebrating this were Mayor Adams, Congresswoman Velasquez, Councilmember Aviles, the EPA, the City’s Parks Department, lots of community members, and five CB6 Members, including Red Hook’s Leroy Branch, Board Secretary Karen Broughton, and our Parks Chair Glenn Kelly. It’s expected to get colder tonight, but while we were out there ( I could only attend briefly), it was beautiful and served as an excellent reminder of how important parks are.

Secondly, an annoyingly regular reminder to get tested, vaccinated, and boosted against Covid-19 if you haven’t already done so. The rate of infection, especially reinfection, is ticking back up, and the best way to stay safe is to take such precautions.

Third, if you park a private vehicle on public streets, please note that Alternate Side Parking is suspended from tomorrow, Thursday, April 21st, through Saturday, April 23rd. However, it’s not a complete reprieve as Parking Meters will still be in effect. 

More items are listed below my contact info. I suggest you check them out, but enjoy the rest of your day, no matter what you think of my suggestions.

I hope this email finds you well as we begin the workweek. I’ll briefly highlight three items and offer a familiar suggestion.

First, the Office of Emergency Management has issued a Flood Watch and a Wind Advisory for tonight until tomorrow morning. With winds at up to 50 MPH and possible flooding, caution is advised.

Secondly, with Covid-19 still, very much around, the state has extended authorization for us to meet on Zoom until June 9th. item.title: Thursday, April 14, 2022
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well on this warm and rainy Thursday. For all those who are celebrating, Happy Holy Thursday.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well on this warm and rainy Thursday. For all those who are celebrating, Happy Holy Thursday.

As advertised, last night was our April Full Board meeting. Everything we voted on was overwhelmingly approved. Peter Fleming’s Chairperson report included motions to approve the March minutes and staff cost of living payroll adjustments. Our Landmarks/Land Use and Permits& Licenses committees also had motions for review.

Alec Schierenbeck presented the LMLU motions. One was the disapproval of an application to the Board of Standards & Appeals to build in a mapped but unutilized privately owned prolongation of Clinton Street to facilitate the development of a logistics center at 728 Court Street from three buildings to two buildings. The other 2 were approvals for applications to the Landmarks Preservation Commission for Certificates of Appropriateness (C of A) from the Landmarks Preservation Commission(LPC). One C of A’s was to install a rooftop solar array at 188 Prospect Park West (Nitehawk), and the other was for a newly enlarged 2-story rear yard extension at 19 Tompkins Place.

Rebecca Kobert pinch-hit for Rachel Freeman and presented the P & L motions. All three motions for On-Premises Liquor Licenses were approved overwhelmingly. Those licenses were for  Cousin John's Park Slope Inc. at 60 7th Avenue, Don Abel LLC at 226 7th Avenue, and Docky's of Red Hook LLC at 354 Van Brunt Street.

We also heard from Councilmembers Aviles & Restler, Assemblymember Simon, and representatives from other legislative offices. If that summary doesn’t cut it, you can watch the entire meeting on our Youtube page.

More items are listed below my contact info. I suggest you check them out, but stay safe and be at peace the rest of your day, no matter what you think of my suggestions.

item.title: Tuesday, April 12, 2022
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: As I’m sure you know, just over in Sunset Park, at the 36th Street Subway Station, at least 16 people were injured, ten by gunfire both inside a subway car and on the platform. I’ve been in touch with NYPD and FDNY all day, and they’ve…
item.content:encoded:
As I’m sure you know, just over in Sunset Park, at the 36th Street Subway Station, at least 16 people were injured, ten by gunfire both inside a subway car and on the platform.  I’ve been in touch with NYPD and FDNY all day, and they’ve been quick to answer any questions I’d passed along from constituents. I’d particularly offer thanks to FDNY Assistant Commissioner Jason Shelly.

We can't yet know the full human impact of this incident. What we do know is that NYPD is searching for the suspect. The D, N, and R subway lines are shut down, and there are extended delays on the subway system and roads. But, it’s free to ride the South Brooklyn NYC Ferry.  As I learn more, I’ll be sure to share it. 

Please don’t forget that our Full board meets tomorrow, Wednesday, April 13th, over Zoom at 6:30 PM. if you want to register for the meeting, review the agenda and March Minutes, click here or go to: bit.ly/Apr13BKCB6

item.description: I hope this email finds you well on this cloudy first Tuesday and 5th day of April. I’d like to draw your attention to a popular theme of the New York Government right now.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well on this cloudy first Tuesday and 5th day of April. I’d like to draw your attention to a popular theme of the New York Government right now. That theme is budgeting.

First, the legislative and executive branches of New York is ironing out the budget for Fiscal Year 2023. It’s technically late, but a stop-gap measure has been passed to hold things in place. While the budget is at issue other matters are expected to be part of any final agreement. Issues like Criminal Justice reform, a possible casino in NYC, and subsidies for a Buffalo Bills football stadium are some of the outstanding items. I’d recommend clicking here and checking out the New York Times overview of where things stand and clicking here for a guide to this opaque Albany tradition.

Secondly, at the City Level, the budget isn’t due until July 1st, but the process is already in motion. The Council released their counter to the Mayor’s preliminary budget, and you can read that here. If reading budget documents makes you want to have a more direct say, then vote in Participatory Budgeting(PB) process. PB will be run through Sunday, April 10th.

More details on these items, Covid stats, and more are listed below, so I suggest you check them out; but, whatever you think of my suggestions, stay safe, and enjoy the rest of your Tuesday.

item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well on this twenty-fifth day of March as we head into the first full weekend of spring with a possible polar vortex headed our way. I have three items to highlight today; one recap and two reminders.

First, last night, our CB6 Landmarks/Land Use (LMLU) Committee met and reviewed three items, two from LM and one from LU. First up was an application to the Board of Standards and Appeals(BSA) to allow for a mapped but unbuilt prolongation of Clinton Street to facilitate the development of a logistics center at 728 Court Street. This application garnered the most discussion of the evening's agenda with much community and committee participation. After the discussion, the committee voted to disapprove the application 7 to 4.

The 2 LM items, applications for Certificates of Appropriateness (C of A) from the Landmarks Preservation Commission(LPC), were overwhelmingly approved. The first of those 2 “ C of A’’s was to install a rooftop solar array at 188 Prospect Park West in the Park Slope Historic District, while the other was for a newly enlarged 2-story rear yard extension at 19 Tompkins Place in the Cobble Hill Historic District.

If that summary doesn’t suffice, you can relive all the action on our YouTube page. Also, please remember that these three items will now move to a vote from our full board at our April 13th general board meeting. You can register for that meeting by clicking here or going to bit.ly/Apr13BKCB6.

Secondly, our Permits and Licences Committee meets this Monday, March 28th, at 630 PM to review applications for three liquor licenses. You can register for that meeting by clicking here or going to bit.ly/March28Permits. Those three items are expected to join the LMLU items on the April Agenda.

Third, we’ve got lots of stuff happening this weekend, such as Stoop Sales for Ukraine. This weekend over 90 households in Boerum Hill, Cobble Hill, Carroll Gardens, and Gowanus are hosting a stoop sale to raise money for humanitarian efforts in Ukraine. You can find more details by clicking here or going to: tinyurl.com/stoopforukraine.

item.description: I hope this email finds you well as we close out the work week and winter. I have two items I’d like to highlight before some suggestions.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well as we close out the work week and winter. I have two items I’d like to highlight before some suggestions.

Regardless of the outcome in Albany, we’ll be on Zoom through at least our April 13th Full board meeting. This is thanks to Governor Hochul signing an extension of an Executive Order that has allowed us and other similar governmental bodies to meet virtually since the Spring of 2020. As a result, with the increased accessibility, we’ve seen higher attendance and participation rates throughout the pandemic.

Secondly, while Saint Patrick’s day has passed, the celebration hasn’t stopped. So, as mentioned yesterday, I’ll remind you that this Sunday, March 20th, the Brooklyn Saint Patrick’s Day makes its triumphant return to Prospect Park West beginning at Noon. It’s a unique event on a much smaller scale than the more famous parade on Manhattan’s 5th Avenue yesterday. item.title: Thursday, March 17, 2022
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Happy Saint Patrick’s Day to all those celebrating, and if you’re not, I’d still hope this email finds you well. Today was a marker in the city’s long road to a new normal as it was the first New York City Saint Patrick’s parade since…
item.content:encoded:
Happy Saint Patrick’s Day to all those celebrating, and if you’re not, I’d still hope this email finds you well. Today was a marker in the city’s long road to a new normal as it was the first New York City Saint Patrick’s parade since 2019, with the parade not being held due to Covid in 2020 & 2021. The parade had been held for over 250 consecutive years before the 2020 cancelation. So while I have the bias of Irish ancestry, it’s undoubtedly good to see such a tradition return. 

Today’s parade is more widely recognized, but this Sunday, March 20th, the Brooklyn Saint Patrick’s Day Parade will be held for the first time since 2019 and will take place right here in our district. Not only does it march through our district (Prospect Park West between 15th and 9th street at Noon), the Grand Marshall is a great friend to Brooklyn Community Board 6, Brooklyn Parks Commissioner Martin Maher. It won’t be as big as the parade today, but that doesn’t mean the Brooklyn’s isn’t better. I recommend stopping by if you have the chance. 

I’d also recommend scrolling down past my contact info for more information on items such as next week’s Landmarks/Land Use meeting and more. No matter what you choose to do, stay safe, and enjoy the remainder of the day.

item.title: Thursday, March 10, 2022
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well in the wake of March’s full board meeting. It was a busy meeting, and I’ll summarize in the upcoming paragraphs and follow that with a suggestion to scroll further down this email.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well in the wake of March’s full board meeting. It was a busy meeting, and I’ll summarize in the upcoming paragraphs and follow that with a suggestion to scroll further down this email.

Looking back to last night, once we had a quorum, the meeting was called to order, and we heard from Council Member Lincoln Restler who was followed by our new  Brooklyn Borough President Antonio Reynoso. It was great to have the BP be part of the meeting and hear about interfacing with community boards and other parts of his new role. However, I know many folks were especially grateful for the praise he gave for the Gowanus rezoning, referring to it as  “a model for rezoning.” 

After that, our Chairperson, Peter Fleming continued with the Gowanus rezoning and announced that we’d named four people to the initial stage of the rezoning’s oversight committee. Those four folks were David Briggs, Angelica Ramdhari, Tiffany Reid-Brown, and Alec Schierenbeck, with the focus for the group at this stage being the hiring of a facilitator. As noted last night, as the committee grows, so will the number of people named to it.

The next portion of the meeting presented four new on-premises liquor licenses from our Permits and Licenses (P&L)  by Committee Chair, Rachel Freeman. All four applications were approved overwhelmingly. For those wondering the 4 licenses will be at,215 Union Street, 787 Union Street, 278A 5th Avenue, as well 74 5th Avenue.

After P&L, we moved to items from our Landmarks & Land Use Committee (LMLU). With our LU Chair Alec Scherinbeck unavailable to attend, the LM  Chair, David Briggs, pinch-hit and presented all five of the committee's items. Three of those five were applications to the Landmarks Preservation Commission for "Certificates of Appropriateness." All three were approved unanimously. The "C of A" 's were at 305 President Street, 480 Henry Street, and 243 Garfield Place, respectively.

The LU items were for a ULURP and a variance and were approved overwhelmingly. The BSA item was to reduce the total number of required accessory off-street parking spaces from 75 to 38 at 218 Hamilton Avenue. The very need for this request led to the committee asking that the city looks to update requirements for parking and pedestrian safety along Hamilton Avenue. The ULURP was to rezone 41 Summit Street (Block 352, Lot 60 and p/o Lot 1) from an M1-1 to R6B zoning district to facilitate the development of a Use Group 2 four-story plus basement residential building with a total floor area of 5000 sq. ft. (2.0 FAR) and four dwelling units. As mentioned in the chat, and during the community session last night, Borough President Reynoso is holding a hearing on the 41 Summitt Street rezoning tonight at 6 PM. 

When we finished the voting portion of the meeting we heard from representatives from Nydia Velasquez, Assemblymember Simon, Senators Kavanah and Myrie, Councilmembers Hanif and Avelis, as well as the Captain of the 78th Precinct. The meeting adjourned a little after 8:30 and if that summary doesn’t cut it you can watch the entire meeting on our Youtube page.

Happy International Women’s day. I hope this email finds you well on this considerably colder than yesterday, March meeting eve. I have three items, and I’ll go through them as quickly as I can.

First, be mindful that despite recent rollbacks of Covid-19 safety measures (masks in schools, vaccine screenings), we’re still seeing people test positive, and an Omicron subvariant is spreading. The intent of mentioning this is not to increase pandemic fatigue or panic but to maintain an accurate assessment of where we are to enable us to move forward safely and never go back to various restrictions that I don’t think anyone remembers fondly. 

Second, as mentioned in the first sentence, don’t forget tomorrow, Wednesday, March 9th at 6:30 PM over Zoom, we have our March Full Board meeting. We will be voting on nine items coming from two of our committees. Four of them are liquor license applications from our Permits & Licences Committee, while the other five will be from our Landmarks/Land Use Committee. Three of those five items seek landmark Certificates of Approritatentess, one is a ULURP, and the other is a BSA application. If you haven’t already done so, you may register for the meeting at bit.ly/Mar9cb6.

Third, if you're looking to read something dense, I'd strongly recommend the city's waterfront plan. To read the full plan, click here or go to the plan's website: www.waterfrontplan.nyc.

item.description: I hope this email finds you well as you begin a week with warmth and Wednesday's board meeting about forty-eight hours from now. I have three items I’ll go through as quickly as I can.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well as you begin a week with warmth and Wednesday's board meeting about forty-eight hours from now. I have three items I’ll go through as quickly as I can.

First, the Covid-19 pandemic entered a new chapter in New York City today as mandates requiring masks in public schools and proof of vaccination for various activities were lifted. However, masks are still required in hospitals, healthcare settings, and public transportation. So, hopefully, the infection rate and risk stay low, and any concerns of new variants and that this is too early end up being misplaced. 

Secondly, on the very border of our district, the 57-year-old war memorial at Bartel-Pritchard Square was hit by a driver in the early hours of Sunday. The driver caused a fire and destroyed the memorial. There were relatively minor injuries, but this only reinforces our continuing support for safety measures on our streets.

Third, a reminder that the FDNY recommends checking your smoke and carbon monoxide detector batteries as we approach daylight savings time this coming Sunday, March 13th. These smoke detectors don’t have anything to do with daylight savings directly. Still, the timing of “Springing” ahead and “Falling behind” are good timelines to follow when ensuring these safety devices have power if necessary.

I hope this email finds you well as we begin the third month of the year, and for those who celebrate such things, Happy Mardi Gras! I have four items to which I’d like to draw your attention.

First, I start with some sad news. South Brooklyn's Cecilia Cacace, a member of Brooklyn Community Board 6 from 1982 until 2008, has passed away. I only met Cecilia a few times before she reluctantly moved to Wisconsin in 2013. Still, her reputation preceded her as someone who could never be ignored and who advocated for her beliefs and helped people any way she could. I hope that for all who did know her, may her memory, especially her deep commitment to community, be a blessing and inspiration going forward.

Secondly, as previewed, our Permits & Licenses committee met last night. The committee reviewed four new on-premises liquor license applications, and all four were overwhelmingly approved. If you’re interested but didn’t attend last night or want to relive it, you may watch all the action on our Youtube page. However, if you’d prefer to only look to the future, those four applications, just like last week's Landmarks & Land Use Items, will next be up for a vote from our Full Board a week from tomorrow on Wednesday, March 9th. Again, like last night’s meeting, the Full Board meeting will be held over Zoom and begin at 6:30 PM and you can register for it by clicking here or going to bit.ly/Mar9cb6.

Third, since today is Mardi Gras or “Fat Tuesday,” tomorrow, March 2nd, is Ash Wednesday, and as such Alternate Side Parking Regulations will be suspended. However, please take note that parking meters will remain in effect. 

Fourth, don’t forget that Thursday’s BQE meeting is CANCELED. Thanks to everyone who has amplified that on social media.

The other three are applications for Certificates of Appropriateness, one in the Cobble Hill historic district, another in the Carroll Gardens historic district, and the last one in the Park Slope Historic District.

Tonight’s meeting is the second and final CB6 committee meeting for this week. Next week, just like this week, we have meetings on Monday and Thursday. item.title: Tonight, Last Night
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well in the wake of February’s full board meeting. Following the month’s example, the meeting was comparatively short.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well in the wake of February’s full board meeting. Following the month’s example, the meeting was comparatively short.

Soon after calling the meeting to order, we heard from State Senator Jabari Brisport. Senator Brisport took advantage of the technical tools of the virtual format with a brief slide presentation on the state budget process, funding options, the open meeting law, and redistricting. Unfortunately, part of redistricting is that beginning January 2023, Jabari’s 25th senate district will no longer overlap with our community district. 

Following the Senator’s slides, we approved the minutes from our January meeting and moved on to three items for a vote. Two were liquor license applications to the Staten Liquor Authority (SLA) from our Permits & Licenses (P&L) committee. The first was for a fusion and fried chicken restaurant at 244 Flatbush Avenue, and the second was for a Italian restaurant at 272 3rd Avenue. Both license requests were unanimously approved and now move on to the SLA.

Before moving on to the third voting item, we were joined by Council Member Lincoln Restler with updates on what he’s been doing in his first month and a half representing the 33rd district. Lincoln told us he and the entire Brooklyn council delegation are opposing huge ConEd rate hikes. He spoke about local hiring at Wyckoff and mentioned that on February 23rd, he’s hosting a panel discussion titled Community Board 101 (CB 101), explaining what community boards can do and why folks should apply to become members. I’m a panelist at CB101, so I concede a bias, but I think that will be a great event for anyone interested in applying to be part of their community board. 

The third voting item was from the Landmarks portion of our Landmarks/Land Use Committee. That item was for a Certificate of Appropriateness(C of A) from the Landmarks Preservation Commission(LPC) to restore the front facade and stoop, install a new roof deck at the middle section of the roof, and a two-story rear yard extension with a roof deck and a glazed rear opening at 205 Clinton Street in the Cobble Hill Historic District. It was approved on the condition that the applicant considers mitigation of visibility of the rooftop components (railings, deck, and chimneys). During the discussion of this item, there was some surprise when folks learned that neighboring 205 Clinton Street was a Gun Club, the Metropolitan Rod & Gun Club at 162 Pacific Street.

Closing out the meeting, we heard from the offices of Congresswoman Velasquez, Senator Kavanagh, Assembly Members Carroll, Simon, and Council Member Hanif.

If that summary doesn't cut it, or you want to relive the action, you can watch the meeting here on Youtube. Our next full board meeting is Wednesday, March 9th at 630 PM. Also, don't forget that DEP is hosting a meeting on the Owls Head CSO tonight, Thursday, February 10th, at 7 pm. To register, go to bit.ly/feb10dep.

If you keep scrolling down this email, you’ll find additional interesting items and happenings. However, whether you read past here or not, stay safe, enjoy the rest of your day, and hopefully, I’ll see you later.

item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well as we begin February, the Year of the Tiger, and Black History Month. I have a few brief items to which I’d like to draw your attention.

First, the Red Hook Recreation Center has reopened. The hours of operation are Monday through Friday, 6 am until 8 pm, and Saturdays from 8 am until 4 pm.

Secondly, the new district lines for the New York State Assembly and Senate have been released. Like with congressional lines, they are expected to be approved this week, and many of us may end up in a new district or with new representation in the state legislature. If you’d like to see what district you’ll be living in or what changes are proposed,  go to redistrictingandyou.org and find all the legislative lines.

Third, as you may already know, over 500 units at the Gowanus houses were without heat and hot water last night.  Around midnight, the heat and hot water were restored, and thankfully, during the disruption, Council Member Lincoln Restler, as well as Gowanus Mutual Aid, secured 500 gallons of water. Mayor Adams was also on sight to ensure the work was completed. I mention this not just to share information but to reiterate how important, as I discussed with Lincoln this morning, the 200 million dollars dedicated to NYCHA repairs in the Gowanus Rezoning POA is, and it can’t get here soon enough. That funding for NYCHA was a major, if not the “the” major, condition of supporting the rezoning for not just us as CB6 but others such as GNCJ and, at the time, Borough President, and now Mayor, Adams. Last night was a reminder of why and the immediate attention from the  Mayor and Council Member is, hopefully, a good indicator that the necessary and long-term improvements will be made. 

Lastly, alternate side parking regulations are suspended through Saturday, February 5th, and if you keep scrolling down this email, you’ll find some additional interesting items. However, whether you read past here or not, stay safe and enjoy the rest of your Tuesday.

Second, Covid cases are down over 90% from their peak just a few weeks back on the pandemic front. However, people are still being infected, ending up in the hospital and dying. However, those vaccinated and boosted are way less likely to end up in the hospital or dead, and as of yesterday, 75% of New Yorkers are fully vaccinated. Also, as the Mayor announced yesterday, people who test positive for Covid can receive free same-day at-home delivery of oral antiviral pills to treat it by calling 212-COVID19.

Third, the next few weeks have a lot going on, so it may be helpful to scroll down and mark your calendar now. The "going on" includes our board meeting next Wednesday, February 9th, and a meeting that DEP is hosting on Thursday, February 10th, focusing on the Gowanus Canal "Owls Head" combined sewer overflow facility.

Whether you read past here or not, stay safe and enjoy the final hours of January and begin, for all those who celebrate Lunar New Year, the Year of The Tiger.

item.title: State of Snow
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well and warm as we brace for some snow. The estimates run a range, but the most likely amount is somewhere between 8 and 12 inches.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well and warm as we brace for some snow. The estimates run a range, but the most likely amount is somewhere between 8 and 12 inches. 

A state of emergency has been declared, The New York City Office of Emergency Management issued a hazardous travel advisory, and the National Weather Service has issued a Winter Storm Warning. The advisory and warning will go into effect tonight, Friday, January 28th, at 7 pm and be in effect until tomorrow, Saturday, January 29th, at 7 pm. In practical terms, it amounts to staying inside through Saturday. 

While it may not have been done to reduce the Fear Of Missing Out (FOMO) while staying in, fewer services will be available. For example, Sanitation will be focusing on snow operations, so collections are likely to be delayed; the MTA has said outdoor portions subways could stop at some point, outdoor dining will be suspended, libraries and city-run Covid-19 vaccine & testing sites will be closed. Also, NYC Department of Education sponsored activities are canceled. If other announcements are made, I’ll be sure to share them ASAP.

Before my regular suggestion to read below my contact information, I’d like to highlight some CB6 specific information. First, at last night’s CB6 Landmarks/Land Use (LMLU) meeting, the Certificate of Appropriateness for 205 Clinton Street was approved and will move forward to be voted on at our February 9th meeting. However, the other application for 305 President Street was tabled, and we’ll hear from them again at a future LMLU meeting. If you missed the meeting or want to rewatch it, you can do so on our YouTube page. Also, we have an update coming up on parks in our district on Wednesday, February 16th, at 6:30 pm.

There are more things worth reading about listed later in this email, so I’ll stop here and suggest checking those out. But no matter what you choose, I hope you stay safe and enjoy the snowy weekend.

item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: The National Weather Service announced a Winter Storm Watch for NYC starting at 7 PM tomorrow, Friday, January 28th, until 7 pm on Saturday, January 29th. The snow accumulation is expected to be anywhere from 6 to 12 inches, with winds as…
item.content:encoded:
The National Weather Service announced a Winter Storm Watch for NYC starting at 7 PM tomorrow, Friday, January 28th, until 7 pm on Saturday, January 29th. The snow accumulation is expected to be anywhere from 6 to 12 inches, with winds as high as 45 miles per hour. As of now, there haven’t been any changes to sanitation, alternate side parking, or anything else, but if that changes, I’ll be sure to let you know.

But before any snow, we have tonight’s Landmarks / Land Use (LMLU) meeting, which begins at 630pm. So this is the final reminder if you want to be part of the action as LMLU reviews two applications for Certificates of Appropriateness; one at 305 President Street and another at 250 Clinton Street.

There are more things worth reading about listed below my contact info, so I’ll stop here and suggest checking those out. But no matter what you choose, I hope you stay safe and enjoy the rest of the evening.

item.title: Wednesday, January 26, 2022
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: In the coming days, we’re expecting a storm that could leave us with anywhere from 2 to 20 inches of snow. If any announcements are made regarding schools, sanitation, alternate side parking, or anything else, I’ll share it, but for…
item.content:encoded:
In the coming days, we’re expecting a storm that could leave us with anywhere from 2 to 20 inches of snow. If any announcements are made regarding schools, sanitation, alternate side parking, or anything else, I’ll share it, but for today, I’ll keep with the more usual fare.

Fare such as the importance of NYCHA funding and why it was a “deal-breaker” condition in our, and others, support for the Gowanus Rezoning. I mention this because, thankfully, there’s been media coverage of the issue. Specifically, yesterday there was a story on flooding and, at the same time, no running water in Gowanus Houses. I was able to speak to Councilman Lincoln Restler, and the water has been restored. However, as Lincoln noted, the $200 million designated in the Gowanus Rezoning to fix these issues can't happen fast enough.

Before recommending some reading, I’ll remind you of 2 upcoming CB6 meetings. First, tomorrow, Thursday, January 27th, we have our Landmarks/ Land Use committee meeting, and two weeks from tonight, Wednesday, February 9th, is our February full board meeting. Both meetings are on Zoom and begin at 6:30 PM.

Now for the reading recommendations, I promised above. I recommend reading below my signature to find out some happenings and items of interest. No matter what you think of the recommendations, stay safe and enjoy the rest of your evening.

item.title: Tuesday, January 25, 2022
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well on this previously sunny Tuesday with some snow on the horizon. I’ll be quick with a recap and some reminders.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well on this previously sunny Tuesday with some snow on the horizon. I’ll be quick with a recap and some reminders.

As previewed in prior newsletters, last night, our Permits & Licenses (P&L) committee met to review two applications for on-premises liquor licenses.  The meeting was chaired by Glenn Kelly, who pinch-hit for Rachel Freeman, and both applications, Cafe Mars at 272 3rd Ave & COOP ONE at 244 Flatbush Avenue, were approved as presented. If that summary left you wanting to learn more about the meeting, you can watch, or relive, the action on our YouTube page.

If looking back doesn’t interest you, look ahead to roughly 48 hours from now when our next committee meeting takes place. To be more specific and not dependent on when you read this, our next committee meeting will be Thursday, January 27th at 6:30 pm with the CB6 Landmarks/ Land Use (LMLU) Committee meeting to review 2 Certificates of Appropriateness applications. One application is at 250 Clinton Street in the Cobble Hill Historic District, and the other is in the Carroll Gardens Historic District at 305 President Street. If you’d like to attend, register by clicking here or go to bit.ly/Jan27LMLUCB6.

The items reviewed by P&L and those to be reviewed by LMLU will also be on the agenda for our February 9th Full Board Meeting, which you may register for by clicking here or going to bit.ly/Feb9CB6. 

As always in our community, plenty is happening not under the CB6 umbrella, and I’ve listed a bunch of it below my signature. I’d suggest looking it over, but no matter what you make of such a suggestion, stay safe, get boosted, and enjoy the evening.

item.title: Permits & Licenses Meeting Tonight

I hope this email finds you well as we kick off the week with some snow and sun. I’ll be brief with a few reminders.

First, tonight’s Permits & Licenses (P&L) Committee meeting, 6:30 pm over Zoom, is one of two CB6 committee meetings we have this week. The committee will review two new on-premises liquor license applications. One license is for 272 3rd Avenue, while the other is for 244 Flatbush Avenue. Please note that all of our meetings are open to the public, and if you’d like to attend, click here or go to:bit.ly/Jan24CB6Liquor.

The second CB6 meeting of the week will be on Thursday, January 27th, when our Landmarks/Land Use (LMLU) Committee meets over Zoom at 6:30 pm. The agenda consists of 2 “Certificates of Appropriateness“ applications. You may register to attend by clicking here or going to:  bit.ly/Jan27LMLUCB6

The next step for the items being reviewed by P&L and LMU this week will be a vote at our full board meeting in about two weeks on Wednesday, February 9th. Like the committees mentioned above, the full board starts at 6:30 pm and takes place on Zoom. If that interests you, like the nearly 30 folks, who have already done so, register by clicking here or going to bit.ly/Feb9CB6.

There’s a lot more stuff happening this week not under the umbrella of CB6 that are listed below my signature, so I’d recommend checking those out ASAP. For example, tomorrow, Tuesday January 25th, Councilmember Lincoln Restler will be giving out free Covid Tests and masks at Wyckoff Gardens from 4:30 until 6 PM while at 6:30 pm, there’s a Red Hook East Residents Association meeting at 167 Bush Street.

Whether you check those other items out or not, stay safe, stay warm, and enjoy the rest of your day.

I hope this email finds you well on this frigid Friday. We’ve got a fair amount happening over the coming week, both directly in and near the CB6 orbit, so I’ll do my best to summarize.

For one, this Sunday, January 23rd, is the final day for idea submissions to Participatory Budgeting. While on Monday, January 24th, as we’ve supported, the NYC ferry will begin year-round and weekday service to Governors Island from Red Hook as part of the South Brooklyn NYC Ferry route. Also, on Monday the 24th, our Permits & Licenses Committee will meet at 6:30 pm. There’s a Discretionary Funding Application Workshop for non-profit organizations looking for funding from the New York City Council on Monday as well. Later next week, on Thursday, January 27th, our Landmarks/ Land Use Committee will meet.

There are more items of interest that I’ve listed below, and I recommend checking them out. For example, the Park Slope Civic Council Community Grant Application is now open.

Whether you check those other items out or not, stay safe, stay warm, and have a great weekend.

Secondly, I’d like to remind you that one week from tonight, Thursday, January 27th, our Landmarks/Land Use committee meets beginning at 6:30 PM. item.title: Wednesday, January 19, 2022
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well on this sunny Wednesday, the 19th day of January. I'll be brief with some reminders, such as Alternate Side Parking being suspended tomorrow, Thursday, January 20th.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well on this sunny Wednesday, the 19th day of January. I'll be brief with some reminders, such as Alternate Side Parking being suspended tomorrow, Thursday, January 20th.

First, the current covid wave is heading in the right direction. However, heading towards a destination doesn’t guarantee arrival, which means that Covid-19 is still very much with us. Yesterday I mentioned that Congresswoman Velasquez has a breakthrough infection, while today, I found out that our chair, Peter Fleming, also has Covid-19. Like the Congresswoman, Peter is vaccinated and boosted, and he isn’t experiencing severe symptoms. This anecdote matches the studies telling us to get vaccinated and boosted. The more people do so, the speed we are heading in the right direction will increase.  

Secondly, don’t forget to order FREE Covid-19 tests delivered to your door by the United States Postal Service by going to COVIDtests.gov. 

Third, and the last item before suggesting that you read below my email signature is to note that this is the last week for idea submissions to participatory budgeting. Councilmembers Hanif and Avelis are both participating, and you can submit ideas until this Sunday, January 23rd.

Best,

item.title: Tuesday, January 18, 2022
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well on this Tuesday, the 18th day of January. Before suggesting you scroll down, I’d like to draw your attention to items that run the gamut of government.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well on this Tuesday, the 18th day of January. Before suggesting you scroll down, I’d like to draw your attention to items that run the gamut of government. What I mean is that the items I’m referring to involve Federal, State, and City government with macro and micro implications.

First, Congresswoman Nydia Velasquez announced that she’s tested positive with a breakthrough Covid-19 infection. We, of course, hope the Congresswoman experiences the most minimal symptoms, recovers quickly and completely. That is more likely to occur since the Congresswoman received three vaccine doses. As her statement read, she encourages everyone to get vaccinated and boosted.

Staying at the federal level, you may now order free Covid-19 tests from the United States Postal Service at COVIDtests.gov. The site “officially” launches tomorrow, Wednesday, January 19th, but you can order four free tests per household now with the expectation that they will be received later this month.

Second, on the state level Governor Hochul unveiled her budget proposal for FY 2023. I haven’t gone through it any detailed way, but you can read it all right here. The headlines I’ve seen highlight increased funding for education, healthcare, transportation along with property tax relief for homeowners coming to a total of 216.3 Billion. The state budget has an April 1st deadline and isn’t official until the New York Senate and Assembly approve it.

Sticking with the State legislative process, some may recall that during last week's meeting, I mentioned that the legislature voted to approve government bodies, such as community boards, being allowed to meet remotely until the Covid-19 emergency is over. Like the budget, this change required the approval of the legislature and governor. So I'm happy to report that Governor Hochul signed the bill (S7623-A /A08591) and Community Boards can meet remotely for the foreseeable future. 

So it’s fitting to remind you that CB6 has two such committee meetings next week. The first is the Permits & Licenses Committee, which meets Monday, January 24th, and the second will be the Landmarks/Land Use Committee which meets on Thursday, January 27th. Both Meetings start at 6:30 pm.

I suggest you check out the happenings and items of interest listed below my email signature; stay safe, get boosted, but no matter what you choose to do, I hope you enjoy the rest of your day.

item.title: Friday, January 14, 2022
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well as we head into a holiday weekend culminating in honoring the great Martin Luther King Jr’s life this coming Monday, January 17th.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well as we head into a holiday weekend culminating in honoring the great Martin Luther King Jr’s life this coming Monday, January 17th.

There are opportunities to, if one is able, dedicate Monday to service. One example is the Red Hook Community Cleanup led by the Red Hook Community Justice Center. Part of the reason more folks can dedicate the day to service is that it’s a holiday with many businesses and offices closed. This could of course change as the weather forecast is predicting snow on Sunday and Monday.

I can’t speak to the status of individual businesses but, this Monday, January 17th, most government agencies are closed, schools and libraries are closed. Still, if you're specifically concerned, I’d contact that agency or check their website. Also, alternate side parking is suspended, as is the postal service. Sanitation pickup is suspended, but due to the weather forecast, they plan to transition to snow operation Sunday and continue that work Monday.

On that note, I’ll stop and suggest you check out the happenings and items of interest listed below my email signature, stay safe, get boosted, and have a great weekend.

item.content:encoded:
There are some signs that the “Omicron Wave” of Covid-19 has crested. However, just because the infection stats aren’t breaking records doesn’t mean it’s over or that it’s not straining our healthcare systems. What the numbers do show is that being vaccinated and boosted against Covid-19 makes you far less likely to become very sick if infected and thus not end up in a hospital or a morgue. 

Anyway, I'll stop here and suggest you scroll down this email for more information on things like tonight's Red Hook Justice Center Housing workshop, Comptroller Lander's "good cause" town hall, a CEC15 meeting, and more. item.title: Tuesday, January 4, 2022
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: While it didn’t snow yesterday, there is a chance of snow Thursday night. If snow does fall and things like schools, alternate side parking, or sanitation are impacted, I’ll let you know ASAP.
item.content:encoded:
While it didn’t snow yesterday, there is a chance of snow Thursday night. If snow does fall and things like schools, alternate side parking, or sanitation are impacted, I’ll let you know ASAP. With that, I’ll briefly touch on two points.

First, Covid hospitalizations in NYC have surpassed 5k for the first time since the spring of 2020. This is straining the city’s healthcare and 911 systems. With that in mind, I was able to speak with FDNY Assistant Commissioner Jason Shelly. He explained that FDNY asks people to only call 911 for true emergencies. However, mild Covid symptoms are not such an emergency. Also, ambulances do not provide testing for COVID-19, and patients are not transported to a hospital to be tested upon request. Of course, this highlights a need for at-home tests to be made readily available. But I digress and remind you to click here for Covid testing locations and the best way to avoid needing Covid services; getting vaccinated and being boosted!

Secondly, while we’re in the first days of a term for New York City Mayor, Comptroller, and Council, those representing New York in the state and federal legislatures next year are TBD. It’s not just TBD who will run but in what districts because the legislative lines for next year are still being determined. The New York State Independent Redistricting Commission met Monday to approve a set of newly-drawn maps that would shape the boundaries for state and federal elections for the next ten years. You can see those maps here, but there are still many possibilities before this process is done in February.

On that note, I’ll stop and suggest you start scrolling down this email. If you don’t scroll down, I still wish for you to stay safe, enjoy the rest of your Tuesday.

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Thursday, December 23, 2021
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well and to all the rest of us celebrating a Happy Festivus. Today, for maybe the last time in 2021, I’ll focus on the two most popular newsletter topics: the Gowanus Rezoning and Covid-19.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well and to all the rest of us celebrating a Happy Festivus. Today, for maybe the last time in 2021, I’ll focus on the two most popular newsletter topics: the Gowanus Rezoning and Covid-19.

First, concerning the Gowanus Rezoning, you may recall that the Points Of Agreement (POA) includes funding for community facilities. One of those facilities is The Old Stone House (OSH) which today was presented with a check for 10.95 Million dollars from Mayor de Blasio to upgrade facilities and improve accessibility. It was an honor to represent BKCB6 as the funding announcement was made alongside Comptroller-Elect Brad Lander, Assembly Member Robert Carroll, Brooklyn Parks Commissioner Marty Maher, and of course, the OSH’s Executive Director Kim Maier. Today's event reinforced everyone’s hard work and the details that went into the Gowanus rezoning. It is a testament to the dividends a community working together can bring about. As someone who went to MS51, which shares Washington Park with OSH, it’s amazing how far this historical site has come under Kim Maier’s leadership. There is no doubt that she’ll use this funding to benefit our community greatly.

Secondly, on Covid, I’d suggest you scroll down past my signature for information that’s focused on Covid-19 safety. Information such as how and where to get tested, vaccinated, and boosted.

So on that note, stay safe, air your grievances, and enjoy the rest of Festivus.

item.content:encoded:
First, thank you to everyone who attended last night's Economic, Waterfront, Community Development, and Housing(EWCDH) Committee meeting. I'd especially like to thank Senator Jabari Brisport, Assemblymember Mitaynes, and Dan Wiley, who represented Congresswoman Nydia Velasquez. As previewed, the meeting focused on last-mile warehouses, and while I’m sure we’ll have more meetings on this matter, but if you weren’t on the Zoom last night or want to relive it, you can watch it on on our YouTube page.

Secondly, the citywide Covid-19 positivity rate is now 10.2%, with somewhat lower rates in our district but still way higher than we’d ever like it to be. So it’s even more important to get tested, vaccinated, and boosted. Take note that getting boosted isn’t just in the best interest of your health; it’s in your financial interest as you’ll get 100 dollars if you do so at a city-run site.

With that I’ll stop and suggest you continue reading, stay safe, and be happy knowing the sun stays out later every day from now until June 21st.

item.title: Friday, December 17, 2021
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Covid-19 cases are multiplying, testing lines are long, omicron is spreading, events are postponed, places are closed, and it’s almost cliche to say it’s reminiscent of 2020. However, there are some real differences between now and then.
item.content:encoded:
Covid-19 cases are multiplying, testing lines are long, omicron is spreading, events are postponed, places are closed, and it’s almost cliche to say it’s reminiscent of 2020. However, there are some real differences between now and then.

First, the New York Times hasn’t profiled anyone moving out of the city, or heading to a second home, as evidence of the city’s permanent decline. More importantly, we have vaccines, safety protocols, and, despite the wait, testing. If you recall, tests were hard to come by at the beginning of the pandemic. Now you can wait in line or at City-run brick & mortar test sites; if there is a line, you will have the option of being given a self-test kit to take home.

I don’t want to take up much of your time or attention; I suggest you scroll down for some useful and safe information. I’d especially want to remind folks about Monday’s committee meeting, focusing on last-mile warehouses and freight. The committee will be joined by State Senator Brisport and Dan Wiley of Congresswoman Velasquez’s office.

On that note, stay safe and have a great weekend.

Best,

item.title: Wednesday, December 15, 2021
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Earlier today Mayor de Blasio, the Department of Transportation (DOT), and the NYC Economic Development Corporation (EDC) unveiled a plan for the future of freight shipping. The “ Delivering Green ” proposal aims to move more goods via…
item.content:encoded:
Earlier today Mayor de Blasio, the Department of Transportation (DOT), and the NYC Economic Development Corporation (EDC) unveiled a plan for the future of freight shipping. The “ Delivering Green ” proposal aims to move more goods via boats, trains, and bikes instead of trucks.

As coverage of today’s announcement noted, Red Hook is seeing a major influx of delivery facilities. We’ve pushed to reduce truck traffic and today’s announcement is, potentially, a step in the right direction. Still, it will require more specific and concrete actions to make it a reality headed in the right direction. In that vein, as it’s been a topic at multiple meetings, this Monday, our Economic, Waterfront, Community Development, and Housing Committee will be discussing this issue along with State Senator Jabari Brisport.

On that note, I’ll stop and suggest you keep scrolling, get vaccinated and boosted, stay safe and enjoy the rest of your Wednesday.

item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well with the 2021 fall finale, aka the winter solstice, less than a week away and four weeks from our January 2022 board meeting.

I mention this as there’s an Instagram trend of people posting pictures of themselves from January 2020  and being “blissfully unaware” of what was to come. Unfortunately, as the infections continue to rise, it seems it’s going to be a bit longer until we’re “blissfully unaware” of Covid-19. Still, we’ll get there sooner(if ever) the sooner more and more people are vaccinated and boosted.  We’re doing pretty well on vaccines but check out the Department of Health's numbers for a complete update, broken down by zip code.

I’ll stop here, suggest scrolling, staying safe, and enjoying the rest of your Tuesday.

item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: The new statewide indoor mask mandate has gone into effect. It means that unless an establishment checks for proof of vaccination, they must require that patrons be masked.
item.content:encoded:
The new statewide indoor mask mandate has gone into effect. It means that unless an establishment checks for proof of vaccination, they must require that patrons be masked. It’s likely to be more of a change in places outside of the city as we’ve already had vaccination requirements at businesses such as restaurants, theatres, and arenas. Either way, it should remind or motivate everyone who hasn’t been vaccinated or boosted against Covid-19 to do so ASAP, especially as infections are rising.

We’ve got a busy week ahead, including State Senator Kavanagh’s Virtual Town Hall tonight and two webinar’s on the city’s "Streets Plan", among other happenings listed below my signature. So I’d recommend scrolling down and seeing those listings, but either way, stay safe and enjoy the rest of your Monday.

item.title: Thursday, December 9, 2021
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well following our final full board meeting of 2021. It was an efficient meeting with Eric McClure temporarily taking the reins as chair as Peter Fleming is under the weather.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well following our final full board meeting of 2021. It was an efficient meeting with Eric McClure temporarily taking the reins as chair as Peter Fleming is under the weather. But, of course, we hope Peter is feeling better asap. 

The voting agenda consisted of 2 liquor licenses which were unanimously approved. One was for Pasta Louise at 1114 8th Avenue, which was most recently, and for a long time, the Johnny Mack’s Location. The second liquor license application was a class change from an existing Wine, Beer & Cider license to a full On-Premises Liquor License on behalf of Simply Greek at 242 5th Avenue.

Along with the votes we heard from Assemblymembers Simon & Carroll, and Senator Myrie.  Councilmember Brad Lander spoke to us for the final time as a Council member but promised to make the occasional appearance as Comptroller, We also heard from Senator Kavanagh’s Office and the Department of Sanitation representatives. While on the subject of sanitation, there were inquires about the upcoming disposal of Christmas Trees; they’ll be collected starting on January 6 through January 15th.

If that summary doesn’t cut it, or you want to relive the action, you can watch the meeting here on Youtube. On that note, I’ll stop and suggest you check out the happenings and items of interest listed below my email signature, stay safe, get boosted, and enjoy the rest of your Thursday.

item.title: Friday, November 12, 2021
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well as we head into the weekend—a weekend following a week that included our penultimate full board meeting of 2021.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well as we head into the weekend—a weekend following a week that included our penultimate full board meeting of 2021.

If you missed the full board or want to relive it, it’s up on YouTube. A busy meeting had our current slate of CB6 Board officers elected for another one-year term. So congratulations to our Chair Peter Fleming, 1st Vice-Chair Eric McClure, 2nd Vice-Chair Jerry Armer, Treasurer Tom Miskel, and Secretary Karen Broughton. The meeting also resulted in the approval of our FY 2023 budget recommendations, 2 liquor licenses, a landmark item, and changes to traffic patterns on Columbia Street. Another approval that was a topic during our meeting had taken place earlier that day when the City Council's Subcommittees on Zoning and Franchises and Land Use voted to approve an amended Gowanus Rezoning, which will now head to a vote by the entire City Council on November 23rd.

As noted during the meeting, what the City Council voted on was, in large measure, aligned with our conditions for support of the rezoning and the similar conditions set forth by the Gowanus Neighborhood Coalition for justice. This is especially true regarding the 200 Million in new funding to repair apartments in NYCHA properties at Gowanus and Wyckoff and hundreds of millions for flood reduction & stormwater infrastructure. This includes $174m for the 4th Ave sewer and community oversight of the rezoning. There’s more detailed coverage of the rezoning that you can find from NY1, City Limits, The Brooklyn Paper, Patch, and others.

On that note, I’ll stop and suggest you scroll down for some information and ideas for the weekend, the coming week, and beyond. Even if you don’t read any further, thanks for reading this far; stay safe, and have a good weekend.

item.title: Full Board Tonight
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I’ll be brief in advance of our November Full board meeting, which begins tonight at 6:30 PM over Zoom. We’ve got a fuller agenda than last month, with votes scheduled on items from our Budget, Landmarks, Permits & Licences, and…
item.content:encoded:
I’ll be brief in advance of our November Full board meeting, which begins tonight at 6:30 PM over Zoom. We’ve got a fuller agenda than last month, with votes scheduled on items from our Budget, Landmarks, Permits & Licences, and Transportation Committees. Speaking of committee votes, you may already know that the City Council's Subcommittees on Zoning and Franchises and Land Use have voted to approve the Gowanus Rezoning, which will now head to a vote by the entire City Council on November 23rd.

What the City Council voted on was, in large measure, aligned with our conditional support of the rezoning and the conditions set forth by the Gowanus Neighborhood Coalition for Justice(GNCJ). This is especially true regarding the 200 Million in funding to repair NYCHA properties at Gowanus and Wyckoff and hundreds of millions for flooding & stormwater infrastructure, including $174m for the 4th Ave sewer.

You can read more details here, and I look forward to seeing many of you tonight over Zoom. Also, with tomorrow being Veterans Day, Brooklyn Community Board 6 thanks all who have served.

On that note, thanks for reading this far along; stay safe, and enjoy the rest of your day.

item.title: Wednesday, November 3, 2021
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I’d like to start by looking back to yesterday and congratulating everyone who won elections as they’ll have the great privilege of leading our city into the future. On the city and borough-wide level, congratulations to Eric Adams on…
item.content:encoded:
I’d like to start by looking back to yesterday and congratulating everyone who won elections as they’ll have the great privilege of leading our city into the future. On the city and borough-wide level, congratulations to Eric Adams on becoming the 110th Mayor of New York City, Anthonio Reynoso as his successor as Brooklyn Borough President, Jumanee Williams, on his reelection as our Public Advocate and Brad Lander to be our city’s next comptroller. On the councilmanic side of the ballot, I’d like to congratulate Lincoln Restler, who will succeed Steve Levin in the 33rd District, Alex Avila, who will succeed Carlos Menchcha in the 38th; and Shahana Hanif, who will succeed Brad Lander in the 39th District and who made history as the first Muslim woman to be elected to the New York City Council.

Some results are still being tabulated and waiting on absentee and affidavit ballots. If you’re interested in keeping an eye on such things, click here for the Board of Elections’ current count.

I’ll stop here but remind you that Alternate Side Parking is suspended tomorrow and that a week from now, on Wednesday, November 10th, we have our monthly full board meeting via zoom. On that note, I’ll thank you for reading this far along and hope that you enjoy the rest of your day.

item.content:encoded:
Good afternoon,

I hope this email finds you well as we start October and head into the weekend.

Last night, as mentioned and promoted, our Transportation and Public Safety Committee met. The focus of the meeting was an update from the New York City Department of Transportation (DOT) on both short- and long-term changes to the BQE Triple Cantilever that included a wide-ranging discussion of traffic issues affecting neighborhoods across CB6. If you couldn’t make it but want to catch up on the information, you can watch the meeting on YouTube and click here for DOT’s presentation.

Looking to the weekend, a lot is going on that’s much more enjoyable or would seem to be than BQE and traffic issues, particularly if you take public transit, bicycle, or walk. Happenings like the Van Alen Institutes Block Party, the 4th Avenue Yarn Bomb, the Atlantic Antic, and more.

Those items and others like the paving schedule are listed below my signature, so I’ll stop and suggest you check them out. Stay safe, find out if you’re eligible for a covid booster shot, and have a great weekend.

Michael Racioppo, District Manager

250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201 .

w. www.BrooklynCB6.org

e. Mike@bkcb6.org

P.S Please forgive any typos or brain freezes in the text as I get these updates out in haste at the end of the day, and if there is a community-centric itoem you think I should know about please reach out.

item.description: I hope this email finds you well as we await October. Let me draw your attention to three brief items before my regularly scheduled suggestion to scroll further down the email.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well as we await October. Let me draw your attention to three brief items before my regularly scheduled suggestion to scroll further down the email. 

First up, and the final reminder, tonight, beginning at 6:30 pm, The Department of Transportation will present to our Transportation & Public Safety Committee updates and changes for the Brooklyn Queens Expressway. Many have already registered for the meeting, but you can do so by following this link. Second, it’s impressive but not surprising; our community district had the most sign-ups for curbside composting of any district in the city. Compost pickup for those who signed up will begin this coming Monday, October 4th. Of course, you may sign up to receive composting by clicking here. But whether you signed up or not, it’s worth reading coverage of the program’s return and how sign-ups reflect heightened socioeconomic inequality. 

Lastly, Brooklyn has the lowest Covid-19 vaccination rate of the five boroughs, so please, for your health and civic pride, if you haven’t already, get vaccinated asap.

Whether you scroll or not, stay safe and enjoy the rest of your Wednesday. 

Best,

item.description: I hope this email finds you well as we head into the weekend with 80% of NYC adults at least partially vaccinated against Covid-19. Such stats make it possible that this pandemic, which feels likes like an unending bad dream, could…
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well as we head into the weekend with 80% of NYC adults at least partially vaccinated against Covid-19. Such stats make it possible that this pandemic, which feels likes like an unending bad dream, could eventually end, at least locally.

Speaking of dreams, you may have heard that the Grand Prospect Hall will not be landmarked. However, based on the communication I’ve received, you may not have realized that it is not within our district. I mention this not just for clarification regarding the event space famous for its commercials, but because district lines, NOT for community boards but for NY’s state legislative and congressional seats, are in the process of being changed as they are every decade. So, even if you don’t move, a different representative may have chosen you as one of their likely voters the next time you vote for State Assembly, State Senate, and Congress. You can see the current proposals and let the redistricting commission know what you think by various means here. 

Keeping with a theme of things to see, the Gowanus Rezoning’s Final Environmental Impact Statement (FEIS) can be seen, and read, here.

On that note, I’ll stop and suggest you scroll down for more information on various happenings and items of interest, such as our BQE meeting, visual experiences, art, building blocks, java, and more meetings.

item.title: Monday, September 13, 2021
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well after a weekend of a solemn anniversary. I know that wasn’t the only thing happening as there were lots of great block parties and other happenings.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well after a weekend of a solemn anniversary. I know that wasn’t the only thing happening as there were lots of great block parties and other happenings. I’d include the VMA ‘s among those happenings but I’m too old and unhip to know what was happening or who was on stage.

Speaking of happening, today was the first day of fully in-person learning in our city's schools since March 2020. For all those who returned, or had someone in their family return to the classroom today, we hope it was a good, or as good as possible, first day at the start of a safe and successful school year. 

Sticking with safety, we’re seeing a drop in Covid-19 infection rates and hope that’s permanently sustained. However, the best way to sustain that is not to hope but through vaccination against Covid-19. If you need more convincing of the 1.3 million infections, just 4%(58k) of them were among the unvaccinated. 

In addition to convincing for the sake of survival, There is an exhortation for the sake of socializing. I say that as today begins the enforcement of the city’s vaccine mandate for many indoor activities such as gyms, restaurants, movies and museums, and more. Some of the events listed below my signature require vaccination and I’d suggest scrolling down and checking them out. 

But even if you don't scroll down, stay safe and enjoy the rest of your Monday.

Best,

item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well as we head into the first weekend of September, which is, for public school students, the final weekend of summer vacation. 

The weekend begins with the 20th anniversary and remembrance of our collective loss on September 11. We also celebrate our steadfast community efforts toward recovery, resiliency, and commitment to our first responders.

Some may be away savoring summer, but there’s still plenty happening right here in our community; for example, later today, the Brooklyn Conservatory of Music has its Fall Fest, and Portside New York has an exhibit on the maritime response to 9/11 running through September 26th. More things are happening in the coming days that you may want to check out listed below my signature, so scroll on down. 

However, whether or not you keep reading, get vaccinated, and if you’re in the north slope, be mindful of street use changes due to Video Music Awards and have a great weekend!

item.title: Thursday, September 9, 2021
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I think it’s safe to say the two most popular, or most mentioned, topics of this newsletter is Covid-19 and everything related to it (especially vaccines) and the Gowanus Rezoning and everything related to it. With that in mind, I’ll start…
item.content:encoded:
I think it’s safe to say the two most popular, or most mentioned, topics of this newsletter is Covid-19 and everything related to it (especially vaccines) and the Gowanus Rezoning and everything related to it. With that in mind, I’ll start with a friendly reminder to get vaccinated against Covid-19 ASAP. This is a key issue as so much of our city and community is off-limits to those not vaccinated.

Secondly, regarding the Gowanus rezoning, it’s great to see Congresswoman Velasquez and Assemblymember Simon hold a rally and write a letter spurred by Ida's nationwide devastation highlighting concerns about Gowanus's resiliency and infrastructure. Many, but not all, of their concerns, were previewed and overlapped with those contained in our conditional rezoning approval. The main overlaps concern Combined Sewer Overflows(CSO), EPA compliance, stormwater, and the need for the final Environmental Impact Statement to be adjusted and corrected on issues such as sewer capacity. 

Also, as an advisory body, it’s always welcome news when additional elected authorities reference our specific conditions, as with Congressmember Velasquez Simon’s letter to Mayor de Blasio. You can read their letter and our conditional approval side by side by clicking here.

On that note, I’ll stop and suggest scrolling down, staying safe, getting vaccinated if you haven’t already, and enjoying the rest of your Thursday.

I hope this email finds you well after the holiday weekend as fall, unofficially, begins. For all those celebrating Rosh Hashanah, may you have a happy, healthy, and sweet new year. 

First, if you need help dealing with Ida's impacts, such as removing flood water or filing a damage claim, please go to nyc.gov/ida, call 311 or stop by an Ida Recovery Service Center. The Brooklyn service center is on Sullivan Street (Red Hook) at PS 15 and is open until 8 PM. Also, now that President Biden has approved an expedited Major Disaster Declaration, you can apply for disaster assistance at www.disasterassistance.gov/ or call FEMA at (800) 621-3362.

Secondly, vaccination requirement enforcements begin less than a week from today for many activities, including indoor dining, movies, and gyms. For that reason, don’t miss out and get vaccinated ASAP. There are more items of interest, some that may require vaccination, below my signature, and I’d suggest checking them out.
