item.title: Thursday, September 2, 2021
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Last night our city set a new record for rainfall, and 12 of our fellow New Yorkers died due to Ida’s impact. Not that I don’t mean it every day, but I’d like to emphasize that I hope this email finds you well on a day like this.
item.content:encoded:
Last night our city set a new record for rainfall, and 12 of our fellow New Yorkers died due to Ida’s impact. Not that I don’t mean it every day, but I’d like to emphasize that I hope this email finds you well on a day like this.

Hopefully, you’re able to stay home and not travel as subways are limited and extremely delayed, while all non-emergency vehicles are advised to stay off of streets and highways to allow the cleanup to proceed.  This reinforces the need for increased resiliency, greener infrastructure,  and reduced reliance on fossil fuels and other generators of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere. Hopefully, we act as quickly as necessary I don’t enjoy living through concurrent and compounding crises, but maybe that’s just me

Of course, one of those other crises is Covid-19, and due to it, we postponed our September board meeting. However, thanks to the state's recent actions, we are allowed to meet virtually again. But that’s no reason not to get vaccinated, so please do so ASAP if you haven’t.

On that note, I’ll suggest you scroll down to check not just happenings but ways to report damage and other, unfortunately, necessary items after last night.

I hope this email finds you well on this 26th day of August that is Women's Equality Day. Of somewhat less significance, but very popular on social media, it’s also National Dog Day. We are, as is clear to anyone that’s been outside, experiencing extreme heat and a heat advisory remains in effect. 

I’ll be brief but want to remind folks of mosquito spraying that will be occurring later tonight from 8:30 PM until 6:00 AM tomorrow. Check here to find out more specific locations that will be sprayed to reduce exposures to the West Nile Virus. If weather doesn’t allow for the spraying it will be rescheduled for August 30th. While spraying is one way to reduce the risk of a virus, another way to reduce a different virus, specifically Covid-19, is for as many people as possible to get vaccinated ASAP.  

On that note, I won’t hold anyone up from getting vaccinated or checking out the events and information below my email signature. But no matter what you choose to do, stay cool, safe, and enjoy the rest of your Thursday.

item.content:encoded:
As you may already know, Tropical Storm Henri was “upgraded” to Hurricane Henri and was most recently “downgraded” back to being a tropical storm. Regardless of classification, there’s more than a “touch of grey” as this weather is a serious enough situation that the mayor, outgoing governor, and president, all declared a state of emergency.

Last night, a month's worth of rain and a previous rain record fell, with plenty of flooding also occurring. However, Henri is still forecast to intensify throughout the day. So, avoid traveling if you can, charge all your devices and read on below for more hurricane-related info. 

So please stay safe, “Know Your Zone” and I’ll be sure to keep you posted on any related changes.

item.title: Friday, August 20, 2021
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: There’s been a fair amount of media attention(as far as community boards go) concerning what meetings will look like in the fall. Unfortunately, with the expiration of emergency declarations the law lacks any room for adjustments, and so…
item.content:encoded:
There’s been a fair amount of media attention(as far as community boards go) concerning what meetings will look like in the fall. Unfortunately, with the expiration of emergency declarations the law lacks any room for adjustments, and so all meetings must be in person and cannot allow for virtual participation. 

Of course, just because the law is a certain way at the moment doesn’t mean it should or will remain that way or, even more importantly, that a virus would just adjust its plans accordingly. For those reasons, and others such as a lack of available spaces for meetings that would allow for social distancing, we signed on to a letter to the state legislature, with a majority of other Brooklyn Community boards asking for flexibility in such matters. 

I’ll keep everyone reading this updated if anything changes, but, again, as of now, our next meeting is entirely in person on Wednesday, September 8th at the Van Alen Institute and set to begin at 6:30 PM.

I’ll again remind folks of the importance of getting vaccinated against Covid-19 and where to find out more information.  On that note, I’ll recommend you to kick off the weekend by reading the items below, but no matter what, stay safe and be well!

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.description: The City announced that 75% of its adults have now received at least one Covid-19 vaccination shot. However, in a city of more than 8 million, that’s still many people unvaccinated.
item.content:encoded:
The City announced that 75% of its adults have now received at least one Covid-19 vaccination shot. However, in a city of more than 8 million, that’s still many people unvaccinated. Within those numbers is a range varying by neighborhood, income, race, and overall lack of equity.

For that reason, it’s still super important that everyone keep safety measures in place and get vaccinated ASAP and for the immunocompromised to get booster shots ASAP. Without more people being vaccinated, the pandemic will go longer, and folks won’t be able to go to bars, restaurants, concerts, and gyms. If you are concerned about the booster shots, click here, and you’ll find answers to many frequently asked questions about the booster shots. 

Anyway, there’s lots of stuff happening in our community, and much of it is listed by my signature, so I recommend checking it out. But, even if you don’t check it out, stay safe and enjoy the rest of your Thursday. 

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager

item.description: I hope this email finds you well on this 18th day of August, with a possible tornado spinning our way.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well on this 18th day of August, with a possible tornado spinning our way.

I’m glad to find at least four diligent readers among our subscribers. I say this because in the first newsletter I sent yesterday, I typed, regarding the vaccine mandate, that to “dine outdoors,” one would require one shot of a Covid-19 vaccination. What I meant to type was that folks need at least one shot to “dine indoors.”

Receiving one shot of a Covid-19 vaccine is required for many activities across our city. I, for one, was glad to be asked to prove my vaccination status last night at one of the many fine establishments on Smith Street. Keeping with the theme of vaccination, immunocompromised folks can receive a 3rd, aka “booster,” shot now. By clicking here, you'll find answers to many frequently asked questions about the booster shots. For those who aren’t immunocompromised, please note that the FDA will likely approve receiving a booster shot for everyone, and The city is expected to start offering those shots as soon as September.

Anyway, there’s lots of stuff happening in our community, and much of it is listed by my signature, so I recommend checking it out. But, even if you don’t check it out, stay safe and enjoy the rest of your Wednesday.

Best,

item.content:encoded:
The Mayor's executive order means that to dine indoors, go to a gym, movie theater, or museum, you’ll have to get at least one shot. Today, it’s a “soft” mandate as enforcement will begin on September 13th. But, regardless of enforcement, it would be safer for you, me, and everyone to be vaccinated. So figure out where and when to get vaccinated by going to vax4nyc.gov or calling 877-VAX-4NYC asap. 

There’s a lot of stuff happening listed below my email signature, like the Old Stone House’s “Battle Week,” so I’ll stop and let you get to reading it(or not).

Either way, stay safe and enjoy the rest of your Tuesday. Lastly, thank you to the dedicated readers, including a prominent blogger, that caught my mistake of writing"outdoors," where I mean to write "indoors" in my earlier email.

item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well as we begin the workweek. I’ll begin with one of the two most popular newsletter topics, COVID-19 vaccinations.

As always, I’ll remind everyone that it’s a great idea to get vaccinated ASAP. However, there is more incentive because, as of tomorrow, Tuesday, August 17th, the unvaccinated are excluded from partaking in much of what this community, and this city of ours, has to offer. Beginning tomorrow, proof of vaccination grants you access to indoor dining, fitness clubs, and shows at indoor entertainment venues, including nightclubs, concert halls, and movie theaters. Tools to prove your vaccinated status include your paper immunization card, the state’s Excelsior Pass app, or the city’s NYC COVID SAFE app. The way to get vaccinated or start the process is by going to vax4nyc.gov or calling 877-VAX-4NYC.

The other most popular topic for this newsletter, the Gowanus Rezoning, widened its coverage due to an article appearing in the NY Times this weekend, and you can read about it here and among the items of interest listed below.

I’ll stop now and recommend you peruse those items, but no matter what, stay safe and enjoy the rest of your Monday.

item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well on this very hot Friday, the 13th. Hopefully, Saturday the 14th and other upcoming days will be less hot than it currently is and has been. Due to that heat, I’ve been using my air conditioner, but note that cooling centers remain open.

However, I did face the heat directly at the Gowanus Houses earlier today to stand with Borough President Adams, Councilman Lander, Gowanus Tenant Association President Ed Tyree, and the Gowanus Neighborhood Coalition for Justice(GNCJ). The purpose of this was Borough President Adams’s announcement of conditional support for the Gowanus Rezoning. The conditions are strong and similar to our own, especially NYCHA, and can be read here.

As the board has made clear for years, these conditions were and remained deal-breakers. So it’s encouraging to see that there is a shared commitment to them in addition to our advisory voice in what is likely to be the incoming Mayoral administration. That commitment includes both the Borough President and Councilmember Lander, who made it clear that our conditions are his conditions as well.

Anyway, I’ll stop here, remind you to get vaccinated against COVID-19 ASAP, check out the items below my signature, stay safe, and have a great weekend!

item.title: Monday, August 9, 2021
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I’ll start by urging everyone to get vaccinated against Covid-19 ASAP. As noted yesterday, today is the last day for public school students between the ages of 12 and 17 to be fully vaccinated in time for the first day of school.
item.content:encoded:
I’ll start by urging everyone to get vaccinated against Covid-19 ASAP.  As noted yesterday, today is the last day for public school students between the ages of 12 and 17 to be fully vaccinated in time for the first day of school. 

Moving to a topic, I haven’t brought it up as much lately, the Gowanus rezoning.  Regular readers and dedicated CB6 followers will recall we voted to conditionally approve the rezoning back in June. 

In our board discussions, public statements, communications to the city, and final vote to conditionally approve the Gowanus rezoning, we made clear that we wanted a racial impact study.  The purpose of the study is to make sure the Rezoning would increase neighborhood diversity, and we are glad to see that one has now been done. The study shows Gowanus would become MORE diverse after the rezoning.  

The studies findings reinforce why, as part of those conditions, we also asked that when it came to the policy of “Community preference” for affordable housing, we demanded that particular preference be given to residents of public housing and considering the demographics of our district (157K Median Household Income) contrasted with neighboring districts that the preference is expanded to include residents of Community District 7, 8 and 9 in addition to 2 and 6.   

You can read the study here, as well as about the study here.

On that note, I’ll urge you to read below my signature, as well as the Racial Impact Study; stay safe and enjoy the rest of your Monday.

item.title: Immunity in time
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I make it a habit not to send out newsletter updates on weekends. However, with school starting soon and the Delta variant spreading, vaccination against Covid-19 is as important as ever.
item.content:encoded:
I make it a habit not to send out newsletter updates on weekends. However, with school starting soon and the Delta variant spreading, vaccination against Covid-19 is as important as ever. There is another deadline looming. For students between the ages of 12 and 17 to be fully vaccinated by the first day of public school, September 13th, they’d have to get their first dose by tomorrow, Monday, August 9th.

All this means is that public school students must receive their first shot today or tomorrow for full immunity to be reached on the first day of school, September 13th. Of course, this doesn’t make them ineligible to go to school or anything of that sort, but it makes them safer.

On that note, enjoy the rest of your weekend and click here to find out where to get vaccinated and receive 100 bucks.

item.description: On the 16th day of August, New York City will become, as some argue it should have already been, the first U.S. city to require proof of at least one dose of a Covid-19 vaccine for various activities.
item.content:encoded:
On the 16th day of August, New York City will become, as some argue it should have already been, the first U.S. city to require proof of at least one dose of a  Covid-19 vaccine for various activities. This will apply to employees and patrons and include indoor dining, gyms, and performances. While the start date is August 16th, that will begin a transition period, and enforcement will begin September 13th.

Hopefully, this is enough incentive, along with 100 dollars, to get those who remain unvaccinated to change that status so we can be in a post-pandemic place

As noted last week, one way to confirm you vaccination status is to hold onto your vaccination card; another is to download the New York State Excelsior Pass. Now the city has an app to verify your COVID-19 vaccination status and test results and it can be download it for Apple and Droid.

Before my usual recommendation of scrolling past my signature, I’ll remind you that tonight is National Night Out Against Crime. In our district, the 78th precinct will host their event at Grand Army Plaza from 6 until 8 pm, while the 76th will be in Red Hook’s Coffey Park from 4 pm until 7 pm.

With that, I’ll stop; I hope you stay safe and cool while enjoying the rest of your Tuesday.

item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well as August begins, a month that Sylvia Plath referred to as the “odd uneven time.” I’d argue that the past 18 months have all fit this bill of odd unevenness, but I digress to bring you some reminders, happenings, and Items of interest. 

Firstly, a reminder to get vaccinated against COVID-19 ASAP. This has always been important, but with the Delta Variant spreading with the ease of chickenpox, the best thing one can do is get paid 100 dollars and get vaccinated ASAP. 

If you don’t, it’s less likely that our next Full Board meeting will be in person. For those who like to mark their calendars, it’s currently scheduled for Wednesday, September 8th, at the Van Alen Institute, which is located at 303 Bond Street between Union and Sackett. We will, of course, share any changes to that, but, as of this writing, the open meeting law is not suspended, and we’re required to meet in person.

Before that, there’s certainly a lot happening, all at a safe distance and predominantly outdoors, such as the 76th & 78th Precinct’s National Night out Against Crime, Art Gowanus Open Studios registration, drawing classes, and Jam Sessions. 

Those items, and more, are listed past my signature, so I’d recommend checking them out. So stay safe and cool while enjoying the rest of your Monday.

item.description: It was weeks and days of anticipation leading up to it, but last night we had our joint CB6 & CB7 last mile warehouse meeting. Again, there was excellent attendance from the leadership of both boards, elected officials, government…
item.content:encoded:
It was weeks and days of anticipation leading up to it, but last night we had our joint CB6 & CB7 last mile warehouse meeting. Again, there was excellent attendance from the leadership of both boards, elected officials, government agencies, and the community. Hopefully, this is a tangible step forward in getting the City to do more than what they did last night, which was listen. 

Not that listening is bad; in fact, you can listen to and watch the entire meeting here on YouTube. But we, and others in our community, have highlighted this issue and repeatedly asked for truck route changes and a traffic study; it’s certainly frustrating to hear that the city is still just listening. However, suppose the community continues to work together on this. In that case, it could lead the City to make up for lost time and [tackle the land-use challenges inherent in the widespread and unchecked growth of last-mile facilities,] change traffic patterns and street uses, to better adapt to the world we live in.

Speaking of the world we live in, it’s still very much in a Covid-19 pandemic, especially for the unvaccinated, but the delta variant can even breakthrough, albeit in milder forms. So, if you’re among those unvaccinated, please click here and figure out where to change that and protect yourselves and your children as far as when the answer is NOW.

On that note, I’ll wrap up, suggest scrolling past my signature, and hope you have a great weekend.

item.content:encoded:
First, congratulations to our Brooklyn Borough President Eric Adams and Councilmember Brad Lander on their primary victories and, so near certainty, of becoming our City’s next Mayor and Comptroller, respectively. 

While it wasn’t reported on the front page of the New York Times, our Executive Committee, during our Full Board hiatus, met last night. ULURP’s to allow for the construction of EPA-mandated CSO tanks, rezoning of 506 and 530 Third Avenue, text amendments for the easier establishment of Fitness Centers, and expanding the Fresh Program were approved. At the same time, the committee voted to disapprove a Hotel Special Permit text amendment. Along with those land-use items, a new liquor license for 1114 8th Avenue was approved, and the committee made a motion to support legislation making ‘to-go” cocktails permanently legal.

I’ll end here and suggest you stay cool, read on below, get vaccinated, and enjoy the rest of your Wednesday.

item.title: Wednesday, June 23, 2021
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Last night was our June full general board meeting. We approved everything on the agenda and heard from elected officials, their representatives, as well as members of our community.
item.content:encoded:
Last night was our June full general board meeting. We approved everything on the agenda and heard from elected officials, their representatives, as well as members of our community. 

As far as approvals, we first reviewed 3 liquor license applications followed by two landmark applications. After that, we went into the much anticipated “main event,” the Gowanus Rezoning. Following the conditional approval at last week's land use committee meeting, the full board voted by a margin of 26 votes in favor and 6 opposed, with 2 abstaining to approve the Rezoning. I admire our board members for thoughtfully crafting the nearly 14 pages of insightful community-enhancing conditions that our councilman stated would serve as a road map as the process moves forward.

Some highlights of the conditions are fully-funded NYCHA capital improvement, EPA review of all environmental issues, community oversight, and expansion of the Industrial Business Zone.  You can read about it in Bklyner, Patch, and The Brooklyn Paper. Now it’s off to the Borough President for a June 30th hearing and further comment.

Tonight, Thursday, June 24, we’ve got more Gowanus on the docket at another Landmarks/Land Use meeting with two ULURP items on the agenda. One is for the demapping for a Gowanus CSO tank and the other to rezone a part of an M2-1 district to a C4-4A district along Third Avenue between 12th and 13th Streets.

Lastly, if you haven’t already, get vaccinated against Covid-19 ASAP; enjoy the day!

item.content:encoded:
We are continuing to make vaccination progress as marked by a fireworks display last night.  However, if you haven’t yet been vaccinated, please do so ASAP.  Vermont is beating us by 10%. We can't let Senator Sander's adopted state do better than his birthplace.

I’ll be brief, as tonight, Wednesday, June 16th, the theme is of schools and Red Hook. What I mean is that the Red Hook Initiative will host a meeting about last-mile warehouses while our Youth Services and Education Committee will hear from Superintendent Anita Skop about the elementary school rezoning, which the CEC voted to approve last night. 

One week from tonight, we have our full board meeting and vote on the Gowanus Rezoning. However, sooner than that, tomorrow night at 6:30 PM, our Landmarks/ Land Use committee will hear from DCP and vote on the rezoning. After that, whatever the committee ends up saying will be passed on to the full board for a final resolution and vote at our June 23rd meeting. The process then moves on to the Borough President for his recommendation(s) on June 30th.   Once again, here is the draft resolution that the committee is currently circulating. Also, another refresher, click here for all the previous presentations we’ve been given and statements we’ve made on the rezoning. 

On that note, I’ll finish by recommending reading past my signature or clicking here to check out the coverage of demands for fully funding NYCHA capital improvements. However, no matter what you choose, enjoy the rest of your day.

item.title: Tuesday, June 15, 2021
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: The busy work week I referred to yesterday carries on as we inch closer to a post-pandemic world. The state has ended most remaining COVID-19 restrictions on capacity, social distancing, and more.
item.content:encoded:
The busy work week I referred to yesterday carries on as we inch closer to a post-pandemic world. The state has ended most remaining COVID-19 restrictions on capacity, social distancing, and more. However, not everyone is vaccinated against COVID-19, so if you haven’t yet been vaccinated, click here and change that ASAP. 

Tonight, while they are not CB6 meetings, the City’s Parks Department & EPA will hold an update on the Red Hook Ball Fields, and the  Community Education Council(CEC) will vote on District 15 Elementary school rezoning plans. 

Tomorrow, Wednesday, June 16th, we’ll stick with the themes of schools and Red Hook. What I mean is that the Red Hook Initiative will host a meeting about last-mile warehouses while our Youth Services and Education Committee will hear from Superintendent Anita Skop about the elementary school rezoning. 

The following day, Thursday, June 17th, another form of rezoning will be the focus, and that’s of the land use variety and the Gowanus Rezoning. Again, we’ll hear from DCP, and the Land Use committee will then vote on the rezoning. After that, whatever the committee ends up saying will be passed on to the full board for a final resolution and vote at our June 23rd meeting. The process then moves on to the Borough President for his recommendation(s). Once again, here is the draft resolution that the committee is currently circulating. Also, another refresher, click here for all the previous presentations we’ve been given and statements we’ve made on the rezoning. 

In those previous statements and the currently circulating resolution, you’ll notice an emphasis on the need for NYCHA capital funding. I mention that not just because it’s inherently important but because today I was able to join, in person at the Gowanus Community Center, NYCHA tenant leaders, GNCJ, Councilmembers Lander & Levin in emphasizing the importance of this funding and reaffirming that NYCHA residents shouldn’t have to settle for subpar living conditions under any circumstances. 

On that note, I’ll finish up by recommending reading past my signature and, no matter what you choose to do, enjoying the rest of your day.

Looking beyond the weekend, we’ll hold three committee meetings next week. Both will be held over zoom and get started at 6:30 PM. 

Our 3rd meeting of the week on Thursday, June 17th, over Zoom, beginning at 6:30 PM, is our Landmarks/Land Use Committee meeting which will feature a vote on the Gowanus Rezoning. After that, whatever the committee says will be passed to the full board for a final resolution and vote at our June 23rd Full Board meeting. The process then moves on to the Borough President for his recommendation(s).

There’s more going on in the coming days, such as a Red Hook Initiative-led discussion regarding last-mile warehouses, details of which you can check out below my signature. item.title: Thursday, June 10, 2021
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: First, get vaccinated against COVID-19 asap. For yourself, others, and a normal that may seem a lot better than it was.
item.content:encoded:
First, get vaccinated against COVID-19 asap. For yourself, others, and a normal that may seem a lot better than it was. 

I’m not going to stop reminding folks to get vaccinated against COVID-19 ASAP, but I will pass along that we’ve reached “functional” immunity against the virus amongst our population. That’s, of course, welcome news, but until we reach true “herd immunity,” we’ll keep losing the lives of fellow New Yorkers.

The sun’s out later, and later, it makes sense that people want to stay outside with more daylight. Nonetheless, I feel obligate to loop folks in on some civic stuff that won’t be outdoors. For example, the NYC Campaign Finance Board's first Comptroller debate is tonight, while mayoral candidates will debate for the 2nd time in person. Not sure why both debates start at seven, but either way, it’s good to know as much as possible as early voting begins this Saturday and will go on until Tuesday, June 22nd. If you still want to vote by mail, request a ballot by this Tuesday, June 15th. 

On voting, of the nonelectoral kind, note that a week from today, on Thursday, June 17th, over Zoom, and beginning at 6:30 PM, our Landmarks/Land Use Committee will meet and vote on the Gowanus Rezoning. After that, whatever the committee says will be passed to the full board for a final resolution and vote at our June 23rd meeting. The process then moves on to the Borough President for his recommendation(s).

There’s more going on soon, including CB6 meetings and Canal Crawls, that you should check out below. But regardless of whether you check do or don't check it out, stay safe and enjoy the rest of your day.

item.content:encoded:
I hope this message finds you well overly sunny 9th day of June. In this heat, considering the sun and hear, I’ll be especially brief.

First, get vaccinated against COVID-19 asap. For yourself, others, and a normal that may seem a lot better than it was. 

Second, if you’re interested in the potential D15 school rezoning, check out tonight’s CEC meeting, or if you’re unsure about Ranked Choice Voting, check out tonight’s Southwest Brooklyn Tenant’s Union RCV workshop. You can start ranking candidates as soon as this Saturday, June 12th, so it’s good to know what RCV is, if you don’t already, ASAP. 

Our community is always busy, so these aren’t the only things happening in the near future. For example, tomorrow, there’s an Open Street Book Day in Red Hook and plenty more you can read about below my signature. 

Whether you check out the happening above or below, stay safe, get vaccinated, and enjoy the rest of your day!

item.title: Tuesday, June 8, 2021
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: As we strive to move past the Covid-19 pandemic, people are still dying from the virus, so we’re not past it yet. Reports indicate the B.1.617.2 (Delta) variant is a threat to reopening around the world.
item.content:encoded:
As we strive to move past the Covid-19 pandemic, people are still dying from the virus, so we’re not past it yet. Reports indicate the B.1.617.2 (Delta) variant is a threat to reopening around the world. Being vaccinated is the best defense, so do so for free without even needing an appointment ASAP. 

Shifting to city civics, don’t forget early voting for the next city government (Mayor, Comptroller, City Council) begins this Saturday, June 12th, with the “election day” finale coming on Tuesday, June 22nd. If neither alternative suits your voting needs, you can request an absentee ballot until June 15th, and if you have questions about the Ranked Choice Voting (RCV) System check out tomorrow’s Southwest Brooklyn Tenant’s Union RCV workshop.

Aside from our meetings, there’s more happening that you can check out by scrolling down below. However, before you do that, I’d recommend checking out some coverage of the Monadnock ULURP that we approved back in December.

But no matter what you choose to do, stay safe, get vaccinated, and enjoy the rest of your day!

item.content:encoded:
Covid-19 numbers keep sliding in the right direction as we’re down to numbers not seen since the earliest stages of the pandemic. However, those stats don’t mean the pandemic is over, and small numbers still represent real people and thus, it’s really important to get vaccinated ASAP.

Shifting to the CB6 sphere of influence, thank you to everyone who submitted testimony for the Gowanus Rezoning. That testimony will be used to inform the Land Use Committee as they vote next Thursday, June 17th, and for the Full Board when it votes on June 23. After that, the ULURP calendar flips over to the Borough President’s review, where his office will also hold a hearing before issuing recommendations.

However, before that, we’ve got some other non-Gowanus-related meetings. A week from today, Monday, June 14th, our Economic, Waterfront, Community Development, and Housing Committee (EWCDH) will meet. The agenda will focus on last-mile warehouses in Red Hook. Also, next week, on Wednesday, June 16th, our Youth Human Services and Education Committee will hear from district 15 Superintendent Anita Skop on the proposed elementary school rezonings. 

Of course, community activity doesn’t start and stop solely with CB6 meetings, so I’d recommend checking out the listings, and other items, below my signature.

Lastly, stay safe, get vaccinated, and enjoy the rest of your day!

item.title: Friday, June 4, 2021
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Yesterday we held a public hearing on the Gowanus rezoning. It was 6 hours long, and over 150 people testified over Zoom and from Washington Park.
item.content:encoded:
Yesterday we held a public hearing on the Gowanus rezoning. It was 6 hours long, and over 150 people testified over Zoom and from Washington Park. They expressed a wide variety of views on the current plan. Those views ran the gamut from unequivocal support to total opposition and everything in between. In contrast, reviews for Land Use Chair Alec Schierenbeck were overwhelmingly positive. His calmness throughout the 6 hours even led to one CB6 member's tweet that sainthood may be in his future. It certainly showed why he’s already Deputy Solicitor General of a state, a Clerk to United States Supreme Court Justice Breyer, and published in the New York Times. 

Regardless of a resume or canonization, this is about the community, and you can watch all the testimony here on YouTube as well as coverage in The Brooklyn Paper, City Limits, and Crain’s.  

Many of those that testified at the hearing also emailed a written statement. So if you’d like to submit testimony, please do so ASAP and certain before Monday by emailing me. I ask for it ASAP as I’m compiling what I receive to share with our Land Use Committee, so when we make a recommendation on Thursday, June 17th, and vote at the full board on June 23rd, it can be done with as much information as possible. 

We, and the community writ large, have been busy, and things show no signs of slowing down, so read on below for more information on such happenings. Lastly, if you haven’t already, get vaccinated against Covid-19 ASAP; enjoy the weekend!

On that note, unlike Dylan on Maggie’s Farm, I’m NOT going to pray for rain.

item.title: Tuesday, June 1, 2021
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: The Covid numbers of our community and city are as low as they’ve been since we've been tracking such numbers. We’re not done yet, and if you’re not vaccinated, please click here and find out how to change that.
item.content:encoded:
The Covid numbers of our community and city are as low as they’ve been since we've been tracking such numbers. We’re not done yet, and if you’re not vaccinated, please click here and find out how to change that. Please remember that the vaccination is truly free and not one of those awful instances of surprise medical billing. 

I’ll digress and shift to CB6 specifics. While it may be unofficially summer, we’re not in any way on summer hiatus this month. We’ve got multiple Gowanus Rezoning meetings coming up.

The first of those is this coming Thursday, June 3rd. . The hearing will start at 3:30 PM, and people will be able to participate over zoom and in person at Washington Park. For details on how to submit testimony and register, click here. This hearing also has a rain date for the following Thursday, June 10th. Before listing the other meetings, I’d like to thank everyone who has continued to spread the word about Thursday’s meeting.

Second, to limit the amount of possible rescheduling and force us to hold a late Friday meeting, the Landmarks/ Land Use Committee will meet on Thursday, June 17th. At the June 17th meeting, it is expected that a motion will be made to approve or disapprove, with various conditions, the Gowanus Rezoning.

The third meeting will be our June 23rd Full Board meeting. During the June 23rd meeting, the anticipated motion from the Land Use Committee will be considered by members, followed by their vote.

Fourth, the day after the June Full Board meeting, on Thursday, June 24th, we'll hold another Landmarks/Land Use meeting with, at this point, at least two ULURP items. One for the Gowanus CSO tank/ salt lot demapping and another an M2-1 to C4-4A along Third Avenue between 12th and 13th Streets.

On that note, I’ll recommend reading on, staying safe, and enjoy the rest of the day and month!

item.title: Friday, May 28, 2021
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this message finds you well as we head into Memorial Day Weekend and the unofficial start of summer.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this message finds you well as we head into Memorial Day Weekend and the unofficial start of summer.

It seems like there is more and more hope that this summer will be closer to “normal” than last year as the covid infection rate is down to the lowest level (0.93%) of the pandemic. As greater numbers of people are vaccinated, the more likely we'll be permanently able to keep that rate down so, if you haven’t already, click here and find out how to get vaccinated ASAP. 

As mentioned in previous newsletters, last night we had our Landmarks/Land Use meeting, and it was a late one lasting around three and a half hours. After a brief time taken to approve two landmarking items, DCP gave an informational presentation on the proposed Gowanus Rezoning. If you were “there” on zoom, or if you want to rewatch, you can do so here on Youtube and see the presentation here. 

But of course, we’re not done with Gowanus, and we’ve got 4 Gowanus Rezoning/Rezoning Adjacent meetings coming up. I’ll run those down before wishing everyone well for the weekend.

First, as officially announced earlier this week, Thursday, June 3rd, is our joint public hearing with Brooklyn Community Board 2. The hearing will start at 3:30 PM, and people will be able to participate over zoom and in person at Washington Park. For details on how to submit testimony and register, click here. This hearing also has a rain date for the following Thursday, June 10th.

Second, to limit the amount of possible rescheduling and force us to hold a late Friday meeting, the Landmarks/ Land Use Committee will meet on Thursday, June 17th. At the June 17th meeting, it is expected that a motion will be made to approve or disapprove, with various conditions, the Gowanus Rezoning.

The third meeting will be our June 23rd Full Board meeting. During the June 23rd meeting, the anticipated motion from the Land Use Committee will be voted on by the entire board.

Fourth, the day after the June Full Board meeting, on Thursday, June 24th, we'll hold another Landmarks/Land Use meeting with, at this point, at least two ULURP items. One for the Gowanus CSO tank/ salt lot demapping and another for a rezoning of an M2-1 to C4-4A along Third Avenue between 12th and 13th Streets.

On that note, I’ll recommend reading on, staying safe, and having a great Memorial Day Weekend!

item.content:encoded:

On that note, I’ll recommend reading on; remind you that this Friday, May 28th, is the deadline to register to vote, stay safe, and enjoy your evening!

item.title: Tuesday, May 25, 2021
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Disregarding any annoyance that repeating this may cause, Covid numbers continue to look better, but we’re not done with the pandemic yet. Still, we are inching closer every time someone gets vaccinated.
item.content:encoded:
Disregarding any annoyance that repeating this may cause, Covid numbers continue to look better, but we’re not done with the pandemic yet. Still, we are inching closer every time someone gets vaccinated. So, if you haven’t yet,  click here to change that ASAP.

Moving to things not directly related to Covid-19. Last night, our Permits & Licenses Committee met and approved 3 Liquor Licence applications. If you want to relive the meeting or see it for the first time, watch it here on youtube. The next CB6 committee meeting will be on Thursday when our Landmarks/Land Use Committee meets over Zoom at 6:30 PM. Don’t forget that this meeting will include an informational presentation from the Department of City Planning on the Gowanus Rezoning. 

If you crave Gowanus and rezoning-related content, you won’t have to wait until Thursday. In fact, at 6:30 PM, the Gowanus CAG will have its virtual May meeting. You may be interested in the letter sent to the EPA by many of our elected officials, including Councilmembers Lander & Levin, asking the EPA to evaluate the City’s Environmental Impact Statement regarding whether or not the rezoning would impair the canal remediation.  As noted, we’ve asked that the water quality standards for the canal be raised as recently as December 2019. The discussion of Gowanus-related matters can go on for quite some time, so  I’ll stop here and remind you of next Thursday’s public hearing and click here for other CB6 rezoning adjacent meetings in the coming weeks. 

On that note, I’ll stop, recommend reading on for more information, and hope that you enjoy the rest of your Tuesday.

item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Covid numbers continue to look better but don’t forget millions of New Yorkers are yet to be vaccinated against Covid-19. If you’re not vaccinated, click here to change that ASAP.
item.content:encoded:
Covid numbers continue to look better but don’t forget millions of New Yorkers are yet to be vaccinated against Covid-19. If you’re not vaccinated, click here to change that ASAP.

Before focusing on the week ahead, I’ll mention the great turnout last night at the Old Stone House for the candidate forum we co-sponsored. Thanks to everyone who helped make it happen. Those thanks extend especially to Park Slope Civic Council Trustee Timothy Giles, Old Stone House Executive Director Kim Maier, and the moderators, Sadef Kully and Ben Verde.  

Looking to the near future and CB6 meetings, tonight at 6:30, our Permits & Licenses Committee meets to review three liquor license applications over zoom. On Thursday, May 27th, our Landmarks/ Land Use Committee Meets at 6:30 PM to review 3 Landmark items and host an informational presentation from DCP regarding the pending rezoning of Gowanus. 

Speaking of the proposed Gowanus Rezoning, as mentioned in previous newsletters, CB6 is holding a joint public hearing with Brooklyn Community Board 2 next Thursday, June 3rd. The hearing will allow for both in-person testimony at Washington Park and remote testimony via zoom. To accommodate the great level of interest, the hearing will begin earlier than our usual meeting time. The hearing starts at 3:30 PM, and it is expected to go later than usual. For information on this, please see the hearing notice. 

On that note, I’ll stop, recommend reading on for more information, note that there will not be a remote option for school this fall, and stay safe.

item.title: Thursday, May 20, 2021
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I’m happy to report that Covid-19 numbers are still looking as good as they have in months. However, while we’ve got millions vaccinated, there are still millions of our fellow New Yorkers who have not been vaccinated yet.
item.content:encoded:
I’m happy to report that Covid-19 numbers are still looking as good as they have in months. However, while we’ve got millions vaccinated, there are still millions of our fellow New Yorkers who have not been vaccinated yet. So we’ve got to be safe as I don't think anyone wants to go back to lockdowns and more deaths than we can bear. If you’re among the millions yet to receive a vaccine, you can get one ASAP, but if you still have questions, read up on some of the facts. 

Moving to the CB6 universe last night, as previewed, we had our second CB6 meeting of the week with our Parks Committee meeting via zoom. The focus was a follow-up with the City’s Parks Department following the district-wide parks tours Committee Chair Glenn Kelly led earlier this month. If you missed the meeting or want to relive it, you can watch it here on Youtube. 

Suppose 2 CB6 meetings in a week is part of what makes a week great. If so, you’re in luck because we’ve got two meetings next week too. On Monday, May 24th, Permits & Licences meets while Landmarks/ Land Use meets on Thursday, May 27th. Both will take place over zoom and begin at 630 PM. 

However, before either of those meetings, on Sunday, May 23rd, from 5 until 630 PM, at the Old Stone House, we’re co-sponsoring a 39th Council District Forum. 

I’d recommend checking out all of those, as well as reading below my signature but most importantly, stay safe and enjoy the rest of your Thursday.

item.title: Wednesday, May 19, 2021
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: As of today, most venues can reopen at full capacity, as the universal indoor mask mandate has been lifted. Covid-19 stats are looking better than they have in months, but caution is still necessary.
item.content:encoded:
As of today, most venues can reopen at full capacity, as the universal indoor mask mandate has been lifted. Covid-19 stats are looking better than they have in months, but caution is still necessary. People across our city are still dying of Covid-19 every day, and too many people are yet to be vaccinated. So, if you’re eager to return to a pre-pandemic level of caution or want to be safer, get vaccinated ASAP. 

Tonight, Wednesday, May 19th, at 6:30 PM, our Parks Committee meets over zoom. Representatives from the Parks Department will be there to discuss the state of parks in our community. If that interests you, register here.

There’s other stuff happening between now and the weekend, but I’d like to draw your attention to some civics this Saturday and Sunday. On Saturday, May 22nd, the Red Hook Initiative hosts a candidate forum for the 38th council district in Coffey Park. While on Sunday, May 23rd, from 5 until 630 PM, at the Old Stone House, we’re co-sponsoring a 39th Council District Forum. The forum will be moderated by two excellent CB6 based journalists, Sadef Kully and Ben Verde, so RSVP ASAP. If you read that and, like most people, haven’t memorized which council district is which, use this handy search engine to find your district.

With that, I’ll make my regularly scheduled recommendation to read past my signature, stay safe, and enjoy the rest of your Wednesday.

If you’d like to combine these three things, and you’re not vaccinated, I’d recommend riding the subway to one of these stations and getting vaccinated. 

Shifting to the CB6 sphere of influence, we have two committee meetings this week. The first is tonight, Monday, May 17th, at 6:30 PM, when our Economic, Waterfront, Community Development, & Housing Committee(EWCDH) meets over zoom. Speaking of the EWCDH committee, one of its committee/ CB6 members and small business owner, Natasha Amott, recently had a piece published on the issue of retail and commercial rents that's certainly worth reading. 

The second CB6 committee to meet this week will be our Parks Committee. That meeting will be held over zoom on Wednesday, May 19th, and begin at 630 PM. You can register for these meetings by clicking blue text, or you can find out more, about these and other meetings, at linktr.ee/BKCB6.

item.content:encoded:
I’m sure most people reading this have already heard about the CDC guidance on the mask from a source with a wider reach than this newsletter. For those who haven't, it boils down to this - fully vaccinated people don't need to wear face coverings except in certain settings. Among those settings here in NYC are subways and buses. No matter how you cut it, that makes a great argument for getting vaccinated against COVID-19 ASAP. Our city, and community, stats are looking good, and they’ll look even better as more people are vaccinated. 

Looking toward the weekend mentioned in the first sentence, we’ve got a lot going on. Tomorrow, Saturday, May 15th, Arts Gowanus kicks off an outdoor art market at the Old Stone House, the Dredgers host a dance party, and the Brooklyn Conservatory of Music will have 20 stages of free music across Park Slope. There’s more happening and info than I could expect anyone to tolerate in a newsletter intro/musing happening across our community, so check out the calendars for the Old Stone House, Gowanus Dredgers and, the Brooklyn Public Library , Prospect Park, and Brooklyn Conservatory of Music.

Looking past the weekend, our EWCDH committee meets on Monday, May 17th and our Parks committee will meet on Wednesday, May 19th. Both of these meetings will take place over zoom and begin at 6:30 PM. 

Briefly looking back, for those who missed it or want a refresher on Wednesday’s board meeting, you can watch it all here on Youtube. As far as news, aside from CB6 resident, Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer, having stopped by, discussed the latest court order for the Gowanus Rezoning ULURP. In practical terms, that means we are now scheduled to hold a public hearing, in partnership with Brooklyn Community Board 2, on June 3rd, and it's to feature both in-person and outdoor options for testifying at a public hearing. There will also be a rain date scheduled for the following Thursday, June 10th. Further specifics and logistics are being worked out for this, and as they are finalized, I’ll readily share them. The goal, of course, is to have everyone who wants to participate get a chance to do so. To make this happen, we had to move our June board meeting to the 4th Wednesday of the month, June 23rd. 

They’ll be more about next week, next week. On that note, I’ll recommend reading past my signature, staying safe, and having a great weekend!

item.title: Thursday, May 13, 2021
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope my email finds you well on this sunny Thursday. It was good to “see” and hear from folks at last night's board meeting.
item.content:encoded:
I hope my email finds you well on this sunny Thursday. It was good to “see” and hear from folks at last night's board meeting. To all those celebrating, have a very happy Eid.

Before a brief recap of last night’s meeting, I'm pleased to repeat that our COVID-19 statistics continue to move in the right direction. Let’s keep it that way by, if you haven’t already, getting vaccinated ASAP. Vaccine eligibility now includes those from twelve to fifteen years old.

Now back to last night. We had a brief voting agenda which consisted of 3 liquor licenses that were all approved unanimously. Our chair, Peter Fleming, discussed some updates surrounding the public review process of the Gowanus Rezoning. First, the judge, who had “paused” the ULURP clock and put the Temporary Restraining Order in place, issued a further order lifting it. 

In practical terms, that means we are now scheduled to hold a public hearing, in partnership with Brooklyn Community Board 2, on June 3rd to feature both in-person and outdoor options for testifying at a public hearing. There will also be a rain date scheduled for the following Thursday, June 10th. Further specifics and logistics are being worked out for this, and as they are finalized, I’ll readily share them. The goal, of course, is that everyone who wants to participate will be able to do so. To make this happen, we had to move our June board meeting to the 3rd Wednesday of the month, June 23rd. 

In terms of other meetings in which aspects of the Gowanus Rezoning are likely to be discussed, our EWCDH committee meets on Monday, May 17th, and our Landmarks/Land Use committee meets on Thursday, May 27th. In between those two meetings, our Parks committee will meet next Wednesday, May 19th. All 3 of these meetings will take place over zoom and begin at 6:30 PM. 

You may have also heard that our meeting featured a CB6 resident and Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer visit. He gave updates on various things that have happened and are happening at the federal level. Senator Schumer showed off his state of the art flip phone, discussed the filibuster, unveiled his firm grasp of Brooklyn vernacular by using another word that starts with the letter “F,” and was the first CB6 attendee to have been impersonated on Saturday Night Live. All joking aside, thank you to Senator Schumer for joining our meeting and spending so much time. If that recap doesn’t do the trick, you can relive all the magic mentioned here on Youtube. 

On that note, I’ll suggest you keep reading past my signature, stay safe and enjoy the rest of your Thursday.

item.title: Tuesday, May 4, 2021
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well this Tuesday, the 4th day of May. I can’t feign interest in Star Wars, so this isn’t the place for puns about “the force” being with us.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well this Tuesday, the 4th day of May. I can’t feign interest in Star Wars, so this isn’t the place for puns about “the force” being with us. After all, we’re an advisory body.

I’ll briefly reiterate how easy it is and important it's is to get vaccinated ASAP as herd immunity remains doubtful. Hopefully, as Congresswoman Velasquez has noted, this should serve as a rallying cry to motivate everyone to get vaccinated so we can get to be a post-pandemic city. 

I’ll also suggest reading the Gowanus Rezoning DEIS. It’s not just a rehash for the sake of it but because, as articles like this highlight, there’s new information to be evaluated. 

On that note, I recommend reading on to remind yourself of just how active our community is and that our May Full Board meeting is a week from tomorrow. But no matter what, stay safe and enjoy the rest of your Tuesday.

item.description: Earlier today, Governor Cuomo announced that beginning on May 19th, most capacity restrictions will be lifted for most brick and mortar businesses. Without his usual dissimulation of not controlling it, the Governor announced the subway…
item.content:encoded:
Earlier today, Governor Cuomo announced that beginning on May 19th, most capacity restrictions will be lifted for most brick and mortar businesses. Without his usual dissimulation of not controlling it, the Governor announced the subway would resume 24/7 service. It can’t be proven, but it suits my conceit to tell myself this resumption is due to the letter we wrote back in January, as COVID-19 vaccinations began, insisting such service be resumed. 

Speaking of vaccines, if you haven’t been vaccinated, please walk into one of these locations or make an appointment to do so ASAP. It’s even more important as health experts say that “herd immunity” due to vaccine hesitancy will likely be unattainable, and COVID-19 will be with us in a “manageable” way for years to come. 

On that note, I recommend reading on to remind yourself of how active our community is. But no matter what, stay safe and enjoy the rest of your Monday.

item.description: Good Afternoon, I hope this email finds you well on this warm Wednesday. I’ll be brief with some more canal content. Last night at the Gowanus CAG meeting, after many shared their memories of Linda Ma
item.content:encoded:
Good Afternoon,

I hope this email finds you well on this warm Wednesday. I’ll be brief with some more canal content.

Last night at the Gowanus CAG meeting, after many shared their memories of Linda Mariano , the EPA reported that 35 thousand cubic yards of sediment have been dredged and phase 1 and 2 of the dredging is complete. The EPA and NYC will be meeting to determine a new Universal Administrative Order (UA0) that would lay out what the City must do to support the canal’s cleanup. The City may still face penalties for missing deadlines outlined in previous Gowanus-related UAO’s. However, you can find out more by watching a recording of the meeting here .

I’d again recommend reading the Gowanus rezoning Draft Environmental Impact Statement (DEIS ) for more canal content. Also, it's very important that we, as a community, are as informed as possible, so it’s very much appreciated that other people and organizations have shared the DEIS and highlighted various portions. So big thanks to the Gowanus Alliance , the Gowanus Dredgers , Gowanus Current , Gowanus Canal Conservancy , the Gowanus Neighborhood Coalition for Justice , and anyone else that I may have missed.

On that note, I’ll stop, remind you to get vaccinated, check out the items below, don’t forget that Alternate Side Parking is suspended tomorrow and Friday, and enjoy the rest of your Wednesday.

Michael Racioppo, District Manager

w.  www.BrooklynCB6.org

e.  Mike@bkcb6.org

item.content:encoded:
You may have heard that former and ostensibly future CB6 resident Mayor de Blasio announced that the city would “fully reopen” on July 1st. I’ve had a few inquires about this, and, aside from public statements, I have no further knowledge of what it means. However, the Mayor called this the “ Summer of New York,” so we hope it turns out better than the “Summer of George.” 

Speaking of hope, there is good reason to believe that if President Biden’s plans, outlined in his address last night to Congress, passes, the goals of congresswoman Velasquez’s Public Housing Emergency Response legislation will be closer to being met. That would mean billions of dollars for long-needed capital improvements in NYCHA properties and is why we passed a resolution to support the legislation earlier this year. 

On that note, I’ll stop avoid rambling about other legislative issues and recommend reading on below, remembering Alternate Side Parking is suspended tomorrow, getting vaccinated, and enjoying the rest of your day.

At this point, I’ll shift to more CB6 specific items. 

First, the Temporary Restraining Order(TRO) that delayed the certification of the Gowanus Neighborhood Rezoning has been lifted by Judge Katherine Levine. The City intends to certify the rezoning today, and just this afternoon, the Draft Environmental Impact Statement(DEIS) was published. Once the rezoning is certified, the formal Uniform Land Use Review Procedure will begin. We will have online and in-person (outdoor) options for our joint public hearing with CB2. As the specifics of that are determined, we will share them. 

This week will again be a busy one in our community with 2 of our committee’s meetings. Tonight EWCDH meets, and on Thursday, our Landmarks/Land Use committee meets. Also, take note that a week from tonight, our Permits & Licenses Committee will meet.

item.title: Thursday, April 15, 2021
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope my emails find you well on this rainy Thursday. It was good to “see” and hear from folks at last night's board meeting.
item.content:encoded:
I hope my emails find you well on this rainy Thursday. It was good to “see” and hear from folks at last night's board meeting. If you missed it or want to rewatch it, you can see it here on YouTube. 

Before offering an attempted recap, I’ll remind you that tonight our Transportation and public safety committee is meeting right now. The agenda will feature an MTA presentation on the elevator and ADA improvements for the 7th Ave F and G Subway stop and DCP’s Zoning for the Accessibility text amendment. 

Shifting into reverse and last night, we had four items on our voting agenda, and they were all overwhelmingly approved. 

One was from our Economic Waterfront Community Development and Housing Committee and was presented by Housing Chair Ariel Krasnow. It was a motion to support the Gowanus Dredgers Canoe Club Open Street request. The street in question was 2nd Street between Bond Street and the Gowanus Canal, between 10 am and 9 pm on Friday, Saturday, and Sunday. While not a motion or resolution, EWCDH, specifically the “Community Development portion” had some news last night as Samara Trilling, a software engineer for JustFix.nyc was announced as our new Community Development Chair. 

Another item was presented for Permits & Licences chair, Rachel Freeman. Despite being unable to attend the committee meeting, she didn’t skip a beat. She presented a motion to approve an application for an on-premises Liquor License at 223 Smith Street. This establishment will serve American cuisine and is owned by the same people who own and operate Verde on Smith across the street. 

The other two voting items were from the Landmarks/ Land Use Committee. Land Use has a new chair. Mark Shames, who remains as our Waterfront Chair and member of the committee, stepped down from his role, and Alec Scherinbeck has stepped. Peter expressed his appreciation to Mark. Alec knows he has big shoes to fill, but his resume indicates he’s very much up to the task.Alec lives in Park Slope just a few blocks away from where he was raised. He currently works as the Deputy State Solicitor for New Jersey. He is a whiz with questions of procedure: Previously, he was counsel to Speaker Nancy Pelosi in McCarthy v. Pelosi, a constitutional challenge brought by House Republicans to the House’s novel remote-voting procedures that were adopted during COVID to allow the House to vote without gathering in person. His thoughts about public policy have been published widely, including on the New York Times Opinion page. 

But I digress and get to the items that were up for review. The Landmarks item presented by David Briggs was for legalizing changes to the fence at 441 14th Street in the Park Slope Historic District. The Land Use item, presented by Alec Schierenbeck, was for an application to the Board of Standards and Appeals to permit residential use in a three-story, single-family home with a cellar in an M1-1 zoning district contrary to Zoning Resolution section 42-10 at 166 Coffey Street. 

On that note, I must stop typing as I am scheduled for a COVID-19 vaccination appointment. Speaking of vaccination appointments, there are many available, so make one, stay safe, and have a good evening

item.description: I hope this email finds you well on this, now sunny, Tuesday, the 13th day of April, and the eve of our full board meeting.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well on this, now sunny, Tuesday, the 13th day of April, and the eve of our full board meeting.

Again, our full board meeting will be held tomorrow in about 24 hours, and in about 48 hours, our Transportation & Public Safety Committee will meet. Click here to register for those meetings as well as the two committee meetings we’ll be having next week. On Monday, April 19th, EWCDH will meet, and Landmarks/ Land Use meets on Thursday, April 22nd. You can also find out about these meetings just by walking around our community.

Onto things outside our orbit. The city has suspended the use of the Johnson & Johnson(J&J) COVID-19 vaccine in line with CDC guidelines. If you are scheduled to receive the J&J vaccine, you’ll be rescheduled for a Moderna or Pfizer vaccine dose. Please note that this suspension is based on only 6 cases out of the nearly 7 million J&J doses that have been given. It is, in the truest sense, done with an abundance of caution to reduce vaccine hesitancy.

The Department of Education and the Department of Youth and Community Development announced the new Summer Rising initiative. It’s a free summer program open to all kids from Kindergarten through 12th grade that will be in person and safe, utilizing outdoor space. It will provide school-based academic and social enrichment programs in advance of the next, hopefully, more normal, school year. However, you’ll be able to find out more here, and applications for the grades Kindergarten through 8th Grade will be available here beginning April 26th. 

In closing, I’d suggest reading on, getting vaccinated, and enjoying the rest of your Tuesday.

item.title: Eligibility, Crash, Council, Expo
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: With today viewed as a tale of hope, the sun stands for the shining prospect that, in New York, EVERYONE who is at least 16 years old is now ELIGIBLE to receive a COVID-19 VACCINE. You can find appointments here or, if you’re at least 75…
item.content:encoded:
With today viewed as a tale of hope, the sun stands for the shining prospect that, in New York, EVERYONE who is at least 16 years old is now ELIGIBLE to receive a COVID-19 VACCINE. You can find appointments here or, if you’re at least 75 years of age or tag along with such a senior, you can walk into the Brooklyn Army Terminal and get a shot without making an appointment. You can even get one on one of the 20 buses administering vaccines. No matter how you chose to get it, get it ASAP. 

On a less optimistic note, the crash that occurred this morning at 4th Avenue & 3rd Street led to 5 injuries hospitalizations. Luckily there are no fatalities, but it certainly reinforces our consistent support and commitment to increasing street safety and traffic calming. As more information is received, I’ll share it.

﻿

We’ve got lots happening the rest of this week, and next week, you can read about below my signature. On that note, stay safe, get vaccinated and enjoy the rest of your Tuesday.

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Draw, Participate, Vaccinate, Council, Comedy
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well after an enjoyable weekend that encompassed both Passover and Easter.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well after an enjoyable weekend that encompassed both Passover and Easter. 

While we don't have any CB6 meetings, our community and members remain busy this coming week. That busyness ranges from drawing classes to roofless comedy, a 76th Precinct Community Council meeting chaired by CB6 public safety chair Jerry Armer, and a Participatory Budgeting expo led by our very own CB6 environmental protection co-chair, Angelica Ramdhari. These events are virtual or held with safe distancing because we're not yet past the COVID-19 pandemic.

However, according to Health Department Advisor Dr. Jay Varna, there is some hope that if we pick up the vaccination pace, the city could be “completely out of this in six to eight weeks.” That's a sunny position, but no matter what, the sooner people get vaccinated, the sooner we will get “completely out” of this. To be clear, no one can know exactly what “completely out” ends up looking like.

Keeping with the theme of getting past the pandemic, I’ll remind anyone reading that as of tomorrow, Tuesday, April 6th, ALL NEW YORKERS OVER the age of 16 will be ELIGIBLE to receive one of the COVID-19 vaccines. You can click here to make an appointment. Suppose you’re at least 75 years of age, or tag along with somebody who is, you can walk into the Brooklyn Army Terminal and get a shot without making an appointment. No matter how you chose to get it, get it ASAP.

On that note, I’ll recommend reading on, staying safe, and enjoying the rest of your day.

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: No Fools, Free, Accessibility
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: For everyone observing Holy Thursday, hopefully, it’s a blessed day. The same goes for everyone celebrating Major League Baseball’s opening day.
item.content:encoded:
For everyone observing Holy Thursday, hopefully, it’s a blessed day. The same goes for everyone celebrating Major League Baseball’s opening day. 

As mentioned previously, our Youth, Human Services and Education committee met last night. One of the agenda items was a presentation from the Brooklyn Conservatory of Music (BKCM). BKCM highlighted how they’ve adapted during the pandemic to remain safe and still provide music education and experience with online lessons and streaming recitals. They also highlighted their FREE spring benefit that will offer outdoor music across our community. I’ve been lucky to attend BKCM events on pre-pandemic days, and if you like checking out different kinds of music, you should mark your calendar for Saturday, May 15th. 

The NYC Test & Trace Corps presented with a focus on Covid Stats that reinforce that we’re not done, by any means, yet. Further supporting that reality is that two committee and CB6 members, Joe Anne Brown and her daughter Tiffany Reid Brown currently have COVID-19. Being fortunate enough to know Tiffany and Joe Anne, I’m not surprised they made it to the meeting via zoom, but it’s still impressive. I’m also happy to know they are feeling better than they did last week. 

Shifting from a previous meeting to a reminder for a future meeting, two weeks from tonight, Thurs, April 15th, at 630 PM, our Transportation & Public Safety Committee will meet over zoom. The agenda will have two items. First is a presentation from the MTA on the planned elevator and other ADA improvements to the 7th Ave & 9th Street F & G Subway stop. The second will be a presentation from the MTA & DCP on a text amendment to increase the accessibility of subway stations. 

On that note, I’ll stop typing and suggest you read on below but most importantly, stay safe and get a COVID-19 vaccine when you can.

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Tonight, Tomorrow, Tanks
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Tonight at our YHSE committee meeting, we’ll hear from the NYC Test and Trace Corps and the Brooklyn Conservatory of Music. It will start at 6:30 PM and be held over Zoom.
item.content:encoded:
Tonight at our YHSE committee meeting, we’ll hear from the NYC Test and Trace Corps and the Brooklyn Conservatory of Music. It will start at 6:30 PM and be held over Zoom. You may also want to note our April full board meeting is two weeks from tonight on Wednesday, April 14th at 6:30 PM, also over Zoom.

As for why we meet over zoom, the COVID-19 pandemic virus is adaptive and we may see a fourth wave. I think it’s safe to say we shouldn’t help this unrelenting virus. No matter how weary we are of all things pandemic, as experts keep saying, don’t give up now, get vaccinated ASAP, maintain distance and mask up. 

Before ending my routine of well wishes and recommend reading, I’d draw your attention to 2 Gowanus-related items. First, the EPA issued an administrative ruling requiring the city to construct sewage retention tanks for the Gowanus Canal Superfund Cleanup. Secondly, BKLYNER has coverage of the Van Alen Institute’s(VAI) presentation given during Monday’s EWCDH meeting. Specifically, VAI’s Gowanus Neighborhood Fellowship. This is an excellent opportunity to be paid to plan and get involved. However, if you’re reading a community board newsletter, you’re probably doing it already.

On that note, I'll remind you that Alternate Side Park Regulations will be suspended tomorrow, and no, I didn't miss that marijuana will be legal. Lastly, I recommend reading on, getting vaccinating ASAP, and enjoying the rest of your Wednesday.

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Fellowships, Ferries, Tomorrow
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Last night, as advertised, our EWCDH committee met and had presentations from the Van Alen Institute and Gowanus Dredgers. If you weren’t able to join the meeting or want to relive it, you can watch the meeting on YouTube or check out the…
item.content:encoded:
Last night, as advertised, our EWCDH committee met and had presentations from the Van Alen Institute and Gowanus Dredgers. If you weren’t able to join the meeting or want to relive it, you can watch the meeting on YouTube or check out the presentations here. If you're interested in applying for Van Alen’s Neighborhood Design Fellowship, which their presentation focused on, click here. I wasn’t able to attend last night but have heard nothing but rave reviews for both presentations. Additionally, on the EWCDH front, as we’ve asked, ferries to Governors Island will run from Red Hook and pier six starting May 1st.

Keeping with CB6 committees, tomorrow night at our YHSE committee meeting, we’ll hear from the NYC Test and Trace Corps and the Brooklyn Conservatory of Music. Just like last night, it will start at 6:30 PM and be held over zoom.

Again, with COVID-19 rates going up, I’d remind you to get vaccinated as soon as you’re eligible. Anyone over 30 is now eligible for vaccination, and a week from today, Tuesday, April 6th, anyone over the age of 16 will be eligible. If you’re over 75 years old,  you and one person of any age that comes with you can arrive without an appointment and get vaccinated at the 24/7 locations of Brooklyn Army Terminal, Bathgate, and Citi Field. You have less reason for not being vaccinated by the day, so please do so ASAP. 

On that note, as usual, I recommend reading on, getting a vaccine if you can, and enjoying the rest of your Tuesday.

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201

item.title: Tonight, Tomorrow, Eligible, Access & Appointments
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well after a weekend that celebrated a wide range of religious cultures and traditions. All the best wishes if you observed any, or all, of those holidays-Passover, Palm Sunday and Holi.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well after a weekend that celebrated a wide range of religious cultures and traditions. All the best wishes if you observed any, or all, of those holidays-Passover, Palm Sunday and Holi. 

You may have heard or noticed, public schools are closed for the week, but your CB tries to emulate our City's reputation and never sleep, so we have two committee meetings. At 6:30 PM, when EWCDH hears from the Gowanus Dredgers and Van Alen Institute, two days later, on March 31st, YHSE will feature presentations from the Brooklyn Conservatory of Music and the NYC Test and Trace Corps. Both will be held on zoom and start at 6:30 pm.

As for the reason we’re still meeting over zoom, the COVID-19 pandemic, it’s not over by any means. We’re in an race between additional cases and the expansion of vaccine eligibility and vaccination supply. Starting tomorrow, anyone over 30 will be eligible for vaccination, and next Tuesday, April 6th, anyone over the age of 16 will be eligible. This is good and, soon, the there will be no caveat of eligibility when telling people they should schedule an appointment ASAP.

So on that note, I recommend reading on getting a vaccine if you can and enjoy the rest of your Monday.

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: A Brooklyn Ploy & The Week Ahead
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well as we head into the weekend and, for those who celebrate, a Happy Passover. While hardly divine intervention, Passover is why Alternate Side Parking will be suspended this coming Monday and Tuesday while…
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well as we head into the weekend and, for those who celebrate, a Happy Passover. While hardly divine intervention, Passover is why Alternate Side Parking will be suspended this coming Monday and Tuesday while public school students have their spring break as public schools are closed for the week.

While schools are closed for the week, just as was the case this week, we have 2 CB6 committee meetings. They’ll feature four presentations (2 for each) from interesting sources on various topics that will lead to good discussions and maybe a vote or 2. On Monday, March 29th, EWCDH will hear from the Gowanus Dredgers and Van Alen Institute, while two days later, on March 31st, YHSE will feature presentations from the Brooklyn Conservatory of Music and the NYC Test and Trace Corps. There’s other stuff happening that you can discover by reading on beyond my email signature.  

I know I keep saying if you can get a vaccination, get it. However, if you aren’t inspired by many knowledgeable and trustworthy sources urging you on, maybe a free Junior’s Cheesecake will provide a creamy yummy incentive. I don’t know if there is a ploy quite that esoterically Brooklyn.  

On that note, I’ll stay safe and have a good weekend.

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: The city has injected residents with 3.5 million vaccine shots, and a number of others have antibodies from contracting the disease, but infection rates tell us
item.content:encoded:
The city has injected residents with 3.5 million vaccine shots, and a number of others have antibodies from contracting the disease, but infection rates tell us 

we have not reached herd immunity yet, so the meetings I refer to will be or have been virtual.

Virtual meetings like tomorrow night's landmarks/ land use committee meeting or last night’s Gowanus CAG meeting. At the CAG, the EPA reported that 30 thousand cubic yards of sediment had been excavated from the canal so far and that phase 1 & 2 of dredging north of Carroll Street has been completed.

Speaking of dredging, as mentioned earlier in the week, EWCDH will hear from the Gowanus Dredgers and Van Alen Institute this coming Monday, March 29th. One week from tonight, at YHSE, we’ll see presentations from the Brooklyn Conservatory of Music and the NYC Test and Trace Corps.

On that note, I’ll stop and recommend scrolling down for more events and more information. Stay safe, get vaccinated when you can, and enjoy the evening.

item.title: Elevating in April
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Last night, as previewed in prior newsletters, our Permits & Licenses Committee met. CB6 Board Secretary Karen Broughton stepped up to chair the meeting, unsurprisingly did an excellent job, and the committee approved an application for an…
item.content:encoded:
Last night, as previewed in prior newsletters, our Permits & Licenses Committee met. CB6 Board Secretary Karen Broughton stepped up to chair the meeting, unsurprisingly did an excellent job, and the committee approved an application for an on-premises Liquor License at 223 Smith Street. This establishment will serve American cuisine and is owned by the same people that own and operate Verde on Smith. Verde is on the side of the block at 216 Smith Street. The next stop for this application is our April 14th full board meeting. 

While looking to April, those interested in the Avenue F/G station elevator should mark their calendars or register for April 15th’s Transportation & Public Safety Committee meeting. The reason being that the MTA will present their plans during this meeting, and it’s something the community has fought and advocated to make a reality for many years. 

Of course, don’t forget about other meetings we have, including Landmarks/Land Use on Thursday, EWCDH next Monday, and YHSE next Wednesday. 

Other things are happening before, during, and after these meetings that you can read about below, So on that note, I’ll stop and recommend scrolling down for more events and more information. Stay safe, get vaccinated when you can, and have a good weekend.
