item.title: Springing, Zooming, Meeting
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well as it no longer just feels like spring; it has arrived on your calendar, as well. Our focus today is on a few items directly in the BKCB6 orbit.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well as it no longer just feels like spring; it has arrived on your calendar, as well. Our focus today is on a few items directly in the BKCB6 orbit.

The first week of spring will have two BKCB6 committee meetings. The first of those is tonight, Monday, March 22, at 6:30 pm, with Permits & Licenses congregating over Zoom. The second committee meeting is our Landmarks/ Land Use Committee on Thursday, March 25, also over Zoom and also at 6:30 PM.

We will also have 2 BKCB6 Committee Meetings next week. One week from tonight, Monday, March 29, at 6:30 pm, our Economic Waterfront Community Development and Housing Committee will meet with an update from the Gowanus Dredgers and a presentation from the now locally-based non-profit, Van Alen Institute. On Wednesday, March 31st, our Youth, Human Services, and Education committee will meet and hear from the Brooklyn Conservatory of Music. Speaking of Youth Services, the Summer Youth Employment Program (SYEP) application is now open. You may recall in last year’s budget, we were, among many others, successful in our opposition to defunding this program. 

Other things are happening before, during, and after these meetings that you can read about below, So on that note, I’ll stop and recommend scrolling down for more events and more information. Stay safe, get vaccinated when you can, and have a good weekend.

It wasn’t a review item, but if you have concerns or questions about Citibike, as Transportation Chair Eric McClure noted, let DOT know and feel free to copy us. Big thanks to Captain Souffrant and Emily Riquelme, and her colleagues from DOT that joining us last night. 

As always, our community will be busy through the weekend and the upcoming work week. That includes two CB6 committee meetings, Permits & Licenses on Monday, Landmarks/ Land Use on Thursday. 

On that note, I’ll stop and recommend scrolling down for more events and more information. So stay safe, get vaccinated when you can, and have a good weekend.

item.title: Bikes, Precincts, Zoning
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope that this email finds you well on this rainy Thursday. I’ll be brief with a couple of quick items.
item.content:encoded:
I hope that this email finds you well on this rainy Thursday. I’ll be brief with a couple of quick items.

First, it may interest people to know that the City Planning Commission approved Zoning for the Coastal Flood Resiliency (ZCFR), citywide zoning rules. The hope is that ZCFR will allow homeowners to build or raise homes above current levels making significant weather events such as Hurricane Sandy less damaging. This would be a good thing, and it may sound familiar since we approved of it in December, and it now moves to the City Council. 

As previously mentioned, tonight, our Transportation & Public Safety Committee meets via zoom at 6:30 PM. The public safety portion, chaired by Jerry Armer, introduces the community to Captain Frantz Souffrant, the recently appointed Commanding Officer of the 78th precinct. On the other side of the committee’s equation, Transportation, chaired by the Prospect Park West bike lane’s namesake, Eric McClure, will focus on CitiBike. Specifically, a presentation from DOT on plans from the program’s expansion. If that interests you, click here and join the fun. 

More things are happening, but for those, you must read on. So stay safe, get vaccinated and enjoy the rest of your day. 

Related tools

Best,

item.title: Lá Fhéile Pádraig sona duit
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: If you’re wondering what the subject line of this email, “Lá Fhéile Pádraig sona duit!”, meant you probably aren't Irish. What the phrase translates to from Gaelic is “Happy Saint Patrick’s Day to You.” Please indulge me.
item.content:encoded:
If you’re wondering what the subject line of this email, “Lá Fhéile Pádraig sona duit!”, meant you probably aren't Irish. What the phrase translates to from Gaelic is “Happy Saint Patrick’s Day to You.” Please indulge me. Despite my last name and the placement of the “O” in it, I am the son of an Irish-American mother.

Even if you won’t indulge me or don’t care for this day, I hope this email finds you well. I’ll be brief with a quick reminder of the last normal Saint Patrick’s parade here in Brooklyn back in 2019. That day, our community marched in the first truly inclusive Brooklyn Saint Patrick’s Day Parade. The Brooklyn Irish LGBTQ Organization (BILO) became the first LGBTQ group to march in the event. Folks such as Assemblymember Robert Carroll and our Chair, Peter Fleming, had been part of a fight to make that a reality, and it should sustain our price and give us some hope going forward. 

Speaking of going forward, tomorrow, Thursday, March 18th, our Transportation & Public Safety Committee will meet beginning at 6:30 PM. The agenda will feature CitiBike expansion and the new commanding officer of the 78th Precinct. If that interests you, register here. 

More things are happening, but for those, you must read on. So stay safe, get vaccinated and enjoy the rest of your day.

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Vaccines, Parades & Reality
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Today is the day before Saint Patrick’s Day, last year’s parade was canceled entirely, and this year there’s only a virtual parade. Despite it being virtual, the celebration will be real, and hopefully, next St.
item.content:encoded:
Today is the day before Saint Patrick’s Day, last year’s parade was canceled entirely, and this year there’s only a virtual parade. Despite it being virtual, the celebration will be real, and hopefully, next St. Patrick's Day, people can celebrate together. So get the COVID-19 vaccine when eligible.

Speaking of vaccine eligibility and Saint Patrick’s Day, beginning tomorrow, eligibility will expand to public-facing, governmental, non-profit, and building service workers. If you fall into one of those categories, use that City or State site to schedule an appointment. You can also call 877-VAX-4NYC or 877-829-4692 to schedule an appointment. I'm told that, while imperfect, it is getting easier as vaccine supplies have been increasing. 

However, civic life will remain largely virtual for the foreseeable future. Tonight, as mentioned by his representative at last week’s board meeting, Comptroller Stringer will hold an event on Work, Family, and Caregiving in COVID-era. Also tonight, and mentioned at last week’s board meeting, the Fifth Ave. Park Slope BID and Heat/Cool Smart Brooklyn host a webinar on green options for small businesses. 

This week and next, more things are happening, like 2 CB6 committee meetings this Thursday, March 18th, and this coming Monday, March 22nd. 

More things are happening, but for those, you must read on. So stay safe and enjoy the rest of your Tuesday.

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Et tu, Newsletter? Share this email a link
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well as we make our way through the, regardless of snow or a marmot’s predictions, last week of winter.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well as we make our way through the, regardless of snow or a marmot’s predictions, last week of winter.

As many were reminded last night, it’s been a year since we lost the first of over 30 thousand fellow New Yorkers to COVID-19. With vaccinations becoming more widely available and infection rates dropping, we are starting to see the light at the end of the proverbial tunnel. However, there is still some oncoming traffic in the tunnel, and we cannot let up. I don’t think anyone wants to be in another lockdown as we see in Italy right now. 

Rest assured, that doesn’t mean letting up concerning civic involvement, as there are plenty of safe options. Those options include, but are not limited to, a Gun Violence Town Hall tonight, Small Business Webinars tonight & tomorrow, a Rent Freeze Webinar Thursday, and our Transportation & Public Safety Committee will meet Thursday evening. 

On that note, I’ll recommend that you keep reading but get vaccinated if you can and, most importantly - beware the ides of March!

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well as we make our way through the, regardless of snow or a marmot’s predictions, last week of winter.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well as we make our way through the, regardless of snow or a marmot’s predictions, last week of winter.

As many were reminded last night, it’s been a year since we lost the first of over 30 thousand fellow New Yorkers to COVID-19. With vaccinations becoming more widely available and infection rates dropping, we are starting to see the light at the end of the proverbial tunnel. However, there is still some oncoming traffic in the tunnel, and we cannot let up. I don’t think anyone wants to be in another lockdown as we see in Italy right now. 

Rest assured, that doesn’t mean letting up concerning civic involvement, as there are plenty of safe options. Those options include, but are not limited to, a Gun Violence Town Hall tonight, Small Business Webinars tonight & tomorrow, a Rent Freeze Webinar Thursday, and our Transportation & Public Safety Committee will meet Thursday evening. 

On that note, I’ll recommend that you keep reading but get vaccinated if you can and, most importantly - beware the ides of March!

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Recent Past, Near Future
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well as we enter a spring-like weekend and, for antiquated reasons, lose an hour of sleep. Although, in the time of COVID, time seems to be a flat circle.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well as we enter a spring-like weekend and, for antiquated reasons, lose an hour of sleep. Although, in the time of COVID, time seems to be a flat circle. Regardless of how time is experienced, our community remains active. This week and the next few will be no exception.

This coming Thursday, our Transportation & Public Safety Committee meets and will hear from DOT about the CitiBike program’s expansion and be introduced to the new Commanding Officer at the 78th Precinct. Before that, specifically tomorrow, Saturday, Match 13th, Congresswoman Velasquez will host a small business workshop over Zoom.

Speaking of Congresswoman Velasquez, she’s re-introduced legislation that would ban non-essential helicopter traffic over NYC. I mention this since we’ve been supportive of it in the recent past. Hopefully, based on the volume of complaints, literally and figuratively, this bill draws enough legislative support to become law. 

On that note, I’ll recommend you keep reading but, more importantly, that you stay safe, have a good weekend, and check your clocks!

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201

item.title: Friday, March 5, 2021
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Yesterday, I highlighted an article in the Times about Amazon’s expansion and how it has reminded me of our repeated calls for DOT to release the Smart Freight Management plan and conduct a comprehensive traffic study for Red Hook. At the…
item.content:encoded:
Yesterday, I highlighted an article in the Times about Amazon’s expansion and how it has reminded me of our repeated calls for DOT to release the Smart Freight Management plan and conduct a comprehensive traffic study for Red Hook. At the risk of living in yesterday’s news, the article highlighted the important point that NYC has far less industrial space than many and even much smaller cities. 

For example, Chicago, which has a 3rd of our population, has nearly ten times the industrial square footage with 1.2 billion square feet. Such stats help reinforce why we’ve insisted that, among other conditions, the pending Gowanus rezoning must tie into the expansion of the neighboring Southwest Brooklyn Industrial Business Zone(IBZ).

Speaking of the IBZ, the only virtual ULURP we've reviewed so far, which is for the planned Monadnock Headquarters at 300 Huntington Street, had its first City Planning Commission hearing yesterday. The application was to change the M2-1 zone to an M2-3 zone resulting in a substantial reduction in parking space requirements. After an extensive hearing back in December, we approved it unanimously, with the applicant agreeing to return and present the final design and details to us in the future. 

On that technical, and I’m sure exciting note, I’ll recommend you keep reading but more importantly, that you stay safe and have a good weekend!

item.content:encoded:
As March gets going, we’re approaching several anniversaries. These aren’t celebratory milestones; we’re now a year into a pandemic. Thursday, March 5th, 2020, our Transportation & Public Safety (TPS) Committee met at the 78th precinct, and it was the last time we met in person. 

This is a mundane milestone and one I’d prefer to forget and hadn’t realized until I scheduled our Thursday, March 18th, 2021 TPS Committee meeting. The agenda has two items. The first will introduce the committee to the new commanding officer at the 78th Precinct, Captain Frantz Souffrant. The second will be a presentation from the NYC Department of Transportation about its expansion of the CitiBike program. If this is of interest to you, register here. 

There is, of course, stuff happening between now and then, such as our March 10th General Board meeting and other items you can find out about by scrolling on down.

item.description: Last night, living up to its advanced hype, our Landmarks/Land Use Committee met to review the Board of Standards Appeals(BSA) application for 145 Wolcott Street. The meeting lasted over two and a half hours, with participation from the…
item.content:encoded:
Last night, living up to its advanced hype, our Landmarks/Land Use Committee met to review the Board of Standards Appeals(BSA) application for 145 Wolcott Street. The meeting lasted over two and a half hours, with participation from the community, its Councilperson, and our Committee. The participation and discussion resulted in a motion to disapprove based on BSA guidelines.  If you weren’t able to Zoom in or want to relive it, the meeting is posted on our YouTube channel. The next stop for this application is at our March 10th Full Board meeting.

I usually end with a suggestion to keep reading below my signature, and today is no exception. However, more important than your reading decisions, please take note that as we approach a year since the first documented COVID-19 case in our city, we are at “extremely High Risk” so please stay safe and have a good weekend.

item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well on the 24th day of February without about 24 hours until our next meeting.

The meeting I’m referring to is tomorrow’s Landmarks/Land Use Meeting held over Zoom. There’s only one agenda item, but it’s an application that has garnered a lot of interest as close to 200 people have already registered. The application I’m referring to is seeking approval from us, the Board of Standard and Appeals (BSA), and a 15 story mixed-use building at 145 Wolcott Street in Red Hook. While we’re counting down until tomorrow’s meeting, if you haven’t already you, may want to take note that two weeks from tonight, our March full board meeting will be held beginning at 630 PM. 

Shifting gears, as we know, it’s been a rough year 12 months for folks in almost all walks of life, but small businesses, freelancers, and independent contractors have had it especially rough. More should and could be done, but just a heads up that the Paycheck Protection Program will only accept applications from businesses with fewer than 20 employees. This also applies to independent contractors and freelancers who may consist of only one person. When I heard this, I reached out to Rafael Espinal, the head of the Freelancers Union, and his organization is helping freelancers who have issues applying. If you need such help, please send them an email. 

On that note, I’ll suggest reading on, staying safe, continuing to countdown, and enjoying the rest of your Wednesday.

item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well on this slushy Monday. It starts a week that will feature 2 CB6 committee meetings. Before mentioning those meetings, I’d like to thank everyone who congratulated me on turning 36. 

The first of those meetings puts the “H” in EWCDH. H is for Housing, specifically federal legislation titled the Public Housing Emergency Response Act. This legislation was introduced in the House of Representatives by Congresswoman Nydia Velasquez, and her District Director, DanIel Wiley, will join us to discuss it. The meeting starts at 6:30 PM, and you can register here.

At the same time of day, but on Thursday, Feb 25th, our Landmarks/ Land Use Committee will meet and review an application to the Board of Standards and Appeals (BSA) for 145 Wolcott Street in Red Hook. In the most simplified sense, it’s an application to permit a 14-story mixed-use (office, light manufacturing, residential) building. If you'd like to know more, I’d suggest registering for the meeting, checking out related documents, and commenting. 

On that note, I’ll let you deal with the snow or whatever you’re involved in, recommend checking out the items below, staying safe and enjoying the rest of your day.

item.title: Tuesday, February 16, 2021
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well after a weekend that included a, for some, romantic Valentine’s Day on Sunday and a, also for some, patriotic Presidents Day on Monday.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well after a weekend that included a, for some, romantic Valentine’s Day on Sunday and a, also for some, patriotic Presidents Day on Monday.

This week, in CB6’s direct orbit, as we await the resolution of litigation and public schools are out for mid-winter recess, things are likely to be relatively quiet. Next week, however, we'll hold 2 CB6 committee meetings via zoom.

The first of those is an EWCDH committee meeting, a week from yesterday, Monday, Feb 22nd, at 6:30 PM. revolves around a discussion with Congresswoman Velasquez’s office about the Public Housing Emergency Response Act. Three nights later, on Thursday, Feb 25th, our Landmarks/ Land Use Committee will meet and review an application to the Board of Standards and Appeals (BSA) for the construction of a 14 story mixed-use (residential and commercial with light manufacturing) building at 145 Wolcott Street in Red Hook. There’s been some coverage of this proposal, and our upcoming meeting, in publications such as the Brooklyn Paper. You can register for EWCDH here and Land Use here. 

Keeping the focus on Red Hook, on Friday, Bklyner published an article about Amazon’s lease signing and our request for a traffic study. Based on some misconceptions and questions I’ve received, it’s important to clarify that Amazon is operating within the parameters of the existing zoning a/k/a “as of right,” which means they don’t need a variance. We are neither approving or disapproving these pending developments (Amazon, UPS, TBD). What we are asking for boils down to getting a look at traffic impacts so that we can best plan and advocate as a community. 

On that note, I recommend checking out the items below,staying safe, and I hope your week is off to a good start and continues as such.

item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well as we head into February’s first weekend, which could see some more snow.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well as we head into February’s first weekend, which could see some more snow.

Before anything else, I have to thank the Park Slope Civic Council (PSCC) and its trustees for inviting me to be their guest speaker last night. I look forward once they return to in-person meetings, hopefully in late 2021, to congregate at the Old Stone House house. Still, it is rewarding, even via zoom, to discuss our community and do my best to answer questions among folks who are so civically committed.  

Speaking of commitment, I feel compelled to reiterate the appreciation I expressed last night for their work, alongside CB6 and the community at large, in advocating for the elevator that will be installed at the 7th Avenue F/G stop. Lastly, I want to thank PSCC President Joe Rydell for pulling off the rare feat of nailing the pronunciation of my last name on the first go around.

As daily readers may know, earlier in the week, we wrote to DOT reiterating the need for a comprehensive traffic study for Red Hook. We expect an influx of delivery fulfillment sites, and the truck traffic that will surely follow as night the day. The reasons for pressing the request are the naming of a new DOT Commissioner and the advancement of Amazon’s Red Hook plans.

As with ULURPs there are legal questions surrounding virtual voting Amazon asked the National Labor Relations Board to mandate that the vote to certify the union only take place in person. Amazon’s request was denied in a two sentence order. For those who support unionization, this is surely welcome news as we head into the weekend.

But, whether you agree or not, I hope you have an opportunity to check out the items below, have a good weekend, and stay safe, warm.

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201

item.content:encoded:
I’m sure there will be more articles with more explicit legal statements on the process. Still, for those who open these emails seeking rezoning related news, I can humbly share my understanding. Today the court held a further virtual hearing on the permissibility under state and city law of a virtual ULURP. The court has not yet issued a decision clarifying whether our community process can move forward. For now, we will have to wait for the Judge's decision. Hopefully, this is done sooner rather than later. If you want to experience an unchallenged virtual ULURP to fill the void, you can always watch one we've already approved.

Also, I’d like to thank everyone who reached out, shared, liked, or retweeted our letter reiterating our request for a comprehensive traffic study in Red Hook—continuing thanks to folks such as Jim Tampakis, groups such as Resilient Red Hook, and other members of the Red Hook community for bringing this issue to the forefront. Now we have to keep it there and make sure this necessary study happens.

On that note, I'll end and remind you that we have a board meeting a week from yesterday and recommend checking out the items below. Most importantly, stay safe and enjoy the rest of your Thursday.

item.description: For those who don't follow the comings and goings of various city agencies, one may not know that CB6 resident Polly Trottenberg has left the city's Department of Transportation and joined the Biden Administration as the Deputy Secretary…
item.content:encoded:
For those who don't follow the comings and goings of various city agencies, one may not know that CB6 resident Polly Trottenberg has left the city's Department of Transportation and joined the Biden Administration as the Deputy Secretary of the United States DOT. We're appreciative of her service to the city, and her impact will long benefit the city and will surely benefit the nation in the years ahead. With that, her successor at NYC DOT, Hank Guttman, was introduced today.

We at CB6  wasted no time and sent a letter congratulating him and making sure he’s aware, if he wasn't already, of our insistence that a comprehensive traffic study is done in Red Hook. As the letter states,  As the “development of multiple package-fulfillment centers in Red Hook progresses,” the study should include “analysis of all potential traffic impacts, and options for how best to deal with them.”. The letter also highlights that our concerns are not limited to worries about safety, pollution, and truck traffic, but extend to preserving the neighborhood’s historic character and that cobblestones be maintained wherever possible, and where not, to have them repurposed elsewhere in Red Hook.

On that note, I'll end and remind you that we have a board meeting a week from today and recommend checking out the items below. Most importantly, stay safe and enjoy the rest of your Wednesday.

Speaking of CB6’s environs, it’s certainly been getting more attention than usual. From the pending Gowanus rezoning to the last mile product fulfillment centers in Red Hook, these are issues that have been in the spotlight. Our community cares deeply about both issues while maintaining various perspectives. For Gowanus, that means a speedy response from the Department of City Planning to our request for the release of the Environmental Impact Statement. On both of these issues, when I know more, I’ll share it, and you’ll know more as well.

item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Apologies for emailing so late but today has been crazy, and I’ve got a newsletter streak to maintain, and like every other day, I hope this finds you well.
item.content:encoded:
Apologies for emailing so late but today has been crazy, and I’ve got a newsletter streak to maintain, and like every other day, I hope this finds you well.

One year ago today, the CDC announced the first case of COVID-19 in the United States. Sadly it was far from the last as was suggested then, and new records are broken every day. Hopefully, with a new presidential administration focusing on safety measures, vaccinations, and financial help, we can return to a new normal sometime soon. 

Speaking of “new’” normal, we’ve written to the Department of City Planning regarding virtual ULURP for Gowanus. The letter, with the support of 37 of our 44 board members, including NYCHA tenant leaders, states that after years of in-person meetings, multiple precertification meetings, notices via email, and discussion at board meetings, the process should move forward virtually. 

This letter should not be read as an endorsement of the proposal that’s yet to be released. It is a request for an opportunity to evaluate the DEIS and plan. Our members hold several varying perspectives on the rezoning and the issues—from environmental justice to housing affordability and manufacturing jobs—that the rezoning encompasses. The way for the community’s voice to be heard is to let the community process move forward—not to stifle our community’s voices just as this vital dialogue is set to begin formally.

Anyway, I’m sure the above paragraphs will produce some great discussions, but I’d still recommend reading below my signature. Either way, stay safe and enjoy the remaining hours of Thursday. 

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201

I hope this email finds everyone well on this 19th day of January that feels like a Monday but is, in fact, a Tuesday. 

Some may have noticed that Friday’s newsletter was sent out a little later than usual. I was planning to include a recommendation of weekend reading of the Gowanus Draft Environmental Impact Statement (DEIS), which was expected to be released late on Friday. It wasn’t released owing to a lawsuit, and temporary restraining order, opposing the legality of a virtual Universal Land Use Review Process(ULURP).

I can't speak to the law but we have had a virtual ULURP action during the pandemic. It was for 300 Huntington Street, in the IBZ along the Gowanus Canal. It was unanimously approved, thanks to a motion, by our Landmarks/Land Use Committee and full board in December. I’ll share more information on the rezoning if and when I receive it. However, until then, I continue to recommend reading what’s currently available from DCP, as well as our writings and our comment form. 

With vaccine doses dwindling, I hope we will have more interesting, and indeed, happier news to share sooner than later. For now, I’ll recommend checking out the Items below,  including our support for Ferry Service to Governors Island from Red Hook, staying safe and enjoying the rest of the day.

item.title: Meetings, Manifesto
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: As mentioned over and over again, last night was our first board meeting of 2021. It was good to “see” and hear from folks whether they were themselves or making an appearance incognito.
item.content:encoded:
As mentioned over and over again, last night was our first board meeting of 2021. It was good to “see” and hear from folks whether they were themselves or making an appearance incognito.

With over 100 attendees, including 40 of 44 board members, representatives from various levels of government, and community stakeholders, we had a good turnout. We approved all 3 items on our voting agenda. 

The first of those 3 approvals came from our Landmarks Committee. The item was for a Certificate of Appropriateness in order to allow for an enlarged masonry opening to accommodate new doors on the second floor rear facade at 424 7th Avenue, which is located in the Park Slope Historic District. The second application was from our Permits & Licenses Committee and was for a new on-premises liquor license for 259 4th Avenue. The applicant intends to do business as Whisk & Whiskey, focusing on introducing customers to the transcontinental flavors of Cambodian & Trinidadian baked goods and seasonal cocktails. The 3rd approval was from our EWCDH Committee and supported continued Governors Island ferry service from Red Hook. 

If that brief overview of last night’s meeting left you wanting to view it or relive it, you can watch it here on Youtube. 

A specter, to some, not dissimilar to the one that haunted Europe in 1848, now haunting the board, is the pending Gowanus rezoning. To paraphrase, the history of all hitherto existing community boards is the history of land use struggles.

To clarify, the only thing we are absolutely certain of is that it will not be certified, until January 19th. At that point our formal public review begins. In advance of that date, you may want to check out our writing on these matters, watch the precertification meetings that we co -sponsored, and comment on our trusty comment form. 

On that note please check out the items below, clicking here if you want to let DOT know what you think about Neighborhood Loading Zones (NLZ), stay safe and enjoy the rest of the day.

I’d like to thank everyone that liked, shared, and reposted our letter to the Mayor, urging him to work with the MTA to ensure that the subways run during all the hours that vaccinations are being given. Speaking of vaccines, New Yorkers ages 65 and over are now eligible for vaccination (it was 75 and over). To schedule an appointment, click here or call 877-VAX-4NYC.

Hopefully, this helps us get to the necessary immunity levels so we can do things like go to restaurants, concerts, see family whenever we’d want, and of course, attend Community Board meetings. item.title: Monday, January 11, 2021
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well on this busy Monday in a week that will feature our first general board meeting of 2021.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well on this busy Monday in a week that will feature our first general board meeting of 2021.

Today, COVID-19 vaccine eligibility expanded to group 1-B, which includes those ages 75 and older, grocery store workers, first responders, transit workers, educators, as well as those living and those living or working in homeless shelters. Over the weekend, some 24/7 vaccination sites were opened. This should help in ramping things up.

It gets harder to fully activate 24/7 sites if subways are not also running 24/7. With that in mind, we, including over 35 board members, just this morning signed on to a letter to the Mayor, with the MTA cc’d urging the coordination between the city and the MTA to get on the same page and ensure that subways are clean and available at all hours that vaccines are available.

For those who read that and were wondering, “ where and when can I get the vaccine?” check out the health department's vaccine page.

With that, I’ll recommend reading on below, staying safe, and having a good Monday.

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager

item.title: Alternate Side Suspension & Other Items
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: When I send an email, I hope that it finds you well. Today, Tuesday, January 5th, 2021, is no exception.
item.content:encoded:
When I send an email, I hope that it finds you well. Today, Tuesday, January 5th, 2021, is no exception.

With the new, more contagious strain of COVID-19 having appeared in New York and infection rates rising, 2021 is starting on a discordant note. However, we still have 360 days to make it a better year. A significant part of that is adherence to safety protocols and the city vaccinating as many people as possible as fast as possible. 

In that vein, as mentioned yesterday, we’ve sent a letter to CB6 resident/our Mayor and the NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene expressing these concerns. As coverage in the Brooklyn Paper shows, we aren't the only ones expressing such sentiments. We don't weigh-in for the sake of complaining but to advance a positive outcome. We can and have done better, and other places are currently doing better. For example, we vaccinated 6 million people against smallpox over a month in 1947. With a population of ninemillion, which is similar to that of NYC, Israel is on pace to have its entire population vaccinated by March.

Moving on just a quick heads up that Thursday’s Landmarks/ Land Use meeting will start at 6:30 PM instead of the usual 6 PM start time.

As always, scroll down, stay safe, and enjoy the rest of the new year’s first Tuesday.

item.content:encoded:
I hope this finds you well and ready for 2021 to, hopefully, surpass its predecessors’ very low bar. 

With that hope in mind, we’ve written to the Mayor and Health Department urging faster and more equitable distribution of vaccines. In the letter, we cite council legislation and Comptroller Stringers' suggestions as possible paths forward, and we offer to do anything we can to help at the community level. Even under the best circumstances, we’ll be zooming for meetings for the foreseeable future. 

Our first meeting of 2021 will occur this Thursday, January 8th, at 6:30 PM, when our Landmarks/Land Use Committee meets with a 2 item agenda. We begin with an application for a Certificate of Appropriateness in the Park Slope Historic District at 424 7th Avenue and conclude with a Board of Standards and Appeals application for 166 Coffey Street.

I’ll stop here as some things are worth knowing beyond CB6’s immediate orbit, many of which are listed below my signature. So scroll down, stay safe and let's hope the first of the 52 weeks of 2021 is off to a good start.

item.title: Happy New Year From CB6!
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: The year 2020 is indelibly imprinted on our memories. We've all lost something significant over the last year, and many have lost more than anyone should have to bear.
item.content:encoded:
The year 2020 is indelibly imprinted on our memories. We've all lost something significant over the last year, and many have lost more than anyone should have to bear. 

Let's also remember that throughout the year, our community has risen to the occasion and shown compassion, generosity, resilience, and dedication. For those reasons, there is no doubt we can continue to get through this. One day, we’ll return to in-person meetings and, even when passionately disagree, we will gain a new appreciation for each other.

If we stay safe by maintaining the protocols, that will happen sooner rather than later in 2021. Enjoy the final hours of the year, and to all best wishes in 2021.

Brooklyn Community Board 6 Wishes you a very Happy New Year!

Peter Fleming

Chairperson

item.title: The final 60
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Last night, as previewed in prior newsletters, our Permits & Licenses committee met and unanimously approved an application for a new on-premises liquor license for 259 4th Avenue. The applicant intends to do business as Whisk & Whiskey,…
item.content:encoded:
Last night, as previewed in prior newsletters, our Permits & Licenses committee met and unanimously approved an application for a new on-premises liquor license for 259 4th Avenue. The applicant intends to do business as Whisk & Whiskey, focusing on introducing customers to the transcontinental flavors of Cambodian & Trinidadian baked goods and seasonal cocktails. Big thanks to Glenn Kelly for stepping up and pinch-hitting as chair of the meeting. The application now moves to a full board vote at our January 13th meeting. The Landmarks/Land Use committee meets next Thursday with an agenda that is still in formation.

But turning to a more pressing matter than any item above is the life and death consequences of COVID’s second wave. Positivity rates are above 7% citywide, and more of our fellow New Yorkers are dying every day. I hope in the spirit of the holidays you celebrated at home or rates will continue rising into the New Year. Even as vaccines are being slowly and sporadically distributed, we cannot act like this is over just because we, and this includes me, want it to be.

With that, I’ll recommend reading on beyond my signature, stay safe, and follow all protocols and enjoy your Tuesday.

item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you safe after having more snow in the last 24 hours than in the previous year.

We are nearly, but not quite, back to the old new normal. As evidence, unlike today, school buildings will be OPEN tomorrow, Friday, December 18th, for in-person learning. However, alternate side parking rules will be suspended through at least Saturday, December 19th.

DSNY remains on snow patrol, but don’t worry; you can put your trash and recycling materials out for collection like normal if you’d like. Just remember that it may be picked up a little later than usual. Also, if you see downed trees or branches, please report them to 311. The city has crews working to make sure hazards are removed ASAP.

Unrelated to the accumulation of snow stories, please remember we have some meetings coming up in the final weeks of 2020 and the beginning of 2021. This coming Monday, December 21, the EWCDH committee, led by Rick Luftglass, will meet to see a presentation about a rezoning proposed for Governors Island. I think it’s important to note that Governors Island isn’t part of our district even though it’s closer to us than Manhattan CB1, but that’s not the presenters' fault, and we appreciate them coming to us despite not being required to do so.

If any of the information above or below changes, I’ll be sure to let you know. Anyway, stay safe, stay warm, and enjoy the rest of your Thursday.

item.title: Alternate Side Parking Suspended, Governors Island & More
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well as we brace for a snowstorm. The snow forecast has already activated an Alternate Side Parking (ASP) suspension for tomorrow, Wed, Dec 16, and Thursday, Dec 17.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well as we brace for a snowstorm. The snow forecast has already activated an Alternate Side Parking (ASP) suspension for tomorrow, Wed, Dec 16, and Thursday, Dec 17. Please note that parking meters remain in effect. Moving on from private vehicle storage, I'll highlight some happenings that shouldn't be impacted by snow.

Tonight Assemblymember Carroll will host a virtual panel led by Haskins Global Literacy Hub, focused on literacy and learning in the time of COVID-19. Tomorrow, as noted above, you can keep your car in the same space and get your caf, half-caf, or decaf fix with Assemblymember Simon in another "Java with Jo Anne."

Of course, there are other things listed below, but I'd like to highlight this coming Monday's Economic Waterfront Community Development & Housing Committee meeting. The agenda has only 1 item, and that's the proposed Governors Island South Island rezoning. Governors Island is part of Manhattan's 1st community district, even though it is physically closer to our district. Nonetheless, I am glad we are allowed to find out and comment on this proposal.

As I understand it, the gist of it is to expand the island's uses to allow it to be more of a year-round entity as opposed to just a weekend happening. I've been a few times, and it's lovely. As much as I like what it is now, I can also see why those in charge of the island want to utilize more of it with a mix of uses such as another academic institution (the harbor school is already there), commercial, non-profit, and cultural, hospitality uses.

Anyway, it should be interesting, and I wanted to draw more attention to it as there's some interest in it based on the number of folks already signed up to zoom.

Anyway, I'll stop here and offer you safe wishes as unique snowflakes prepare to fall.

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: It’s not light yet, but it’s getting there
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds everyone having had a good weekend as we kick off a week that starts with a COVID-19 vaccine rollout and possible snowstorms, and yes, the title of the email is a reference to a Bob Dylan song. Without a doubt, this…
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds everyone having had a good weekend as we kick off a week that starts with a COVID-19 vaccine rollout and possible snowstorms, and yes, the title of the email is a reference to a Bob Dylan song. Without a doubt, this is the most prominent and most immediately needed vaccine we’ve had since the polio vaccine became available.  Three hundred thousand deaths, so many of which were preventable, is nothing in which to take pride. However, while we see the light at the end of the tunnel,  we are still in the darkness. It’s why indoor dining is shutdown starting today and why so many need help to survive. 

There aren’t any official CB6 meetings until a week from tonight, but that doesn’t mean we are in for a week in the doldrums. Two prime examples of community activity are events being held by Assemblymember Carroll and Assemblymember Simon.  

Tomorrow night Assemblymember Carroll holds a virtual panel with leading reading experts from the Haskins Global Literacy Hub to learn about free resources to support your child’s learning during COVID-19. The following morning you can get your caffeine or decaffeinated fix while discussing community issues and concerns with Assemblymember Simon in another “Java with Jo Anne.”  

This week, other things are happening, I hope I haven't missed any, but most are listed below my email signature.  

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Indoor dining done after a busy week
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Before I recap any of the other news of the week, if you didn't already hear, unfortunately, Indoor dining will be prohibited starting Monday, December 13th. Indoor dining has reportedly been the main source of COVID-19 infections.
item.content:encoded:
Before I recap any of the other news of the week, if you didn't already hear, unfortunately, Indoor dining will be prohibited starting Monday, December 13th. Indoor dining has reportedly been the main source of COVID-19 infections. This makes it even clearer that we need emergency relief policies to help our restaurants and small businesses; sustain themselves or there won't be places left to go to when the pandemic is finally over. 

I know I want the vaccine to be safely distributed as fast as scientifically possible but first we must survive physically and financially to get there. Speaking of quick, I'll be brief, but as I said we had a busy week inside the CB6 orbit. 

Our Permits & Licenses Committee met, we found out the date for the Gowanus Rezoning certification, and held our final full board meeting of 2020. 

There has been some media coverage of the full board meeting, but if you'd rather watch or rewatch it, you can find all the meeting materials here or on YouTube.

While that was the final board meeting of 2020, we have at least two more committee meetings this year. On Monday, December 21st, our Economic, Waterfront, Community Development, and Housing committee meets, and the week after that, we again have a Permits & Licenses meeting. Beyond that, our first full board meeting of the coming year will be on Wednesday, January 13th. 

However, before all that there are interesting things happening, all at a safe distance and/or virtually, listed below my signature, and I recommend you check them out.

As always, stay safe and have a great weekend!

Mike Racioppo, District Manager

item.title: Recap & Relive
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Before going any further, I’d like to wish all celebrants a Happy Hannukah! I hope this email finds you well after the exhilaration of last night’s board meeting.
item.content:encoded:
Before going any further, I’d like to wish all celebrants a Happy Hannukah! I hope this email finds you well after the exhilaration of last night’s board meeting. It was good to “see” and hear from folks whether they were themselves or making an appearance under an alias

With over 100 attendees, including 38 board members, representatives from all levels of government, and community stakeholders, we had a good turnout. We approved all 5 items on our voting agenda after thoughtful discussion. We heard 2 landmark items, two land-use items, and one liquor license application.  

The landmarks items were both in the Park Slope historic district. At 473 9th Street, the first was to legalize a reduction in size for the 2nd and 3rd-floor windows in a previously approved alteration to the rear facade. The other landmark item was for 282 Garfield Place to amend a Certificate of No Effect and allow new, larger masonry openings at the 2nd and 3rd floors and the penthouse and relocate two stained-glass windows. 

The land use items consisted of one ULURP and one text amendment. The ULURP application was to change the zoning at 300 Huntington Street from an M2-1 to M2-3 to reduce existing parking requirements. The text amendment was for the Department of City’s planning proposed Waterfront Text Amendment for Zoning for Coastal Flood Resiliency.

As for the liquor license, it was for a new Mediterranean restaurant at 285 Nevins Street. The community may already be familiar with the operators of this restaurant as they also run the very popular French Louie and Buttermilk Channel. 

If that brief overview of last night’s meeting left you want to view it or relive it, you can watch it here on Youtube and get ahead of the pack for the January general board meeting by registering here. If committee meetings are what you crave, register for the December 21st Economic, Waterfront, Community Development, and Housing meeting here, and you’ll be all set to hear about plans for Governors Island and more as the agenda develops. 

Some things are happening inside and outside CB6’s sphere of influence that you’ll find listed below my email signature, and I recommend you check them out. 

No matter what, stay safe and enjoy the rest of your Thursday.

item.title: Board Meeting Tomorrow, Certified Next Year
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: You can register and see the meeting agenda here. As previewed yesterday, and due to our Permits and Licenses committee approval, the agenda is now set and includes the liquor license request for 285 Nevins Street.
item.content:encoded:
You can register and see the meeting agenda here. As previewed yesterday, and due to our Permits and Licenses committee approval, the agenda is now set and includes the liquor license request for 285 Nevins Street. There’s a lot more on the agenda, so we will have to move quickly unless folks want to zoom well into the night.

Speaking of agendas, our most significant charter mandated role will be activated in 2021. The Department of City Planning made its much-anticipated announcement that they plan to certify the Gowanus Neighborhood Plan on January 19th, 2021. At that point, our public review, as part of what is known as the Uniform Land Use Review Process (ULURP), begins

It feels like a long time ago (and it was), but I'm looking forward to getting answers to things we laid out in the close to 30 pages of scoping questions and comments we submitted back in the spring of 2019. If you want to see those questions along with our other statements regarding the pending rezoning, click here.

We will undoubtedly have several post-certification meetings in addition to the precertification meetings held over the past few weeks, and I’m optimistic that DCP staff members will be regular presenters at the meetings.

The pending Gowanus rezoning is the most extensive rezoning of the Mayor’s term and the most significant thing, as far as land use, that’s been before CB6 in my time and maybe ever. While this is a necessary process under the City Charter, we have a solemn obligation to our community and city, so it is critical that we as a board focus on the proposal's content.

Anyway, that’s all I’ve got to say, for now, don’t forget tomorrow night's board meeting, stay safe and have a good Tuesday.

item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well as we head into what’s expected to be a rainy and possibly snowy weekend.

Last night our Landmarks/ Land Use Committee met and made recommendations to approve all four agenda items. The first two were landmark items in Park Slope, followed by two Land Use Items. The first of those was a presentation from the Department of City (DCP)on a text amendment for Zoning for Coastal Flood Resiliency. The second was a ULURP application for a mixed-use at 300 Huntington Street for a reduction in parking requirements and a change from M2-1 to M2-3. If that description left you wanting more, you can watch the meeting on YouTube and check out all the meeting materials here. These items will now move to a vote at our General Board meeting this coming Wednesday.

However, before Wednesday, we’ve got our Permits and Licenses committee meeting on Monday with a liquor license application that will also end up on Wednesday's agenda. So it’s safe to say next week like this one was, will be another typically busy one in our community.

So I’ll stop and suggest you keep reading on and stay safe and have a great weekend whether you keep reading this newsletter or not.

item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well as our COVID-19 rate continues to climb. We’re up to a 7 day percent positivity rate of 5.19%. So please do all that you can to stay safer and lower that rate. There is increasingly good news regarding the COVID-19 vaccine, and some New Yorkers may receive it by December 15th. Of course, this all would be a lot easier if we had a  Government, especially at the federal level, that met the moment with policies that alleviated so much excess pain during this pandemic.

Anyway, returning to the CB6 virtual orbit last night was, as had been mentioned many times in this space, DCP’S precertification presentation dealing with Gowanus Infrastructure improvements. You relive the magic all here on Youtube or via this Google folder, which, like the Public Place meeting materials, includes the attendance, chat, and presentation. item.title: 3 for 1
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Last night the Gowanus CAG, as announced in previous newsletters, met via zoom. The EPA let it be known that some changes were made to the dredging sequence, but these changes would not slow the momentum of the substantial clean up that is…
item.content:encoded:
Last night the Gowanus CAG, as announced in previous newsletters, met via zoom. The EPA let it be known that some changes were made to the dredging sequence, but these changes would not slow the momentum of the substantial clean up that is now underway. The change was due to unanticipated site conditions. It should also be noted that all environmental-monitoring data will be regularly posted to gowanussuperfund.com.

Meanwhile, the EPA Project Manager is setting what he considers to be a very generous timeframe for the smaller stormwater retention tank to be operational by 2028 and the larger tank by 2028 or 2029. The EPA continues to suggest that the City change its land use and acquisition approach concerning the larger tank. 

Shifting from the recent past to the near future, we’ve got a lot going on this evening. One thing canal related, another EPA linked, and another safety-related. One could argue that all of these are interrelated, and they are certainly all important to our community. However, in this case, I am referring to 3 zoom meetings taking place tonight. 

At 6 PM, with a CB6 assist, the Department of City Planning's next pre-certification meeting and presentation will focus on Gowanus infrastructure. At 6:30 PM the Parks Department and & EPA will be giving an update on the Red Hook ball field’s remediation while the 76th Precinct Community Council, chaired by our very own Jerry Armer, will meet on zoom as well. 

As noted before, you can attend all three so that you couldn’t pre-pandemic, but either way, I will share any information I receive on these meetings ASAP. We also have our Landmarks meeting tomorrow, and our December General Board meeting is one week from tonight. 

Of course, I assume everyone else sincerely misses being able to meet in person. When we can, I don’t think I'll ever complain about a projector screen not being down or some other slight inconvenience again. 

Anyway, stay safe, read on, and enjoy the rest of your Wednesday.

item.title: Virtually Essential
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Welcome to this year's final month. I hope this email finds you well in light of the problems our city still faces.
item.content:encoded:
Welcome to this year's final month. I hope this email finds you well in light of the problems our city still faces.

The Covid-19 seven-day positivity rate is now 4.14, and the daily rate is

at 5.72 percent. So it makes sense that the Governor is saying we may hit "PAUSE" again, and the city's health commissioner, Dr. Dave Chokshi, issued a new advisory. The advisory states that older adults and those with conditions that put them at high risk for COVID-related illness stay at home and limit all activities except for medical or essential purposes.

We are pleased to provide forums where our wise elders still fully participate. Virtual meetings are the place to be. For example, tonight, the Gowanus CAG meets, and tomorrow we've got a busy night. Under the CB6 umbrella, we're a Zoom conduit for the Department of City Planning's next pre-certification meeting and presentation, which will focus on Gowanus infrastructure. Unfortunately, at the same time, the Parks Department and & EPA will be giving an update on the remediation of the Red Hook ball field while the 76th Precinct Community Council, chaired by our very own Jerry Armer, will meet at 7:30 pm.

Fortunately, in this modern world, you can "attend" all three without leaving your home. Another possibly good aspect is that by receiving this newsletter, you're guaranteed I'll share any information I get with you.

Read on, stay safe, and enjoy the rest of your Tuesday.

Best,

item.title: Foreseeable Future
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope everyone had a good Thanksgiving and started the holiday season on a positive Covid negative note. As COVID-19 numbers rise, we aren't out of the woods by any stretch of the imagination.
item.content:encoded:
I hope everyone had a good Thanksgiving and started the holiday season on a positive Covid negative note. As COVID-19 numbers rise, we aren't out of the woods by any stretch of the imagination. If anything, we can expect, after the traveling people did for Thanksgiving, the inevitable increase in infections.

However, there does seem to be some good news on the vaccine front, with some front line workers being vaccinated as soon as December 21st. That would make for a pleasant solstice celebration. However, we’re not there yet, we've had an Astrozenica setback, and we have to maintain protocols, like virtual meetings, for the foreseeable future. We have such meetings taking place this week and next. 

On Wednesday, December 2nd, we serve as the Zoom conduit for the Department of City Planning's next pre-certification meeting. It will be the same format as the previous DCP presentation. The difference is that, instead of a public place, the topic will be Gowanus infrastructure improvements. You can join the hundreds already registered here. Unfortunately, at the same time, the Parks Department and & EPA will be giving an update on the Red Hook ball fields. You can register for that here. As I told you last week, I’ll share the information I get from both for you to absorb at your convenience.

On Thursday, December 3rd, we have a crowded agenda for our Landmarks/ Land Use committee meeting. It includes landmark items, a DCP presentation of an update on the proposed zoning text amendment Zoning for Coastal Flood Resiliency, and a ULURP application for a mixed-use site at 300 Huntington Street.Next week, one week from tonight, our Permits & Licenses committee will meet while our General Board meeting is Wednesday, December 9th. 

In other non-board but area related activities, the Gowanus CAG meets tomorrow, Tuesday, December 1st. 

Of Citywide note, one week from today, as announced yesterday, school buildings will be reopening for in-person learning on Monday, December 7th. We trust that will not be a day that will live in infamy.

You can find more information on these items below my signature. If you stop reading, I’d still hope that you have a good Monday and stay safe.

item.title: Setting, Thanking, Expanding
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Unfortunately, the literal sunset isn't the only one taking place. Sadly former Mayor David Dinkins passed away at the age of 93.
item.content:encoded:
Unfortunately, the literal sunset isn't the only one taking place. Sadly former Mayor David Dinkins passed away at the age of 93. I was fortunate enough to meet Mayor Dinkins a few times and discuss our shared love of tennis. I offer my deepest condolences to his family and to the many people who knew and admired him.

Mayor Dinkins famously called New York City a beautiful mosaic. I hope we as a community honor his legacy by making choices that reinforce and expand upon his vision for New York City.

The first step is to understand better his role in shaping the city we live in today. I hope that in death, people rediscover Mayor Dinkins' achievements and impact. Remembering that community policing started the crime rate falling throughout the 90s and that and other policies for which his dye stained successor took credit was primarily attributable to him.  

On that note, I'll stop typing and recommend checking out the items below my signature and stay safe as we prepare to give thanks.

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Rituals, Rev, Meet
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well after the weekend and before the beginning of the holiday season. I'm interested to see, out of sheer curiosity, in a year in which days blend, will the holiday season be notable in an uplifting or Covid…
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well after the weekend and before the beginning of the holiday season. I'm interested to see, out of sheer curiosity, in a year in which days blend, will the holiday season be notable in an uplifting or Covid spreading way? 

An indicator of people maintaining holiday-related rituals is our packed airports and the remarkably long Covid tests lines. I've got no inherent problem with rituals, but I hope these behaviors don't intensify Covid's second wave.

Either way, the only certainty is a persistent lack of clarity about what measures will be taken, what’s potentially remaining open or will be required to close. Pick a color from our (Red, Orange, Yellow) zone-based system? Industry based? Schools closed based on localized infection rates? I don’t know, but if it gets to that point, or any such changes are made, I’ll share whatever info I get. 

This week, in deference to Thanksgiving, we are light on meetings. We will be revving right back up in the first two weeks of December. So I recommend marking your calendar for next Wednesday, December 2nd, for DCP’s Gowanus infrastructure presentation and Thursday, December 3rd for our Landmarks/ Land Use meeting. 

I also recommend reading below my email signature. But even if you choose not to stay safe while enjoying the rest of your Monday.

item.title: Opinions, Orbiting, Options
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: In the CB6 universe, we held and/or co-sponsored 4 meetings. The first was on Monday with our Economic, Waterfront, Community Development committee meeting and after that, on Tuesday we co-sponsored a Heat/Cool Smart meeting, Wednesday was…
item.content:encoded:
In the CB6 universe, we held and/or co-sponsored 4 meetings. The first was on Monday with our Economic, Waterfront, Community Development committee meeting and after that, on Tuesday we co-sponsored a Heat/Cool Smart meeting, Wednesday was our General Board meeting and last night with over 400 attendees we co-sponsored the DCP led the presentation on Public Place/ Gowanus Green.

There has been some coverage of the meeting, but if you’d rather watch or re-watch it you can find all the meeting materials here or on Youtube. In the most condensed summary possible the meeting and presentation were about the news that the city’s plans are for about 950 units all of which will be below market rate aka affordable housing together with space set aside for a school and 1.5 acres of open space. Regarding the ever-important question “affordable for whom?” at least half of the project’s apartments will be for households earning less than half of area median income(AMI). That translates into roughly an income of $50,000 for a family of three. In addition, I'm happy to report that 15% of the units will be set aside for the formerly homeless.

As is the case with any proposal of this magnitude there were a lot of varied and thoughtful opinions expressed. In this case, those included outright opposition with the suggestion of alternative uses and suggested alterations based on the proposal. Sadly there were some inappropriate comments that I hope, as a community, we will all refrain from making going forward. The next opportunity to redeem ourselves by exhibiting universal civility will be on December 2nd when DCP will present on Gowanus Infrastructure. 

Speaking of future meetings we have committee meetings coming up on December 3rd (Landmarks/Land Use) and December 7th (Permits & Licenses). Our next General Board Meeting will be held on December 9th. All three of these meetings will be via zoom and their agendas are still in formation. 

With that, I will recommend you check out the items below my email signature, enjoy the weekend, and stay safe. 

Related tools

Mike Racioppo, District Manager

Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Yesterday, Today, Tonight
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well as we continue apace with meetings on this 19th day of November. It was great to “see” so many folks last night at our November board meeting.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well as we continue apace with meetings on this 19th day of November. It was great to “see” so many folks last night at our November board meeting. We started things off by hearing from Assembly Robert Carroll and District 15 Schools Superintendent Anita Skop. Superintendent Skop wasn’t originally on the agenda but was gracious enough to adjust her schedule and speak with us after the late announcement that school buildings would be closed starting today. All students will shift to remote learning. School buildings will be closed, at least through the Thanksgiving holiday, so that the earliest they could reopen is November 30th.

We appreciate Anita making time for us as I think it’s safe to say her plate is full with Covid-19 related issues and the education she is charged with providing. She gave encouraging examples of the ongoing work of her administrators, teachers, and staff.

After Anita spoke, we made our way through the agenda. We approved all agenda items. Starting with our board officers (congratulations to each of you), followed by approval of a liquor license application, a landmark item, an assessment of District Needs with recommendations for the city’s budget, and finally 2 Red Hook related transportation items. We also heard from Assemblymember Simon, Senator Kavanagh, and reps from Comptroller Stringers office, Councilman Lander, Senator Myrie and Congresswoman Velasquez. If you want to relive the magic, it’s all here on Youtube. 

During the meeting, there was also a reminder about tonight’s Zoom based presentation from DCP & HPD on the Public Place/ Gowanus Green presentation. It gets started at 6 PM, and a few hundred folks have already registered for it. 

Before that meeting, I’d recommend checking out the items below my signature, and please stay safe.

item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Last night, as previewed in the newsletter leading up to it and on social media, our Economic, Waterfront, Community, Development, and Housing Committee met. If you weren’t able to make it or want to relive the magic, you can watch the…
item.content:encoded:
Last night, as previewed in the newsletter leading up to it and on social media, our Economic, Waterfront, Community, Development, and Housing Committee met. If you weren’t able to make it or want to relive the magic, you can watch the meeting and go over the presentations by clicking here. A big thank you to everyone who attended and presented from the Citizens Housing & Planning Council and the Department of City Planning (DCP). Tonight we are co-sponsoring the Heat/Cool Smart webinar, and thank you to our Environmental Committee Co-Chair Angelica Ramdhari for making this happen. 

Tomorrow night, Wednesday, November 18th, at 6:30 PM, we’ll hold our General Board Meeting Via Zoom. On Thursday, November 19th, starting at 6 PM, we are, for lack of a better term, a “Zoom Conduit” for DCP & HPD as they present and take questions regarding the updated Public Place/Gowanus Green Development proposal. You may have seen and heard about this on some kiosks around town. 

Those meetings, since they part of our virtual reality, won’t be impacted by Covid spikes or snowstorms. There will still be in-person learning at least for tomorrow at NYC Schools as the COVID test positivity rate remains under 3%. The City’s infection rate dropped .3% to 2,74%. That’s still perilously close to the 3% that would make all schools shift to remote learning. However, as we saw in the fall, our plans & policies can change, so we’ll keep you posted. As a community, let’s keep up the excellent work as our rates are remaining low, and in some zip codes, rates are dropping. 

Anyway, I hope you keep reading beyond my email signature, maybe read up on cynicism ceding to joy and find out more about what’s happening across our community. As always, I hope you and yours stay safe. 

Best,

item.title: Rules, Rides, Reflections
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well as we head into the foreboding of a Friday, the 13th weekend. As has been noted elsewhere, the most recent instance of the 13th day of a month landing on a Friday was back in March.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well as we head into the foreboding of a Friday, the 13th  weekend. As has been noted elsewhere, the most recent instance of the 13th day of a month landing on a Friday was back in March. I know I’m not alone in having a tough time distinguishing between days in the time of Covid-19, but March 13th was when the city declared a state of emergency. 

I wish the parallels ended there. Unfortunately, cases are rising once again, with the citywide rate going from 2.60% to 2.72% since yesterday. If the rate goes up to 3%, schools could have to switch to entirely remote learning as soon as Monday. If any such announcements are made, I’m sure media outlets with a bigger reach than this newsletter will report, but I’ll let you know as well. 

The infection rates are low in CB6 and have even dropped in some zip codes to our community’s credit and good fortune. However, we don’t live in closed-off zip codes or districts; we live in and share a city with millions of people. We can also keep doing our part to make our rates even lower by rigorously following all safety protocols. 

Looking to the week ahead, since they are zoom based, CB6 associated meetings are Covid resistant and will not be impacted. I say “associated” because we have official CB6 meetings and are also co-sponsor of other important meetings. On Monday, our Economic, Waterfront, Community, Development, and Housing Committee meets, and on Wednesday, we have our General Board meeting. On Tuesday night, we are co-sponsors of a Heat/Cool Smart webinar, and of course, Thursday, beginning at 6 PM, the Department of City Planning will present on plans for the "Public Place" site. 

On that note, I’ll recommend you read on past my email signature, take note of new night-time restrictions, and stay safe!

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Percentage, Public & Places
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well, even in the face of the rise in COVID infections. We aren’t yet at the levels we saw in the spring, but there are similarities.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well, even in the face of the rise in COVID infections. We aren’t yet at the levels we saw in the spring, but there are similarities. I hope I am wrong about the implications of the Governor's slow-walking arbitrary restrictions. Specifically, starting tomorrow, all bars, restaurants, and gyms will be required to close at, or before, 10 PM. Beware of the virus at 10:01 PM. Along with those changes, private gatherings, whether indoors or outdoors, are limited to 10 people. 

To our community’s credit and good fortune, the infection rates are low in CB6. However, we don’t live in closed-off zip codes or districts; we live in and share a city with millions of people. Citywide, the percentage of positive tests has risen to 2.60%, and at the rate, it’s been rising, close to .10 percent a day; we will hit 3 percent early next week.

If we do hit 3 percent, all city schools would then shift to remote learning. It would likely lead to more restrictions on dining and other businesses, and with it, more job losses and more pain for those that can least afford it. It is a no-brainer that we need federal aid on the scale of the Heroes Act and state legislation such as Assemblymember Carroll’s Business Interruption Insurance bill. 

Let me hop off my soapbox for now and get more CB6 centric. One week from tonight, the Department of City Planning will present on proposed plans for the Public Place/Gowanus Green site beginning at 6 PM. We are “co-sponsoring” the meeting, but it is not a committee or full board meeting. We are serving as a “Zoom Conduit” to enable the community to participate as much as possible at this pre-certification stage. 

With that, I recommend that you keep scrolling so you can find some exciting items and happenings this week and next. 

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Congrats, Covid, Continue
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: First, a reminder/clarification that, since tomorrow is Veterans Day, our board is not meeting on it’s usually scheduled second Wednesday of the month. Instead, it will be held next Wednesday, November 18th, at 6:30 PM.
item.content:encoded:
First, a reminder/clarification that, since tomorrow is Veterans Day, our board is not meeting on it’s usually scheduled second Wednesday of the month. Instead, it will be held next Wednesday, November 18th, at 6:30 PM. It’s great to see that, based on the over one hundred people already registered, civic interest seems to be increasing, but I apologize if this schedule throws anyone off.

Moving to less mundane matters, I’d like to congratulate all of those honored by our Borough President today as Brooklyn Covid Heroes. Those honored included Dr. Fauci and our friends at the Gowanus Dredgers Canoe Club, Redemption Church, Red Hook Relief and CB6 member, and incoming Warren Street Tenant Association president Joe Ann Brown. Our community is indeed lucky to have them. 

Speaking of COVID, we are still seeing a steady increase and fearing and nearing another shutdown. Schools shifting to fully remote learning and the city no longer allowing indoor dining, are some of the first things that will happen if we don’t flatten the curve out once again. So, for the sake of students, local businesses and everything else we care about, please stay safe, keep your distance, and wear a mask.

While not a safety precaution, I recommend scrolling down and checking out the items, including notice of three meetings happening next week that appear below my signature.

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager

item.title: Celebrating, Stopping, Safety
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: As always, I hope this email finds you well. From the moment the winner of the presidential election was announced, the weekend became a surreal celebratory scene across our community and city.
item.content:encoded:
As always, I hope this email finds you well. From the moment the winner of the presidential election was announced, the weekend became a surreal celebratory scene across our community and city. I don’t know what my mental capacity will be for the rest of my life, but I can’t see myself forgetting the celebrations, and the only time horns honking didn’t irritate me. 

However, while even a cynic like me enjoyed the celebration, we mustn’t lose sight of the downside of large gatherings. There is a new wave of COVID infections. Nearly all of our metrics to assess the spread of the virus have ticked up passed worrying thresholds. The 7-day rolling average test positivity rate is 2.26% citywide and far higher in some hotspot neighborhoods. Fortunately, the average in CB6 zip codes is lower, but that will only remain the reality if we stay vigilant up to and even after getting the vaccine that seems to be coming out of the phase three trial.

I’ll end with that and recommend reading below my email signature to find out some more happenings for the week. Lastly, when it’s safe and legal to meet in person again, I’ll see if we can arrange a meeting amid plantings at The Four Seasons.

Enjoy the rest of your Monday. 

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201

item.title: Opting, Blending, Spinning
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Please excuse the lateness, but I’ve learned from Nevada that it’s best to “keep em waiting.” As easy as it is, at least for me, to get wrapped up in absorbing all available absentee ballot info, it’s essential to take a deep breath and…
item.content:encoded:
Please excuse the lateness, but I’ve learned from Nevada that it’s best to “keep em waiting.” As easy as it is, at least for me, to get wrapped up in absorbing all available absentee ballot info, it’s essential to take a deep breath and remember the earth is still spinning. Not only is it still turning, but COVID-19 is spreading to new highs across the country and is also ticking up here in the city. The 7-day infection rate average is 1.81 and is headed in the wrong direction. The Mayor, when discussing these numbers, said that “We’ve got to buckle down and push these numbers back.”. 

In this instance, the Mayor is right, and we do need to buckle down, and that means limiting possible exposure to Covid-19. Keeping that in mind, we’ve written to the Mayor and Chancellor asking that the Department of Education not rush parental decision making and so create an additional opt-in period for families to go from Remote to Blended learning in early 2021. As of now, the only enrollment period ends on November 15th. As our letter states, they are forcing families to choose as cases rise creates a situation in which some may want to blend in but are hesitant to take that risk.

We’re not the only ones with this perspective, as we’ve signed on in support of PS321’s School Leadership Team's petition. If you, or a school, would like to sign on, you can do so here.

Anyway, I’ll stop here and recommend checking out what’s going on past my email signature. Please check out the items below and note that two weeks from tonight, DCP will present on Public Place.

Related tools

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201

I don't know about anyone else, but I'm tired of repeatedly refreshing my web browser and alternating between Kornacki & King.
