item.title: In Session, In Nature, In Transit
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: We inch closer to “reopening,” but even when we do, there’s likely to be a new normal that includes mask-wearing for the foreseeable future. This should be the expectation until some guarantee of safety via vaccine or proven (bleach free )…
item.content:encoded:
We inch closer to “reopening,” but even when we do, there’s likely to be a new normal that includes mask-wearing for the foreseeable future. This should be the expectation until some guarantee of safety via vaccine or proven (bleach free ) treatments, as it’s the safest route we’ve got and remember, while not as dramatic, or profitable, as mask-wearing superheroes, doing so saves lives.

As always, I write this hoping it finds you well. While there is no legislative anniversary equivalent to yesterday’s 85th New Deal Anniversary, our state legislature’s back in session and there is always the possibility it will make history of its own. Hopefully, policies to help tenants, landlords, and businesses become law sooner than later. One example, at the state level, would be Assemblymember Carroll’s Business Interruption bill and at the federal level, Congresswoman Maloney’s bill .

There are more things “in session” listed below as well as some reminders and natural resources. If you choose to check them out, that’s great, but no matter what you decide to do, enjoy the rest of your Thursday.

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Too Much Loss, Need Something New
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: While local statistics such as deaths, infections, hospitalizations, and other measures of the COVID-19 pandemic move in the right direction, as a country, we have now lost 100,000 thousand people with the death toll continuing to climb.…
item.content:encoded:
While local statistics such as deaths, infections, hospitalizations, and other measures of the COVID-19 pandemic move in the right direction, as a country, we have now lost 100,000 thousand people with the death toll continuing to climb. To all those who lost anyone to this vicious virus, I offer my deepest condolences and sympathy. 

I know every weekday, at some point, you receive an email from me expressing the hope that it finds you well followed by, especially during this crisis, some policy ideas, and a heads up about resources listed below my email signature. However, it is only today that I can remind you that it was on this date in 1935, that FDR without pause signed the New Dea l into law. I mention this not just to highlight a significant historical event, but because we are in need of bold policy's mirroring the thought that went into crafting the New Deal, if we are to work our way back and, hopefully, reach a better place. 

Whether that means some form of a WPA program , or other options for aiding our restaurant and entertainment industries, and reinforcing our city’s industrial capacity , it is a call for action. No matter what, it’s going to take a lot, hopefully starting with the passage of the Heroes Act . Our vulnerabilities were exposed and exacerbated by the pandemic, but they were there and called for a remedy.

More information, including more basic reminders and resources, can be found by scrolling on down. If you choose to check them out, that’s great, but no matter what you decide to do, enjoy the rest of your Wednesday. 

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Upcoming, Alternate, Reality
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well on this Tuesday that might feel like a Monday but is just one big blur. Anyway, I hope you took some time to reflect and then enjoyed Memorial Day, as well as the previous 2 days that made up the weekend.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well on this Tuesday that might feel like a Monday but is just one big blur. Anyway, I hope you took some time to reflect and then enjoyed Memorial Day, as well as the previous 2 days that made up the weekend.

The COVID-19 crisis continues with regions closer to us and even land masses to which we are attached, such as Long Island, beginning to open up . Also, when things do “open,” keeping our distance and covering our faces will still be a key to staying open until a vaccine is found. 

When a vaccine is found, I’m sure you’ll hear about it before my newsletter makes mention of it, but I doubt that source will give you updates on the Alternate Side Parking regulations. Speaking of Alternate Side regulations, they are suspended until June 7th , while parking meters remain in effect. 

Items, such as parking regulations and upcoming zooms, are included below.

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Howard Beale, Beaches, Businesses
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I don't think I have ever worn or would wear white pants, but in years past, I probably would have started with some, attempted, humor on how Memorial Day weekend means its socially acceptable to wear them until Labor Day. This year, with…
item.content:encoded:
I don't think I have ever worn or would wear white pants, but in years past, I probably would have started with some, attempted, humor on how Memorial Day weekend means its socially acceptable to wear them until Labor Day. This year, with all the pain we're experiencing, we solemnly, with respect and appreciation, remember all those who gave their lives for our country.

What we are experiencing is a health crisis that has led to an economic crisis . Just like the audience in Network didn't need Howard Beale to tell them things were bad , I doubt anyone reading this email needs me to highlight such facts unless it's as a cathartic scream.

However, there is some hope for a vaccine ; thresholds for reopening and virtual meetings to be had. You can read about those and other items of potential use and interest below. 

If you have questions about any of those items, I will try my best to answer and direct you as best I can. No matter what, stay safe, remember that alternate side parking will be suspended this upcoming week, order directly from restaurants, and enjoy the unofficial start of summer at a safe distance.  

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Registrations, Reminders, Waves & Spikes
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: There is one month left in spring, and a month and 2 days until the June 23 rd election. I love voting and reminding people to vote, so here’s another reminder to click this link so you can vote by mail and here to find out what will be on…
item.content:encoded:
There is one month left in spring, and a month and 2 days until the June 23 rd election. I love voting and reminding people to vote, so here’s another reminder to click this link so you can vote by mail and here to find out what will be on your ballot. I’d recommend doing this ASAP as the city’s Board of Elections Board of Election is not known for its speed or even envelope supply.  

While some of the numbers regarding COVID-19 move in the right direction, we still have to stay safe and at a distance with our faces covered. I understand not wanting to do this, but just because we want something to be over, unfortunately, that doesn’t mean it is over. I’d recommend looking at the waves and infection spikes that occurred from 1918 until 1920 to gain some context for what’s happening right now .  This isn't negativity I’m highlighting it so take our best shot at a safe and sustainable recovery. To reinforce my positive altitude, get some (non-bleach) based hope here . 

In the more immediate future, Alternate Side Parking regulations are back in effect tomorrow, and in a bit later on today, Congresswoman Clarke will be hosting a virtual town hall for small businesses and nonprofits. Speaking of virtual events, you can register here for our June 17th “Check-in.”

Related tools

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: An Old Friend, A Town Hall, SYEP
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I’ll be brief but just wanted to highlight a few items as quarantine fatigue seems to set in, and we hope for a safe “reopening” sooner than later.
item.content:encoded:
I’ll be brief but just wanted to highlight a few items as quarantine fatigue seems to set in, and we hope for a safe “reopening” sooner than later.

First, our old friend, the Gowanus Rezoning, is back in the news but only to acknowledge it's in limbo (there is still a hold on ULURP's ) and perhaps even farther than before from being certified. On the less wide-reaching, but more immediately impactful, Alternate Side Parking regulations are suspended tomorrow, Thursday, May 21st, but will be in effect Friday. 

Also happening tomorrow, Congresswoman Yvette Clarke will be hosting a Small Business & Non-Profit Town Hall that you can register for here. The town hall is being held in partnership with Congressmembers Hakeem Jeffries & Nydia Velasquez, Councilmember Lander, and Assemblymember Carroll.

If you feel that registering for one event isn’t enough for today, register for our June 17th “Check-In” here like over 50 people have done already. I'm sure that during the “Check- in” the city budget, which is due June 31st, will come up. A big issue surrounding the budget is whether or not the Summer Youth Employment Program(SYEP) will be funded and the City Council held a hearing on it today. For that reason, I think it’s appropriate to highlight that we were on the record opposing these cuts when they first announced in April.

There are some more useful items below, so I welcome you to read on, but no matter what, stay safe and enjoy the rest of your Wednesday.

Related tools

Mike Racioppo, District Manager

item.title: Closed beaches, Summer School, Freelance
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well on this Sunny Spring Tuesday. With the weather being all over the place, just over a week ago it was near freezing, I’ve lost any seasonal sense.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well on this Sunny Spring Tuesday. With the weather being all over the place, just over a week ago it was near freezing, I’ve lost any seasonal sense. I didn’t realize this coming weekend (Memorial Day Weekend) was the unofficial start of summer until I was asked to confirm that beaches would be closed . Of course, the official start of summer arrives on June 21st, just four days after our June 17th “check-in.” You can register for it here . But a lot is happening before that as we navigate “ reopening ” our city. 

Reopening safely requires proper policies and enforcement. That means funding hopefully from the Heroes Act for such things as street usage , summer school , and more. For too many now, it, unfortunately, means navigating Unemployment Insurance. Thousands are still waiting to collect. An overwhelming percentage of those still waiting are freelancers ( 84% of freelancers haven’t received any benefits ). With that in mind, I spoke with Rafael Espinal, Executive Director of the Freelancers Union today, about his organization's efforts in helping freelancers during this crisis, as well as what folks can do to help or help themselves. He recommended reaching out to them and using resources designed that are designed specifically for freelancers . 

If you scroll down, you’ll find some items of potential interest, use, and other happenings. If you don’t scroll down, I’ll take no offense and wish you the best until tomorrow when I’ll make a similar suggestion.

item.title: 1st Draft
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I guess it’s not surprising that, in the midst of the COVID-19 pandemic, people seek out or draw historical parallels in the hopes of finding a bit of guidance or historicsl context for what we’re going through. The most “apples to apples”…
item.content:encoded:
I guess it’s not surprising that, in the midst of the COVID-19 pandemic, people seek out or draw historical parallels in the hopes of finding a bit of guidance or historicsl context for what we’re going through. The most “apples to apples” comparison seems to be the 1918 flu epidemic. While the historical details of it are undoubtedly interesting, what’s I’ve found most surprising is that there’s a great deal of writing on how it faded from society’s collective memory, almost like a past fad or trend. Decades later, when asked about this, the writer HL Mencken said: “The human mind always tries to expunge the intolerable from memory, just as it tries to conceal it while current.”.

It seems to me that Mencken is correct. Nobody with the possible exception of those profiteering off of it could conceivably want to experience this crisis again, and denial can serve a rational purpose in that case. But we should admit that there are problems that are now glaring that could have been avoided before this crisis had we been paying proper attention and should not be swept back out of sight when our ongoing crisis is over. 

As it is not over, keep your distance, cover your face, and, if you have a car, no matter what block you’re on (yes, that means open streets, as well), move it as per Alternate Side Parking regulations that were again updated today. I have no idea why or how this specific policy was changed on “open streets,” but regardless, it is the policy, and nobody wants to see an orange envelope on their windshield. I just hope DOT remembers to be more communicative throughout the rest of this crisis and beyond. 

Speaking of communication, on a much better note, I texted with Congresswoman Clarke today regarding the Heroes Act as she and her colleagues are working to make sure the bill they passed Friday becomes law. If and hopefully, when passed into law, it would prevent millions from suffering further, and the suffering should not be compounded by inaction.

The Heroes Act will also impact the city’s budget , which is due June 31st. The budget will certainly be a topic at our June 17th “Check-In.” You join the nearly 40 people who have already signed up here.

There’s another link to sign up below, along with other items of use and interest below my email signature, but you’re under no obligation to check any of them. So either way, stay safe and enjoy the rest of the day. 

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201

item.title: A loss, Pause, Check- In
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Sadly, I begin with the news of a loss for our CB6 and Red Hook communities as Carolyn Broughton, the sister of CB6 member and Secretary Karen Broughton, has lost her life to the COVID-19 virus. As Assemblymember Felix Ortiz noted, the…
item.content:encoded:
Sadly, I begin with the news of a loss for our CB6 and Red Hook communities as Carolyn Broughton, the sister of CB6 member and Secretary Karen Broughton, has lost her life to the COVID-19 virus. As Assemblymember Felix Ortiz noted, the Broughton family’s dedication to our community has spanned generations. We, as a community, and indeed as a Community Board, were fortunate to have had Karen and Carolyn's mother, Emma as a board member for many years. We have been helped by their dedication and offer our deepest condolences and sympathy. May Carolyn’s memory be a blessing to all those who knew her. This also serves as a reminder of how serious, and close to home, this ongoing crisis is.

The ongoing crisis is why the “ PAUSE ” has been extended through May 28th for those of us here in New York City, while some regions of the state “reopen.” The only way, until there is an effective and available vaccine , to get through this and be able to return to a semblance of normal is by continuing to keep our distance and covering our faces. This will save lives, and it’s not “ emasculating ” or other such nonsense.

There has been significant support but also a great deal of opposition, from every perspective to the city’s new open street plans. I repeat that we want to have input on this and hope DOT allows that to happen. Either way, no matter what your thoughts on the program are, I’d recommend letting DOT know and if you’d like copying me on the email. I will also continue to share any comments directly with the appropriate agencies. 

Agencies, including DOT, have a good track record of being part of our community check-ins, and for that, among other reasons, we’re having another one at 6:30 PM on Wednesday, June 17th, via zoom. You can register for it here and now. I’d like to again thank the close to 400 attendees we’ve had at our first 2 “ Check-ins .”Not only is it great to see such civic enthusiasm but, especially when submitting questions in advance, it allows the meetings to be focused on sharing information based around our community’s concerns.

Another place you can find information based on community concerns is below my email signature, so I hope you check it out. Even if you choose not to, stay safe, order from restaurants directly, and have a good weekend.

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Thursday, May 14, 2020
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Good evening I hope this email finds you well as we await some warmer weather. As it gets warmer, people will want to spend more time outside, but it’s still imperative to keep a safe distance (and co
item.content:encoded:
Good evening

I hope this email finds you well as we await some warmer weather.

As it gets warmer, people will want to spend more time outside, but it’s still imperative to keep a safe distance (and cover your face). One of the ways to enable that is by opening up streets for pedestrians. But, of course, how this is determined, and what streets are opened, is an important and difficult question. It’s a new process and as such is a work in progress, but as we’ve said before , our voices should and still could be made a part of it and hope it is going forward.

The community board has not taken specific policy positions, but I have forwarded questions and comments for clarification. The most common questions that I’ve received boil down to “ Can I move/park my car? Will I still receive deliveries? Can Emergency Vehicles get on the block?”. The answer to that is a resounding “Yes”. I spoke to Commissioner Bray again today and he made clear that residents on these blocks can use their cars to come and go, park, receive deliveries and would be accessible to a fire truck, ambulance or any other emergency vehicle. Also, while Alternate Side Parking regulations return next week they will NOT be returning on the designated open streets.

If you have any questions, concerns, or comments let DOT know and I will continue to share your comments as well.

Just like other weekdays there are some interesting items and information below my email signature and I’ll once again say, if you are able to afford ordering from a restaurant, legislation not withstanding , order directly from them. 20% matters.

No matter what you do, stay safe, and enjoy the rest of your Thursday.

item.title: Streets, Seamless, Al Smith,More
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: You may recall that earlier this week, I mentioned " Hope ," and a letter we wrote , urging the city to find a way to regulate 3rd Party Apps such as Seamless to prevent their fees from choking off the only revenue streams restaurants have…
item.content:encoded:
You may recall that earlier this week, I mentioned " Hope ," and a letter we wrote , urging the city to find a way to regulate 3rd Party Apps such as Seamless to prevent their fees from choking off the only revenue streams restaurants have right now. Well, earlier today, the New York City Council passed legislation capping fees at 20%, and the Mayor is expected to sign it into law. Unfortunately, this law caps fees at 20%, which is still double the earlier proposal to cap fees at 10%, but it is a step in the right direction. At 20%, restaurants will still be better off if you order directly, as they need every dollar possible while apps are seeing record profits. 

Also, it is a good time to be looking over the next wave of streets that will be opening across the city, including blocks in our community district. I spoke to DOT's Borough Commissioner today to make clear that more community input on these matters is of the utmost importance as balancing necessary uses and open space isn't easy, but it is important. To quote Al Smith , "the cure for the evils of democracy is more democracy".

Speaking of democracy, vote by mail applications , along with other useful items, are available below, along with other useful items.

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Wednesday, May 13, 2020
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: While the discussion shifts towards reopening, today is a reminder of not only what we’re going through but why we should not rush and risk a second wave. As another Brooklynite made clear today, rushing to ”reopen” would risk needless…
item.content:encoded:
While the discussion shifts towards reopening, today is a reminder of not only what we’re going through but why we should not rush and risk a second wave. As another Brooklynite made clear today, rushing to ”reopen” would risk needless suffering and death . Also, I’m not citing any scientific polling, but it doesn't take a clairvoyant to know we don't want to reopen only to shut down again. So continue to keep your distance and cover your face when you can’t.

Staying “closed” comes at a cost, and we need policies to offset that cost and achieve what could be called “release velocity” for the economy when we do open up. Some of that will have to come as federal aid , but the state and city are looking at what options they have.

One option we all have this year is voting by mail . The same goes for the census, which can be completed right here in under 10 minutes.

Voting, and completing the census, are among the most efficient ways to improve society and we can do both while staying at home. So, if you haven’t yet filled out the census or registered to vote by mail , the time is now. If you already have, maybe remind a friend to do so.

No matter what you choose to do after reading this email, stay safe and enjoy the rest of your Tuesday.

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Monday, May 11, 2020
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: With everything happening, if there was ever a time to yell, “ serenity now ”, it would be today. Having said that, I hope this message finds you well on this, now sunny, previously rain and hail filled, Monday.
item.content:encoded:
With everything happening, if there was ever a time to yell, “ serenity now ”, it would be today. Having said that, I hope this message finds you well on this, now sunny, previously rain and hail filled, Monday. 

We kick off the week with some encouraging infection indicators. Still, if we want to safely “reopen” anytime soon, we all must continue to practice social distancing and cover our faces especially when we can't. Remember, what we do now, during the crisis, will determine our future. That continues to mean keeping a social distance, but also being mindful of other other practices and policies. 

Policies and changes that could or should be made have been a consistent theme of these updates and our " Check - ins ". Keeping that in mind, you may recall that in mid-Ma rc h , we sent a letter looking for a way to suspend fees from 3rd party food apps such as Seamless. Well, Jersey City beat us to it, but there seems to be a reason for hope in the City Council . However, until such laws are enacted here, I’d urge everyone who is fortunate enough to order out to order directly from restaurants, so they don’t get further squeezed. 

If Jersey city can do it, I’m confident New York City can find a solution. I’m not leaving, but Jersey doing something first makes me understand why someone could say “ Howdy East Orange ”.

I hope you stay safe and please check out the information, including an Alternate Side Parking update, below my email signature. 

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: May 8
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you doing as well as could be expected these days. Paraphrasing a great song, it's certainly hard times in New York.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you doing as well as could be expected these days. Paraphrasing a great song, it's certainly hard times in New York.

As New York's COVID-19 numbers continue to move in the right direction in the conversation turns to how we move forward and "reopen." Of course, we can't do so without extensive testing because even if things are "open," when people feel unsafe, it won't matter. The city and state continue to push for more testing but will still need more resources from the federal government for that and much more.

Until the time we are safe, it's still important to keep our distance and cover our faces. It's not a tyrannical demand, but a slight adjustment to protect us all. It can be done. This crisis is not an inevitable consequence of living in a large city. It's noteworthy that Iowa now has more COVID-19 cases than South Korea . 

As always, I hope you find the information below my email signature useful. But either way, Please support local businesses and order directly from restaurants . 

Lastly, I know we are all finding our unique way through this, but I figured I'd mention that I found this article about John Lennon to be helpful, and sometimes radio does the trick. 

Have a good weekend, happy Mother's Day to all the moms, and stay safe. 

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Relive, Recap, Resources
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I'd like to start by thanking everyone, especially the technical support from Brad Lander and his staff, which made our May "Check-in" happen. I appreciate the participation of all the panelists, including State Attorney General, Tish…
item.content:encoded:
I'd like to start by thanking everyone, especially the technical support from Brad Lander and his staff, which made our May "Check-in" happen. I appreciate the participation of all the panelists, including State Attorney General, Tish James , and City Comptroller, Scott Stringe r. We are blown away by the community engagement of the close to 200 "attendees." You can  click here  to relive the magic or see it for the first time via YouTube. Lastly, thanks for all the feedback during and after the "Check-in," which ran the gamut from my lack of a haircut to my favorite hockey team. 

As much as I enjoyed "emceeing," I'd rather have our meetings in person, but of course, this pandemic requires changes and will for at least awhile longer . Some of those changes, especially through policy, were discussed last night, and we covered a lot of topics, including state and city legislation, fiscal matters, the 2020 census, small businesses, schools, streets, buildings , banks , utilities, and hospitals. 

You can find out more about those items by scrolling below my email signature. Still, before that, I'd recommend checking out the Governor's announcement that the State's eviction moratorium is extended until August 20th, as well as this interesting opportunity from NYU's Tandon School of Engineering.

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201

item.title: Restaurants, Registration, Check, Legislation
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I only recalled this afternoon that it's Cinco De Mayo. Failing to remember the significance of a date is one of the most direct ways I'm reminded just how different things are right now.
item.content:encoded:
I only recalled this afternoon that it's Cinco De Mayo.  Failing to remember the significance of a date is one of the most direct ways I'm reminded just how different things are right now. But don't forget why they have to be.

In previous years people would, for better or worse, take the opportunity to crowd into bars and restaurants to celebrate and socialize. Of course, this year, these establishments are limited to take out and delivery orders. I don't think anyone wants businesses, especially independent ones, to have disappeared whenever we "reopen." A way to do that is by ordering directly from these establishments . Another way to help would be through the passage of Assemblymember Carroll's legislation , which would make insurance companies honor their business interruption policy claims,

This legislation is a topic that will certainly be discussed at tomorrow night's "Check-in." The structure will be similar to April's " Check-in ." It will include Councilmember Brad Lander , State Senator Kavanagh , Assemblymembers Carroll & Simon , Comptroller Scott Stringer , and the DOE , DOT , and our district's biggest healthcare provider, NYP Brooklyn Methodist . To be clear, this list is fluid, and we may have some  " Check-in " changes. 

If you keep scrolling, you'll find a mix of interesting items, resources, and reminders. If you stop scrolling, enjoy the rest of the day and stay safe.

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Mistake of 98, Congratulations Congresswoman, Teacher Appreciation
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Never a Stars Wars fan I prefer, as I'm sure most of you do as well, to associate today with the 123rd anniversary of New York's legislature approving the consolidation of the 5 Boroughs that now make up New York City. It didn't go into…
item.content:encoded:
Never a Stars Wars fan I prefer, as I'm sure most of you do as well, to associate today with the 123rd anniversary of New York's legislature approving the consolidation of the 5 Boroughs that now make up New York City. It didn't go into effect until Jan 1st of the following year, which may explain some folks, including deceased relatives of mine, referring to it as the " mistake of 98" . Speaking of mistakes, or potential mistakes, even though COVID-19 numbers have moved in the right direction, we cannot stop keeping a safe and socially appropriate distance as we don't want to face another wave of infections. 

Moving on, congratulations to Congresswoman Nydia Velasquez on her appointment to the House of Representatives Select Committee on the COVID-19. She'll do an excellent job as always with an added personal understanding of the power of the virus. We are thankful for her recovery. Also, when folks are clapping and cheering at 7 PM, please remember that it's Teacher Appreciation Week and that they, along with everyone who is part of our school system, are doing an incredible job under most difficult circumstances. 

Education and closed schools will certainly be discussed during Wednesday's "Check-in."  In addition to the Department of Education, we'll have Councilmember Brad Lander, State Senator Kavanagh, Assemblymembers Carroll & Simon and, Comptroller Scott Stringer. That is the line up "as of now" because this list is still fluid, and like last month , we may have some more folks to " Check-in ."

If you keep scrolling, you'll find a mix of interesting items, resources, and reminders. If you stop scrolling, I hope you enjoy the rest of your Monday and that you stay safe.  

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Tom Joad, Schools, Streets, Sound
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well as we kick off May and head into the weekend with COVID-19 numbers continuing to move the right way .
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well as we kick off May and head into the weekend with COVID-19 numbers continuing to move the right way . 

There are 2 important updates about things we've recently weighed in on. 

First, schools are now officially closed for the remainder of the academic year , while

a decision on summer school will be announced by the end of May. As noted

earlier in the week, whenever school does resume, necessary safety protocols

need to be in place . 

Another issue we have weighed in on is the city's open streets plan and the need for

community input. The first part of that plan has been announced , and the plan

currently indicates that beginning on Monday, May 4th, Prospect Park west from Garfield to 3rd street will be open to pedestrians. I'm sharing information as I get it, and as the process and particulars are made known, I'll share them. As Commissioner Trottenberg noted, this is the first step, and suggestions can be made here.  

I'm sure policies related to schools and street uses, among other topics, will be

discussed during our 2nd "Community Check-in" this Wednesday, May 6th, beginning at 6:30 PM. You can join the 100 or so people that have already registered, by clicking here. Considering today's date and the pain being felt by so many, it's probably worth discussing policies that call to mind the ghost Tom Joad.  

There is more information, including some sounds , if you scroll below my email signature. If this is where you stop reading, stay safe, feel free to share information, and enjoy the weekend.  

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Face & Letter Coverage, 1 AM, 5 AM
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: While the Covid-19 numbers move in the right direction, nobody is just assuming it will remain that without continuous efforts and flexible policies. Two important policy and service updates to take note of are that for the duration of the…
item.content:encoded:
While the Covid-19 numbers move in the right direction, nobody is just assuming it will remain that without continuous efforts and flexible policies. Two important policy and service updates to take note of are that for the duration of the "Pause" subways, to allow for cleaning, will not be running from 1 am until 5 am and starting this Saturday, and the city be distributing free face coverings. 

Of course, those changes are occasioned by the crisis. Maybe it's a product of quarantine fatigue, but I think it's important to also look at new policies for our permanently altered reality. It's going to require consideration of a vast range of ideas and include all aspects of policy making. A prime local example would be the Gowanus Alliance seeing a need for tax relief in the Industrial Business Zone as a very helpful tool in working our way out of this crisis.

Policy possibilities for during & after this crisis will come up at next Wednesday's "Check-in" and if you'd like register do so here . There is more information, including coverage of our letter asking for community input for DOT's open street plans, if you scroll below my email

signature. 

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Upcoming & Optimism
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you as well on this cloudy and unseasonably cold, Wednesday that seems to fit the times.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you as well on this cloudy and unseasonably cold, Wednesday that seems to fit the times.

While we continue to slow the spread of COVID-19, the economy shrinks at an accelerating pace . I don’t say that to be pessimistic; I say it as I remain optimistic. Not just because there is some hope about a new treatment , but by understanding the full scope and impact of this crisis, we as a community can implement necessary policies to get through it with less heartbreak then we foresaw.

Policy discussions will certainly be on the docket a week from today during our 2 nd "Community Check-in" but also tomorrow morning at Assemblymember Simons “Java w/ Jo Anne” and tomorrow evening during Senator Kavanagh’s Town Hall . 

There is more information, including c overage of our letter regarding school safet y and other potentially useful, resources if you scroll past my email signature. If this is where you stop reading, I still hope you stay safe, feel free to share this information however you’d like and make the best of what remains of the day. 

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201

item.title: Letter to the Commissioner, Grading, Java, More
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well on this sunny Tuesday. Before we get started on the daily update, I want to remind you that our small but dedicated district office staff, Ty and Liza, along with myself, even while working remotely, are…
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well on this sunny Tuesday. Before we get started on the daily update, I want to remind you that our small but dedicated district office staff, Ty and Liza, along with myself, even while working remotely, are still interfacing with government and elected officials to deal with all those local issues that were always of concern and may be exacerbated in this crisis. Please continue to email, and we will do our best to be of help.

While the country has now passed 1 million confirmed Covid-19 cases, the trend lines locally continue to move in the right direction. Speaking of moving, especially as the weather continues to become warmer, people are going to be even less inclined to “Stay

Home” but will need to be safe all the same.

As you may have seen mentioned here and elsewhere, the Mayor has announced plans for the city to open at least 40 and possibly up to 100 miles of streets to pedestrians and bicycles as we enter the summer.

In the hope of participating in the process, we sent this letter to the Department of Transportation . The purpose, as the letter states, is to coordinate community input giving the City local knowledge in order to develop and implement the best possible plan while

social distancing guidelines remain in effect. 

I’m sure this plan will come up at next Wednesday’s community check-in. If you haven’t already done so, register here and join the over 100 people who already have signed up.

If you scroll past my email signature, you’ll find useful information such as " Java With Jo Anne " and an updated grading policy for public schools.

I hope you stay safe and that you enjoy the rest of your day and feel free to share this information however you’d like. 

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Safety, Schools, Streets
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Our distancing continues to pay dividends in the form of a decreasing death toll, fewer hospitalizations, and other encouraging COVID-19 numbers. Over the last day, there were 337 deaths , which is the lowest total since March.
item.content:encoded:
Our distancing continues to pay dividends in the form of a decreasing death toll, fewer hospitalizations, and other encouraging COVID-19 numbers. Over the last day, there were 337 deaths , which is the lowest total since March. This total is still horribly high, and just because we are passed an initial surge, we are not through this yet. So we have to remain apart and cover our faces when necessarily out in the world.

However, now is a good time to start figuring out how we may start up again after this “pause.” The Governor and Mayor have sketched outlines for how to do this, but it’s still preliminary. Among the most difficult decisions since the COVID-19 crisis began is how to ensure that we can safely educate the city’s children.

When schools were closed back in March, everyone who is part of our public schools, from students and their parents & guardians, crossing guards, teachers, paraprofessionals, support staff, and administrators, willingly made unprecedented adjustments in their lives and careers. Making sure that when they return to their school building, every step is taken to ensure it’s safe is a public health necessity and the right thing to do. 

For that reason, we wrote this letter to the Mayor on Saturday , indicating that while there can be a reasonable debate in terms of timing for school reopening, having proper safety protocols in place is not up for debate. In the letter, we stated our support for the United Federation of Teachers petition demanding such protocols . 

Schools will certainly be a topic next Wednesday, May 6th, during our Community “Check-in.” If you haven’t already signed up, you can join the over 90 who already have done so by following this link. 

If you scroll past my email signature, you’ll find useful information such as Alternate Side Parking remaining suspended until May 12th. 

I hope you stay safe and that you enjoy the rest of your day and feel free to share this information however you’d like. 

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Range of Ideas, Resources, Reminders
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: One week ago today, you no longer had the option of going outside with your face uncovered. In the week since that requirement was put into place, the positive news of a downward trend in COVID -19 infections and fatalities continued .
item.content:encoded:
One week ago today, you no longer had the option of going outside with your face uncovered. In the week since that requirement was put into place, the positive news of a downward trend in COVID -19 infections and fatalities continued . Nonetheless, stats moving in the right direction don’t give us an excuse to ease up on the restrictions, nor do they allow us to discount any of the pain and suffering our fellow New Yorkers are experiencing.

“Good” COVID-19 stats also fail to speak to the mounting evidence that we are accelerating down a steep road of economic decline . I wish links I’ve been including for unemployment insurance weren’t among the most clicked on. However, that being the realty should serve to remind us why we, just like before this crisis began, we need policies to reduce such widespread pain and suffering. There a lot of ideas and possibilities for how to do that. Even if I were smart enough, I couldn’t cover them all in a single newsletter. 

We’ve been emphasizing , long before this crisis , that we can’t forget how important our city’s Industrial and manufacturing capabilitie s are. Not only in the interest of the small businesses themselves , but in the interest of community cohesion, we need to keep them operating after this crisis is over . No one doubts that we must keep people in their homes and continue, especially having just celebrated Earth Day, to do so in environmentally smart ways .

These topics are part of what will be discussed during our May 6th “Check-In . If you’d

like to have specific questions addressed by elected officials and governmental agencies during the meeting, please send an email here . Doing so helps us to

gather more and better information in advance. Thank you to everyone who has

submitted questions and to the 60 or so people who have already registered.

If you scroll past my email signature, you’ll find, as is the case Monday through Friday, resources, reminders, and items of interest. 

﻿Have a good weekend, please support local business ( maybe buy a raffle ticket? ), cover your face, share this information around the community, and most importantly stay safe.

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Acceleration, Deceleration, Registration
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I’d like to begin by wishing all who celebrate a Happy Ramadan, and I hope that everyone had a good Earth Day and that this email finds you well.
item.content:encoded:
I’d like to begin by wishing all who celebrate a Happy Ramadan, and I hope that everyone had a good Earth Day and that this email finds you well.

In stark contrast to just a few weeks ago, regarding COVID-19, there is a real trend of fewer hospitalizations, intubations, a “flattening” in reported cases and, fewer deaths. We’ve also learned that COVID-19 was in our midst earlier and at much higher numbers than initially thought. This clear deceleration shows that current strategies are working and gives reason to remaining rigorous in continuing to “ pause .”

Conversely to the deceleration in cases, there is an acceleration in negative economic impact and suffering caused by COVID-19. Some are profiting, and even a few are profiteering during this, but they are the exceptions that prove the rule. As highlighted in a report from The New School that I shared last week, if we don’t fight the economic inequality laid bare by COVID-19, we’re going to see unwarranted suffering and hardship, locally and globally , as untreated complications of the pandemic.  

Policies for how we deal with the crisis, in terms of health and economics, will certainly be discussed at our May 6th virtual “check-in.”  As noted, the purpose of the “check-in” is to keep the community informed and answer questions as clearly as possible. One way to do that is to submit questions here so that government agencies and officials that take part in the check-in will be able to provide the best information available. Thank you to everyone who has submitted questions and to the 50 or so people that have registered for the event. 

As always, there are other resources and reminders below my email signature.

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Earth, Ride, Register
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this message finds you safe and healthy. Before moving on to other topics, I’ll remind everyone that the place to be on May 6th at 6:30 PM , at least according to the 40 or so people that have already signed up, is our 2nd virtual…
item.content:encoded:
I hope this message finds you safe and healthy. Before moving on to other topics, I’ll remind everyone that the place to be on May 6th at 6:30 PM , at least according to the 40 or so people that have already signed up, is our 2nd virtual community “Check-in.”

Virtually “checking-in” is new terrain for everyone involved. The purpose, like the first “check-in”, is to keep the community informed and answer questions as clearly as possible. One way to do that is to submit questions here so that government agencies and officials that take part in the check-in will be able to provide the best information available.

One thing that will likely come up is the New York's plan for COVID-19 testing and tracing that was unveiled today and will be rolled out in the coming weeks. 

Lastly, I know people are tired of being told to stay home, and I get it, but while you are there, along with completing the census , I recommend helping to ensure the MTA gets necessary funding by texting “Rider” to “522828” . Without it, the nearly 1 million essential workers who rely on public transportation will be faced with fewer trains and less reliable service. Based on the geography of social distancing, having fewer trains for more people is a bad idea. I’d like to thank CB6 and Red Hook’s own Karen Broughton for putting that on my radar. 

As always, there are some items of interest below, including a very interesting map that CB6 member Joanna Smith brought my attention earlier today, along with other resources and reminders.  

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Tuesday, April 21, 2020
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you as well as possible on this thunderous Tuesday that included a tornado warning . I think all of this is taking “when it rains it pours” to an all too literal place.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you as well as possible on this thunderous Tuesday that included a tornado warning . I think all of this is taking “when it rains it pours” to an all too literal place. 

If only there were better news to share rather than giving context to horrible amounts of fellow new Yorkers dying and suffering at a level, and in ways, few thought they’d ever see outside of a movie or a history book. This crisis will end eventually, but what our community looks like afterward will be affected by what we do now. Of course, part of what we can do now is stay home, socially distance, and cover our faces when we can’t. 

As you may have noticed, this crisis is costing quite a bit of money, and help is needed all around. One very simple thing you can do is fill out a census form to make sure New York gets its fair share. We are as a state, city, and borough lagging in responses. Understandably, the census isn’t the top thing on people’s minds , but it takes 10 minutes, and if you have computer capabilities sufficient to read this email, you should be able to fill it out . The census determines federal funding for hospitals and

money for programs that are supposed to be there to help small businesses in a time like this. Without a proper count, we are less likely, not just now, but for the next 10 years, to get what we need and deserve.

Another thing you could while we are "paused" do is mark your calendar & register for our second Community Check-In on Wednesday, May 6th, beginning at 6:30 PM. We had a great turnout for our last “Check-In” not surprising given the level of engagement in CB6 and environs, and we hope for the same this go around. As more is confirmed and figured out, you’ll be sure to hear about it from me. 

As always, there is some useful information and items of interest below my email signature.

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Monday, April 20, 2020
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: First, our former and longtime Landmarks Committee Chair, Bob Levine, has lost his wife, Kathy Sonderman, after her 34-year battle with Parkinson’s disease. Bob and Kathy were together for more than 45 years, and, in addition to Bob, she…
item.content:encoded:
First, our former and longtime Landmarks Committee Chair, Bob Levine, has lost his wife, Kathy Sonderman, after her 34-year battle with Parkinson’s disease. Bob and Kathy were together for more than 45 years, and, in addition to Bob, she is survived by their two children, Brian and Emily. 

Kathy did a lot of great things in her life, being a mother, teaching autistic children, and volunteering at local hospitals. In communication with Bob, it’s clear one of her greatest accomplishments is in helping those who suffer from Parkinson’s. Indeed she donated her brain to Columbia University’s Neurological Institute in the hope it will lead to greater understanding and, thus, better treatments. I hope that Kathy’s memory can be a blessing for all that knew her and that her example can remind us to do our best to make a difference; anyway we can. If you’d like to, Bob suggests a contribution to Team Kathy at the 2020 Parkinson’s Unity Walk . 

Secondly, as I’m sure many of you saw, the Cobble Hill Health Center , where we have held many meetings over the years, has lost 55 Patients, in a 300-bed facility, to COVID-19. This is not only close to home but on a scale that’s hard to comprehend. I offer my deepest condolences to all those who have lost loved ones during this crisis and the utmost gratitude to everyone working on the front lines of this crisis. Given the Cobble Hill Health Center’s proximity to the former LICH site, it’s hard not to be

reminded of how predictably shortsighted the state was in its decision to sell

the hospital.

As always, there is some useful information and items of interest below my email signature. Stay safe, feel free to share this information, and enjoy the rest of your day. 

Related tools

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Friday, April 17, 2020
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I have no other "Pause" to compare this one too, but it seems like a lot is still happening. For one, as announced yesterday, the "Pause" itself has been extended until, at least, May 15th, and starting tonight at 8 PM , everyone must…
item.content:encoded:
I have no other "Pause" to compare this one too, but it seems like a lot is still happening. For one, as announced yesterday, the "Pause" itself has been extended until, at least, May 15th, and starting tonight at 8 PM , everyone must wear face coverings in public places where they cannot keep six feet away from others. 

From a CB6 centric perspective, this week saw coverage of letters we've written , including a reference to our testing letter in a question posed to the Mayor . We also announced that on Wednesday, May 6th  at 6:30 PM, we'll be holding our next Zoom based "Community Check-In." As more details are confirmed, I'll let you know. 

While the COVID-19 statistics head in the right direction, there is some measured relief but every reason to keep on keeping our distance and covering our faces. These guidelines have proven highly effective in the face of inadequate testing and treatments, as we await a vaccine.

As is the case Monday through Friday, there are some items of interest, reminders, and resources below. Depending on one's circumstances, each item could be more or less important. Still, I'd strongly recommend looking at the items that highlight the extreme inequality in how people are experiencing this crisis. It shows that while we are all in the same boat, many are in steerage or even cargo hold. Correcting this reality should factor into policymaking now and long after this crisis is over. 

Anyway, let me hop off my soapbox to say, have a good weekend, stay safe, and share this information however you'd like. 

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Thursday, April 16, 2020
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: The Governor has announced that the decidedly unrefreshing “Pause” has been extended until, at least, MAY 15th . While we must remain distanced, we need not be incommunicado, so please save the date of May 6th for our second community…
item.content:encoded:
The Governor has announced that the decidedly unrefreshing “Pause” has been extended until, at least, MAY 15th . While we must remain distanced, we need not be incommunicado, so please save the date of May 6th for our second community check-in with more details to follow. Our Mayor released his Executive Budget Proposal , which, he believes, rests on four pillars -keeping city residents safe, healthy, housed, and fed. Beyond that, given the COVID-19 downpour, there will no longer be a rainy day fund, and there will be significant cuts above that.

During today’s press conference , the Mayor was asked, by Kevin Duggan of the Brooklyn Paper, about the letter we sent yesterday regarding COVID-19 making testing sites being available to people without access to a car ASAP. The Mayor didn’t directly respond to the question but did mention that some walk-up sites are opening. We continue to raise concerns and advise as best we can, and hopefully, policies are adjusted accordingly. So, thank you to Kevin for asking the question and a CB6 board member, who doesn’t miss anything, for letting me know that the question had been asked.

In what can be called “ good news ” in the most limited sense of the term, 606 New York residents died yesterday, which is the lowest total of the last 10 days. Fewer people are being hospitalized, fewer people are in ICU’s, and fewer people are being intubated. But that these numbers are coming down only reinforce s why the pause must continue.

There are resources and items of interest below, but whether or not you check them out, please stay safe and cover your face and feel free to share this information however you'd like.

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Beatles, Letters, Requirements, Resources I hope this email finds you well on a day that once had significance as “Hump
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well on a day that once had significance as “Hump Day.” On a normal April 15th I would’ve led with something related to taxes and linked to an appropriate Beatles song (please note that Tax day is now July 15th).
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well on a day that once had significance as “Hump Day.” On a normal April 15th I would’ve led with something related to taxes and linked to an appropriate Beatles song (please note that Tax day is now July 15th). 

﻿Instead, on this April I5th, I'll tell everyone who isn’t already wearing a mask or face covering when outside, that they will be required to wear one w beginning this Saturday, April 18th.

Measures like this help limit the spread of COVID-19, but there is no chance of getting back to a sense of normality we all want until there is widespread testing available, and it can’t just be for people of means or access to a car. That is why we’ve written this letter to the Mayor and The Department of Health and Mental Hygiene , urging that the city does everything in its power to make testing sites readily available that don’t require access to a car. In both high and low-income portions of the city, including Community Board 6, under 50 percent of residents have a car.

Of course, this is new territory for all of us, and we don’t know precisely what shape this would take, but it may involve testing sites coming to people, but the bottom line is testing must be made available to EVERYONE ASAP.

There are, as usual, resources and Items of interest following my email signature. 

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Tuesday, April 14, 2020
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: There is a limit of how “well” anyone can be right now given the COVD19 death toll and clear constitutional language losing meaning by the minute.
item.content:encoded:
There is a limit of how “well” anyone can be right now given the COVD19 death toll and clear constitutional language losing meaning by the minute. 

However, within this reality, there is hope that we are past the worst as states begin coordinating how to “reopen.” Of course, the “how” is most important. The devil, after all, is in the details. If we don’t do it right, and according to proper public health guidelines, our efforts in supporting businesses that are holding on for dear life will be for naught. An important proposal for the “how” can be seen in Assemblymember Carroll’s bill to make insurance companies, that currently have 900 Billion in reserves, to pay “Business Interruption” claims that have been filed, but are in many instances being denied on technicalities. Now is not the time to put up additional roadblocks.

There is more on the bill below, along with other resources and items of interest, such as our letter to DYCD asking to find some other way to avoid canceling the Summer Youth Employment Program(SYEP). If it has to be named the Fall Youth Employment Program, so be it. As the letter states, we don’t want this program to be one more casualty of the pandemic.

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Stay Home, Cover Your Face, Protect you, Protect Me
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well on a rainy and windy Monday. I've always liked rain, but even more so now since it's helping people find a reason to stay inside.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well on a rainy and windy Monday. I've always liked rain, but even more so now since it's helping people find a reason to stay inside. I hope that if you do go outside, you're wearing a face-covering or mask much the way essential workers are now required to.

Encouraging info from our Governor and Mayor that the curve is flattening is a good reason for adhering to this requirement. However, these signs are no argument for relaxing restrictions, and they will likely remain in place, including schools being closed , until there is an indication that community spread is contained.

If you scroll below my email signature, you'll see more information on how inequality is impacting us during this crisis, along with a number of resources and items of interest.

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: No Time For That Now, Context, Resources, Easter
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well as we head into the weekend. For all those celebrating "Good Friday" and Easter on Sunday, I hope as you pray, from home, you draw strength from your faith during these difficult times.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well as we head into the weekend. For all those celebrating "Good Friday" and Easter on Sunday, I hope as you pray, from home, you draw strength from your faith during these difficult times. I extend the same wishes for those continuing to celebrate Passover. 

It feels like every night is unlike any other lately, but, unlike the Talking Heads, I'm not "getting used to it now" . Yet, not being used to this surreal moment in time, is about as good as it currently gets. I'm very fortunate, and I hope you are too, as there is much pain and suffering around us.

As was announced earlier today, we have now lost 7,844 people across New York State to COVID-19 and 777 over the last day. Fortunately, despite these heartbreaking numbers that represent our fellow New Yorkers, there is continued optimism that social distancing is working.

However, a side effect of social distancing is record numbers of people becoming unemployed. For those applying for unemployment insurance benefits, there is information here and below for the application process, which has now been streamlined a bit. The main difference in the process is that applicants will no longer need to call the Department of Labor if a follow-up phone call is necessary. Instead, the Department of Labor will call the applicant within 72 hours. 

There are various resources, including information on how to celebrate Easter remotely across our community, and other items of interest, below my email signature. 

Have a good weekend, stay safe, share this information however you'd like. 

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Stuck Inside of Mobile, Cheer, Share, Flatten
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I had to double-check that it's Thursday as, like when Bob Dylan mixed Texas Medicine and Railroad Gin , I have no sense of time. I mention that as I mistakenly labeled yesterday as Tuesday while it wasn't Tuesday redux, but was most…
item.content:encoded:
I had to double-check that it's Thursday as, like when Bob Dylan mixed Texas Medicine and Railroad Gin , I have no sense of time. I mention that as I mistakenly labeled yesterday as Tuesday while it wasn't Tuesday redux, but was most certainly Wednesday. 

Speaking of time, as I assume you've noticed, every evening at 7:00 PM , cheering breaks out, in a bit of cathartic appreciation for those who can't shelter at home and continue to keep us going as a city. Each person cheering has their unique bit of appreciation, but I know it encompasses so many walks of life and is so earnest that even a curmudgeon such as myself can start to think the glass is half full. 

Based on my conversations, people are cheering for , nurses, orderlies, doctors, pharmacists, E.M.T.s, grocery clerks, teachers, delivery people, restaurant workers, NYPD, FDNY, and DSNY. I'm sure there are other things people are cheering for, and each cheer is unique and uplifting across our community. People have been recording these cheers and simultaneously posting and sharing on social media. If you do that and want it to be shared, "tag" CB6 ( Facebook , Twitter , Instagram ), and I'll be sure to share it (with appropriate attribution, of course).

As far as the purpose of sheltering and social distance, and mask-wearing, we see its efficacy in a "flattening" of COVID-19 hospitalizations . At the same time, the death toll, sadly, continues to climb and break another daily record, with 799 New York State residents passing away over the last day. Assemblyman Ortiz mentioned on our check-in the need for funds for burials and also among our critical workers, funeral directors tell of refrigerated trucks stacking up on Hart Island . These divergent trendlines and statistics highlight why complying with public health guidelines are so important as doing so will literally save lives. 

There are, as is the case Monday through Friday, some resources and items of interest below my email signature. 

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Recap, Raffle,Resources
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this message finds you well and safe, and to those celebrating Passover , I say, “Chag sameach.”
item.content:encoded:
I hope this message finds you well and safe, and to those celebrating Passover , I say, “Chag sameach.”

I’d like to start by thanking the over 100 people who joined last night’s community check-in and to all our panelists. You can click here to relive the magic or see it for the first time via YouTube . 

Before going forward I’d like to reiterate a point that I made at the beginning of last night’s check-in, that as a lot of people flock to the great and less dense neighborhood of Red Hook to exercise and walk around, it is important to maintain a safe distance from each other, wear masks, and if the path ahead is crowding explore a different route. I hear that the Brooklyn Greenway’s path is often getting too congested to maintain proper distancing. Also, now that dog runs are closed, please be extra mindful of cleaning up after your dog. 

The reason for this “PAUSE,” lest anyone forget, is that we are in the middle of a crisis that doesn’t discriminate and, for the second straight day has, with a total of 779 deaths , sadly, seen New York State set a new mark for single day COVID-19 deaths. Again I don’t think it can be expected to cause much immediate comfort, but there is hope that New York is reaching a plateau as hospitalizations are falling and the curve flattens. 

We have seen the unsafe conditions imposed on the voters of Wisconsin ; fortunately, Governor Cuomo will not disenfranchise New Yorkers, and he has announced that we will have the option to vote by mail for the June 23rd primary election. I will keep you posted when we know the mechanism for that.

Of course, we don’t know when this will end, so please keep staying home, and when you are home, if you can, support local businesses. For example, you can enter the Gowanus Dredgers latest raffle or refer to the list of what’s open on 7th Avenue in Park Slope. 

For those who can’t stay home, THANK YOU . 

As is the case every weekday, I hope you keep scrolling and check out the resources below, feel free to share this information however you’d like, and enjoy the rest of the evening. 

Related tools

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this message finds you well and safe this spring Tuesday, as sadly our necessary "Pause" must continue.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this message finds you well and safe this spring Tuesday, as sadly our necessary "Pause" must continue. 

We've already had over 100 people sign up for tonight's "Community Check-In" panel, and once we can have it up on youtube, you'll be able to follow there and on our Facebook page. I will send out a link to everyone on the list, and it should be a few minutes after zoom starts. 

So to reiterate, tonight, Tuesday, April 7th at 6:30 PM, we are co-sponsoring a  " Community Check-In " with Councilman Lander , Assemblymembers Carroll , Simon , and Ortiz with panelists from agencies including the DOHMH , DOE , DOT , Parks , FDNY , NYPD ,  NYC Census 2020 ,  and NYP Brooklyn Methodist and with the recent edition of the Freelancers Union and the MTA .  The list is still in formation and is subject to change.

As for the chilling facts of the crisis, as the Governor announced earlier, yesterday we saw the largest single-day increase of COVID-19 deaths across New York, with 731 people dying . However, as was noted, and it is little comfort to do so, death is a lagging indicator. Yet we can look forward and be encouraged that the rate of hospitalization is falling and that we may be hitting a plateau of the spread of this virus in NY. However, it's still far too early and anecdotal to say for sure, and in any event, a lack of vigilance could lead to another spike.

As is the case every weekday, you'll find some resources and items of interest below my email signature. 

So, please, unless you are needed on the front lines, STAY HOME. While home, if you can afford to support local businesses, please do so. If you are among those keeping society intact, THANK YOU . 

See some of you later, feel free to share this information , enjoy the rest of your day and stay safe! 

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: A Message from Chair Peter Fleming
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: To my fellow Community Board 6 members: I hope that you, your family and friends are well and that you are taking whatever steps are necessary to keep yourselves and those you love safe. Like you, my
item.content:encoded:
To my fellow Community Board 6 members:

I hope that you, your family and friends are well and that you are taking whatever steps are necessary to keep yourselves and those you love safe.

Like you, my husband Brian and I are staying at home and doing our best to stay healthy. Brian is working from home and seems to be constantly on conference calls. I am reading, watching Amazon Prime and news on TV and cooking. Today is Brian’s birthday, so I baked him a cake that we will enjoy tonight. I imagine you and your families are doing much the same.

This COVID-19 crisis is difficult for all of us in varying degrees. As a gay man in his early 60s, I am no stranger to losing friends and loved ones to a health crisis. Like today, the AIDS crisis saw many people die unnecessarily due to the government’s unwillingness to confront the crisis head on. While I would like to think we learned some lessons from that terrible time, some days it seems like some of those teachable were lost to history. Hopefully we will see less of that in the days and weeks ahead.

One of the biggest lessons we learned from the AIDS crisis was the importance of accurate information. With the benefit of a lot of time on my hands, I get my information from a variety of sources including Community Board 6, the city and state of New York, the federal government (at least sometimes) as well as a variety of newspapers and television news. My best piece of advice is to not believe everything you read or see on TV and to gather as much information as you can from a variety of sources. The CB6 daily newsletter tries to provide as much accurate information as it can with a focus on our own city and neighborhoods.

Mike and I are in regular contact and are trying to advocate for causes we feel are important to the people who live in CB6. Mike collects information for his daily newsletter and manages the District Office remotely. Ty and Liza are managing their duties from home as best they can under difficult circumstances. Please feel free to contact us if we can help you in any way while you and your families continue to shelter at home.

As Mike noted in his newsletter, we are co-sponsoring a virtual community check in with representatives from various crisis-relevant agencies and elected officials participating. You can register for it here.

We obviously cannot have a regular board meeting right now. And because of the crisis the city is experiencing, we have no issues to review. As things change in the weeks ahead we will brainstorm ways to bring committees and the community together so that we can help get life in New York City back on the path to normal.

Before I close I wanted to add my thank you to our health care employees, teachers, retail workers, delivery people and others who put their health on the line every day to help keep essential parts of this city running. What you do is so important and I can’t thank you enough.

For now, the most important thing is to stay safe. Try to start each day with a smile. I know I don’t say it enough, but thank you for your dedication and service to our shared community. I look forward to the next time we can meet in person and shake hands, pat each other on the back and continue our efforts to make CB6 a better place to live and work.

Be well…

Peter

Chairperson
