item.title: COVID Context, Resources & More
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Yesterday's update or, to borrow a description from GBD, "Broadsheet" , focused on telling people to fill out the census, and provided COVID-19 statistics along with small business issues.
item.content:encoded:
Yesterday's update or, to borrow a description from GBD, "Broadsheet" , focused on telling people to fill out the census, and provided COVID-19 statistics along with small business issues.

Again today, we'll emphasize that, if you are fortunate enough to afford it, support small businesses. These businesses are featured in the maps listed below and offer delivery and pick up options. The COVID-19 statics are listed here and below but with some additional context for how this is being felt across the 5 boroughs.  

Regarding the census, I had an opportunity to speak with the director of external affairs for " NYC Census 2020 " , Jason Reischel, who shared that in the 2 weeks since the census forms have been sent out 29.4% of Brooklynites have responded, 31.2 percent of New York City has responded while the nation has responded at a rate of 43.1% . 

Of course, we have been dealing with a crisis, which makes it harder to think about responding, but it is one of those things that can be done entirely from home , and it only takes a few minutes. Clearly, we need more resources from the federal government, and being fully counted will put us in a position to get a fairer share. I'd hope there is never such a crisis again, but the 10 minutes you take to respond now may save the lives of some of your fellow New Yorkers during the next 10 years. Sparing 10 minutes for a better 10 years seems like an excellent use of time.

We are still ironing out some of the details, but we are working on a virtual community check-in on Tuesday night, beginning at 6:30 PM. Once the specific link and other info are confirmed, you'll hear about it from me. 

COVID-19 doesn't discriminate. So, please, unless you are needed on the front lines, STAY HOME. If you are among those keeping society intact, THANK YOU .  

Feel free to share this information ; however, you'd like and stay safe. 

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Census Day, Take Out Night
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I never cared for "April Fools," but I'd happily trade the COVID-19 crisis for a situation in which people could go out and about without the worry that we're all experiencing right now. Speaking of being "out and about," as per the…
item.content:encoded:
I never cared for "April Fools," but I'd happily trade the COVID-19 crisis for a situation in which people could go out and about without the worry that we're all experiencing right now. Speaking of being "out and about," as per the Governor's announcement earlier, New York City playgrounds will be closed while parks and open spaces will remain open.

Today is " Census Day ," and despite it being April 1 st, it's no fooling matter. The census determines a lot about what resources New York State will receive over the next 10 years. The closer we are to having everyone in New York counted means more federal aid for things like healthcare, public transportation, housing, and more representation in congress.

Federal aid is always important, but the COVID19 crisis, and the extended impact it's expected to have, show getting what we need from the federal government is as important as it's ever been. Fortunately, the census can be completed online in under 10 minutes.  

After you are done taking the census, you will still have time if you are fortunate enough to be able to afford it, to support local business. With that in mind, tonight, the Fifth Avenue BID (#theother5th) has repurposed their "Taste of Fifth" event to #Atasteoffifthtakeout , which offers the possibility to not only get great food delivered but a chance to win a 50 dollar gift certificate. Please check it out.

Scroll past my email signature to find more information and resources, including the lastest COVID -19 statistics for NYC. Those stats represent the pain and loss of far too many fellows New Yorkers and Brooklynites.

COVID-19 doesn't discriminate. So, please, unless you are needed on the front lines, STAY HOME , if you are among those keeping society intact, THANK YOU .  

Finally, a big thank you to CB6 Human Services Chair, Kathy Park Price , and anyone else who has shared this newsletter and sign up sheet . It's much appreciated and has helped us to share information with a greater number of people across our community.

Feel free to share this information ; however, you'd like and stay safe. 

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Wishing For a Safe and Speedy Recovery, Resources, Community
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I'd like to start by wishing a safe and speedy recovery to Congresswoman Nydia Velazquez , who has been diagnosed with a presumed COVID-19 infection. It is indisputable that she, and her excellent staff, fight for our community every day…
item.content:encoded:
I'd like to start by wishing a safe and speedy recovery to Congresswoman Nydia Velazquez , who has been diagnosed with a presumed COVID-19 infection. It is indisputable that she, and her excellent staff, fight for our community every day and, as her statement noted , that will continue as she fights off this virus.

That hard work, for example, has resulted in help for small businesses. As you know, we daily ask you to support local businesses, if at all possible. Resources, such as information on how to help small businesses and other items can be found by scrolling below my email signature.

Before scrolling down to those resources and items of interest, it's important to keep driving home why it's vital that we STAY HOME . 

Yesterday there were 66,6497 confirmed COVID-19 cases in New York State , 33,474 in New York Cit y , and 8,887 in Brooklyn. Now there are 75,795 confirmed COVID-19 cases in New York State , 40,900 in New York City, and 10,904 in Brooklyn .

Yesterday the number of deaths caused by COVID-19 stood at 1,218 across New York State, 790 in New York City, and 188 in Brooklyn. Now those numbers stand at 1,550 across New York State, 932 in New York City, and 215 in Brooklyn.

COVID-19 doesn't discriminate. So, please, unless you are needed on the front lines, stay at home, if you are among those keeping society intact, THANK YOU .  

So, when something like a ship comes in, don't gather to see it. I love arrivals too, but staying home, as we social distance, is our best and proven option . As a teaser, I want you to know that we are working on setting up an informational (via Zoom) BKCB6 meeting in the near future. When it is set up and confirmed, I'll let everyone know. 

Lastly, but not least, thank you to Sacred Hearts and Saint Stephens , and anyone else who has shared this newsletter and sign up sheet . It's much appreciated and has helped us to share information across our community.

Feel free to share this information ; however you'd like and stay safe. 

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Still Paused, Letter Writing, Resources
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I'd like to start by thanking Gowanus By Design (GBD) , Portside NY and Resilient Red Hook , and anyone else who has shared this newsletter and sign up sheet . It's much appreciated and has helped us share information with a growing…
item.content:encoded:
I'd like to start by thanking Gowanus By Design (GBD) , Portside NY and Resilient Red Hook , and anyone else who has shared this newsletter and sign up sheet . It's much appreciated and has helped us share information with a growing community.

The ongoing Covid-19 emergency has forced many businesses to close, jobs to be lost, and those that remain, struggle to survive the best they can. We've heard from community members, small business owners, business representatives, and the New York Times , that luxury chains, who already have security systems and gates in place, have been boarding up their storefronts even as crime is dropping . This is not conducive to sustaining the minimal commercial activity that's currently possible. For those reasons, we've sent this letter to the Department of Buildings and are hopeful the situation can be resolved. We don't want luxury brands and chains to hurt our local businesses. 

Below my email signature, there are listings of businesses that are still open and, if you can support them, please do. 

Before that, it's important to keep driving home why it's vital that we STAY HOME . 

When I sent out my previous newsletter on Friday , COVID19 had caused us to lose 519 people in New York State, 366 in New York City, and 82 fellow Brooklynites. That number now stands at 1,218 deaths across New York State , 790 in New York City, and 188 in Brooklyn .

There are now 66,6497 confirmed COVID-19 cases in New York State , 33,474 in New York Cit y , and 8,887 in Brooklyn. On Friday, those numbers stood at  44,635 in New York State , 25,573 in New York Cit y , and 6,750 in Brooklyn. 

COVID-19 doesn't discriminate. So, please, unless you are needed on the front lines, stay at home, if you are among those keeping society intact, THANK YOU .  

The more dedicated we are to following these guidelines, the sooner people will be able to greet their neighbors and no longer receive messages from government agencies telling them to stay away from people.  

Feel free to share this information; however, you'd like and stay safe. 

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Home, Resources, Clapping, Counting
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I'm pleasantly surprised by the strong positive response to the Orson Welles/Harry Lyme reference i n yesterday's email . So, thank you to everyone who responded.
item.content:encoded:
I'm pleasantly surprised by the strong positive response to the Orson Welles/Harry Lyme reference i n yesterday's email . So, thank you to everyone who responded. 

COVID-19 is also an attack on our social nature, even in the best of times, staying home can be quite stressful, but it remains necessary. For that reason, especially if you are home alone, the City and State are offering ways to help cope as well as other options listed in the resources section of this message. 

Above all else, unless you have to, please stay home. Those who are working because they must, THANK YOU!

Each day, by varying degrees but relentlessly, brings us worsening statistics that represent the lives of our fellow New Yorkers and Brooklynites of ALL AGES .

People between the age of 18 and 44 account for 44% of all infections, while 34% of those infected are between 45 and 64 years old. The remaining 21 percent of infections are split between 11% of people from the age of 65 to 74, 8% are over 75 years of age, and 2 percent of cases are found in those under 17 years of age

. 

As of now, there are 44,635 confirmed COVID-19 cases in New York State , 25,573 in New York Cit y , and 6,750 in Brooklyn. Yesterday those numbers stood at 37,258 statewide, 21,873 in New York City, and 5,705 in Brooklyn. 

Due to COVID-19, we now mourn the loss of 519 People in New York State, 366 New York City in New York, and 82 fellow Brooklynites. 

Lastly, please voluntarily comply because this " pause " is being enforced. For example, there was a wedding about to take place, yesterday with far too many attendees. When a concerned senior (THANK YOU!) in our community reached out, I was able to coordinate with the 76 th Precinct , led by Inspector O 'Malley, and have the crowd dispersed before all the guests could assemble. This incident was undoubtedly the closest I've ever been or likely will be to "police work." And yes, I feel for the couple but would feel far worse if their happiness turned into tragedy in a few days.

While home, if you can afford to, please support local businesses.

Feel free to share the information above and below my signature however you'd like and stay safe. 

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: While some folks on the national stage, in horrifying fashion, are starting to sound like Harry Lyme , I still hope this update finds you well and staying safe. Even in the best situations, staying home can be quite stressful, but it’s…
item.content:encoded:
While some folks on the national stage, in horrifying fashion, are starting to sound like Harry Lyme , I still hope this update finds you well and staying safe. Even in the best situations, staying home can be quite stressful, but it’s what needed right now. Those who are unable to stay home , THANK YOU!

The reality of this situation becomes more unfathomable every day.

As of now, there 37,258 confirmed COVID-19 cases in New York State , 21,873 in New York Cit y , and 5,705 in Brooklyn. Yesterday those numbers stood at 30,811 statewide, 17,856 in New York City, and 4,656 in Brooklyn.

Due to COVID-19, we now mourn the loss of 385 People in New York State, 281 New York City in New York, and 64 fellow Brooklynites.

People between the age of 18 and 44 account for 44% of all infections, while 34% of those infected are between 45 and 64 years old. The remaining 21 percent of infections are split between 11% of people from the age of 65 to 74, 8% are over 75 years of age, and 2 percent of cases are found in those under 17 years of age. 

 So, again, please STAY HOME!

While home, if you can afford to support local businesses. If nothing else, these past weeks have shown, while we may not be in the same boat, we’re in this together.

Feel free to share the information above and below my signature you’d like and stay safe.

item.title: Orson Welles, Census, Support
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: While some folks on the national stage, in horrifying fashion, are starting to sound like Harry Lyme , I still hope this update finds you well and staying safe. Even in the best situations, staying home can be quite stressful, but it’s…
item.content:encoded:
While some folks on the national stage, in horrifying fashion, are starting to sound like Harry Lyme , I still hope this update finds you well and staying safe. Even in the best situations, staying home can be quite stressful, but it’s what needed right now. Those who are unable to stay home , THANK YOU!

The reality of this situation becomes more unfathomable every day.

As of now, there 37,258 confirmed COVID-19 cases in New York State , 21,873 in New York Cit y , and 5,705 in Brooklyn. Yesterday those numbers stood at 30,811 statewide, 17,856 in New York City, and 4,656 in Brooklyn.

Due to COVID-19, we now mourn the loss of 385 People in New York State, 281 New York City in New York, and 64 fellow Brooklynites.

People between the age of 18 and 44 account for 44% of all infections, while 34% of those infected are between 45 and 64 years old. The remaining 21 percent of infections are split between 11% of people from the age of 65 to 74, 8% are over 75 years of age, and 2 percent of cases are found in those under 17 years of age. 

 So, again, please STAY HOME!

While home, if you can afford to, support local businesses. If nothing else, these past weeks have shown, while we may not be in the same boat, we’re in this together. Feel free to share the information above and below my signature however you’d like and stay safe. 

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Repeat, Pause, Stay Home
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: If we had the right to vote on a day to be trapped in, a la Groundhogs Day , I doubt there would be a single vote cast for our necessary, “ pause ”.
item.content:encoded:
If we had the right to vote on a day to be trapped in, a la Groundhogs Day , I doubt there would be a single vote cast for our necessary, “ pause ”. 

Nonetheless, I hope this message finds you well. Also, big thanks to everyone who signed up for CB6 text updates and for the feedback it’s generated that’s helped make the updates more informative. 

As of this email, there are 30,811 confirmed COVID-19 cases in New York State , 17,856 in New York City, and 4,656 in Brooklyn. We mourn the 285 people who have died in the state, including 199 of our fellow city residents. Available statistics show people between the age of 18 and 44 accounts for 46% of all infections while 33% of those infected are between 45 and 64 years old. The remaining 21 percent of infections are split between 11% of people from the age of 65 to 74, 8% are over 75 years of age and 2 percent of cases are found in those under 17 years of age. 

These numbers reflect an increase of thousands from yesterday alone, and it’s likely to increase for a while. If your labor is necessary and you can’t stay home, THANK YOU for serving others. But if you can stay home , STAY HOME! 

Not staying home will result in a greater time period during which people say (or shout) “ STAY HOME ” by hitting “Caps Lock” in newsletters from governmental agencies. 

Our continuing theme, if you can afford to, please support local businesses. For example you can find listings/suggestions below such as the North Flatbush BID’s listing of establishments taking pickup and delivery orders . 

There are more listings and other bits of information, such as the New York State tax deadline being moved to July 15 th , below. Enjoy the rest of this rainy Wednesday at a safe distance and feel free to share this information however you’d like. 

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.description: can't lose sight of the fact that these aren't dry statistics; they represent people. People that are our neighbors and fellow New Yorkers, and while the risk is statistically higher for the elderly and vulnerable, COVID-19 does not…
item.content:encoded:
can't lose sight of the fact that these aren't dry statistics; they represent people. People that are our neighbors and fellow New Yorkers, and while the risk is statistically higher for the elderly and vulnerable, COVID-19 does not discriminate . Sadly this is driven home by the loss of a 36-year-old Principal in Brooklyn to this virus . So if you're outside because you have to be, keep a safe distance from everyone, but if you have to go out to work, thank you for keeping us all going as we pause and STAY HOME!

While home, if you can afford it, it's a good idea to support local businesses by

ordering pick up or delivery or place a bid to support local businesses like

the raffle set up by the Gowanus Dredgers!

There is more information, including opportunities to help, be helped, and cope,

below my email signature. Enjoy, at a safe distance, the rest of Tuesday that

feels like a flat circle , and feel free to share this information however you'd like.

item.title: Pause to flatten
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Sadly I must begin by offering my deepest condolences to the many people in our community that knew and worked with Nat Allman, who has passed away.
item.content:encoded:
Sadly I must begin by offering my deepest condolences to the many people in our community that knew and worked with Nat Allman, who has passed away. 

I hope this update finds you well and safely isolated during the first day of what is likely to be a prolonged “pause.” It’s our nature to avoid isolation. Isolation is depressing, but it’s nonetheless, what’s necessary to “Flatten the Curve.”

As of this email, there are 20,875 confirmed cases in New York State, 12,339 in New York City, and 3,94 cases in Brooklyn . 157 People have died in the state, 99 people have died in New York City. All authorities indicate that those numbers are going to keep increasing, and the only way to make it more manageable by staying home if you’re not needed on the front lines of this fight.

For those that can’t stay home and are needed, I think it’s safe to say that everyone appreciates and owes a debt of gratitude to you for going out and doing your jobs so that others can be safe, fed, and have garbage not stack up to the sky. The same goes for teachers who are adjusting on the fly and doing their absolute best to provide remote learning options for the biggest public school system in the country. Speaking of schools, please remember that "grab and go" meals are available, and that 3 meals can be picked up at once. 

There aren’t a ton of options when the main thing you can do to help is staying home, but if you can, look for ways to support local businesses. That can include ordering delivery or pick up from a restaurant or liquor store , but that can also include something as simple as letting people know, via email or social media , that a business is open and looking to deliver food and/or beverages. We have a district of over 100 thousand , but the community is, I know it sounds corny, closer than that may imply.

There is more information, including opportunities to help, be helped, and cope, below my email signature. Make the best of what’s remaining of this rainy Monday feel free to share this information however you’d like. 

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: The thing on most New Yorkers’ minds right now is Governor Cuomo putting New York State on, as he referred to it, “pause” with only “essential” businesses and services remaining open. In the most simplified sense, that means business's…
item.content:encoded:
The thing on most New Yorkers’ minds right now is Governor Cuomo putting New York State on, as he referred to it, “pause” with only “essential” businesses and services remaining open. In the most simplified sense, that means business's that provide healthcare and food(pick up/delivery), along with laundromat’s and plumbers, remaining active. You can click here to find out directly from the Governor’s office as information is frequently changing, and I don’t know when you’ll read this email. 

There is more information on schools, businesses, hospitals, and more below. 

Again thanks to all of you who have shared information with me to amplify here and on social media. Sharing has reinforced the only positive theme of the last few weeks- that we’re in this together.If you think someone you know may want to receive these updates (aside from those who received this email), please let them know you can sign up by texting BKCB6 to 22828 or using this link . 

Have as good of a weekend that could be, stay safe, and feel free to share this information however you’d like. 

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager

It's a great excuse to pick up a pastry named for the day from one of our community's great bakery's (my preference is Court Pastry, but they are all great). Speaking of religion, here is an update from Sacred Heart Saint Stephen s and another from Beth Elohim . What's also true is that it may help to take a well-spaced walk . I hope you are well and stay well and feel free to share this information however you'd like.

item.title: Alternate Side, Ar scáth a chéile a mhaireann na daoine
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email, as always, but especially now, finds you well. To all those celebrating, hopefully from a safe distance, happy Saint Patrick’s Day.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email, as always, but especially now, finds you well. To all those celebrating, hopefully from a safe distance, happy Saint Patrick’s Day. 

There can be no parade this year, and last year now seems far away, but, a year ago, in our community, we marched in the first truly inclusive Brooklyn Saint Patrick’s Day Parade. The Brooklyn Irish LGBTQ Organization (BILO) became the first LGBTQ group to march in the event . Our Chair, Peter Fleming, had been part of a long fight to make this into a reality. This example can serve as a reminder to all, including myself, that we can get through really tough times and progress as a community. 

Moving to some more practical matters, I remind everyone with regret that CB6 is not taking walk-in constituents until further notice. Also, due to executive order , all land use review and landmark designations are delayed until further notice.

Please don’t forget to fill out the census and take note that while schools are closed, lunch and breakfast are still available in all schools from 7:30 am until 1:30 pm and that Alternate Side Parking will be suspended starting tomorrow through at least Tuesday, March 24t h. Parking meters will remain in effect. 

I’ve listed more information and reminders below, including Congresswoman Vesasquez’s telephone town hall , which is scheduled for tomorrow night. You can sign up to be part of it here. 

As always, please feel free to share this information however you'd like and all the best to you and yours during these difficult times. 

Ar scáth a chéile a mhaireann na daoine.

Related tools

item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I'm not at my desk, so my apologies if this is a bit disjointed, but I wanted to pass along the news , if you didn't know already, that NYC Department of Education schools will be closed beginning tomorrow, Monday, March 16th.
item.content:encoded:
I'm not at my desk, so my apologies if this is a bit disjointed, but I wanted to pass along the news , if you didn't know already, that NYC Department of Education schools will be closed beginning tomorrow, Monday, March 16th.

Students are not to report to school buildings for instruction as we transition to remote learning. Students in need of breakfast/lunch can pick food up at their local school. For workers who cannot find child care, there will be centrally located locations for their children to go for the day. More information can be found here .

I’ve placed clickable screenshots of updates from the Department of Education , and other institutions such as the Brooklyn Public Library , below.

As has been the case throughout this emergency as more information is received, more information will be shared.

item.description: Until then, I'll continue to share information concerning the current emergency as it's received and remind everyone to complete their census questionnaire online!
item.content:encoded:
Until then, I'll continue to share information concerning the current emergency as it's received and remind everyone to complete their census questionnaire online!

In the city, and across the tri-state area, casinos, gyms and movie theaters will be closed while restaurants and bars will be limited to pickup and delivery only. With that in mind, we have sent a letter to the NYC Department of Small Business Services asking for assistance to our local restaurants in the hope of getting fees waived to them by 3rd party delivery apps, such as Seamless, as we navigate this crisis. You can also call restaurants directly or use their websites to avoid such charges.

While schools are closed, be aware that lunch and breakfast are still available in all schools from 7:30 am until 1:30 pm. 

I've listed various other bits of information and items of interest below. As always, please feel free to share this information however you'd like and all the best to you and yours during these difficult times.

item.title: Not Happening, Fill out the Census, Stay Healthy
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: As always, I hope the message finds you well. I'd like to reiterate that we have suspended any non-time-sensitive CB6 meetings through at least March 31st.
item.content:encoded:
As always, I hope the message finds you well. I'd like to reiterate that we have suspended any non-time-sensitive CB6 meetings through at least March 31st. We'll also remain in contact with governmental agencies, and we will be mindful of possible solutions throughout this, what has now officially labeled an emergency by our city, state, and federal government. 

There are resources and items of interest listed below, as a lot of things are NOT HAPPENING across our community. However, one thing that is still happening is the census, which is super important, takes under 10 minutes and can be done entirely online.

But before that, we again highlight COVID19 hotlines available from New York State (888-364-3065),   NYP Brooklyn Methodist Hotline (646-697-4000), and NYU Langone (877-40-COVID). You can also sign up to receive text updates from New York City's Department Health by texting COVID to (692692).

It remains the case that, as new information is received, it will be shared, so don't be shocked if you receive an email from me over the weekend, but until then, feel free to share this information however you'd like and most crucially stay safe and healthy. 

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

The spread of the coronavirus, and stopping it, is at the forefront of our collective consciousness. With that in mind, and based on the information available, we are going to suspend any non-time-sensitive CB6 meetings through at least March 31st.  

We will remain in contact with appropriate governmental agencies throughout this pandemic to make necessary and possible adjustments.

There is, of course, more information available, such as being able to complete the census online , if you scroll past my signature. But before scrolling, I'd again remind you of various resources such as the NYP Brooklyn Methodist Hotline (646-697-4000), the New York State Hotline (1-888-364-3065), and receive text updates from NYC's Department of Health by texting COVID to 692692.

As has been the case, as new information is received, it will be shared. But for now, feel free to share this information however you'd like, stay healthy and enjoy the rest of your day.

item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: As always, I hope this email finds you well and as a non-partisan space I’d like to think everyone had a super Tuesday.
item.content:encoded:
As always, I hope this email finds you well and as a non-partisan space I’d like to think everyone had a super Tuesday.

Speaking of Tuesday, a big thanks goes out to our Environmental Protection co-chair, Angelica Ramdhari, for representing us at Brooklyn Borough Board last night. Also, if you’re interested in yesterday's Red Hook Parks meeting, whether you attended or not, check out the presentation here.

Tonight, as always, our community is active with a 76th Precinct community council meeting, chaired by our very own Jerry Armer while the Southwest Brooklyn Tenants Union will screen “Decade of Fire ” , a documentary about urban displacement, at 201 Columbia Street beginning at 6:30 PM .

Tomorrow our Transportation & Public Safety Committee meeting will meet at the 78th precinct beginning at 6:30 PM. 

There’s plenty of stuff to read about below but, even if you decide to skip it, have a good night and feel free to share this information however you’d like .

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Packed , Parks, Precinct I hope this email finds you well during this, potentially, rainy Tuesday . It was a pa
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: After speaking with multiple tenants, before, during, and after last night's meeting, it's clear that, as this RAD conversion has taken place, some improvements in living conditions have been made but there is still much progress and…
item.content:encoded:
After speaking with multiple tenants, before, during, and after last night's meeting, it's clear that, as this RAD conversion has taken place, some improvements in living conditions have been made but there is still much progress and clarity to be had. This need for greater clarity is especially true when it comes to scheduling apartment renovations. Without it people have ended up taking days off from work with nobody showing up to make the renovations which leads to lost pay and time for residents on top of a failure to improve living conditions. It should also be noted that many residents want there to be permanent, not temporary, on-site security. 

We'll continue to work with residents and advocate to make sure that the issues are resolved, along with getting necessary funding secured as part of the pending Gowanus rezoning .

Looking ahead, as usual,our community is busy throughout the week. Tonight, the Parks Department will host a Red Hook Parks update at 155 Bay Street beginning at 6:30 PM, tomorrow the 76th Precinct Community Council meets and on Thursday our Transportation Committee meets at the 78th precinct.

There is more below but if this is where we part ways, enjoy the rest of your day, and feel free to share this information however you'd like.

item.title: Warren, Parks, Community, Testing
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: As always, our community is going to be busy as the post- plastic bag era begins. Tonight there is a Warren Street tenants meeting that will get started at 7 PM in the meeting room at 572 Warren Street .
item.content:encoded:
As always, our community is going to be busy as the post- plastic bag era begins. Tonight there is a Warren Street tenants meeting that will get started at 7 PM in the meeting room at 572 Warren Street . The purpose of this meeting is to get further clarity for residents as they transition to the RAD program.

Ensuring that the RAD program, which itself presents issues, is properly implemented, requires continued vigilance by the community. The residents of Warren Street, all of whom have been incredibly welcoming and engaged throughout this process deserve to see follow through on promised upgrades.

Such vigilance doesn’t just apply to Warren Street and, it’s crucial that capital needs and other improvements for NYCHA residents be secured in advance of the pending Gowanus rezoning.

There’s lots more happening throughout the week including a CB6 Transportation committee meeting , a Red Hook Parks update , a 76th Precinct Community Council meeting and other items that you’ll learn about by reading beyond my signature.

Enjoy the rest of the day and feel free to share this information , however you’d like.

item.content:encoded:
Last night, as previewed in previous emails, our Youth Human Services and Education Committee met at the Pacific Street Library. The agenda consisted of 2 presentations.

The first presentation was from the Brooklyn Public Library about necessary renovations to the Carroll Gardens Branch's HVAC system, which will result in a temporary closure of the library beginning next year. As we learn more about the timeline for the closing, we will share it in a future email, and that's a good reason to read these preambles.

The second presentation was from the Noel Pointer Foundation, a music education nonprofit for children, about their plans to establish their headquarters on Degraw Street . If you weren't there or want to try reliving the experience, check out both presentations here.

Today is, of course, a busy one across our community with a Cobble Hill Association meeting at PS 29 , while the YMCA hosts a jobs fair at the Park Slope Armory .There is, as usual, other stuff happening in the not too distant future, like next week's Transportation meeting , and other items you'll find below.

However, if you stop reading and here is where we part ways, have a good night, and feel free to share this information however you'd like.

item.title: Friday, February 14, 2020
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: The meeting was not as short as the agenda may have suggested, but that is a reflection of the thought and care our members put into our deliberations.
item.content:encoded:
The meeting was not as short as the agenda may have suggested, but that is a reflection of the thought and care our members put into our deliberations.

We got started by approving the January minutes , and our Chair, Peter Fleming, gave his report focussing on work the board is doing and will continue to do in terms of updating our Responsible Development Policies. Peter also mentioned that he’d spoken with representatives for the new owners of the 5 th Avenue Key Food site who said that groundbreaking is anticipated for this fall and that they would adhere to the agreement ensuring that a supermarket remains at the location.

Following the chair's report David Briggs , our Landmarks Chair presented 2 applications for Certificates of Appropriateness (C of A). You may recall, from reading the agenda or yesterday’s newsletter, that our Landmarks Committee had recommended approval the “C of A” at 895 Union Street while recommending disapproval for 187 Amity Street . It’s important to mention that because the full board overturned both of those recommendations.

895 Union Street’s application for a rear yard extension was, narrowly, disapproved while their request to replace non-visible mechanical equipment on the roof was approved.

187 Amity Street’s application for a two-story rear yard addition was overwhelmingly approved . The importance of efficient energy uses, such as window type used in passive house design in this case, was valued more than traditional casement windows.

After the voting portion of the evening, I reminded folks that Friday, February 14th, is the deadline to apply for CB membership and a  change of party registration before the presidential primary. I also mentioned tonight’s BQX forum and thanked people for signing up to receive these emails.

The final 2 items were community session and elected official reports.

During the community session, we heard from NYU , FDNY , the Civilian Complaint Review Board , and the Office of Emergency Management .

Finally, we heard from reps for Borough President Adams , Congresswoman Velasquez , State Senators Kavanagh , Montgomery and Myrie , Assemblymember’s Carroll and Simon , and Councilmembers Lander and Levin .

If reading the recap makes you want to know more about what’s going on in our community, please keep reading.

﻿Have a great evening and feel free to share  this informatio n  however you’d like.

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Wednesday, February 12, 2020
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: It begins at 6:30 PM in the NYP Brooklyn Methodist Auditorium ( entrance on 6 th Street between 6 th & 7 th Ave ). It’s important to remember today is the 211 th anniversary of Abraham Lincoln & Charles Darwin’s birth.
item.content:encoded:
It begins at 6:30 PM in the NYP Brooklyn Methodist Auditorium ( entrance on 6 th Street between 6 th & 7 th Ave ). It’s important to remember today is the 211 th anniversary of Abraham Lincoln & Charles Darwin’s birth.

Our general meeting agenda is relatively short as we seek to ratify recommendations from our Community Board 6 Landmarks Committee (CB6LM) of 2 Certificate of Appropriateness (C of A) applications. The first application approved by our LM Committee, is for the construction of a new rear-yard addition at 895 Union Street in the Park Slope Historic District . The second item up for ratification is the CB6LM Committee’s disapproval of an application to build a two-story rear yard extension at 187 Amity Street in the Cobble Hill Historic District .

As always we’ll have community session and reports from our elected official’s or their representatives.If you choose to keep reading, you’ll see lots is happening across our community throughout the rest of the week and further into the future.

Have a great evening, whether you are at the board meeting or not, feel free to share this information however you’d like.

Best,

This past week was a busy one for our community. It included GNCJ releasing their ( in line with what we’ve said ) priorities , GBD’s strategy finale , the CAG’s water quality petition , and the State of The City which included plans for solar power ,   Universal Literacy , housing , and small businesses .

The plans and priorities mentioned above are ideas at this point. Turning them into reality and implemented policies will require a great deal of action and work.

They are also ideas that are broadly in line with what CB-6 and our community at -large support. For that reason, we’ll have to be vigilant to ensure proper implementation.

item.title: Thursday, February 6, 2020
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Keep reading so you don't miss out on things happening across our community and various items of interest such as the State of the City and my personal favorite, a voting reminder.
item.content:encoded:
Keep reading so you don't miss out on things happening across our community and various items of interest such as the State of the City and my personal favorite, a voting reminder.

First up, the  Gowanus CAG has delivered their petition to N.Y. State Dept. of Environmental Conservation asking that the water quality requirements for the Gowanus Canal be updated to reflect current and planned future uses. CB6 has long and proudly supported improvement in Gowanus canal water quality and for that reason signed onto the petition.

We have twice passed UNANIMOUS resolutions, supporting improvements quality. Our support goes back to May of 2012 , and most recently, our Environmental Protection Committee Co-Chair Hildegaard Link presented this at our December 2019 General Board meeting, and we UNANIMOUSLY reiterated our support for reclassification. Big thank you to Hildegaard and her committee’s work and participation in the CAG to ensure we keep pushing in the right direction.

Speaking of appreciation for our Environmental Protection Committee Co- Chair’s, another big “thank you!” to Hildegaard’s counterpart Angelica Ramdhari , who pinch-hit for our Chair Peter Fleming at Brooklyn Borough Board last night.

Keep scrolling for more, have a good evening, and feel free to share this information however you’d like.

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.description: If you choose to read only 71 percent of this email, you may miss something, so I’d recommend scrolling on down.
item.content:encoded:
If you choose to read only 71 percent of this email, you may miss something, so I’d recommend scrolling on down.

No matter your current opinion, the Gowanus Neighborhood Coalition for Justice has set out thoughtful priorities which are largely aligned with those of the board often repeated to DCP . Such as demanding 100% affordable housing on city-owned sites, net-zero CSO’s s, significant improvements and protections for NYCHA and the IBZ.

Resolving these issues is key to creating a Gowanus that people can “Live, Work and Play” in. Of course, as a formal advisor to our City Government, our final position will be expressed in response to the upcoming ULURP .

If you choose to keep reading, as is the norm, you’ll find some happenings across our district, as well as items of potential interest.

Have a good evening; feel free to share  this information  however you’d like.

item.description: Last night our community was plenty active, and it was brought to you by the letters “B” and “Q,” as found in “BQX” and “BQE.”
item.content:encoded:
Last night our community was plenty active, and it was brought to you by the letters “B” and “Q,” as found in “BQX” and “BQE.”

The BQX took up the entire agenda of last night’s CB6 Transportation/Public Safety Committee meeting with a presentation given by EDC on the proposed streetcar. There’s always a healthy skepticism of big projects, and the BQX being no exception. Such feelings were evident and expressed at our meeting. If you weren’t able to attend, or want to try reliving the experience, check out the presentation slides here . You may also be interested in attending an upcoming public workshop to ask more questions and, hopefully, get more answers. Also, a big thank you to the Miccio Center for hosting us last night.

Around the same time, the BQE expert panel report was released. The biggest headlines out of it are recommendations for a reduction of lanes while preserving the promenade, but you can find more detail in articles such as this one . Big thanks to our Assistant District Manager Ty Beatty and Transportation Co-Chair Eric McClure for attending the report’s release at Borough Hall. Eric did impressive double duty since he made it to Red Hook in time to chair our Transportation Committee meeting.

Keep scrolling to find some weekend happenings, as well as some items of interest such as the plans to examine NYC Highways and a report on homelessness.

Have a great weekend and feel free to share this information  however you'd like. 

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager

item.content:encoded:
Our Transportation & Public Safety Committee meets tonight at the Miccio Center beginning at 7:00 PM, as even my most casual readers likely know by now.  EDC will present and take questions about plans for the BQX . There’s another reminder for this meeting below, along with a couple of articles on housing policy and more.

Speaking of housing policy, I’m happy to note that the advocacy work we, along with tenants such as Joe Anne Brown, Councilmember Levin’s Office and the Mayor’s Deputy Chief of Staff, Lincoln Restler did, led to NYCHA extending the lease deadlines as this property goes into the RAD program. While this is in line with the goals of the meetings that started earlier this month, it is distinct from our advocacy to ensure that improvements in the living conditions within NYCHA show tangible results before the pending Gowanus Rezoning goes forward.

Please read on and have a good evening; feel free to share  this information  however you’d like, and don’t forget about the BQX presentation tonight.

item.title: Wednesday, January 22, 2020
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Last night was the Warren Street Tenants meeting that had been repeatedly mentioned in previous updates. The purpose of the meeting was to get some much needed, and deserved, clarity for the residents of 572 & 574 Warren Stree t as the…
item.content:encoded:
Last night was the Warren Street Tenants meeting that had been repeatedly mentioned in previous updates. The purpose of the meeting was to get some much needed, and deserved, clarity for the residents of 572 & 574 Warren Stree t as the property enters the RAD program. Representatives from NYCHA and the development team (they will manage the property and oversee the renovations) ran the meeting and started by answering questions that the tenant association had asked in a letter earlier this month and followed it up by answering additional questions. 

After speaking with tenants this morning as follow up on last night, I am pleased that they felt there was greater clarity from NYCHA and the development team. However, gaining clarity doesn’t mean that all is positive. NYCHA tenants must be treated better, and information has to be given to tenants sooner and more openly. This meeting, yet again, reinforces why tangible improvements to living conditions for NYCHA residents must be secured to move forward with the pending rezoning of Gowanus .

Before moving on to other items, it’s important to thank those who worked tirelessly since our initial “meeting to get a meeting” on January 4th . That includes, but is not limited to, the Warren Street tenants and our very own CB6 member Joe Anne Brown, Assemblymember Simon’s office, Councilman Levin’s office (specifically Ben Solotaire) and the Mayor’s Deputy Chief of Staff, Lincoln Restler.

Of course, that’s not all that’s happening in our community, so it may be a good idea to keep scrolling to see more such as tomorrow’s landmarks/land use meeting, a Red Hook Business Meeting and next week’s BQX presentation to our Transportation/Public Safety Committee .

Have a good evening, feel free to share  this information  however/wherever you’d like

item.title: Thursday, January 9, 2020
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: 1-9-20 I hope this email finds you well on this cold 9th day of January. Our January board meeting, held last night at PS 58 , had a light agenda, but it's likely to be “the calm before the storm” bef
item.content:encoded:
1-9-20

I hope this email finds you well on this cold 9th day of January.

Our January board meeting, held last night at PS 58 , had a light agenda, but it's likely to be “the calm before the storm” before winds of 2020 starting blowing in. We were out of there in under an hour, as there was only 1 item on the agenda for approval.

Prior to dealing with the permits and licensing motion, our Board Secretary Karen Broughton, officially, certified the election of our current officers (Chair, 1 st Vice-Chair, 2 nd Vice-Chair, Secretary, and Treasurer) for another one-year term. It must be noted that Karen’s attendance is particularly impressive as she made it back in time after being in Albany , where she attended the Governor’s “State of the State” address.

The December 2019 minutes were approved. Chairperson Peter Fleming then gave his report, which included informing those in attendance about the revocation of the liquor license for Woodlands and the resale of the 5th Avenue Key food site . Peter made a point of mentioning that the new owners have indicated they will adhere to the agreement to retain a supermarket at the 120 5th Avenue address. We will continue to monitor the situation in conjunction with Councilmember Lander’s office. This is especially important with   so many supermarkets closing in recent years ,  and given how hard the  community worked to make sure a supermarket  would still serve our community. Peter also let folks know that applications for membership on Brooklyn community boards are open and will remain so until February 14th.

On the subject of board applications, my report got rolling by letting folks know that hard copies of the applications were available at the meeting, as well as online and that with few opening becoming a public member was a terrific alternative option. I then mentioned the Noel Pointer Foundation becoming the new tenants at the Degraw Street Firehouse and discussed our involvemen t with Warren Street tenants as an example of how CB6 can work to build better relationships between our neighbors and their city government. Of Course, I mentioned subscribing to this email update as it helps create a dialogue and open lines of communication. If something is going on in our community that you’d like to get on the CB6 radar, please let me know. For example, this update is the reason I’m planning on attending the Park Slope Civic Council meeting tonight at the Old Stone House . Every weekday you can scroll down that day’s email to find out about other community happenings.

Our Permits and Licenses Committee Chair Rachel Freeman presented their recommendation for approval of a sidewalk café at 72 5th Avenue that we overwhelmingly approved .

Representatives from the offices of Borough President Adams , Congresswoman Clarke , Councilmembers Lander and Levin , State Senators Montgomery and Myrie , Assemblymembers Carroll and Simon each spoke on behalf of their principals.

When we went into community session, there was mention of public safety concerns and drug use around Baltic Street and 4 th Avenue/ Gregory Place about and we’ve already reached out to proper authorities.

During New Business, Joe Anne Brown reemphasized the work we’ve been doing at Warren Street and the concerns residents continue to express. Kathy Park Price reminded everyone of the Citizens Squirrel event CB6 is co-sponsoring this upcoming Tuesday, January 14th and 1st Vice-Chair Eric McClure announced that our Transportation /Public Safety committee, with a location & agenda still being ironed out, would be meeting on January 30th which is the 5th Thursday of the month and not the usual 3rd Thursday.

So that, as best I can recall, is the gist of our first General Board Meeting for 2020. Have a good evening, feel free to share this information however/wherever you’d like.

P.S. Please forgive any typos or brain freezes in the text as I get these updates out in haste at the end of the day.

item.title: Monday, January 6, 2020
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: 1-6-20 I hope this email finds you well after a weekend that included a Sunday on which thousands, many BKCB6ers among them, marched against hate . The weekend also included, on Saturday, a Warren Str
item.content:encoded:
1-6-20

I hope this email finds you well after a weekend that included a Sunday on which thousands, many BKCB6ers among them, marched against hate .

The weekend also included, on Saturday, a Warren Street tenant’s initiated meeting with the stated goal of letting residents know that there was going to be a request made to the Mayor asking that NYCHA hold another meeting to answer questions, with greater clarity than there has been, on topics such as lease renewals and the RAD program .

BKCB6 Board member and Warren Street resident, Joe Anne Brown, was kind enough to invite me to this meeting and with that, I was able to extend the invitation to the Mayor’s Deputy Chief of Staff, Lincoln Restler who, like me, accepted the invitation; his attendance allowed the residents, and their meeting request, to be directly heard and responded to. Mr. Restler assured those in attendance, including Ben Solitaire from Councilman Levin’s office & representatives from the Gowanus Neighborhood Coalition for Justice (GNCJ) , that NYCHA will hold an additional meeting accomplishing Saturday’s stated goal.

This Warren Street meeting further reinforces, issues we’ve highlighted throughout the Gowanus rezoning process , that significant improvements must be guaranteed for NYCHA.

Now moving to what will be a busy week that includes tonight’s Permits and Licenses Committee meeting and Wednesday’s General Board Meeting. There are plenty of happenings that you can review by scrolling down.

Of course, it’s always possible you’ve seen something I missed in our active community, so if there is a community-centric item you’d like me to include,  please reach out.

Have a great evening, and feel free to share  this information.

P.S. Please forgive any typos or brain freezes in the text as I get these updates out in haste at the end of the day.

item.title: Happy New Year 2019 2
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: We hope this email finds you well and serves as a recap of 2019 highlights as we count down the hours remaining in 2019.
item.content:encoded:
We hope this email finds you well and serves as a recap of 2019 highlights as we count down the hours remaining in 2019.

A lot happened in our community in 2019. In Gowanus, we saw a draft zoning framework , plans for public place , new landmarks , the canal cleanup start moving forward while we continue to wait for the DEIS in 2020.

One of our New Year resolutions is to continue to make clear , how important it is that NYCHA has definitive and significant capital improvements while the IBZ be upzoned as a manufacturing zone to offset any losses within the rezoning before moving forward and don’t forget water quality should be in line with present and contemplated uses of the canal.

In 2019 we got a new use for the Degraw Street Firehouse , supported electric car charging stations and the introduction of Congresswoman Velasquez’s helicopter legislation , saw authorization for two-way Verrazzano tolling , cut the ribbon on a park and started the process for a redesign of another .

We also, sadly, lost a former board member and great community leader Alan Fleishman this year . Alan’s dedication to the community is the kind of commitment we’ll need to handle the challenges and opportunities in 2020 and beyond.

Looking ahead to 2020, our first General Board meeting of 2020 will be held at P.S 58 a week from tomorrow, Wednesday, January 8 th , while our first committee meeting takes place a week from yesterday, Monday, January 6 th in the Cobble Hill Community Room at 250 Baltic Street with Permits and Licenses reviewing a sidewalk café application. 

Speaking of beyond, we are co-sponsoring, along with with with great organizations such as the Brooklyn Public Library, Citizen Squirrel’s  January 14 th workshop for families with young children.

Finally, from everyone at Brooklyn Community Board 6, have a great and safe New Year!

Peter Fleming

Chairperson

item.title: Carroll Park, Tolls, Supermarkets Hopefully, everyone reading is found well on this cold 18th day of December
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Hopefully, everyone reading is found well on this cold 18th day of December, a day that will feature our Parks Committee meeting at P.S 58 , starting at 6:30 PM, in order to learn more, and have a say, about what’s next for Carroll Park .…
item.content:encoded:
Hopefully, everyone reading is found well on this cold 18th day of December, a day that will feature our Parks Committee meeting at P.S 58 , starting at 6:30 PM, in order to learn more, and have a say, about what’s next for Carroll Park . Links to more information about our Parks meeting, as well as other things happening tonight and throughout the week, are featured below. But before that, it could be a good idea to read up on 2 items of particular interest in our district.

First, BKCB6 has long supported 2-way tolling on the Verrazzano Bridge. This support, based on a belief backed up by traffic studies , is that it would help reduce traffic, especially truck traffic, and the corresponding congestion coming through our district, on roads such as the eastbound BQE . The reason that two-way tolling would reduce congestion is that, by eliminating an entirely free option, drivers would opt for a route that's based on time and proximity as opposed to price. I mention this because, while there is a lot of news, to say the least, coming out of Washington D.C these days, one particular news item is that the spending bill, which is expected to be approved this week, includes a provision that will split the toll for the Verrazano Bridge . 

If you’re wondering why this change requires an act of Congress, it’s because the Verrazzano Bridge is the only bridge in the country, owing to legislation passed in 1986 , to have its toll structure determined by the federal government. 

Second, the site of Key Food at 120 5th Avenue has been sold yet again . We are, of course, concerned about what this means for an agreement that ensured a supermarket would remain at the location. Early indicators are that the agreement will be honored, but we’ll stay vigilant and do everything possible to ensure that it remains that way. We’ve already spoken with Councilmember Lander about working together on this issue. This is an especially important issue with so many supermarkets closing in recent years , and how hard the community worked to make sure a supermarket would still be there. As we find out more, you’ll find out more.

Also, we are still accepting comments regarding  Public Place/ Gowanus Green  and appreciate everyone who already taken us up on this offer.

Have a great evening, as always, feel free to share  this information   howeve r you’d like, and if you want me to include a community-centric happening in a future update,  please reach out .

Best,

item.title: Recap, Reminders, Flyers I hope this email finds you well after last night’s meeting, which capped off another
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well after last night’s meeting, which capped off another decade of general board meetings.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well after last night’s meeting, which capped off another decade of general board meetings.

It was a quick meeting, but we had a wide range of things happening, including hearing from the community, votes on items from 3 of our committees, and reports from representatives of our elected officials.

During “Community Session,” we were informed on two opportunities and one opinion. The first was the 2020 Census and related job opportunities , second was about the Citizens Committee for NYC Grants , and finally, there was a criticism of the City’s plan for Public Place . The offer to send us your questions and/or let us know what you think about Public Place still stands, so email , and we’ll bring it to the attention of the appropriate parties.

Our first vote was on approval of a recommendation from our Environmental Protection Committee, presented by the committee’s Co-Chair Hildegaard Link. We are joining a panoply of organizations by submitting a letter in support of efforts demanding that the New York State Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC) not weaken water classification standards and to reclassify the water quality standard of the canal to more accurately reflect its current and future uses. Please note that we have a history of support for the canal’s reclassification to a higher standard as we also unanimously voiced our support as recently as May 2012 .

Our Permits and Licensing Committee was next on the docket with applications for 3 liquor licenses and 1 sidewalk café. Glenn Kelly, filling in for Committee Chair Rachel Freeman, presented, and all were overwhelmingly approved .

The final voting portion of the meeting was a recommendation from our Transportation Committee to support Congresswoman Nydia Velasquez’s Helicopter Safety Act , which would restrict non-essential helicopter flights across NYC. The board voted unanimously in support!

The meeting closed out with reps from the offices of Borough President Adams , Councilmember Lander , State Senator Montgomery , State Senator Myrie , Assemblymember Simon , Congresswoman Clarke , and Congresswoman Velasquez .

﻿

During new business, it was announced that the Friends of Carroll Park are holding their annual food drive on Saturdays throughout December.

While this wasn’t discussed during the meeting, the former Degraw Street Firehouse will no longer be vacant as it will become the home of Noel Pointer Foundation , which will operate a youth music education center.

That’s all I’ve got for today. If you keep scrolling, you’ll find some flyers for cool stuff happening across our community.

Have a good evening, and, as always, feel free to share this information and if you’d like me to share some community-centric info please reach out. 

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

Also, a heads up that, unlike today, Alternate Side Parking will be in effect tomorrow, Thursday, December 12th .

item.title: Parking Off, Last of The Decade, Complete Count and Civic Grants I hope this email finds you on another unseaso
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you on another unseasonably warm and rainy day. While it’s raining now, snow is headed our way and with that in mind, Alternate Side Parking is suspended tomorrow, Wednesday, December 11th .
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you on another unseasonably warm and rainy day. While it’s raining now, snow is headed our way and with that in mind, Alternate Side Parking is suspended tomorrow, Wednesday, December 11th . However, our December General Board Meeting , which is the last of the year and decade, will still be held at the Cobble Hill Health Center and start at 6:30 PM.

Before that, tonight, Tuesday, December 10th , there’s a “ Know Your Rights Forum ” hosted by Borough President Adams at Brooklyn Borough Hall , and at the  Green Building , they’ll be a panel discussion, featuring our very own Eric McClure, titled “ Net Zero for Neighborhoods .”

I repeat that tomorrow, Wednesday, December 11th, our General Board Meeting will be held at the Cobble Hill Health Center. On Thursday, December 12th , the  Carroll Gardens Association (CGA) will host a  census job workshop  at their  Columbia Street office .

CGA is also one of 3 organizations based in our community district that’s been awarded funds from the 2020 Census NYC Complete Count Fund . The other 2 BKCB6 based groups are the Red Hook Initiative and the Fifth Avenue Committee . So thank you to those groups doing the job of ensuring that all New Yorkers are counted so that we get our fair share of representation and funding .

Speaking of funding awards, the Park Slope Civic Council is seeking worthy applicants to their Community Grant program . These programs may include projects involving art, education, youth, and civic improvement. Click here for more info and how to apply.

A week from tomorrow, our  Parks Committee will meet   on  Wednesday, December 18th  at  PS 58  to hear more about the  Carroll Park redesign , on  Thursday,   December 19th ,    Assemblymember Carroll has an open house   and on Friday,  December 20th   Assemblymember Simon has an open house .

As I say every day, we’re lucky to have such an active community, so there is always a chance I’ve missed something. If there is an event or anything else community-centric happening that you think I/others should know about,  please reach out .

Have a great evening and, as always, feel free to share  this information   however you’d like.

Over in Park Slope, from 11 AM until 5 PM, the Old Stone House hosts a Holiday Book Fair , and from 10 AM until 5 PM, PS 321 will have a holiday market . item.title: More of Monday, Tonight, Tomorrow I hope this email finds you well on this cloudy and cold Wednesday . Again, we
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Again, we begin with Gowanus and Monday night’s EWCDH meeting and the Public Place/Gowanus Green presentation that was given during the meeting by the Department of City Planning (DCP), Housing, Preservation & Development(HPD) and Gowanus…
item.content:encoded:
Again, we begin with Gowanus and Monday night’s EWCDH meeting and the Public Place/Gowanus Green presentation that was given during the meeting by the Department of City Planning (DCP), Housing, Preservation & Development(HPD) and Gowanus Green .

There’s been coverage of the meeting that mentioned our position on affordability, but it’s important to reiterate that Brooklyn Community Board 6 is on the record in support of 100 percent affordable housing on city-owned Gowanus sites . Although it hasn’t been mentioned in any coverage to date, the Gowanus Green development team noted that a 100% affordable project would result in less height and less density.

Let’s be clear that the future of this site, and across Gowanus, is contingent on it being properly cleaned and then monitored. We are fortunate to have EPA region 2 oversight adding an additional layer of scrutiny.

At the meeting, we announced that additional questions and comments are welcomed by the board and that they should be sent via email . The comments we receive will then be directed to DCP, HPD, and the Gowanus Green team.

While Monday’s meeting focused on housing, we aren't for one second losing sight of protections for the Industrial Business Zone (IBZ), substantial monetary infusions for improvements to NYCHA campuses, as well as many other concerns that must be dealt with in the pending rezoning of Gowanus.

Moving to the more immediate future, as usual, our community is busy tonight, Wednesday, December 4th . At Pioneer Works , starting at 6:30 PM, the Theatre of the Oppressed will be performing a piece about gentrification in Red Hook and at 7:30 PM the 76 th Precinct Community Counci l, chaired by our very own Jerry Armer, holds its monthly meeting at the station house.

Tomorrow Thursday, December 5th , from 2:30- 3:30 PM City Comptroller Stringer holds a Senior Town Hall at NYP Brooklyn Methodist . While tomorrow evening will see merchants along Smith & Court Streets celebrating the holidays with extended house hours and free samples , Pig Beach hosts a tree lighting party in Gowanus , and the Park Slope Civic Council meets and celebrates at the Old Stone House !

Lastly, for the last time this year and decade, our next General Board Meeting is a week from today on Wednesday, December 11th , 6:30 PM at the Cobble Hill Health Center .

As I say every weekday, we’re lucky to have such an active community, and there is a chance I’ve missed something. If there is an event or anything else community-centric happening that you think I/others should know about,  please reach out .

Have a great evening and, as always, feel free to share  this information  however you’d like.

PS- Alternate Side Parking is in effect tomorrow, Thursday, December 5th , and if you haven’t done so already, please take the Brooklyn Bus Survey.

The 78th Precinct holds its Community Council meeting beginning at 7:30 PM in the station house while the 76th Precinct has a “Build the Block” meeting, 7:00 PM start time, at Mary’s Star of the Sea . On the east side of the Canal, the Gowanus CAG meets at the Old American Can Factory from 6:30 until 8:30 PM, and at the Miccio Center, from 6 until 8:00 PM, there will be a Red Hook Farm meeting .

Looking a bit further into the week, on Thursday, December 5th, City Comptroller Stringer holds a Senior Town Hall at NYP Brooklyn Methodist , merchants along Smith & Court Streets will be celebrating the holidays with extended house hours and free samples while Pig Beach is hosting a tree lighting party ! 

It's easy to get lost in all the holiday cheer, but please don’t forget that our next General Board Meeting is a week from tomorrow on Wednesday, December 11th , 6:30 PM,at the Cobble Hill Health Center .

As I say every weekday, we’re lucky to have such an active community, and there is a chance I’ve missed something. If there is an event or anything else community-centric happening that you think I/others should know about,   please reach out. .

item.title: Civic Cornucopia, Shopping in CB6 & More..... I hope this email finds you well on this warm 26th day of Novembe
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well on this warm 26th day of November. While this week is shortened by a holiday famous for forgivable gluttony, our community remains a civic cornucopia stuffed with meetings and other such happenings.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well on this warm 26th day of November.  While this week is shortened by a holiday famous for forgivable gluttony, our community remains a civic cornucopia stuffed with meetings and other such happenings.

Tonight,  Tuesday, November 26th, the  Cobble Hill   Association will host its annual fall meeting  in the Episcopal  Chu rch at 326 Clinton Street  from 7:00 until 8:30 PM and, over at the  Grand Army   Plaza Library , a  Census 2020   "Teach-In"  will be held from 6:00 until 7:30 PM. 

Tomorrow, Wednesday, November 27th , is known as “Thanksgiving Eve” or other non-complimentary titles : none of which have anything to do with civic activity. Either way, it’s a “ Gridlock Alert day ” as millions of people move to and fro to spend time with family for Thanksgiving.

On Thanksgiving itself, Thursday, November 27th , one thing people may be thankful for is Alternate Side Parking(ASP) and meters being suspended. If you aren’t eating home, or at someone else’s home, plenty of CB6 restaurants will be open, including 4 of the spots highlighted by BKLYNER .

Don’t let thankfulness turn into regret and remember that, mashed up against Thursday, on Friday, November 29th , ASP & parking meters are back in effect.

While Friday is “Black Friday,” a day famous for shoppers risking danger to get deals,  Saturday, November 30th is “Small Business Saturday.” . The City’s Small Business Services Commissioner, Greg Bishop, has some suggestions, along with shopping locally, for how you can help such business es. One way to get in the spirit of shopping local, right here in our district on Saturday, is by attending the  5th Avenue BID's   tree lighting  , from 4 until 6 PM, at  5th Avenue and 4th Street.

In addition to such commerce, retaining & growing local jobs is why we  continue to emphasize  the importance of the Industrial Business Zone ( IBZ ) in the pending rezoning of Gowanus. It’s also why I consistently mention our most recent letter to the Department of City Planning.

Speaking of Gowanus, please don’t forget that next week, on  Monday, December 2nd  , 6:30 PM, at    P.S 32 , the Department of City Planning (DCP) and Housing, Preservation, and Development (HPD), will be presenting an  update on the Public Place  /  Gowanus Green   site to our  Economic /Waterfront/ Community Development & Housing Committee  . If Gowanus interests you, we hope you can attend. 

On Tuesday, December 3rd , there will be a Red Hook Farms meeting at the Miccio Center from 6 until 8 PM, and during the afternoon of Thursday, December 5th Comptroller Stringer will be hosting a Senior Town Hall at   NYP Brooklyn Methodist .

Lastly, m ark your calendar now for our last General Board meeting of the year, which will be on Wednesday,  December 11th , we will hold our  December General Board Meeting  at the  Cobble Hill Health Center  beginning at 6:30 PM and featuring votes on things such as a Gin Distillery in Gowanus and Congresswoman Velasquez’s helicopter bill .

As I say every weekday, we’re lucky to have such an active community, and there is a chance I’ve missed something. If there is an event or something community-centric happening that you think I/others should know about,  please let me know .

Have a great evening and, as always, feel free to share  this information  however you’d like.

PS- Alternate Side Parking is in effect tomorrow, Wednesday, November 27th , and, if you have the time, read this piece that looks at a “YIMBY vs. NIMBY” divide. 

Related tools

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager

I hope this email finds you well after a restful weekend, a weekend that included a grand celebration of the Gowanus Dredgers 20 th anniversary. This week, despite being truncated by Thanksgiving, has a lot going on.

Tonight,  Monday, November 25 th,  our  Permits &   Licenses Committee  meets in the Community Room at  250 Baltic   Street to review applications for three liquor licenses and one sidewalk café. Tomorrow, Tuesday, November 26 th ,  the  Cobble Hill   Association will host its annual fall meeting  in the Episcopal  C hurch at 326 Clinton Street  from 7:00 PM until 8:30 PM and, on the same night, at the  Grand Army   Plaza Library , a  Census 2020   "Teach-In"  will be held from 6:00 PM until 7:30 PM.  Wednesday, November 27 th , “Thanksgiving Eve” will remain associated with traffic and bars rather than civic involvement.  Thursday, November 28 th,  is, of course, Thanksgiving, and you should know  Alternate Side Parking and   Meters will be suspended  but back in effect on  Friday, November 29 th . I emphasize that because, historically,  a lot of folks don’t seem to realize this , and more parking tickets are written than any other day of the year.

While Friday is “Black Friday,” which is, of course, famous for shoppers risking danger to get deals, Saturday, November 30 th is “Small Business Saturday.” Small (mom and pop), business’s help, and bind a community together making it the great place it is. One way to go local is by attending the 5th Avenue Bid’s tree lighting on Saturday, from 4 until 6 PM, on 5th Avenue and 4th Street.  In addition to such commerce, retaining & growing local jobs is why we continue emphasizing the importance of the Industrial Business Zone( IBZ ) in the pending rezoning of Gowanus.

Speaking of Gowanus, please don’t forget that one week from today, on Monday, December 2 nd   at    P.S 32 , the Department of City Planning (DCP) and Housing, Preservation, and Development (HPD), will be presenting an  update on the Public Place  /  Gowanus Green   site to our  Economic /Waterfront/ Community Development & Housing Committee  . If Gowanus interests you, we hope you can attend. Later next week, on  Thursday, December 5 th   NYC Comptroller Stringer hosts a Seniors Town Hall   at   NYP Brooklyn Methodist Hospital   while the next week, on Wednesday,  December 11 th , we will hold our  December General Board Meeting  at the  Cobble Hill Health Center  beginning at 6:30 PM.

As I say every day, we are lucky to have such an active community, and there is a chance I’ve missed something. If there is an event or something community-centric happening that you think I/others should know about,  please let me know .

Have a great evening and, as always, feel free to share  this information  however you’d like.

PS- Alternate Side Parking is in effect tomorrow, Tuesday, November 26 th, and you may want to read this article and remember it the next time you hear of opposition to a shelter.
