I hope this email finds you well as we head into the Weekend. As usual for a Friday email, it includes  DOT’s weekend traffic advisory , the  MTA "Weekender , " and a heads up that Alternate Side Parking(ASP) will be in effect throughout the weekend.

Our friends at the Gowanus Dredgers are celebrating their 20 th anniversary tonight, Friday, November 22 nd, from 7:00 until 9:30 PM at their boathouse . On Saturday, November 23 rd , the Grand Army Plaza Farmers Market will be held from 8:00 am until 4:00 PM, while on Sunday, November 24th , there are markets at the Old Stone House , in Carroll Gardens , and at Bartell Pritchard Square . 

Heading into next week, on Monday, November 25 th, our  Permits &   Licenses Committee  is meeting in the Community Room at  250 Baltic   Street . On  Tuesday, November 26 th ,  the  Cobble Hill   Association will host its annual fall meeting  in the Episcopal  C hurch at 326 Clinton Street  from 7:00 until 8:30 PM and, on the same night, at the  Grand Army   Plaza Library , a  Census 2020   "Teach-In"  will be held from 6:00 until 7:30 PM. Wednesday, November 27 th , “Thanksgiving Eve” will remain associated with traffic and bars rather than civic involvement.  Thursday, November 28 th, is, of course, Thanksgiving, and you should know Alternate Side Parking and Meters will be suspended but back in effect on Friday, November 29 th . I emphasize that because, historically, a lot of folks don’t seem to realize this and experience less cheer to start the holiday season.

Looking a bit further ahead to Monday, December 2 nd   at    P.S 32 , the Department of City Planning (DCP) and Housing, Preservation and Development (HPD), will be presenting an update on the Public Place  /  Gowanus Green site to our Economic /Waterfront/ Community Development & Housing Committee . So, if Gowanus interests you, we hope you can attend. Later that same week, on Thursday, December 5 th Comptroller Stringer hosts a Seniors Town Hall at NYP Brooklyn Methodist Hospital while the next week, on Wednesday, December 11 th , we will hold our December General Board Meeting at the Cobble Hill Health Center beginning at 6:30 PM.

As I say every day, we are lucky to have such an active community, and there is a chance I’ve missed something. If there is an event or something community-centric happening that you think I/others should know about,  please let me know .

Have a great weekend and, as always, feel free to share  this information  however you’d like.

item.content:encoded:
One week from today, most of us get to lean back after a good meal and be thankful on Thanksgiving, but tonight, Thursday, November 21 st , is a typically busy night across the 6th community district of Brooklyn. In Park Slope, at 6:30 PM, our Transportation and Public Safety Committee meets at the 78th Precinct , and from 6 PM until 8 PM, there will be a Red Hook East & West update meeting at the Miccio Center .

Tomorrow, Friday, November 22 nd , C ouncilmember Menchaca will be holding a Participatory Budgeting meeting at the Red Hook Justice Center from 1-3 pm. Looking to the weekend, we have farmers markets across the district/ district adjacent at Grand Army Plaza , Bartell Pritchard Square , Carroll Garden s and the Old Stone House ; so you may want to fill the larder for Thanksgiving.

Next week, we have one committee meeting, and that's our Permits & Licenses Committee on Monday, November 25 th , at 6:30 PM in the Community Room at 250 Baltic Street .  On Tuesday, November 26 th , the Cobble Hill Association will host its annual fall meeting in the Episcopal Church at 326 Clinton Street from 7:00 until 8:30 PM and, on the same night, at the Grand Army Plaza Library , a Census 2020 "Teach-In" will be held from 6:00 until 7:30 PM. The following day, Wednesday November 27 th , “Thanksgiving Eve,” is known for packed roads and bars rather than civic involvement.

As I mentioned yesterday , on  Monday, December 2 nd  at   P.S 32 , the Department of City Planning (DCP) and Housing, Preservation and Development (HPD), will be presenting an  update on the Public Place / Gowanus Green site to our Economic/Waterfront/ Community Development and Housing (EWCDH) committee. So, if Gowanus interests you, we hope you can attend. The week after the EWCDH meeting, on Wednesday, December 11 th , our final General Board Meeting of 2019 will be held at the Cobble Hill Health Center beginning at 6:30 PM.

As I say every day, we are lucky to have such an active community, and there is a chance I’ve missed something. If there is an event or something community-centric happening that you think I/others should know about, please let me know .

So, that’s all I’ve got for today, have a good evening and feel free to share this information however you’d like.

item.title: Nov 14 19 Ver 3
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well on this 2nd Thursday of November, which means that in 2 weeks it will be Thanksgiving. But before that, let’s recap last night's board meeting.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well on this 2nd Thursday of November, which means that in 2 weeks it will be Thanksgiving. But before that, let’s recap last night's board meeting. 

October’s agenda was   “unique” , but November’s was more traditional in that we heard from the usual suspects. 

The usual suspects being committees that have a responsibility to report to agencies such as the Landmarks Preservation Commission (LPC) and the State Liquor Authority (SLA). Those committees are Landmarks/ Land Use & Permits & Licenses. The meeting still had the unique quality of being chaired by our Vice-Chair, Eric McClure, who most ably filled in for our Chair Peter Fleming who had long-standing plans that prevented him from attending. During Eric’s quick report he reminded everyone to complete the  MTA’s Brooklyn Bus Survey .

Speaking of board officer excellence, all 5 of our officers were re-elected to a second one year term last night. Congratulations to Chair Peter Fleming, Vice Chair Eric McClure, 2nd Vice-Chair Jerry Armer, Secretary Karen Broughton, and Treasurer Tom Miskel.

Another semi-unique aspect was that we moved the community session to the start of the agenda as we promised to do. We heard from community members regarding the  6 th  Avenue/ Northern slope construction problem s , the importance of  accessibility in transportatio n ,  and   Census 2020  from our very own Jason Resichel.

Now, getting back the traditional agenda, our Landmarks Committee, chaired by David Briggs, had two motions from one application for a   Certificate of Appropriateness  at  633 2nd Street  located in the   Park Slope Historic District . We voted to   conditionally, approve both motions .

The next committee presentation was from Permits and Licenses, chaired by Rachel Freeman, with requests for five new on-premises liquor licenses from across our district, which were all unanimously approved.

One of the   approved applications  was advanced by a  Michelin Star Chef, Daniel Eddy , who plans to open a Bakery/Restaurant / Bar at  367 7th Avenue , where Hugo and Sons used to be. Also in Park Slope, on the border of Gowanus, at  548 4th Avenue, a Southern Italian restaurant  that plans to open in January. The other three applications were in the western part of our district. One was for a  small pizzeria in Carroll Gardens at 387 Court Street  and the other 2 in Red Hook- a  T hai restaurant at 380 Van Brunt Street   and at 34 Van Dyke, in the old Rocky Sullivan’s location,  t here wil l be an event/catering hall .

When the voting agenda was concluded, we heard from Representatives from elected official offices. Nicole Hunt spoke for Councilman Levin and reminded folks that  “Code Blue,"  was in effect. Oscar Jonas represented Senator Montgomery and highlighted that her   K inship legislation had been signed into law   while Jonathan Timm represented Senator Myrie and discussed discussed the work  Senator Myrie is doing to ban certain police practices .

Last, but not least, Dan Wiley spoke for Congresswoman Velasquez confirmed that he would be at our  Transportation / Public Safety Committee meeting  next week to discuss  federal helicopter legislation .

During new business Glenn Kelly let folks know that former BKCB6 Vice-chair Lou Sones says hello, Kathy Park Price announced  Citizen Squirrel   is holding an event on January 14th and our chair for the evening, let folks know he’s a METS fan and that Jacob deGrom had just been named  NL Cy Young winner for the second consecutive year . On that positive note The meeting was adjourned at 7:40.

Our next general board meeting is December 11th, 6:30 PM.

If last night, or reading about it wasn’t enough civic engagement for you, tonight at 6 PM,  The   Red Hook Community Justice Center has a grant information session  for artists and organizers, at 7 PM , 78, 8 th  Avenue, the   78th   Precinct hosts a Build the Block meeting   and  The   Old Stone House , from 8:00 until 10:00 pm, will be the place for  an   ecological concert .

That's all I've got for today, have a good evening either way and feel free to share  t his informatio n  anyway you’d like.

P.S, Alternate Side Parking is in effect tomorrow Friday, Nov 15th. 

Related tools

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well on this nearly freezing Friday as we head into Veterans Day Weekend.

As usual for a Friday email, it includes DOT’s weekend traffic advisory , the MTA "Weekender , " and a heads up that Alternate Side Parking will be in effect on Saturday, November 9 & Sunday the 10th, but suspended on Monday, November 11th for Veterans Day.  DSNY pickup will also be suspended for Veterans Day . Before our Monday holiday, and after it, we have plenty of stuff happening across our community in the days ahead.

Tomorrow, Saturday, November 9th many of our elected leaders will walk in support of immigrant children being held at the border . Also, tomorrow, in advance of Tuesday’s MTA Open House , members of the Red Hook community will be meeting at the Red Hook Library to discuss advocacy for their local issues relating to the Brooklyn Bus Redesign .

On Sunday, November 10th, you can do some baking at The Old Stone House and, if you’d like to rid yourself of any pumpkins, but want to do so in a fun/stress relieving and environmentally friendly way, come by the Carroll Gardens Greenmarket and smash them ! 

Monday, November 11th, is, of course, Veterans Day, and Carroll Park will be holding its annual ceremony by the War Memorial to honor all those who’ve fought for our country.

On Tuesday, November 12 th , as mentioned above, the MTA will be hosting an open house at the Park Slope Library , regarding the Brooklyn Bus Network Redesign , and many see this as an opportunity to bring back a revised version of the B71 bus . If you agree and have the time, join our friends at Citizen Squirrel before the open house to rally in support of its return ! On the same night (Nov 12), the 76 th precinct will be hosting a “Build The Block ” meeting at D’Amico’s .

Of course, don’t forget that next Wednesday, November 13th  is our General Board meeting , starting at 6:30 PM and held at M.S 51 .

We are lucky to have such an active community, so there’s always a chance I miss something. If there is any community-centric event or information you’d like me to share,  please reach out .

item.content:encoded:
As always, I hope this email finds you well, but, unlike other days. I also hope the main point of it is made moot.

Our office is closed today, but it won’t stop me from reminding folks they have a chance to shape how our city is governed by voting in today’s election . If one thinks their vote doesn’t matter, please consider that, due to a low turnout, your vote will matter even more than usual.

So, the polls are open until 9 pm tonight, Tuesday, November 5th. If you don’t know who you'll be voting for, click here , if you don’t know what you’ll be voting for, click here and if you don’t know where to vote, click here . 

Also, please be aware that unlike today Alternate Side Parking will be in effect tomorrow Wednesday, November 6th. Lastly, since pickup was suspended today, if Tuesday is your scheduled day for trash and compost pickup please put those materials out today after 4 PM so they can be picked up tomorrow, Wednesday November 6th.

So that's all I've got for today, have a good evening, and feel free to share  this information  any way you’d like.

item.title: November 4 Daily Email 5
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well after a weekend that included the marathon making its way through our district , and kick off the first full week of November- a week that will be stuffed full of happening, including the possibility of the…
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well after a weekend that included the marathon making its way through our district , and kick off the first full week of November- a week that will be stuffed full of happening, including the possibility of the first snow of the season .

Tonight, Monday, Nov, 4th  Congresswoman Velasquez will host a Cancer Awareness  event at the   Red Hook Library . Also in Red Hook, CEC 15 will meet  at P.S 676 , and, on the other side of our district, in the North Slope, the  78 th  precinct will be holding a “Build The Block”  meeting at the  6 th Avenue Baptist Church .

Now, as I’m sure regular readers of these emails know, I love encouraging all things voting. Whether it’s registration , early voting, or any other thing that's relevant to voting, I remind folks about it, as much as humanly possible. So I’d be remiss if I didn’t take this opportunity to remind you that tomorrow, Tuesday, November 5th, is, of course, Election Da y . This year everyone, regardless of party affiliation gets a say in how our city is governed by voting on proposed charter reforms , and as it is a general election, we all get to vote for the citywide office of Public Advocate . If you’re unsure where to vote, click here to find your polling location .

Along with the chance to vote tomorrow, Tuesday, November 5th, please be reminded that Alternate Side Parking and NYC Sanitation will be suspended . Also, NYC Public School STUDENTS have the day off.

Moving on to Wednesday, November 6 th , The 76 th Precinct’s Community Council , chaired by our very Jerry Armer, will meet at the Precinct station house, 191 Union Street (Between Hicks & Henry Streets) . Also on Wednesday, November 6th at 6:30 pm, the Saint John’s Place Community Association will be meeting at the Saint John’s Church to discuss the water main replacement project that has caused plenty of unintended problems in the North Slope .

On Thursday, November 7 th , the Gowanus Canal Conservancy will host its annual meeting at 501 Union Street while the Park Slope Civic Council will meet at the Old Stone House .

We are lucky to have such an active community, so there is always a chance I miss something. If there is any community-centric event or information you’d like me to share, please reach out .

So that's all I've got for today, have a good evening, and feel free to share   this information   any way you’d like.

item.title: November 1 Daily Email 2
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well as November bursts onto the scene with some high-powered winds . We head into a weekend during which an hour of sleep could be be gained, and The New York City Marathon runs at a brisk pace through our…
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well as November bursts onto the scene with some high-powered winds . We head into a weekend during which an hour of sleep could be be gained, and The New York City Marathon runs at a brisk pace through our district. So, be mindful of the Marathon’s route and cheer on the participants if you’d like but also remember to reset your clocks and check the batteries of your smoke/ carbon monoxide alarms. While you’re at it check out DOT’s traffic advisory , the  MTA’s Weekender and note that Alternate Side Parking, which is suspended today , will be in effect through the weekend and on Mon, Nov 4th , but again suspended on Election Day, Tuesday November 5th .

Speaking of the election, you can still vote early through Sunday, Nov 3rd , and the old fashioned way on Tuesday November 5th . .

It was great to see so many people out enjoying Halloween with so many young ghouls roaming across our community. Also, if you want to say goodbye to any pumpkins in your life, you can do so in style by smashing them at the Carroll Gardens Greenmarket next Sunday, November 10th . . However, if you can’t stand to look at a gourd for another week you can venture beyond the boundaries of our district and start smashing as soon as tomorrow, Nov 2nd .In case anyone was wondering, I don’t think Billy Corgan will be receiving royalty checks from this.

Looking ahead to next week, on Monday, Nov, 4th Congresswoman Velasquez will host a Cancer Awarenes s event at the Red Hook Library , and, on the same night CEC 15 will meet at Red Hook’s  P.S 676 . Over in the North Slope, also on Monday, the 78 th precinct will be holding a “Build The Block” meeting at the 6 TH Avenue Baptist Church while their neighboring precinct’s Community Council meets on Wednesday, November 6 th at 191 Union Street (The 76 th Precinct ) . Moving east on Union Street, at 501 Union , and one day ahead on the calendar, the Gowanus Canal Conservancy will host its annual meeting on Thursday, November 7th.

So that’s all I’ve got for today, feel free to share this info , have a great weekend and enjoy some extra sleep.

P.S- if you missed anything in this week's prior updates, you can see them here- Oct 28th . , 29th , 30 th , and 31 st .

item.title: October 31 Daily Email 2
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: As you can see from the screenshot above, not only are we aware that today is Halloween, but we hope it’s a happy and safe one across our community, which has lots of things happening despite the possibility of continued rain .
item.content:encoded:
As you can see from the screenshot above, not only are we aware that today is Halloween, but we hope it’s a happy and safe one across our community, which has lots of things happening despite the possibility of continued rain .

The  Park Slope Civic Council hosts its annual parade  from 7th Avenue and 14th Street down to the  Old Stone House . The  Brooklyn Conservatory of Music  becomes the  Con-spook-atory ,  Cobble Hill will also have a parade  while in Carroll Gardens,  Scotto’s , led by our very own John Heyer   will scare you and then calm you with candy . Also, if you're around Warren Street , stop by and say hi as our very generous Joe Anne Brown will be giving out candy to trick or treaters until 8 pm. Even if you don’t want candy, they’ve got a great decoration display .

A big "THANK YOU" to those who responded to my previous emails asking you to let me know about Halloween happenings . For example, just a little while ago, I was given a heads up about a free puppet show taking place tonight, 5:30 until 9:00, put on by Dzieci Theatre at 241 Garfield Place . Here’s a video of past performances .   

I’ll be back to more mundane reminders before you know it, but please note that Alternate Side Parking (ASP) will be suspended tomorrow , Friday, November 1st. . If you plan on using the subway tomorrow, click here for scheduled service change s  and here for   bus service changes . Also, don’t forget that our November Full Board meeting is 2 weeks from yesterday, November 13 th, at M.S 51 , and, if you haven’t already done so , go vote!

That's all I've got for today, feel free to share this information and have a happy and safe Halloween!

PS- If you have the time, you may want to learn more about the history of Halloween and haunting in our great city.

item.title: October 30 Daily Email 3
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Happy "eve" of All Hallows' Eve. The mist of today isn't the 90s computer game and makes it harder to see, but reading on you’ll, hopefully, see what’s happening across our community a bit more clearly.
item.content:encoded:
Happy "eve" of All Hallows' Eve. The mist of today isn't the 90s computer game and makes it harder to see, but reading on you’ll, hopefully, see what’s happening across our community a bit more clearly.

No amount of rain, or mist, was about to stop the crew at yesterday’s B arnacle Parade or the unveiling of Sandy’s high-water mark in Red Hook . It also won’t deter the Red Hook Civic Association from meeting tonight, Wed, Oct 30th 7:00 PM at P.S 15 or Congresswoman Velasquez from hosting a cancer awareness event on Monday, Nov 4 th at the Red Hook Library.

In another of our water adjacent neighborhoods, the future of the Gowanus remains obscured. However, after yesterday’s Landmark Preservation Commission vote 5 properties were designated as historic landmarks we have a better sense of what the future holds . We proudly supported these designations that maintain a sense of place and time.

As noted by my frightful attempt at humor in the first sentence, tomorrow, Thurs, Oct 31st, is Halloween and lots will be happening. The  Park Slope Civic Council hosts its annual parade  from 7th Avenue and 14th Street down to the  Old Stone House . The  Brooklyn Conservatory of Music  becomes the  Con-spook-atory ,  Cobble Hill will also have a parade  while in Carroll Gardens,  Scotto’s , led by our very own John Heyer   will scare you and then calm you with candy . Also, if you're around Warren Street stop by and say hi as our very generous Joe Anne Brown will be giving out candy to trick or treaters until 8 pm. Even if you don’t want candy they’ve got a great decoration display .

Again , Halloween has a lot going on, so if you think I’ve missed a community-centric celebration,   please reach out , and I’ll be happy to share it.

If you plan on using the subway, tomorrow, Thurs, Oct 31,  click here for planned for service changes  and here for   bus service changes . Also, just like today, Alternate Side Parking (ASP) regulations will be in effect   tomorrow, Thurs, Oct 31,  but suspended the next day on Fri, Nov 1 st .     Regardless of ASP,   you can vote all week and remember our Nov Full Board meeting is 2 weeks from today.

So that's all I've got for today, have a good evening, and feel free to share  this information  any way you’d like.

PS- If you have the time, you may want to check out DCP’s report on the Geography of Jobs or read about some powerful paint.

item.title: October 29 Daily Email 2
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well. Today, October 29 th may be a cloudy Tuesday , but this update will attempt to be crystal clear.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well. Today, October 29 th may be a cloudy Tuesday , but this update will attempt to be crystal clear.     

I want to start by recalling that, during this week of Halloween, the impact of climate change will always be more frightening than any costume. So, on this 7 th anniversary of Superstorm Sandy , it’s essential not to rest easy and remember that we must work quickly and with each other to make the changes necessary to combat climate change. So, while it’s not a pleasant memory for our community, it’s great to see Red Hook come together for the Barnacle Parade , the unveiling of Sandy’s high watermark , and environmental justice workshops .  

While focusing on Red Hook, please be aware that tomorrow, Wed, Oct 30th , the Red Hook Civic Association will meet at P.S 15 with a 7 PM start time. Please also note that the Justice Center and Miccio Center have partnered on a donation drive to collect necessities such as coats, hats, and toothpaste.Continuing with charity, don't forget that P.S 32 is holding a food drive and that tonight is CHIPS night out . 

Speaking of going out in our community, last night, Mon, Oct 28th, our Permits and Licenses committee met and approved 5 liquor license applications . As previously mentioned , a full board vote on these items will take place during our November 13 th  General Board Meeting at M.S 51 .

While the general board meeting is 2 weeks from tomorrow, later this week, there will be lots going on across our district for Halloween. For example, The   Park Slope Civic Council hosts its annual parade  from 7th Avenue and 14th Street down to the Old Stone House . The  Brooklyn Conservatory of Music  becomes the  Con-spook-atory , Cobble Hill will also have a parade  while in Carroll Gardens,   Scotto’s , led by our very own John Heyer will scare you and then calm you with candy . 

Halloween has a lot going on, so if you think I’ve missed a community-centric celebration, please reach out , and I’ll be happy to share it.

If you plan on using the subway, tomorrow, Wed, Oct 30 th , click here for planned for service changes and here for bus service changes . Also, just like today, Alternate Side Parking (ASP) regulations will be in effect tomorrow, Wed, Oct 30th, but suspended this Fri, Nov 1 st .   Regardless of ASP, you can vote all week .

So that's all I've got for today, have a good evening, and feel free to share  this information  any way you’d like.

PS- If you have the time, you may want to check out what the City Council is saying  it will do to be ready for the next superstorm, “ fall back” fixes and package problems .

item.title: October 28 Daily Email first email
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well after a weekend that may have included Halloween celebrations or, for the first time in New York, early voting . If seeing such and civic action left you with a fear of missing out ( FOMO ) rest assured, if…
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well after a weekend that may have included Halloween celebrations or, for the first time in New York, early voting .  If seeing such and civic action left you with a fear of missing out ( FOMO ) rest assured, if you continue reading, you’ll learn how to get in on it.

Speaking of civic activity, tonight at 6:00 pm, our Permits and Licenses Committee meets to review five liquor license applications.   Whatever the committee, chaired by Rachel Freeman, decides those applications will then be put up for our final vote during the Wed, Nov 13th board meeting .

Tomorrow, Tues, Oct 29 th , the   7 th  Annual Barnacle Parade ,  remembering Superstorm Sandy, will march down   Van Brunt Street . If you plan on being part of it, get   there early   (3:15 pm) and check out  Portside’s   unveiling of Sandy’s  high watermark . Tomorrow is also CHIPS night out , which means that, if you eat or drink at one of the participating establishments, 15 percent of your check will be donated to CHIPS. If you’re not familiar with this organization,  CHIPS has been providing food and shelter to those in need for almost 50 years. Services such as this are especially important when one opens up a newspaper and reads that 1 out of every 10 school children in our city is without a home .

Later in the week, on Thurs Oct 31st, Halloween, the  Park Slope Civic Council hosts its annual parade  from 7th Avenue and 14th Street down to the Old Stone House . While the  Brooklyn Conservatory of Music  becomes the  Con-spook-atory , Cobble Hill will also have a parade  while in Carroll Gardens, Scotto’s, led by our very own John Heyer, will keep a Halloween tradition alive .

If you plan on using the subway, which just turned 115 , tomorrow, Tuesday, October 29 th , click here for planned for service changes . As for bus service changes, click here . If you want to let the MTA know what you think of the buses, take this survey and mark your calendar for their Tues, Nov 12th “Open House” at the Park Slope Library . Also, just like today, alternate side parking  (ASP) regulations will be in effect tomorrow, Tues, Oct 29 th .

So, do you remember how I said I would let you know how to get in on the civic action? Well, throughout the entire week, even as I type this, you can vote early and ease any feeling of democratic FOMO. To help with that, here’s a “ who ,  what , and  where “ for this year's election. Don’t forget you can also vote the traditional way next Tues, Nov 5 th .

Have a good evening, and feel free to share this information any way you’d like.

PS- If you have the time, you may want to check out the benefits of free school lunches , legislation to limit helicopters , and a plan for 2021 .

item.title: October 25 Daily Email 2nd
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well as we head into what may prove to be a rainy weekend . As my Friday emails always do, I’ll share the DOT’s traffic advisory , the MTA Weekender , and let you know that Alternate Side Parking Regulations…
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well as we head into what may prove to be a rainy weekend . As my Friday emails always do, I’ll share the DOT’s traffic advisory , the MTA Weekender , and let you know that Alternate Side Parking Regulations will be in effect . However, this is the first time in New York’s history (predating me by quite a few years) that you can be advised that early voting starts tomorrow!

If you choose to vote early, find out who you can vote for , what you can vote for , and where you can vote . 

To put it mildly, not everyone is as revved up about early voting as I am, and I’m aware that other things are happening. For example, in our district, the BKCB6 Landmarks/ Land Use Committee met and conditionally approved an application for a Certificate Of appropriateness (C of A) at 633 2nd Street , Park Slope Historic District . That application will come before us on November 13 th at our general board meeting along will items anticipated from the upcoming Permits & Licenses meeting . 

There is also a lot happening across our district to celebrate Halloween starting as soon as tonight with the 5 th Avenue Business Improvement District’s Halloween Bar Craw l . Tomorrow, Saturday, October 26 th , we’ll have celebrations in  Carroll Park ,  P.S 15 , Thomas Greene Playground , window painting on court street , and a Haunted Walk in Prospect Park . On Sunday, October 27 th , the Urban Meadow hosts its annual parade , and the Old Stone House will host a costume contest and mini-parade .

The celebrations don’t end when the weekend is over. On Tuesday, October 29 th , the 7 th Annual Barnacle Parade , remembering Superstorm Sandy (the ravages of climate change are scary without the need of a costume), will march down Van Brunt Street . If you plan on being part of it, get there early (3:15 pm) and check out Portside’s unveiling of Sandy’s high watermark . On Halloween itself, Thursday, October 31 st , in Park Slope, the Civic Council hosts its annual parade while the Brooklyn Conservatory of Music becomes the Con-spook-atory . Cobble Hill will also have a parade while in Carroll Gardens, Scotto’s keeps a tradition alive .

Having started where I usually conclude with info on trains, traffic, and parking I’ll change it up by saying welcome to all the new subscribers. I hope you find these updates useful and please, ALWAYS , feel free to reach out with any questions. I’d also like to thank our Human Services Chair, Kathy Park Price, for taking the time to promote these daily updates

Have a great weekend, take the bus survey , and feel free to share this information any way you’d like.

PS- I thought about closing with Wegmans , but that’s outside the district and seems to be getting enough attention.

Mike Racioppo, District Manager

item.title: October 24 Daily Email second
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Tonight, as I’ve been mentioning , our Landmarks/ Land Use Committee meets at 250 Baltic Street to review one landmark application.
item.content:encoded:
Tonight, as I’ve been mentioning , our  Landmarks/ Land Use Committee meets at 250 Baltic Street to review one landmark application.

Last night our Youth/ Human Services and Education (YHSE) Committee met at the Brooklyn Public Library’s Red Hook branch . First on the agenda was a presentation from the library about its planned redesign. The presentation was well-received, and if you could not attend, you can see what was presented here . The other agenda item was the NYC 2020 Census Complete Count which focused their work to set up Neighborhood Organizing Census Committees(NOCC). If you are interested in being part of this effort to not only ensure that all New Yorkers get counted but that we get our fair share of funding for things like schools, roads, and buses check out this website .

Moving on to the near future on Monday, October 28 th , we have our Permits and Licenses Committee  meeting at 250 Baltic with a start time of 6:00 pm. On the next page of your calendar, please note that our November Board Meeting will take place at M.S 51 on November 13th.

On to other matters such as Halloween celebrations across our community. On Saturday, October 26th, we’ve got Halloween celebrations in Carroll Park , P.S 15 , and the Old Stone House , and on Sunday, October 27 th , in the Columbia Waterfront, the Urban Meadow hosts their annual parade .

Rest easy as parades will not be limited to the weekend. The 7 th annual Barnacle Parade is Tuesday, October 29 th , The Thomas Greene Playground Halloween Parade is on Wednesday, October 30 th, On Halloween itself, Thursday, October 31 st , Park Slope’s parade will start on 7 th Avenue , Cobble Hill’s parade kicks off at Cobble Hill Park while The Scotto Funeral Home maintains tradition on Court Street and the Brooklyn Conservatory of Music will become the Con-spook-atory .

Now there may be some scary stuff at those parades but nothing to compare with low voter turnouts. So, until the elections are over, I will haunt you with reminders that you can vote early for the first time evert starting this Saturday .

Just like today, alternate side parking (ASP) regulations will be in effect tomorrow, Thursday, October 25th , and, like every other day, there will be planned service changes on   subways  and  buses .

That's all I've got for today, but I hope you have a good evening and feel free to share  this informatio n  any way you'd like.

item.title: October 24 Daily Email 2
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Whether you prefer today’s sun or yesterday’s rain, I hope this email finds you well on this 23 rd day of October.
item.content:encoded:
Whether you prefer today’s sun or yesterday’s rain, I hope this email finds you well on this 23 rd day of October.

Before we look forward, I’d like to draw your attention to some news made last night. At the CEC15 meeting, it was announced that the local school rezoning would be delayed .

Meanwhile, over at the Gowanus CAG , there was an update on the installation of the cut-off wall that is being constructed to prevent the recontamination of the Canal from toxins at the Fulton MGP site . The Environmental Protection Agency’s (EPA) Project Manager Christos Tsiamis stated that it’s on track to be completed by August 2020 and said: “ so far, so good .” Also, the NYC Department of Environmental Protection(DEP) has asked, via letter, that EPA reconsider the initial rejection of their tunnel cleanup plan . However, it seems unlikely that the EPA would agree to DEP’s request given the basis of EPA’s rejection and considering that the EPA is the final authority for approval.

I attended the early voting forum held by Assemblymember Ortiz at the Miccio center, as I’m a zealous advocate of civic participation. I remain on high alert for all things that reinforce the importance of voting. Fitting such criteria are the proposed charter revisions . For example, question 5 would give Community Boards more time to review proposed land-use changes. The New York Landmarks Conservancy has now come out in favor of these changes . Way back in June, we asked DCP to apply such changes to the pending Gowanus rezoning.

Now, looking forward to the near future.

TONIGHT our Youth, Human Services, and Education Committee   will meet at the   Red Hook Library  to hear plans for the library's redesign, as well as a presentation from the   NYC 2020 Census Complete Count . 

Tomorrow, Thursday, October 24 th, our  Landmarks/ Land Use Committee meets at 250 Baltic Street to review one landmark application, and on Monday, Permits and Licenses Committee  meets at the same location. Our November Board Meeting will take place at M.S 51 on November 13 th.  

Just like today, alternate side parking (ASP) regulations will be in effect tomorrow, Thursday, October 24th, and, like every other day, there will be planned service changes on   subways  and  buses .

That's all I've got, but I hope you have a good evening and feel free to share this information  any way you'd like.

I hope this email finds you well on this twenty-second day of October as we are expecting more rain this evening . For those who to keep reading, you’ll find some familiar, as well as new, reminders and something of a parking plot twist. But first I’d like to take this opportunity to congratulate our very own Joe Anne Brown on being honored by her Union, DC 37, as well as the Department of Education for her 20 years of service in our public schools. Congratulations Joe Anne!

Moving to the non-congratulatory portion of this email….

You may be inured to my reminders about all things voting, but I will not be dissuaded, especially in the first year of early voting ! Any questions about early voting? Come by the Miccio Center tonight, from 6:00 pm until 8:00 pm, as Assemblymember Ortiz is hosting an early voting forum .

Also, tonight, CEC15 will be meeting at P.S 38, 450 Pacific Street while the Gowanus CAG meets at Saint Mary's Star of the Sea, 41 1st Street.

As I keep mentioning, 2 of our committees will be meeting this week. On Wednesday, aka tomorrow, our Youth, Human Services, and Education Committee   will meet at the   Red Hook Library  to hear plans for the library's redesign, as well as a presentation from the   NYC 2020 Census Complete Count . On Thursday, October 24 th, our  Landmarks/ Land Use Committee meets  to review one landmark application. 

Looking briefly to next week, on Monday, October 28th, at 6:00 pm , our  Permits and Licenses Committee  meets at 250 Baltic Street in the Cobble Hill Community Room.

Have you read this far? Well, if you did, here comes the plot twist I referred to above. Unlike today,  alternate side parking (ASP) regulations will be in effect tomorrow, Wednesday, October 23 rd, and, like every other day, there will be planned service changes on   subways  and  buses .

item.title: October 18 Daily Email 3
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well as we head into the third weekend of October.It's been a busy week in our community and city at large . So, as we welcome the prospect of restful days ahead, check out some of the items below.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well as we head into the  third weekend  of October.It's been a busy week in our community and   city at large . So, as we welcome the prospect of restful days ahead, check out some of the items below. Those items include our latest statement surrounding Gowanus, upcoming meetings, train changes, and traffic advice, and more.

Keeping things in chronological order, I'll begin   by sharing the letter we hashed out and sent over to the Department of City Planning (DCP ) . The letter contained in the bolded hyperlink above reiterates our priorities and concerns about the pending rezoning of Gowanus.

Speaking of Gowanus, as I've mentioned,  Gowanus Open Studios  is this week and will feature hundreds of artists, including our very own   David Briggs . On Saturday, in Red Hook, you can hop aboard the   Mary A Whalen during Portside's open house  and then on Sunday get a   flu shot at Assemblymember Carroll's   office- call (718)-788-7221 to make an appointment.

After getting a flu shot, you may feel better about going out in public and attending a committee meeting or two, and, as luck would have it, 2 of our committees meet next week. The first is on Wednesday, when our   Youth, Human Services, and Education Committee  meets at the   Red Hook Library  to hear about plans for the library's redesign, as well as a presentation from the   NYC 2020 Census Complete Count . The second is on Thursday, October 24th, when our   Landmarks/ Land Use Committee meets  to review 1 landmark application.

Looking further into the future, our  Permits and Licenses committee meets  the following Monday, October 28th. Due to the expanding agenda, it will get started at 6:00 pm and not it's usual 6:30 pm. Speaking of BKCB6 restaurants and bars, 7 of them, were named to the Michelin Bib Gourmand list.

Just like today, alternate side parking (ASP) will be in effect throughout the weekend and mimicking this week; ASP will   be suspended next Monday and Tuesday . As you travel around, please take note of   MTA changes  and   DOT's advice  regarding traffic.

That's all I've got for today, but I hope you have a great weekend and feel free to share this information any way you'd like.

item.content:encoded:
As we experience some rain , and I keep thinking its Tuesday, I hope you read this email from a waterproof location, and for those who are continuing to celebrate the season of Sukkot, my wish remains that you have a bountiful harvest and ‘Chag Sameach”.

While none of our committees will be meeting this week that doesn’t mean there aren’t a lot of other things going on. For example, tomorrow night, Thursday October 17th, at the Miccio Center beginning at 6 PM, the second of 2 school rezoning meetings will be held, and, at the same time, the Southwest Brooklyn Tenants Union is meeting in the Columbia Waterfront District . While we’re discussing our water adjacent neighborhoods, I suggest checking out Portside’s open house this coming Saturday. Also this Saturday, and Sunday, Gowanus Open Studios will be happening, and it includes the fine art of our very own David Briggs . 

Looking ahead, one week from today, October 23 rd , our Youth Human Services and Education Committee will meet at the Red Hook Library featuring a presentation from the NYC Census 2020 Complete Count. The following night, Thursday, October 24 th , with an agenda still in formation, our Landmarks/Land Use Committee will meet, 6:00 PM, at 250 Baltic Street. Also, four weeks from tonight, our next full board meeting will be held at M.S 51 on November 13th.

Before I reveal whether alternate side parking regulations are in effect, I’d recommend checking out what will be the most crucial item in this year’s election and why more can be done to fight poverty .

So the big reveal is that, just like today, alternate side parking will be in effect tomorrow, Thursday, October 17 th , while the trains and buses , as they do every day, will have some planned service changes.

That’s all I’ve got for today, but, as always, I hope you have a good evening and feel free to share this information any way you’d like.

item.title: October 11 Daily Email 3
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well as we head into what looks to be a typical fall weekend . It was great to see many of you at last night’s Board meeting.
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well as we head into what looks to be a typical fall weekend . It was great to see many of you at last night’s Board meeting. If you weren’t there or want to relive the magic through the written word, please keep reading. 

We had a unique agenda with items from committees we don’t always hear from while not having items from some of the usual suspects. One of those usual suspects, our Permits & Licenses Committee, as was noted, will begin its next meeting at 6:00 PM on October 28th instead of its usual 6:30 pm start time. 

The first agenda Item was from our Economic Waterfront Committee Development & Housing Committee (EWCDH) and concerned the retention of Gowanus businesses, including a quintessential “Gowanus Mix” of commercial, manufacturing, and arts-oriented tenants. At the September EWCDH meeting, the committee unanimously passed a motion to ask that the Department of City Planning (DCP) support these businesses with specific changes to the Draft Rezoning. We asked DCP not to de-map the end of Bond Street where it meets the canal in order to maintain full vehicle access, exempt 98 4th Street & 413 Bond Street from waterfront access requirements, and exempt 413 Bond Street from the required visual corridor between 3rd Street to the canal. The full board approved this motion on the condition that these properties maintain tenancies with their current use group; by a vote of 30 in favor, 0 opposed, and 1 abstention. 

The second item on the agenda was from the Land Use side of our Landmarks/Land Use (LMLU) Committee, which had unanimously passed a motion at its September meeting, supporting a request from owners of The Old American Can Factory (OACF). After a presentation from OACF, the LMLU committee agreed that DCP should include the zoning envelop for the entirety of OACF properties within the ongoing Gowanus DEIS without an increase in Floor Area Ratio (FAR). The committee felt this request meshed with our desire to maintain affordable arts spaces within Gowanus Mix, and should be re-examined, especially in light of the imminent landmark designation. The full board approved this motion with a vote tally of 32 in favor, 0 opposed and 1 abstention. 

The next action was a vote on the plans for Henry Street Park III (LICH) that our Parks & Recreations committee had previously voted to approve conditionally, so long as any water fountains are to be usable year-round. The full board approved this motion with a vote tally of 35 in favor, 0 opposed and 1 abstention. 

The final action was to table a motion from our Transportation Committee, asking that the DCP incentivize transportation-related improvements along the Gowanus corridor in conjunction with the pending Gowanus Rezoning.

Interspersed with these votes, Senator Brian Kavanagh stopped by and spoke, and took some questions about issues such as the new rent laws . Councilmember Brad Lander also stopped by and talked about work he’s been doing, including the latest round of Participatory Budgeting . After the conclusion of the board agenda, we heard from representatives for Congresswoman Velasquez, Comptroller Stringer, Borough President Adams, Senator Montgomery Assemblymember Robert Carroll, and Assemblymember Jo Anne Simon. 

During community session, 3 of our board members spoke. Youth Services Chair, Jason Resichel, reminded everyone about the importance of the 2020 CENSUS and the work the city is doing, including funding for Community Based Organizations , to make sure we all get counted. Briget Rein let the board know that the United Federation of Teachers will be hosting a 9/11 Health forum on October 28th , and Joe Anne Brown invited everyone, and their kids, to the Thomas Greene Playground Halloween parade on Wednesday, October 30th ! 

I hope you enjoyed reading the recap as much as I enjoyed writing the recap. Before we start the weekend I’d remind you that Comptroller Stringer has a town hall tomorrow morning, Alternate Side Parking is suspended Monday and Tuesday , and click here to keep an eye on traffic and here for trains .  

﻿

As always, feel free to share this information anyway/anywhere you’d like. 

﻿

Signing off until Tuesday, 

Related tools

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Wednesday, August 28, 2019
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Before getting to the usual items of interest, I’d like to express our deepest condolences to friends and family of great civic leader, champion of LGBTQ rights, and former CB6 member, Alan Fleishman who we sadly lost yesterday. Many…
item.content:encoded:
Before getting to the usual items of interest, I’d like to express our deepest condolences to friends and family of great civic leader, champion of LGBTQ rights, and former CB6 member, Alan Fleishman who we sadly lost yesterday. Many members of CB6, including our Chair Peter Fleming, were great friends with Alan for decades. I can’t claim to have known him that long, but I know that if everyone who gets civically involved had half the impact Alan did we’d live in a better world.

There are no public arrangements as of now but if that changes I’m happy to pass along such information.

Moving on to the items of potential interest that include a shelter meeting reminder, Walt Whitman, Build The Block meeting and more…..

Have a good night and feel free to share this information anyway/anywhere you'd like.

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201

item.title: Electric Vehicle Reminder 8 1 19 2
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: As has been noted, and supported , electric car charging stations are coming to the district . There will be 3 stations, and over the next few weeks The Department of Transportation (DOT ) will be studying the following locations:
item.content:encoded:
As has been noted, and supported , electric car charging stations are coming to the district . There will be 3 stations, and over the next few weeks The Department of Transportation (DOT ) will be studying the following locations: 

‌

- 13th Street from 5th to 6th Avenue

- 3rd Street from 4th to 5th Avenue

- 7th Street from 7th Avenue to 8th Avenue

- Prospect Park West from 10 to 11th Street

- Prospect Park West 5th to 6th Street

If you’d like to give feedback on these locations I am more than happy to let DOT know what you think but you can also tell them by clicking here .

A very common question is "how many parking spaces will each station take?" The answer is each charger will take a maximum of 2 spots for a total "loss" of 6 across our district .

‌

‌

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager

item.title: Wednesday, July 31, 2019
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Here's to a thunderous Wednesday as a fitting end to the month and, if July was found wanting, let's hope August makes up the difference.
item.content:encoded:
Here's to a thunderous Wednesday as a fitting end to the month and, if July was found wanting, let's hope August makes up the difference.

In these waning hours of the month, I'd suggest taking the time to check out the items below …..

As has been noted, and supported, electric car charging stations are coming to the district. There will be 3 stations, and over the coming weeks The Department of Transportation (DOT) will be studying the following locations: 

‌

- 13th Street from 5th to 6th Avenue

- 3rd Street from 4th to 5th Avenue

- 7th Street from 7th Avenue to 8th Avenue

- Prospect Park West from 10 to 11th Street

- Prospect Park West 5th to 6th Street

If you’d like to give feedback on these locations I am more than happy to let DOT know what you think but you can also tell them by clicking here .

A very common question is "how many parking spaces will each station take?" The answer is each charger will take a maximum of 2 spots for a total "loss" of 6

across our district .

 Tomorrow, August 1st, as previously noted "Java with Jo Anne" features mocha ice cream at the Fireboat House location of Ample Hills.  A week from tonight The Parks Department and The EPA will hold a meeting at the Miccio Center updating the community on the cleanup of the Red Hook Ball Fields. Council Members Lander & Reynoso on the "missed" opportunity regarding comprehensive planning. Alternate Side Parking rules will be in effect tomorrow, Thursday, August 1st. Parking meters will also be in effect. Subway service changes for tomorrow, August 1st. Bus service changes for tomorrow, August 1st.

Have a good night and feel free to share this information anyway/anywhere you’d like.

Related tools

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager

item.description: Let me start start by highlighting how great it was to enjoy the re-imagined Ennis Playground at today’s ribbon cutting ceremony . Huge thanks are owed to Commissioners Maher & Silver of the Parks Department, Councilman Lander, Assistant…
item.content:encoded:
Let me start start by highlighting how great it was to enjoy the re-imagined Ennis Playground at today’s ribbon cutting ceremony . Huge thanks are owed to Commissioners Maher & Silver of the Parks Department, Councilman Lander, Assistant Speaker Ortiz, and Borough President Adams. What made today really special was that the final result was the realization of a vision that the Parks Department came to in collaboration with the community at large (including our board), local business's and neighbors. Our very own Paul Basile, who, along with the Gowanus Alliance , was instrumental in moving this forward when they started planting trees there 8 years ago . Along with Paul it was great to have Joanna Smith present to represent our Parks Committee.

Anyway, seeing that you've stuck with me this long you might as well check out the items below…..

item.content:encoded:
I'd like to point out, for anyone keeping score at home, that we should have been allowed to stay later at last night's board meeting but there was a mix-up and, even though our permit indicated we'd have the room until 9 PM , security a had misconception that it was 8:30 PM. Apologies to all who were negatively impacted by the abrupt shut down. In the hope of making up for it, I asked the elected officials offices that were prevented from addressing the board to send along information, which I have included, below.

Anyway, whether it’s Constant Contact or BCCing everyone, this email will still provide the usual links to weather and reminders below which, as you may have already guessed starts off with Gowanus…

item.title: Monday, February 4, 2019
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Maybe I was a bit too dismissive of the predictive power of groundhogs as Chuck and Phil reached a consensus and suddenly spring is in the air .
item.content:encoded:
Maybe I was a bit too dismissive of the predictive power of groundhogs  as Chuck and Phil reached a consensus  and suddenly spring is in the air .

Starting off the week with some familiar reminders and one explosive tidbit.

1 - Gowanus Construction -  Update from DDC regarding the $26M High-Level Storm Sewers and Water Main Replacement in north Gowanus/ Boreum Hill (CB6 & CB2).

Before sailing away from the Gowanus Canal let me remind you that Wednesday is the Department of City Planning open house at PS 32 .

2 - Tomorrow, February 5th, is Lunar New Year .  NYC Public Schools are closed , alternate side parking is suspended but meters remain in effect.

Check out BKLYNER for some suggestions on how to celebrate.

3 - Tomorrow is the Green New Deal watch party.

4 - I know some  folks in Park Slope had heard a “mysterious boom” last night at around 11:30.  Authorities informed me that it was caused by fireworks.   

5 -  Legislative update from Assistant Speaker Felix Ortiz .

6 -   As mentioned in the second bullet point, Alternate Side is suspended tomorrow, February 5 th  while meters remain in effect.

-Subway service changes for tomorrow, February 5th

- Bus service changes for tomorrow, February 5th

As always, feel free to share this information anyway you see fit!

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Friday, February 1, 2019
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Whether Punxsutawney Phil or Staten Island Chuck see their respective shadows winter never officially ends until the calendar reads March 21st. However, I remain hopeful upon seeing the list of items below and find them pertinent to…
item.content:encoded:
Whether  Punxsutawney Phil  or  Staten Island Chuck  see their respective shadows winter never officially ends until the calendar reads March 21st. However, I remain hopeful upon seeing the list of items below and find them pertinent to your life....

1 -  The 2019 Charter Revision Commission  officially decided on the issues it would explore and evaluate going forward. Its recommendations will be voted on in the November 2019 election ballot (just as was done last year).

The areas of focus will be elections, governance, finance, and land use. Clearly, those are broad topics  so check out this report to get into the specifics which include earlier involvement for Community Boards in the ULURP process and Borough level governance .

2-  Tuesday February 5th is Lunar New Year . Check out these options for celebrations across the city.  

3 - The time for registering by mail in advance of the February 26th Special Election has passed. However, if you, or anyone you know who is not registered, hesitated you need not wallow in the mire as you can still drop off a registration form at the Board of Elections.

Also, to be clear, if you are already a registered voter this does not affect you and you’ll be able to vote just like before, but feel to check your registration status here.

4-  Reminder that our February Board Meeting is coming up on Wednesday February 13th  at PS 32- this is the same location as the Gowanus Open house this coming Tuesday.

5-   Weekend Traffic Advisory

     MTA Weekend Service Updates. 

Feel free to share this information anyone you’d like, have a great weekend and stay warm!

Related tools

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Thursday, January 31, 2019
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: January 31 st isn’t always this frigid but it is always the birthday of the late great Jackie Robinson who would’ve been 100 today.
item.content:encoded:
January 31 st  isn’t always this frigid but it is always the birthday of the  late great Jackie Robinson who would’ve been 100 today.   

As people, and specifically Brooklynites, he is someone who represented the best of humanity. Even though he is renowned for stealing home. Noted CB6 native Pete Hamill summed  up, in a romanticized way I’m sure, what the Dodgers and Robinson meant to Brooklyn . In the midst of this weather it may be corny but it gives me hope and I’d say worth a read.

But you know what’s not corny?

Potentially useful updates.

1 - Seventeen Candidates to choose from on the February 26th Special Election ballot for Public Advocate . However, if you, or anyone you know isn’t registered to vote, and would like to do so by mail make sure you do it by the end of business tomorrow, Friday February 1st.

2 - An intriguing take on the famous  bookstore, landmarks, small business and Amazon. After  yesterday’s city council hearing this is especially interesting.

3-  On  February 13th Assembly Member Robert Carroll will be hosting an education forum.

4-  If you, or someone you know, is interested in helping the  DSNY clean our streets(Pay ranges from 15 to 22 dollars an hour) as snow may start to become a regular occurrence you can sign up at a local DSNY garage.

5- If you missed  last week's  DEP  presentation regarding the CSO tanks click here to see it. 

Obviously is going to be a part of our focus going forward and don't forget  DCP's open house is Wednesday February 6th. 

6-  Alternate side parking and parking meter rules will be in effect tomorrow, February 1 st . If that changes, as it sometimes does, I will let you know ASAP. 

-Subway service changes for tomorrow,  February 1 st .

- Bus service changes for tomorrow,  February 1 st .

As always, feel free to share this information anyway you see fit!

Related tools

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Wednesday, January 30, 2019
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: A snowy day is the perfect opportunity to sit in a warm room and take the time to immerse yourself in the details of an important update.
item.content:encoded:
A snowy day is the perfect opportunity to sit in a warm room and take the time to immerse yourself in the details of an important update. 

1 - The  Department of City Planning has released its draft zoning proposal , it will be the focus  one week from today on February 6 at their open house  at  PS 32.

Check out  the proposal here  and,  as I confirmed earlier today, DCP will be presenting to our Land Use Committee on February 28th.

2-  Only 2 more days to register by mail in order to vote in the  February 26th special election for Public Advocate.

Check out the actual ballot here  to see what those who are not registered will miss out on.

3-  As we head into major processes it’s always important to know where you are, where you’ve been and where you’d like to go.

In that sense it’s worth checking out  Comptroller Scott Stringers Neighborhood Economic Profiles . It can help gain a city wide, borough wide and community focused perspective (we are on pages 50 & 51).

4-  As of now alternate side parking and parking meter rules will be in effect tomorrow, January 30th.If that changes, as it sometimes does, I will let you know ASAP. 

-Subway service changes for tomorrow, January 31st

- Bus service changes for tomorrow, January 31st.

As always, feel free to share this information anyway you see fit!

item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: If you are traveling home, or anywhere, as you read this I hope it goes smoothly and please take into account that there is a “Travel Advisory” in place today and tomorrow.
item.content:encoded:
If you are traveling home, or anywhere, as you read this I hope it goes smoothly and please take into account that there is a  “Travel Advisory” in place today and tomorrow.

1 -If you want to  register, or get someone to register   by mail for the  February 26 th  special election  for  Public Advocate  you need to have it  postmarked prior to this Friday February 1 s t .

2 -One week from now is the  Green New Deal watch party  that I referred to last week.Big thanks again to our very own Hildegaard Link for putting this on my radar.

When you see the consequences of   what 35 Days of a government shutdown can do to hurt this planet , at the very least, it’s   worth tuning in.

3 -Don’t forget that next Wednesday, February 6th, is the Gowanus Open house at PS 32.

4 -  An  interesting Italian incentive .

5 - Sorry to overload with things to do on February 6 th  but the  MTA is hosting a discussion on the accessibility of Subway stations  at  2 Broadway  beginning at  6 PM and ending at 830 pm.

In a district that has long had  advocated for increased accessibility to our subway s,  not to mention the highest elevated  subway station on the planet ,  which by the way is not  ADA accessible , I reckon there will be interest.

6 - As of now alternate side parking and parking meter rules will be in effect tomorrow, January 30th.

 If that changes, as it sometimes does, I will let you know ASAP.

Update for January 29th 2019 From Brooklyn Community Board 6

February approaches with the prospect of biting cold but here's to a happy Monday.

We kick off the remains of January with a few bits of, potentially useful information.

1-  Reiterating that our very own Joe Anne Brown is still collecting, new and slightly worn, sneakers for students at Wingate High School until February 26th.

We have received some donations but can always use more. You can drop them with me at the district office and I will work with Joe Anne to make sure they get to her and the students.  You may also reach out to Ms. Brown directly at (347)282-3599

2 - I ask that you indulge some institutional boasting and check out the new print edition of BKLYNER - available at our district office along with other sites.

We take pride as this edition includes 5 articles focused on Community Board 6 along with profiles of our Chair Peter Fleming and myself . You don’t have to take my word for it, check out what Councilman Lander had to say .

3-  We have been  vocal in our support of School-Zone speed cameras . How the revenue generated from them is used is also important. For that reason, I’ve included a NY Post piece on the subject .For those who’d prefer the city to have an increase say over the way the city’s transportation and safety initiatives are administered, the proposed plan is not a good one.

4-    To offset prohibitive costs it’s interesting to see D.C allowing city technicians to repair resident’s gadgets . As the article states a trip to a chain store for repair can easily cost hundreds of dollars and can be the difference between having and not having access to technology.

5-  Alternate side parking rules, and meters, will be in effect tomorrow Tuesday, January 29 th .

-Subway service changes for tomorrow, January 29th.

- Bus service changes for tomorrow, January 29th.

As always, feel free to share this information anyway you see fit!

Michael Racioppo, District Manager

250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201-6401

item.title: Friday, January 25, 2019
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Friday January 25th, 2019: the day when an agreement seems (as of this writing) to have been put in place to reopen the Federal Government for 3 weeks.
item.content:encoded:
Friday January 25th, 2019: the day when an agreement seems (as of this writing) to have been put in place to reopen the Federal Government for 3 weeks.

Somehow, I feel like I missed the Federalist Paper that explained the founders envisioning government as perpetually, and temporarily, delayed, due to entirely self-imposed crisis.In contrast, our Municipal Government has not suffered the same consequence and for that reason I am able to send out some useful reminders as we head into the last weekend of January.

1 -  I reiterate that on February 6th , from 6 PM until 8 PM at  PS 32 , the Department of City Planning w ill be hosting an open house focused on the next steps in the Gowanus rezoning process. 

Speaking of that process click here to see the Gowanus By Design (GBD) slide presentation that was given at our Landmarks & Land Use Committee meeting last night by our very own David Briggs wearing his other hat as  GBD  executive director.

2 - A week from today, February 1st, is the last day to register by mail to vote in the February 26th special election for the citywide position of Public Advocate.  

3 - Weekend Traffic Advisory

    MTA Weekend Service Updates. 

Have a great weekend and, as always, feel free to share this information anyway you see fit!

While you must cross the border into a neighboring community district no passport is required and it is an excellent opportunity to meet with someone who represents so many of us in the state legislature. 

4 - Tell your children not to forget their hats and mittens;    DSNY has issued a snow alert for tomorrow. Staying with DSNY updates, remember Monday we honor Martin Luther King Jr., there will be no trash, recycling, or organics collections on the holiday.

So if you normal trash or organics collection is Monday’s put it curbside any time after 4 PM so it can be picked up on Tuesday, January 22 nd . I hope this email finds you well after a winter weekend that, based on only from the attire, could've taken place in the fall or spring.

We start by noting that State Senator Velmanette Montgomery , who has represented much of our BkCB6 district for nearly 40 years, announced that she is retiring at the end of her current term . We will miss her tireless work for all, but especially for at-risk children. We thank her for her years dedicated to our community. Whoever succeeds her will have some very large shoes to fill.

Following the thread of concern for children, one of the things happening this week is the Citizen Squirrell workshop . BKCB6 is a co-sponsor, and it is taking place tomorrow, from 3:30 until 5:00 pm at the Park Slope Library . There are of course other items, and happenings, taking place around us but for those and an eminently shareable Citizen Squirrel Flyer , you’ll have to keep scrolling.

Have a good evening, feel free to  share this information  however/wherever you’d like .

item.title: Last Night, Next Week and More..... I hope this email finds you well on this cold 9th day of January. Our January
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Our January board meeting, held last night at PS 58 , had a light agenda, but it's likely to be “the calm before the storm” before winds of 2020 starting blowing in. We were out of there in under an hour, as there was only 1 item on the…
item.content:encoded:
Our January board meeting, held last night at PS 58 , had a light agenda, but it's likely to be “the calm before the storm” before winds of 2020 starting blowing in. We were out of there in under an hour, as there was only 1 item on the agenda for approval.

Prior to dealing with the permits and licensing motion, our Board Secretary Karen Broughton, officially, certified the election of our current officers (Chair, 1 st Vice-Chair, 2 nd Vice-Chair, Secretary, and Treasurer) for another one-year term. It must be noted that Karen’s attendance is particularly impressive as she made it back in time after being in Albany , where she attended the Governor’s “State of the State” address.

The December 2019 minutes were approved. Chairperson Peter Fleming then gave his report, which included informing those in attendance about the revocation of the liquor license for Woodlands and the resale of the 5th Avenue Key food site . Peter made a point of mentioning that the new owners have indicated they will adhere to the agreement to retain a supermarket at the 120 5th Avenue address. We will continue to monitor the situation in conjunction with Councilmember Lander’s office. This is especially important with   so many supermarkets closing in recent years ,  and given how hard the  community worked to make sure a supermarket  would still serve our community. Peter also let folks know that applications for membership on Brooklyn community boards are open and will remain so until February 14th.

On the subject of board applications, my report got rolling by letting folks know that hard copies of the applications were available at the meeting, as well as online and that with few opening becoming a public member was a terrific alternative option. I then mentioned the Noel Pointer Foundation becoming the new tenants at the Degraw Street Firehouse and discussed our involvemen t with Warren Street tenants as an example of how CB6 can work to build better relationships between our neighbors and their city government. Of Course, I mentioned subscribing to this email update as it helps create a dialogue and open lines of communication. If something is going on in our community that you’d like to get on the CB6 radar, please let me know. For example, this update is the reason I’m planning on attending the Park Slope Civic Council meeting tonight at the Old Stone House . Every weekday you can scroll down that day’s email to find out about other community happenings.

Our Permits and Licenses Committee Chair Rachel Freeman presented their recommendation for approval of a sidewalk café at 72 5th Avenue that we overwhelmingly approved .

Representatives from the offices of Borough President Adams , Congresswoman Clarke , Councilmembers Lander and Levin , State Senators Montgomery and Myrie , Assemblymembers Carroll and Simon each spoke on behalf of their principals. 

When we went into community session, there was mention of public safety concerns and drug use around Baltic Street and 4 th Avenue/ Gregory Place about and we’ve already reached out to proper authorities. 

During New Business, Joe Anne Brown reemphasized the work we’ve been doing at Warren Street and the concerns residents continue to express. Kathy Park Price reminded everyone of the Citizens Squirrel event CB6 is co-sponsoring this upcoming Tuesday, January 14th and 1st Vice-Chair Eric McClure announced that our Transportation /Public Safety committee, with a location & agenda still being ironed out, would be meeting on January 30th which is the 5th Thursday of the month and not the usual 3rd Thursday.

So that, as best I can recall, is the gist of our first General Board Meeting for 2020. Have a good evening, feel free to share this information however/wherever you’d like.

P.S. Please forgive any typos or brain freezes in the text as I get these updates out in haste at the end of the day.

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.description: Speaking of 2020" firsts", last night, our Permits & Licenses Committee met and unanimously recommended, without a quorum, a sidewalk café application for Pizza Secret at 72 5th Avenue and will be up for motion and ratification at…
item.content:encoded:
Speaking of 2020" firsts", last night, our Permits & Licenses Committee met and unanimously recommended, without a quorum, a sidewalk café application for Pizza Secret at 72 5th Avenue and will be up for motion and ratification at tomorrow’s meeting.

Another 2020 "first" was this morning's “ Java with Jo Anne , ” which had multiple members of our executive committee i n attendance . If you haven’t been to a “Java” if you have the chance, it’s a great way to get to know Assemblymember Simon and her staff. When the next “Java” is scheduled, you can be sure it’ll be shared in a BKCB6 Update.

If you choose to keep scrolling, you’ll find more things happening for the first time this year, including tonight’s 76 th  Precinct Community Council meeting led by our very own Jerry Armer.

Of course, it’s always possible you’ve seen something I missed in our active community, so if there is a community-centric item you’d like me to include,  please reach out.

Have a great evening, and feel free to share  this information.

P.S. Please forgive any typos or brain freezes in the text as I get these updates out in haste at the end of the day.

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org

item.title: Weekend Meeting, Committee Meeting, Board Meeting, More I hope this email finds you well after a weekend that inc
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: I hope this email finds you well after a weekend that included a Sunday on which thousands, many BKCB6ers among them, marched against hate .
item.content:encoded:
I hope this email finds you well after a weekend that included a Sunday on which thousands, many BKCB6ers among them, marched against hate .

The weekend also included, on Saturday, a Warren Street tenant’s initiated meeting with the stated goal of letting residents know that there was going to be a request made to the Mayor asking that NYCHA hold another meeting to answer questions, with greater clarity than there has been, on topics such as lease renewals and the RAD program .

BKCB6 Board member and Warren Street resident, Joe Anne Brown, was kind enough to invite me to this meeting and with that, I was able to extend the invitation to the Mayor’s Deputy Chief of Staff, Lincoln Restler who, like me, accepted the invitation; his attendance allowed the residents, and their meeting request, to be directly heard and responded to. Mr. Restler assured those in attendance, including Ben Solitaire from Councilman Levin’s office & representatives from the Gowanus Neighborhood Coalition for Justice (GNCJ) , that NYCHA will hold an additional meeting accomplishing Saturday’s stated goal.

This Warren Street meeting further reinforces, issues we’ve highlighted throughout the Gowanus rezoning process , that significant improvements must be guaranteed for NYCHA.

Now moving to what will be a busy week that includes tonight’s Permits and Licenses Committee meeting and Wednesday’s General Board Meeting. There are plenty of happenings that you can review by scrolling down.

Of course, it’s always possible you’ve seen something I missed in our active community, so if there is a community-centric item you’d like me to include,  please reach out.

Have a great evening, and feel free to share  this information.

P.S. Please forgive any typos or brain freezes in the text as I get these updates out in haste at the end of the day.
