item.description: Brooklyn Community Board Six Newsletter October 2018 Welcome Back- The Community Board Never Sleeps Above: CB6 District Manager Mike Racioppo, Council Member Brad Lander, Borough President Eric Adams,
item.content:encoded:
Brooklyn Community Board Six

Newsletter

October 2018

Welcome Back- The Community Board Never Sleeps

Above: CB6 District Manager Mike Racioppo, Council Member Brad Lander, Borough President Eric Adams, NYC Parks Commissioner Mitchell Silver, and NYC Parks Brooklyn Borough Commissioner Marty Maher (Photo: Nathan Haselby)

Welcome Back!

The Community Board Never Sleeps!

In most instances the summer is a time when we, and other Community Boards, are on a “hiatus''. However, here at CB6 our  L and Use & Landmark Committee , Permits & License Committee and  Economic Waterfront Community Development and Housing Committee (EWCDH) remained in session.

The permits and Licensing Committee met to approve liquor licenses ,while the Landmarks/Land Use Committee met to evaluate Certificates of Appropriateness and applications to the Board of Standard and Appeals . The EWCDH Committee met with budget directors from Councilman Lander and Councilman Levin’s offices in order to be best prepared to advocate for our community in the city budget as we prepare to submit our district needs assessment in the fall.

Check out last years District Needs Assessment here.

After these committees met the, their recommendations were then ratified by our executive committee and sent on to the appropriate agency’s such as the the State Liquor Authority and Landmarks Preservation Commission.

Over the summer CB6 also followed through on projects such as the Innis Playground and the 9th Street redesign .

As our new(ish) District Manager, Mike Racioppo has made a point of mentioning(in his District Manager report/ while attending various meetings) he is excited to be working with, and for the community, and if you’d like to connect with him, feel free to send him an email .

Now, as the leaves start to change, the semi-hiatus is over and we are back to regular order!

BKCB-6 Facebooking , tweeting and Instagramming just for you!

We use Social Media to highlight the boards work, openings and exciting activities throughout the community; but in addition we use it as a resource for Carroll Gardens, Cobble Hill, Columbia Waterfront, Gowanus, Park Slope & Red Hook, offering helpful updates and information as seen in  the tweet above  letting folks know about the weeks  paving and milling schedule.

So Please "Like" us on Facebook , Follow on Twitter & Instagram !

Chair's Report

Dear Fellow BKCB-6ers,

On September 18th the City’s Landmarks Preservation Commission voted unanimously to designate the former Hans S. Christian Memorial Kindergarten at 236 President Street, and the adjacent red-brick at 238 President Street as landmark sites .

We were very pleased to learn this news, as the protection of a valuable piece of our community’s fabric is extremely important to us. You may recall that earlier this year, upon hearing about the potential demolition of these important, and historic, buildings, we immediately sent a letter asking the Landmarks Preservation Commission (LPC) and the Department of Buildings to look into this matter . LPC calendared the properties for land marking consideration and our board voted, unanimously, to support landmark designation.

As cited by various reports and noted in the board's resolution this location was important in the social reform movements of the 20th century and, thanks to hard work from members of our community, our elected officials, and many others we have preserved a tangible reminder of that great history.

Also, we are restarting tradition of giving out the  CB6 Youth Acknowledgement Awards and the Robert Acito Award for Youth Involvement.

Youth Acknowledgement Awards will be given to youth between the ages of 10 to 19 who reside, attend school or volunteer for some organization serving the CB6 district. The contribution must have occurred in 2018 and may include, but is not limited to, tutoring, participating in community-based projects, assisting the needy, or triumphing over a personal challenge. Only volunteers will be considered eligible for this award.

The Robert Acito Award for Youth Involvement will be given to an adult member of the CB6 community who has demonstrated a commitment to young people and has proven to be a positive force in their lives. Robert Acito served as District Manager from 1980-1993 and in his lifetime worked tirelessly on behalf of the youth of the district. Since his passing, the Community Board has chosen to honor Bob’s memory by selecting an adult member of the community who has demonstrated a similar sense of purpose.

Nomination forms can be found below :

Youth Acknowledgement Award Application Form

Robert Acito Award for Youth Involvement Application Form

Lastly, we are looking for public members for the following committees Parks & Recreation , Permits & Licences , Youth Human Services and Education , Economic/ Waterfront Community Development and Housing ,

If you are interested in serving on any of these committees please apply here .

Landmarks

Over the summer, Brooklyn Community Board 6 also reviewed and commented on two applications for Certificates of Appropriateness(a/k/a C of A) . Both applications were with respect to properties in the Park Slope Historic District .

An application at 513 11th Street was approved with respect to the front of the building, however it was disapproved with regard to the rear extension, and sunken backyard as inconsistent with the context and integrity of the historic district while the application for a penthouse rooftop addition was conditionally approved with reduced glazing.

The application with for 535 1st Street , was disapproved. as the extension is too large and out of character with the historic district, the glazing on the sides of the extension is overwhelming and inconsistent with glazing pattern of other extensions, and since no buildings on the block maintain historic balustrades restoration of a historic balustrade is no longer in context.

Next Landmarks & Land Use Committee Meeting:

October 25th, 6 PM

Location& Agenda TBD

Land Use

On the Land Use front Community Board 6 approved an application to the Board of Standard and Appeals for a modification to zoning to permit the construction for residential use of a new four-story building, in an M1-1 zoning district at 104 Degraw Street (Between Van Brunt and Columbia) subject to the condition that the first floor be designated and used only for commercial space as presented by the applicant.

Next Landmarks & Land Use Committee Meeting:

October 25th, 6 PM

Location& Agenda TBD

Permits & Licenses

In what was once the Tea Lounge ( 837-839 Union Street 6th & 7th Ave ) , BKCB-6’s Permits and Licenses Committee approved a new on-premises liquor license application submitted to the State Liquor Authority on behalf of EJ Clarke LLC, which will do business as The Slope Lounge .

The slope lounge plans to have a kitchen that serves up light Jamaican fare and features a Sunday brunch. It will also have various forms of entertainment from puppet shows for kids, to poetry and comedy at night!

item.title: Monthly Newsletter, April 2018
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: Board Meeting Wednesday March 14, 6:30 p.m. Brooklyn Community Board Six Monthly Newsletter April 2018 Welcome to Our New Newsletter Welcome to the new Brooklyn Community Board Six Newsletter. The fir
item.content:encoded:
Board Meeting Wednesday March 14, 6:30 p.m.

Brooklyn Community Board Six

Monthly Newsletter

April 2018

Welcome to Our New Newsletter

Welcome to the new Brooklyn Community Board Six Newsletter. The first thing you will notice is that the name is blank. The Sixth Sense is a name from the past, and while we at BKCB-6 will always respect and build upon our strong history and foundation, we need to move away from the last century* and look towards the future.

Our community is strongest when we celebrate our diversity and acknowledge that Red Hook, Park Slope, Gowanus, Columbia Waterfront, Cobble Hill and Carroll Gardens are each amazing neighborhoods, but when knit together to form Community Board Six make for an even stronger community. It is with that understanding and the desire to ensure that residents and businesses that call our district home are aware of what the Board is doing we have revamped the newsletter to better reflect our motions and votes.

Some of our goals with this monthly newsletter are to:

More clearly demonstrate the motions BKCB-6 takes on issues

Increase the dialogue between those who receive the newsletter and the Community Board office

Through the increased dialogue provide greater transparency

Provide community updates

General information sharing

Thanks and have a great month!

An early test of the back and forth with the community, is the fact that we want to hear from you as to what we should name the newsletter. We will accept names over the next month and then bring it to a vote of the BKCB-6 Executive committee. Please send all names to info@brooklyncb6.org.

*The Sixth Sense , a film starring Bruce Willis, Haley Joel Osment and Directed by M Night Shyamalan, came out in 1999

Chair's Report

Normally the Chair's Report is filled with recaps of meetings, acknowledgements and thanks. This month’s report actually featured two items that ultimately came up for a vote. While unusual, these were time sensitive matters that couldn’t or shouldn’t wait for the following month’s committee meetings.

Support of Congress Member Nydia Velazquez Superfund Enhancement Act. Congress Member Velazquez has asked for community support prior to introducing this bill, which would enhance the current Superfund program by reinstating the "Superfund Tax" on chemical and oil industries. The Superfund Tax was repealed in 1995 due to pressure from the Chemical and Oil lobbies. The reinstated Superfund Tax would finance:

Tax deductions for small businesses, home owners, and renters forced to relocate from in or near a Superfund site. The maximum tax deduction would be $10,000.

A "Disaster Loan" pilot program, administered by the Small Business Administration, annually appropriating $10,000,000 for fiscal years 2019 through 2023, providing direct loans to eligible small businesses, home owners, and renters that have been forced to relocate from a Superfund site.

Economic Injury Loan program for small business forced to relocate from a Superfund site.

It is important to note that the bill language originally offered tax deductions and the Disaster Loan Pilot Program only to small businesses. Feedback from our Economics, Waterfront, Community Development and Housing committee led to the bill including home owners and renters in both of those programs. The Board voted unanimously to support the bill.

A motion was made to request that the NYC Department of Transportation immediately undertake a study to ensure pedestrian safety at 5th Avenue and 9th Street in the wake of the horrific accident on March 5th. The Board voted unanimously to support the motion. To view the Board's letter to Mayor de Blasio and NYC DOT Commissioner Polly Trottenberg, click here.

Economics, Waterfront, Community Development and Housing

NYCHA Wyckoff Gardens

The committee and the Full Board passed a motion to send a letter drafted by the Wyckoff Gardens Tenant’s Association to NYCHA, requesting that NYCHA respond to the letter and share the information with us prior to our upcoming review of the City’s Next-Gen Housing proposal for the parking lot at Wyckoff Gardens. To view the Board's letter to NYCHA Chair Shola Olatoye, click here .

Landmarks

236 / 238 President Street

The Board was made aware of an attempt by neighbors of 236 and 238 President Street to receive an individual Landmark designation for both addresses. As such, we formally asked the Landmarks Preservation Commission to expedite their initial review of this application to determine if it was worth sending to our Landmarks committee for consideration. In conjunction, we asked the Department of Buildings to refrain from granting any permits for work that would alter the exterior historical character of these buildings until the Landmarks Preservation Commission had an opportunity to review the matter and determine if it was worthy of referral back to BKCB-6. At this time, BKCB-6 took no official position on the properties landmark designation. To view the Board's letter to the Landmarks Preservation Commission and the Department of Buildings, click here .

On Tuesday, April 10th, the Landmarks Preservation Commission ruled that they would calendar these two addresses for consideration in the coming months.

Additionally, our Landmarks committee took two motions for conditional approval to the March Full Board, and both were ratified:

Approval of a Certificate of Appropriateness application for storefront facade renovations, a new secondary egress door, and a rear yard extension at 76-82 St. Marks Avenue, under the condition that the applicant use brick or brick veneer on visible sides of the rear yard extension. (31 Yeas, 4 Nays, 0 Abstentions)

Approval of a Certificate of Appropriateness application for a new rooftop staircase bulkhead, near placement of stained glass windows, and a new first floor double door at 608 5th Street, under the condition that the applicant reduce the size of the bulkhead from front to rear so as to be less visible from the street. (29 Yeas, 6 Nays, 0 Abstentions)

Land Use

Proposed 280 Richards Street Overhead View

Our Land Use committee sent two motions to the March Full Board.

Conditional approval of an application submitted to the Department of City Planning for a grant of authorization pursuant to Section 62-822(a) of the New York City Zoning Resolution to modify the location, area and minimum dimension requirements of Section 62-50 (General Requirements for Visual Corridors and Waterfront Public Access Areas) and, in conjunction therewith, 62-332 (Rear Yard and Waterfront Yards); and an application for the grant of authorization pursuant to Section 62-822(b) of the New York City Zoning Resolution to modify the requirements of Section 62-513 (Permitted Obstruction in Visual Corridors) and Section 62-60 (Design Requirements for Waterfront Public Access Areas) at 280 Richards Street.

The applicant must commit in writing to include a public bathroom on the esplanade.

The applicant must enter into an agreement with the New York State Department of Environmental Conservation to remediate debris on the site.

The applicant must conduct an independent investigation into causes of flooding on Beard Street and present their findings to the NYC Department of Environmental Protection.

The applicant must cover the existing piles of dirt on the site immediately.

Approval of an application submitted to the Board of Standards and Appeals for a special permit pursuant to Section 73-44 of the New York City Zoning Resolution to permit the reduction of accessory parking spaces for a proposed altered building at 288 4th Avenue with uses in the parking requirement category B1.

Both motions passed the full board. 280 Richards Street was supported by a vote of 25 Yeas, 7 Nays, and 4 Abstentions. 288 4th Avenue was supported unanimously. To view the Board's resolution regarding 280 Richards Street, click here . To view the Board's resolution on 288 4th Avenue, click here .

Permits & Licenses

Our Permits & Licenses committee voted to deny - for the second time in a row - the renewal of the liquor license for Woodland (AKA Prime Six, Inc.) at 242 Flatbush Avenue. This vote was based on years of community feedback and page upon page of 311 complaints made by residents of the surrounding blocks. The Board voted to ratify the motion to deny with a vote of 32 Yeas, 0 Nays, and 1 Abstention.

Our District Office and Permits & Licenses committee have supported the back-to-back denial votes by participating in repeated attempts over multiple years with a wide range of stakeholders to bring Woodland into compliance not just with the State Liquor Authority (SLA) regulations, but with prior agreements they've made with the community and with basic, dignified and neighborly consideration. The view the Board's letter to the SLA on this matter, click here.

The SLA has finally recognized the situation. Woodland's liquor license is currently operating under the State Administrative Procedure Act (SAPA), which is to say Woodland is under review by the SLA for a series of violations.

Brooklyn Community Board Six has long been on record with the SLA regarding the issues surrounding this establishment. We ask that neighbors experiencing these issues continue to report them to 311, the 78th Precinct, the SLA, and your State elected officials and continue to communicate with our District Office.

The Permits & Licenses committee took five other motions to the March full board, each of them passing unanimously:

Motion to approve a new on-premises liquor license application submitted to the State Liquor Authority on behalf of Popina NYC LLC at 127 Columbia Street (between Kane Street/Degraw Street).

Motion to approve an alteration to an existing on-premises liquor license submitted to the State Liquor Authority and an application to the New York City Department of Consumer Affairs to permit a sidewalk café with 4 tables and 8 chairs on behalf of Varrio 408 at 412 5th Avenue (between 7th Street/8th Street).

Motion to approve an alteration to an existing on-premises liquor license application submitted to the State Liquor Authority and an application to the New York City Department of Consumer Affairs to permit a sidewalk café with 5 tables and 10 chairs on behalf of Chela at 408 5th Avenue (between 7th Street/8th Street).

Motion to approve a new on-premises liquor license application submitted to the State Liquor Authority on behalf of The Bklyn Juice Co., LLC at 75A 5th Avenue (between St. Marks Avenue/Prospect Place).

Motion to approve a new on-premises liquor license application submitted to the State Liquor Authority on behalf of Waterfront Partners LLC at 215 Columbia Street (between Sackett Street/Union Street).

Transportation & Public Safety

Proposed Bike Corral outside PS 118

Our Transportation & Public Safety committee brought one motion to the full board - Approval of a NYC Department of Transportation plan to install a bike corral at the northwest corner of 7th Street and 4th Avenue, outside of PS 118. The corral was requested by PS 118. The Board unanimously ratified the motion to approve the bike corral.

April Full Board Meeting Information

Tuesday, April 24 at 6:30pm

P.S. 32 Auditorium

317 Hoyt Street (between Union Street and President Street)

Brooklyn, NY 11231

Click Here for Meeting Agenda

Click here to preview the April Full Board Presentations

Things to Do in the District

Join PortSide New York aboard the Mary A. Whalen for Second Sunday TankerTime from 5pm until Midnight on May 13th at its docked location in Atlantic Basin. TankerTime repeats on the second Sunday of every month, from May through September.

Bring dinner, drinks, a book... Lounge in a hammock, read books from the PortSide maritime library. Stretch out in a lounge chair, immerse yourself in the maritime ambiance of the Mary Whalen's location. At 9 pm, the musicians jam of Mediterranean music starts and runs until midnight.

Part of the PortSide New York's MARY Month of May festival in honor of the 80th Birthday of the Mary A. Whalen on May 21, 2018.

Join the Gowanus Canal Conservancy for Expo Gowanus in Thomas Greene Playground, Saturday May 19 from 11am - 3pm. Visit over 30 activity stations with environmentally-themed art, science, engineering, dance and music performances. Try hands-on activities with solar power, weaving, painting, robotics, and more! The event will feature the  Carnival of Connectivity , Gowanus artists, poets and performers who will engage adults and children in playful, spontaneous experiences.

Friends of Brooklyn Community Board 6, Inc. supports the work of Brooklyn Community Board 6 in improving the quality of life in the district. Friends provides planning, advocacy, research and administrative resources to supplement the limited capacities and budget of the Community Board, thus enabling it to properly carry out its City Charter mandated tasks of evaluating the needs of the district and advocating on behalf of its communities.

Friends of Brooklyn Community Board 6, Inc. is a registered 501(c)(3) non-profit organization (Federal EIN 04-3780020). Donations are welcome and are tax-deductible to the fullest extent allowed by law.

item.content:encoded:
March 1, 2018

Dear residents, business owners and friends of Brooklyn Community Board Six,

At the last full board meeting ,  I very enthusiastically announced that our Finance, Personal and Law (FPL) committee had received city approval and publicly posted our open District Manager position.

This is great news for our Board and means that we are that much closer to having a full staff in our district office. The hard work that our district office staff has been undertaking has been much appreciated, but for BKCB-6 to be the great Board I know we can be and that each of you deserves ,  we need to fill the District Manager position.

Please share this  job posting  with all qualified candidates in your network. The FPL committee is reviewing applications on a rolling basis and will be calling in prospective District Managers for interviews over the next month. We would like to have all applications in by March 15 th , but may extend that date pending the number and quality of applications we have received.

Sincerely,

Sayar Lonial

Chairperson

item.title: Monday, January 8, 2018
item.dc:creator: Mike Racioppo
item.description: We've just had Christmas and New Year’s eves and yes they are undeniably big events. However, we have now arrived at the biggest eve of them all; it is the day before the January BCB6 General Board Meeting .
item.content:encoded:
We've just had Christmas and New Year’s eves and yes they are undeniably big events. However, we have now arrived at the biggest eve of them all; it is the day before the  January BCB6 General Board Meeting . This awesome confab will take place tomorrow night, beginning at 6:30 PM, at  New York-Presbyterian Brooklyn Methodist Hospital  and will conclude with a motion to adjourn. 

Along with that important reminder I’m sending along a few bits of information that, I hope, can be put to good use.

1 - Next Wednesday, January 16 th  at my Alma Mater,  MS 51 , we are co-sponsoring, with  CEC15 ,  BKCB7  and other groups, a forum on the  Mayor's plan to improve diversity at Specialized High Schools.   

Check out the  flyer here.

 2 - Want to thank our very own Victoria Alexander for putting the  Red Hook Winter Coat giveaway on my radar.  Check it out.

3 - Alternate side parking rules, and meters,  will be in effect tomorrow Wednesday, January 9 th .

-Subway service changes for tomorrow, January 9th.

-  Bus Service Changes for tomorrow, January 9th.

Of course, as always, feel free to share this information with anyone, by any means you see fit!

Best,
Mike Racioppo, District Manager
Brooklyn Community Board 6 · 250 Baltic Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
Mike@bkcb6.org
